title: Energy intake and appetite are suppressed by glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) in obese men.
journal: International journal of obesity and related metabolic disorders : journal of the International Association for the Study of Obesity
population: Obese male subjects with body mass index (BMI) 45.5 kg/m2
intervention: Intravenous infusion of GLP-1 (glucagon-like peptide-1) at 0.75 pmol/kg/min for eight hours
comparison: Intravenous infusion of saline
outcomes_primary: Ad libitum energy intake at lunch and dinner
outcomes_secondary: Appetite sensations using visual analogue scales (VAS) including hunger ratings; blood glucose, insulin, C-peptide, GLP-1, and peptide YY concentrations; gastric emptying measured using paracetamol absorption technique; nausea
extraction_notes: Small sample size (n=8). Cross-over design. Primary outcome not explicitly designated; energy intake and appetite appear to be co-primary based on study objective.

title: Continuous subcutaneous infusion of glucagon-like peptide 1 lowers plasma glucose and reduces appetite in type 2 diabetic patients.
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes
intervention: GLP-1 (glucagon-like peptide 1) 2.4 pmol/kg/min administered by continuous subcutaneous infusion for 48 hours
comparison: Saline administered by continuous subcutaneous infusion for 48 hours
extraction_notes: Small sample size (n=6). Crossover design with randomized order. Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract. Outcomes assessed included: appetite measures (hunger, prospective food intake, satiety, fullness), plasma glucose (fasting and 24-hour mean), insulin, C-peptide, glucagon, postprandial lipidemia (triglycerides, free fatty acids), blood pressure, heart rate, basal metabolic rate, and side effects.

title: Inhibition of sham feeding-stimulated human gastric acid secretion by glucagon-like peptide-2.
journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
population: Healthy volunteers
intervention: GLP-2 infused intravenously at a rate of 0.8 pmol/kg x min during sham feeding
comparison: Saline infusion during sham feeding
outcomes_primary: Gastric acid secretion
outcomes_secondary: Gastric volume, osmolarity, plasma concentrations of GLP-2, GLP-1, gastrin, cholecystokinin, and secretin
extraction_notes: Crossover design with eight subjects studied twice on separate days. Primary outcome not explicitly designated; listed based on study focus. Sample size is small (n=8).

title: Effect of glucagon-like peptide 1(7-36)amide in insulin-treated patients with diabetes mellitus secondary to chronic pancreatitis.
population: Patients with diabetes mellitus secondary to chronic pancreatitis treated with insulin (9 patients) or sulfonylurea (1 patient); normal subjects also included as control group
intervention: Glucagon-like peptide 1(7-36)amide (GLP-1) infused intravenously at doses of 0.4 or 1.2 pmol/min/kg body weight for 4 hours
comparison: Saline infusion (fasting state)
outcomes_primary: Blood glucose levels
outcomes_secondary: Plasma C-peptide concentration; plasma glucagon concentration
extraction_notes: Small sample size (10 patients, 5 normal subjects). Primary vs secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract; classification inferred from emphasis. Study appears to be a crossover design with each subject receiving saline and both GLP-1 doses.

title: Effect of glucagon on carbohydrate-mediated secretion of glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) and glucagon-like peptide-1 (7-36 amide) (GLP-1).
population: Healthy men aged 23.6 years with body mass index of 24.0 kg/m²
intervention: Intravenous infusion of glucagon with 100 g oral carbohydrate load containing 1.5 g paracetamol
comparison: Intravenous infusion of saline with 100 g oral carbohydrate load containing 1.5 g paracetamol
outcomes_secondary: Plasma glucose concentrations, plasma GIP concentrations, plasma GLP-1 concentrations, plasma insulin concentrations, plasma paracetamol concentrations (marker of gastric emptying)
extraction_notes: Small sample size (n=6). Primary outcomes not explicitly distinguished from secondary outcomes. Study duration for measurements was 6 hours post-carbohydrate load. Crossover design implied but not explicitly stated.

title: Effects of intraduodenal glucose and fructose on antropyloric motility and appetite in healthy humans.
journal: American journal of physiology. Regulatory, integrative and comparative physiology
population: Healthy volunteers
intervention: Intraduodenal infusion of 25% fructose, 2 ml/min for 90 min
comparison: Intraduodenal infusion of 25% glucose (2 ml/min for 90 min); Intraduodenal infusion of 0.9% saline (2 ml/min for 90 min)
extraction_notes: Small sample size (n=10). Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished; measured outcomes included antropyloric pressures, blood glucose, plasma insulin, gastric inhibitory peptide (GIP), glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1), and food intake at buffet meal. This appears to be a crossover study design based on methodology description.

title: The effect of glucagon-like peptide-1 on energy expenditure and substrate metabolism in humans.
journal: International journal of obesity and related metabolic disorders : journal of the International Association for the Study of Obesity
population: Healthy, normal weight men (body mass index 20.3-25.7 kg/m2), aged 20-31 years
intervention: GLP-1 (glucagon-like peptide-1) infusion, 50 pmol/kg x h, started simultaneously with initiation of test meals
comparison: Saline infusion (placebo)
outcomes_primary: Diet-induced thermogenesis (DIT); energy expenditure; substrate oxidation (carbohydrate, fat, protein oxidation)
outcomes_secondary: Desire to eat specific types of food assessed by visual analogue scales; palatability of test meals; plasma hormone and substrate concentrations (including NEFA, CCK, GLP-2)
extraction_notes: Cross-over design with 20 subjects. Primary vs secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract; categorization based on stated objectives. Infusion duration not explicitly stated.

title: Influence of acarbose on post-prandial insulin requirements in patients with Type 1 diabetes.
population: Patients with Type 1 diabetes (T1DM)
intervention: Acarbose 100 mg administered orally with a standardised meal
comparison: Placebo administered with a standardised meal
outcomes_primary: Insulin requirement for maintenance of normoglycaemia over 3-hour post-meal period, assessed using closed-loop insulin infusion system (artificial pancreas, Biostator)
outcomes_secondary: Post-prandial triglyceride levels; glucagon levels; gastrointestinal peptide levels including gastric inhibitory polypeptide (AUC, Cmax, tmax); gastric emptying; oxidative glucose metabolism; blood glucose control
extraction_notes: Cross-over design with 10+/-3 day washout period. Sample size of 10 patients. Primary outcome not explicitly labeled but inferred from stated primary objective. Blood glucose was normalised before meal administration.

title: Short-term treatment with GLP-1 increases pulsatile insulin secretion in Type II diabetes with no effect on orderliness.
population: Type II (non-insulin-dependent) diabetes mellitus patients (n = 8)
intervention: GLP-1 infusion at 1.2 pmol/l x kg(-1) x min(-1) with plasma glucose clamped at initial concentration by variable glucose infusion
comparison: Saline infusion (randomised cross-over design, 2 separate days)
outcomes_primary: Pulsatile insulin secretion measured by secretory burst mass and secretory burst amplitude
outcomes_secondary: Serum insulin concentrations; basal insulin secretion; fraction of insulin delivered in pulses; regularity of secretion measured by spectral analysis (normalised spectral power), autocorrelation analysis (autocorrelation coefficient), and approximate entropy statistic
extraction_notes: Short-term infusion duration not explicitly specified. Primary vs secondary outcomes not explicitly designated in abstract; categorization based on study aims.

title: No effect of glucagon-like peptide-1 on short-term satiety and energy intake in man.
population: Non-obese male subjects, n=10
intervention: GLP-1 (glucagon-like peptide-1) infusion at 1.2 pmol/kg per min for 1 hour, administered peripherally starting at 18:00 hours
comparison: Saline infusion (control)
outcomes_primary: Gastric emptying of a 400 ml water load (measured at 20 minutes after starting infusion)
outcomes_secondary: Energy intake from ad libitum buffet meal (at 40 minutes); self-assessment of hunger and satiety using behavioural self-rating scales; circulating GLP-1 concentrations; circulating insulin levels; glucose levels
extraction_notes: Randomized single-blind within-subject crossover design. Primary outcome not explicitly designated; gastric emptying listed first and appears to be the main physiological measure. Duration of follow-up beyond the acute study period not specified.

title: Diet-induced change in fatty acid composition of plasma triacylglycerols is not associated with change in glucagon-like peptide 1 or insulin sensitivity in people with type 2 diabetes.
journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
population: Overweight people with type 2 diabetes
intervention: High-MUFA diet (20.3% of total energy from monounsaturated fatty acids) for 24 days
comparison: High-PUFA diet (13.4% of total energy from polyunsaturated fatty acids) for 24 days
outcomes_primary: Insulin sensitivity measured by short-insulin-tolerance test; glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1) levels (fasting and postprandial incremental area under the curve)
outcomes_secondary: Plasma triacylglycerol linoleic-oleic acid ratio; phospholipid linoleic-oleic acid ratio; total to HDL cholesterol ratio; glucose, insulin, triacylglycerol, and nonesterified fatty acids (fasting and postprandial incremental area under the curve)
extraction_notes: Small sample size (n=9). Randomized double-blind crossover design. Diets were isoenergetic.

title: Circulating levels of incretin hormones and amylin in the fasting state and after oral glucose in GH-deficient patients before and after GH replacement: a placebo-controlled study.
population: 24 GH-deficient adults
intervention: GH replacement therapy: daily evening injections of 2 IU GH/m² for 4 months
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_secondary: Plasma concentrations of glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1), glucose-dependent insulin-releasing peptide (GIP), total amylin, non-glycosylated amylin in fasting state and after oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT); plasma concentrations of glucose and insulin; ratio between amylin and insulin
extraction_notes: Primary outcomes not explicitly distinguished from secondary outcomes in the abstract. Study described as double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel design. Dose unit appears to be per square meter body surface area (2 IU GH/m²).

title: Glucagon-like peptide 1 increases secretory burst mass of pulsatile insulin secretion in patients with type 2 diabetes and impaired glucose tolerance.
population: Type 2 diabetic patients and subjects with impaired glucose tolerance (IGT); Type 2 diabetic patients: age 64±9 years, BMI 28.9±7.2 kg/m2, HbA1c 7.7±1.3%; IGT subjects: age 63±10 years, BMI 31.7±6.4 kg/m2, HbA1c 5.7±0.4%; Healthy volunteers for comparison: age 62±7 years, BMI 27.7±4.8 kg/m2, HbA1c 5.4±0.5%
intervention: Exogenous GLP-1 (glucagon-like peptide-1) administered intravenously at 1.2 pmol/kg/min, started at 10:00 PM the evening before and continued during fasting state
comparison: Placebo (same subjects studied on separate occasions); Healthy volunteers studied with placebo only
outcomes_primary: Pulsatile insulin secretion characterized by insulin secretory burst mass, amplitude, and frequency (assessed by deconvolution, autocorrelation, and spectral analysis); Approximate entropy (degree of randomness)
outcomes_secondary: Plasma glucose concentrations; Period (lag time) between subsequent maxima of insulin concentrations
extraction_notes: Crossover design implied but not explicitly stated. Eight subjects per group (type 2 diabetes, IGT, healthy controls). Primary vs secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in the abstract.

title: Effect of metformin on glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1) and leptin levels in obese nondiabetic subjects.
population: Obese nondiabetic male patients
intervention: Metformin 2,550 mg/day orally for 14 days
comparison: Untreated obese control subjects
outcomes_primary: GLP-1(7-36)amide/(7-37) levels before and after oral glucose load during euglycemic hyperinsulinemic clamp
outcomes_secondary: Leptin levels before and after oral glucose load; GLP-1(7-36)amide degradation in human plasma and buffer solution containing dipeptidyl peptidase IV (DPP-IV)
extraction_notes: Small sample size (n=10 per group). Study design appears to be non-randomized controlled trial. Primary vs secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract.

title: Additive glucose-lowering effects of glucagon-like peptide-1 and metformin in type 2 diabetes.
population: Type 2 diabetic patients
intervention: Combination therapy with GLP-1 (continuous subcutaneous infusion of 2.4 pmol x kg(-1) x min(-1)) and metformin (1,500 mg daily orally) for 48 h
comparison: Metformin monotherapy (1,500 mg daily orally for 48 h); GLP-1 monotherapy (continuous subcutaneous infusion of 2.4 pmol x kg(-1) x min(-1) for 48 h); no treatment
outcomes_primary: Fasting plasma glucose; 24-h mean plasma glucose
outcomes_secondary: Plasma insulin; C-peptide; glucagon; appetite scores
extraction_notes: Semiblinded randomized crossover design with seven patients; fixed energy intake during study; primary outcome not explicitly designated, inferred from main focus of analysis

title: The effect of physiological levels of glucagon-like peptide-1 on appetite, gastric emptying, energy and substrate metabolism in obesity.
journal: International journal of obesity and related metabolic disorders : journal of the International Association for the Study of Obesity
population: Obese men
intervention: GLP-1 (glucagon-like peptide-1) infusion at physiological dose
comparison: Saline infusion (placebo)
outcomes_primary: Appetite sensations (hunger, prospective food consumption), energy intake at ad libitum lunch, gastric emptying rate
outcomes_secondary: Resting metabolic rate (RMR), substrate oxidations (carbohydrate oxidation), plasma hormone profiles (GLP-1, GLP-2, GIP, insulin, glucagon), plasma substrate profiles (glucose, lactate, NEFA, TAG), thirst, comfort, palatability of test meals
extraction_notes: Study design is placebo-controlled, randomized, single-blinded, cross-over. Sample size is 18 participants. Specific GLP-1 dose not provided in abstract beyond 'physiological dose'. Primary vs secondary outcome distinction not explicitly stated in abstract.

title: Antidiabetogenic action of glucagon-like peptide-1 related to administration relative to meal intake in subjects with type 2 diabetes.
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes treated with oral sulphonylureas
intervention: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) 17 nmol administered as 3-hour stepwise intravenous infusion started at different times relative to a standard meal (550 kCal): (A) at onset of meal, (B) at 30 minutes after meal start, or (C) at 60 minutes after meal start
comparison: Placebo (control meal)
outcomes_primary: Postprandial glycaemia
outcomes_secondary: Postprandial insulin levels, postprandial glucagon levels, gastric emptying (determined by paracetamol test)
extraction_notes: Crossover design with random assignment to treatment sequence. Primary outcome not explicitly designated; inferred from objectives. Sample size is small (n=8).

title: Glucagon-like peptide-1 infusion must be maintained for 24 h/day to obtain acceptable glycemia in type 2 diabetic patients who are poorly controlled on sulphonylurea treatment.
population: Type 2 diabetic patients poorly controlled on sulfonylurea treatment, hospitalized
intervention: GLP-1 (glucagon-like peptide-1) continuous infusion at 4 or 8 ng/kg/min for either 16 or 24 hours per day for 7 days
comparison: Placebo infusion
outcomes_primary: Change in average plasma glucose (area under the curve for day 7 minus AUC for day 0 divided by 24 h)
outcomes_secondary: Nocturnal and fasting plasma glucose levels; insulin AUC and profiles; glucagon AUC; adverse events; clinical chemistry and hematology
extraction_notes: Multiple active treatment arms with different doses and durations (4 ng/kg/min and 8 ng/kg/min, 16h and 24h). Primary outcome not explicitly labeled but inferred from main efficacy analysis. Sample size: 40 patients randomized.

title: Inhibition of gastric emptying by acarbose is correlated with GLP-1 response and accompanied by CCK release.
journal: American journal of physiology. Gastrointestinal and liver physiology
population: Healthy subjects
intervention: Acarbose 100 mg administered with solid meals of varying nutrient composition (mixed meal, carbohydrate-free meal, carbohydrate-free meal given 2 hours after sucrose ingestion)
comparison: Same meals without acarbose (crossover design, random order, at least 1 week apart)
outcomes_primary: Gastric emptying determined with scintigraphy
outcomes_secondary: Plasma responses of gut hormones including insulin, glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP), CCK, glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1), and peptide YY (PYY)
extraction_notes: Sample size not reported. This appears to be a physiological study rather than a therapeutic intervention trial. Primary outcome not explicitly designated; outcomes listed based on stated objectives.

title: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (7-37) augments insulin-mediated glucose uptake in elderly patients with diabetes.
journal: The journals of gerontology. Series A, Biological sciences and medical sciences
population: Elderly patients with type 2 diabetes (age range 76 ± 1 years, body mass index 28 ± 1 kg/m²)
intervention: Primed-continuous infusion of GLP-1 (7-37) at a final rate of 1.5 pmol/kg/min administered from 30 to 180 minutes during 180-minute euglycemic insulin clamp (insulin infusion rate 40 mU/m²/min)
comparison: Euglycemic insulin clamp with glucose and insulin infusion alone (no GLP-1)
outcomes_primary: Glucose disposal rate (Rd) measured using tritiated glucose methodology
outcomes_secondary: Glucose production rate (Ra), insulin values
extraction_notes: Small sample size (n=8). Crossover design with random order. Age and BMI values appear to describe study population characteristics rather than strict inclusion criteria ranges.

title: Bedtime administration of NN2211, a long-acting GLP-1 derivative, substantially reduces fasting and postprandial glycemia in type 2 diabetes.
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes
intervention: NN2211 (long-acting GLP-1 derivative), single subcutaneous injection, 10 microg/kg, administered at 2300 h (bedtime)
comparison: Placebo (double-blind, crossover design)
outcomes_primary: Fasting plasma glucose, meal-related area under the curve for glucose, insulin secretory rates
outcomes_secondary: Plasma glucagon levels, gastric emptying (assessed by 3-ortho-methylglucose AUC), glucose pulse entrainment (high frequency regularity of insulin release), pharmacokinetic profile (T1/2, Tmax), gastrointestinal side effects
extraction_notes: Primary vs secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract; outcomes listed based on emphasis in reporting. Sample size n=11. Study used crossover design.

title: Postprandial glucose, insulin, and incretin responses to grain products in healthy subjects.
journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
population: Healthy men and women with normal glucose tolerance
intervention: Whole-kernel rye bread, whole-meal rye bread containing oat beta-glucan concentrate, dark durum wheat pasta; each product provided 50 g available carbohydrate, served with breakfast
comparison: Wheat bread made from white wheat flour providing 50 g available carbohydrate
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly designated; outcomes measured included plasma glucose, glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP), glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1), serum insulin, and paracetamol concentrations at fasting and 8 postprandial timepoints over 3 hours. Study design appears to be a randomized crossover study with each product served in random order except beta-glucan rye bread served at last visit. Sample size was 10 men and 10 women (n=20 total).

title: Effects of glucagon-like peptide-1(7-36)amide on motility and sensation of the proximal stomach in humans.
population: Healthy male volunteers
intervention: Synthetic glucagon-like peptide-1(7-36)amide (GLP-1) intravenous infusion at 0.3 pmol/kg/min (low dose) or 0.9 pmol/kg/min (high dose)
comparison: Saline infusion
outcomes_primary: Fundus tone and volume waves measured by barostat; gastric compliance derived from isobaric distension
outcomes_secondary: Perception of gastric distension (sensation scores); total volume displaced by volume wave events; pressure at half maximum bag volume
extraction_notes: Sample size is 11 subjects. Study used crossover design with random order. Duration of basal and peptide infusion periods was 60 minutes each. Primary vs secondary outcome distinction not explicitly stated in abstract.

title: Effect of GLP-1 on gastric volume, emptying, maximum volume ingested, and postprandial symptoms in humans.
journal: American journal of physiology. Gastrointestinal and liver physiology
population: Healthy human volunteers
intervention: Intravenous GLP-1 (glucagon-like peptide-1)
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Gastric volume measured by 99mTc-single photon emission computed tomography imaging; gastric emptying of a nutrient liquid meal (Ensure) measured by scintigraphy
outcomes_secondary: Maximum tolerated volume (MTV) of Ensure; postprandial symptoms 30 minutes after MTV; human pancreatic polypeptide (HPP) response to the Ensure meal as assessment of vagal cholinergic function
extraction_notes: Sample size not specified in abstract. Dose, frequency, and duration of GLP-1 infusion not specified. Study described as placebo-controlled but blinding not explicitly stated.

title: Impaired beta-cell function, incretin effect, and glucagon suppression in patients with type 1 diabetes who have normal fasting glucose.
population: Subjects with type 1 diabetes manifested by glucose >11.1 mmol/l 120 min after an oral glucose load but with normal fasting glucose levels, compared to age-matched nondiabetic control subjects
intervention: Not applicable - observational study comparing metabolic characteristics
comparison: Age-matched nondiabetic control subjects
outcomes_primary: Parameters of islet hormone secretion including: first-phase insulin response, insulin secretory response to intravenous arginine, slope of glucose potentiation of insulin response to arginine, maximum insulin response to arginine
outcomes_secondary: Incretin effect, plasma levels of GLP-1 and GIP, glucagon suppression after oral and intravenous glucose administration, glucose effectiveness, insulin sensitivity
extraction_notes: This is an observational/comparative study, not an interventional trial. No therapeutic intervention was administered. Study characterizes metabolic phenotype rather than testing an intervention.

title: The pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, safety and tolerability of NN2211, a new long-acting GLP-1 derivative, in healthy men.
population: Healthy male subjects
intervention: NN2211 (fatty acid derivative of GLP-1) subcutaneous administration at five dose levels (1.25, 5.0, 7.5, 10.0, 12.5 microg/kg) on day 1 and days 5-11 (seven days treatment)
comparison: Placebo, with randomization ratio of 2:1 (active:placebo) at each dose level
outcomes_primary: Safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics (84-h profile including half-life, accumulation index, AUC, Cmax), pharmacodynamics (24-h glucose and insulin profiles)
outcomes_secondary: Adverse events, vital signs, ECG parameters, physical examination, safety laboratory parameters, diuresis, packed cell volume
extraction_notes: This is a Phase I dose-escalation study in healthy volunteers, not patients with diabetes. Six subjects allocated per dose level. Primary vs secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract.

title: Acute ingestion of a meal rich in n-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids results in rapid gastric emptying in humans.
journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
population: Healthy women aged 50-62 years
intervention: Mixed meal containing 40 g oil rich in n-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids with 100 mg [1-(13)C]octanoic acid added
comparison: Mixed meal containing 40 g oil rich in saturated fatty acids; mixed meal containing 40 g oil rich in monounsaturated fatty acids; mixed meal containing 40 g oil rich in n-6 polyunsaturated fatty acids (each with 100 mg [1-(13)C]octanoic acid added)
outcomes_primary: Gastric emptying assessed by labeled octanoic acid breath test (recovery of 13C in breath)
outcomes_secondary: Gastrointestinal hormone concentrations (cholecystokinin, glucagon-like peptide 1); plasma lipid concentrations
extraction_notes: Single-blind, randomized crossover design with 4 separate study visits. Sample size is 10 subjects. Primary versus secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract.

title: Pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, safety, and tolerability of a single-dose of NN2211, a long-acting glucagon-like peptide 1 derivative, in healthy male subjects.
population: Healthy male subjects
intervention: NN2211 (long-acting glucagon-like peptide 1 derivative), single subcutaneous dose at eight consecutive dose levels: 1.25, 2.5, 5.0, 10.0, 12.5, 15.0, 17.5, and 20.0 microg/kg
comparison: Placebo (3:1 active:placebo randomization)
outcomes_primary: Safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics of NN2211 including half-life and time to maximal plasma concentration
outcomes_secondary: Pharmacodynamics including 24-h glucose, insulin and glucagon profiles; area under the curve (0-9 h) for insulin and glucagon; intravenous glucose tolerance test (IVGTT) measures including insulin secretion, glucagon levels, glucose levels, and glucose disappearance constant; adverse events
extraction_notes: Study design: double-blind, randomized, dose-escalation, placebo-controlled. Eight subjects per dose level. Three subjects at each dose level assigned to IVGTT substudy.

title: Plasma glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) responses to duodenal fat and glucose infusions in lean and obese men.
population: Healthy lean men (BMI 19.1-24.6 kg/m²) and obese men (BMI 31.3-40.8 kg/m²)
intervention: Intraduodenal infusion of glucose at 2.86 kcal/min for 120 min; Intraduodenal infusion of fat at 2.86 kcal/min for 120 min
comparison: Lean vs obese subjects; glucose infusion vs fat infusion (crossover design on two separate days)
outcomes_primary: Plasma GLP-1 levels measured at baseline and every 20 min during infusion
extraction_notes: This is a mechanistic/physiological study, not a therapeutic trial. Sample size is small (n=7 per group). Primary vs secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract.

title: The effects of miglitol on glucagon-like peptide-1 secretion and appetite sensations in obese type 2 diabetics.
population: Obese type 2 diabetic women
intervention: Miglitol 100 mg orally three times a day for 2 days (six doses total)
comparison: Placebo three times a day for 2 days (six doses total)
outcomes_primary: Postprandial plasma GLP-1 levels in response to a 720 kcal mixed meal, measured periodically over 3 hours
outcomes_secondary: Postprandial plasma GIP levels; postprandial plasma insulin levels; postprandial plasma glucose levels; appetite sensations assessed by visual analogue scales (VAS) for hunger and satiety measured hourly for 6 hours; food intake measured by number of tuna sandwiches consumed at lunch
extraction_notes: Small sample size (n=8). Study design is double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled crossover. Primary outcome not explicitly designated; classification based on study objectives.

title: High-fat diet effects on gut motility, hormone, and appetite responses to duodenal lipid in healthy men.
journal: American journal of physiology. Gastrointestinal and liver physiology
population: Healthy men
intervention: High-fat diet for 14 days followed by 90-minute duodenal lipid infusion (6.3 kJ/min)
comparison: Low-fat diet for 14 days followed by 90-minute duodenal lipid infusion (6.3 kJ/min)
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished. Outcomes assessed included: appetite (hunger), antropyloroduodenal pressures (pyloric tonic and phasic pressures, number of antropyloroduodenal pressure-wave sequences), plasma CCK levels, plasma glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) levels, and food intake. Sample size was 12 participants. Randomized crossover design.

title: The effects of fiber enrichment of pasta and fat content on gastric emptying, GLP-1, glucose, and insulin responses to a meal.
population: Healthy subjects (n=10)
intervention: Pasta enriched with 1.7 g psyllium fiber and/or pasta served with fat (30 g sunflower oil and 3 g sodium propionate); meals containing 50 g available carbohydrate
comparison: Control pasta without psyllium enrichment; tomato sauce without fat (240 kcal per meal) versus with fat (520 kcal per meal)
outcomes_primary: Gastric emptying (measured using paracetamol absorption test); incremental area under the curve (IAUC) for GLP-1, insulin, and glucose
outcomes_secondary: Visual analog scales for feelings of hunger, pleasantness, and nausea; buffet meal consumption at end of study
extraction_notes: Two-by-two factorial design with single blind randomized crossover; specific subject characteristics (age, sex, health status) not provided in abstract; blood samples taken for 240 min following meal

title: Casein and whey exert different effects on plasma amino acid profiles, gastrointestinal hormone secretion and appetite.
population: Not explicitly stated; appears to be healthy adults based on context but specific eligibility criteria not provided
intervention: 1700 kJ liquid preload containing 48 g whey protein
comparison: Equivalent casein preload (1700 kJ liquid preload containing casein)
outcomes_primary: Not explicitly designated; Study 1: Energy intake from ad libitum buffet meal at 90 min post-preload; Study 2: Postprandial plasma amino acid concentrations over 3 h
outcomes_secondary: Subjective ratings of hunger and fullness (satiety); Plasma cholecystokinin (CCK); Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1); Glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide; Gastric emptying (assessed by plasma paracetamol profiles)
extraction_notes: Two separate studies described within one publication. Population characteristics (sample size, age, sex, health status) not explicitly stated in abstract. Primary vs secondary outcome designation not specified by authors.

title: Differential effects of saturated and monounsaturated fats on postprandial lipemia and glucagon-like peptide 1 responses in patients with type 2 diabetes.
journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
population: Overweight patients with type 2 diabetes
intervention: Control meal (energy-free soup with 50 g carbohydrate) plus 80 g olive oil (monounsaturated fat-rich meal)
comparison: Control meal (energy-free soup with 50 g carbohydrate) alone; Control meal plus 100 g butter (saturated fat-rich meal)
outcomes_secondary: Postprandial responses (8 h) of glucose, insulin, fatty acids, triacylglycerol (total plasma, chylomicron-rich fraction, chylomicron-poor fraction), HDL-cholesterol, gastric inhibitory polypeptide, and glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1)
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract; all outcomes listed as secondary. Crossover design with randomized meal order. Study duration for postprandial measurements was 8 hours per meal.

title: Effect of glucagon-like peptide 1 (7-36 amide) on insulin-mediated glucose uptake in patients with type 1 diabetes.
population: Patients with type 1 diabetes; 6 women and 5 men
intervention: GLP-1 (glucagon-like peptide 1, 7-36 amide) at 1.5 pmol/kg/min intravenous infusion during hyperinsulinemic-euglycemic clamp (480 pmol/m²/min)
comparison: Hyperinsulinemic-euglycemic clamp alone (without GLP-1 infusion); paired randomized crossover design
outcomes_primary: Insulin-mediated glucose uptake
outcomes_secondary: Hepatic glucose production; plasma glucose levels; plasma insulin levels; plasma C-peptide levels; plasma GLP-1 levels; plasma glucagon levels
extraction_notes: Paired randomized crossover study design. Baseline characteristics reported (age 41±3 years, BMI 25±1 kg/m², diabetes duration 23±3 years) appear descriptive rather than strict eligibility criteria. Primary outcome not explicitly labeled but glucose uptake is the main focus based on study objective.

title: No effect of physiological concentrations of glucagon-like peptide-2 on appetite and energy intake in normal weight subjects.
journal: International journal of obesity and related metabolic disorders : journal of the International Association for the Study of Obesity
population: Healthy, normal weight young subjects; 18 participants (8 women, 10 men)
intervention: GLP-2 infusion at rate of 25 pmol/kg body weight for 4.5 hours
comparison: Placebo infusion
outcomes_primary: Appetite sensations measured by visual analogue scales every 30 minutes; ad libitum energy intake from test meal
outcomes_secondary: Palatability of test meals; blood glucose levels; GLP-1 levels; insulin levels; GIP levels; glucagon levels; GLP-2 concentrations
extraction_notes: Randomised, blinded, placebo-controlled crossover design. Primary outcome not explicitly designated; appetite and energy intake appear to be co-primary based on study objective.

title: Effects of fat digestion on appetite, APD motility, and gut hormones in response to duodenal fat infusion in humans.
journal: American journal of physiology. Gastrointestinal and liver physiology
population: Healthy, young, lean men
intervention: Duodenal infusion of a triglyceride emulsion (2.8 kcal/min) for 120 minutes with 120 mg tetrahydrolipstatin (lipase inhibitor)

intervention: Teduglutide administered as daily subcutaneous injections for 8 days at ascending doses: 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 50, and 80 mg as a 50-mg/mL formulation, or 20 mg as a 20-mg/mL formulation
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Pharmacokinetics of teduglutide (plasma concentrations, systemic exposure, apparent clearance, peak plasma concentrations)
outcomes_secondary: Safety and tolerability (adverse events, injection site pain)
extraction_notes: This is a Phase 1 pharmacokinetic study in healthy subjects rather than a therapeutic efficacy trial. Primary and secondary outcomes are not explicitly distinguished in the abstract; classification based on study objectives.

title: Reducing dietary fat from a meal increases the bioavailability of exogenous carbohydrate without altering plasma glucose concentration.
population: Overweight subjects with body mass index = 30 ± 1 kg/m2; 5 men, 4 women; n=9
intervention: Low-fat meal (~530 kcal; 100 g carbohydrate, 1 g fat, 30 g protein) containing [13C]glucose (3 mg/kg body weight)
comparison: 1) Control meal (~800 kcal; 100 g carbohydrate, 31 g fat, 30 g protein) containing [13C]glucose; 2) Low-fat meal plus lipid infusion (same low-fat meal with ~30 g fat provided via intravenous lipid infusion to match control meal energy at 800 kcal)
outcomes_primary: Recovery of ingested [13C]glucose in plasma (bioavailability of exogenous carbohydrate)
outcomes_secondary: Plasma glucose concentration; plasma insulin concentration; plasma concentration of gastrointestinal peptides: glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP), glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1), and peptide YY3-36 (PYY3-36)
extraction_notes: Crossover design with subjects consuming all three meals on separate occasions. Primary vs secondary outcomes not explicitly designated in text; classification based on stated primary goal of study. 5-hour postprandial observation period.

title: Pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, and tolerability of the dipeptidyl peptidase IV inhibitor LC15-0444 in healthy Korean men: a dose-block-randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, ascending single-dose, Phase I study.
population: Healthy Korean male subjects aged 19-39 years
intervention: LC15-0444 capsules administered as a single oral dose at 25, 50, 100, 200, 400, or 600 mg
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Pharmacokinetic parameters (Tmax, t1/2, AUC, fraction of unchanged drug excreted in urine, renal clearance); Pharmacodynamic parameters (DPP IV activity inhibition)
outcomes_secondary: Food effect on pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic parameters (100-mg dose group with high-fat diet); Tolerability and adverse events assessed through investigator inquiries, spontaneous reports, physical examinations, vital sign measurements, 12-lead electrocardiography, clinical laboratory tests, and computerized impedance cardiography
extraction_notes: This is a Phase I study in healthy volunteers, not patients with type 2 diabetes. Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract; categorization based on study objectives described.

title: Acute effects of breakfasts containing alpha-lactalbumin, or gelatin with or without added tryptophan, on hunger, 'satiety' hormones and amino acid profiles.
population: Healthy subjects with BMI 22-29 kg/m2, aged 19-37 years
intervention: Subject-specific breakfast containing alpha-lactalbumin (high in tryptophan) with 10% energy from protein, 55% from carbohydrate, and 35% from fat
comparison: Breakfast containing gelatin (low in tryptophan); Breakfast containing gelatin with added tryptophan (gelatin+TRP, high in tryptophan)
outcomes_primary: Hunger suppression
outcomes_secondary: Glucagon-like peptide (GLP)-1 concentrations; Ghrelin concentrations; Plasma amino acid concentrations; Tryptophan concentrations; Plasma ratio of tryptophan to other large neutral amino acids (TRP:LNAA); Energy intake during subsequent lunch
extraction_notes: Randomised, single-blind design. Sample size is 24 subjects. Primary outcome not explicitly designated; hunger appears to be the main outcome of interest based on study objectives. Exact doses of tryptophan not specified.

title: Efficacy and safety of exenatide in patients of Asian descent with type 2 diabetes inadequately controlled with metformin or metformin and a sulphonylurea.
population: Asian patients with type 2 diabetes inadequately controlled with metformin alone or metformin and a sulphonylurea
intervention: Exenatide 5 microg twice-daily for 4 weeks then 10 microg twice-daily for 12 weeks
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Change in HbA1c from baseline to endpoint
outcomes_secondary: Proportion of patients achieving HbA1c ≤7%, weight change, adverse events including nausea, incidence of symptomatic hypoglycaemia
extraction_notes: Total treatment duration is 16 weeks (4 weeks at 5 microg + 12 weeks at 10 microg). Route of administration not explicitly stated in abstract but exenatide is typically subcutaneous injection.

title: Pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, tolerability, and safety of exenatide in Japanese patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus.
population: Japanese patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus
intervention: Subcutaneous exenatide at multiple dose levels: 2.5 microg, 5 microg, 10 microg, and 15 microg; administered as single dose on day 2, then twice daily (bid) on days 3-10
comparison: Placebo (n=2 per group)
outcomes_primary: Pharmacokinetics (t(max), t(1/2), exposure), pharmacodynamics, tolerability, and safety of subcutaneous exenatide
outcomes_secondary: Postprandial glucose concentrations, adverse events, E(max) model for glycemic response
extraction_notes: Single-blind study design; primary vs secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract; specific allocation was n=8 exenatide and n=2 placebo per group across 4 groups (total N=40)

title: Oral glutamine increases circulating glucagon-like peptide 1, glucagon, and insulin concentrations in lean, obese, and type 2 diabetic subjects.
journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
population: Three groups of subjects: healthy lean volunteers (BMI <25 kg/m2), obese subjects with type 2 diabetes or impaired glucose tolerance (BMI >30 kg/m2), and obese control subjects with normal glucose tolerance (BMI >30 kg/m2, age- and BMI-matched to diabetic group). Exclusion criteria: excessive alcohol intake, liver/kidney/thyroid disease, anaemia, treatment with weight loss or lipid-lowering agents, previous bowel surgery, documented malabsorption. No subjects in diabetic group were taking oral hypoglycaemic agents.
intervention: Oral glutamine 30g in 300ml water administered over approximately 2 minutes on a single occasion after overnight fast
comparison: Oral glucose 75g in 300ml water (positive control); water 300ml alone (negative control); administered on three separate days in random order
outcomes_primary: Plasma concentrations of GLP-1, GIP, insulin, glucagon and glucose measured over 120 minutes
extraction_notes: Crossover design with each subject receiving all three treatments. Primary outcome not explicitly labeled as such; outcomes listed are the measured variables. Sample size of 8 per group (24 total). GIP measured in subset of 11 subjects; glucagon measured in 18 subjects.

title: Raisins and walking alter appetite hormones and plasma lipids by modifications in lipoprotein metabolism and up-regulation of the low-density lipoprotein receptor.
population: 34 subjects (17 men and 17 postmenopausal women) matched for weight and sex
intervention: 1 cup raisins per day (RAISIN group), or increased steps walked per day (WALK group), or combination of both interventions (RAISIN + WALK group) for 6 weeks following a 2-week run-in period
comparison: Three-arm parallel comparison: RAISIN vs WALK vs RAISIN + WALK
outcomes_primary: Lipoprotein metabolism markers including plasma apolipoprotein concentrations, cholesterol ester transfer protein activity, LDL receptor mRNA abundance; appetite hormones including plasma ghrelin and leptin concentrations
extraction_notes: No explicit designation of primary vs secondary outcomes in the abstract. All outcomes listed under primary by default. The comparison structure is between three parallel intervention groups rather than intervention vs placebo/control.

title: The effect of a high-MUFA, low-glycaemic index diet and a low-fat diet on appetite and glucose metabolism during a 6-month weight maintenance period.
population: Subjects who completed an 8-week low-energy diet (LED) and a 2-3-week refeeding period
intervention: MUFA diet: moderate-fat (35-45 energy percentage fat), high in monounsaturated fatty acids with low glycaemic index, for 6 months; LF diet: low fat (20-30 energy percentage fat), for 6 months
comparison: CTR (control) diet: 35 energy percentage fat, for 6 months
outcomes_secondary: Appetite ratings; glucose metabolism; postprandial glycaemia; postprandial insulinaemia; fasting insulin; body weight; energy intake; appetite regulating peptides (pancreatic polypeptide, peptide YY, glucagon-like peptide-1, glucagon-like peptide-2); appetite scores
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract; all outcomes listed as secondary. Total of 131 subjects randomized but meal test subgroup included 42 subjects completing both tests. Study design includes comparison of post-LED period to post-6-month intervention period in addition to between-diet comparisons.

title: Dipeptidyl-peptidase-IV inhibition augments postprandial lipid mobilization and oxidation in type 2 diabetic patients.
journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus, body mass index between 28 and 40 kg/m², 20 patients
intervention: Vildagliptin (selective DPP-4 inhibitor) for 7 days, with a standardized test meal on day 7
comparison: Placebo for 7 days, with a standardized test meal on day 7
outcomes_primary: Venous DPP-4 activity, catecholamines, free fatty acids, glycerol, glucose, (pro)insulin, dialysate glucose, lactate, pyruvate, glycerol
extraction_notes: Randomized, double-blind, crossover study design. The abstract lists main outcome measures but does not distinguish between primary and secondary outcomes. All listed outcomes placed under primary.

title: No increased risk of hypoglycaemic episodes during 48 h of subcutaneous glucagon-like-peptide-1 administration in fasting healthy subjects.
population: Healthy men, fasting subjects
intervention: GLP-1(7-36 amide) continuously infused subcutaneously, titrated to a dose of 4.8 pmol/kg per min, for 48 hours during fasting followed by a 3-hour oral glucose tolerance test
comparison: Placebo continuously infused subcutaneously
outcomes_primary: Safety in terms of hypoglycaemia, hypoglycaemic episodes during fasting
outcomes_secondary: Reactive hypoglycaemia after oral glucose tolerance test, plasma glucose levels, insulin levels, C-peptide levels, glucagon levels, GH levels, free fatty acid levels, intact GLP-1 levels, norepinephrine levels, cortisol levels, counter-regulatory response
extraction_notes: Sample size is small (eight healthy men). Primary outcome not explicitly distinguished from secondary outcomes in abstract; categorization based on study objective. Protocol specified withdrawal criterion of plasma glucose ≤2.8 mM with neuroglycopaenic symptoms.

title: Orlistat accelerates gastric emptying and attenuates GIP release in healthy subjects.
journal: American journal of physiology. Gastrointestinal and liver physiology
population: Healthy subjects
intervention: Orlistat 120 mg in pellet form administered orally with a solid mixed meal with moderate energy load
comparison: Same meal without orlistat (control)
outcomes_primary: Gastric emptying measured by scintigraphy (t lag, t half, area under the gastric emptying curve)
outcomes_secondary: Plasma responses of gut peptides: glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP), cholecystokinin (CCK), glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1), pancreatic polypeptide (PP), peptide YY (PYY), and insulin
extraction_notes: Study design appears to be crossover (random order). Sample size not reported in abstract. Primary vs secondary outcome distinction not explicitly stated - classified based on study focus.

title: Effects of high and normal soyprotein breakfasts on satiety and subsequent energy intake, including amino acid and 'satiety' hormone responses.
population: Healthy subjects
intervention: High-protein soy custard breakfast with 25/55/20 En% protein/carbohydrate/fat
comparison: Normal-protein soy custard breakfast with 10/55/35 En% protein/carbohydrate/fat
outcomes_primary: Satiety ratings measured by Visual Analogue Scale (VAS)
outcomes_secondary: Subsequent energy intake at ad lib lunch; plasma glucose concentrations; insulin concentrations; Glucagon-like Peptide 1 concentrations; ghrelin concentrations; plasma amino acid concentrations
extraction_notes: Randomized, single-blind design. Study involved two sets of experiments. Sample size (n=25) and baseline characteristics (BMI, age) reported but not as explicit inclusion criteria.

title: Mastication of almonds: effects of lipid bioaccessibility, appetite, and hormone response.
journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
population: Healthy adults
intervention: Chewing 55 g almonds 40 times
comparison: Chewing 55 g almonds 10 times; Chewing 55 g almonds 25 times
outcomes_primary: Appetite measures (hunger, fullness); Lipid bioaccessibility (fecal fat excretion, fecal energy losses)
outcomes_secondary: Hormone response (glucagon-like peptide-1 concentrations, insulin concentrations)
extraction_notes: Crossover study design with all participants receiving all three chewing conditions. Primary vs secondary outcomes not explicitly designated in abstract; categorization based on study objective emphasis.

title: Effects of 1 and 3 g cinnamon on gastric emptying, satiety, and postprandial blood glucose, insulin, glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide, glucagon-like peptide 1, and ghrelin concentrations in healthy subjects.
journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
population: Healthy subjects
intervention: Rice pudding with 1 g cinnamon or 3 g cinnamon
comparison: Rice pudding without cinnamon
outcomes_primary: Gastric emptying rate measured by real-time ultrasonography
outcomes_secondary: Postprandial blood glucose; plasma insulin concentrations; incretin hormones (glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide and glucagon-like peptide 1); ghrelin response; satiety
extraction_notes: Crossover trial design with 15 subjects. Primary outcome not explicitly distinguished from secondary outcomes in abstract; gastric emptying rate listed first in objectives suggesting it may be primary.

title: Vildagliptin enhances islet responsiveness to both hyper- and hypoglycemia in patients with type 2 diabetes.
journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
population: Drug-naive patients with type 2 diabetes and baseline glycosylated hemoglobin of 7.5% or less
intervention: Vildagliptin 100 mg/d for 28 days
comparison: Placebo for 28 days
outcomes_primary: Change in plasma glucagon levels during hypoglycemic (2.5 mM glucose) clamp; Incremental (Delta) glucagon area under the concentration-time curve from time 0 to 60 min (AUC 0-60 min) during standard meal test
extraction_notes: Secondary outcomes not explicitly stated in abstract. Crossover design with 4-week between-period washout.

title: Comparison of 2 diets with either 25% or 10% of energy as casein on energy expenditure, substrate balance, and appetite profile.
journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
population: Healthy subjects, body mass index 22.4 ± 2.4 kg/m², age 25 ± 7 years
intervention: 25% of energy from casein diet (25En% casein diet): 25% protein, 20% fat, and 55% carbohydrate of energy, isoenergetic according to subject-specific energy requirements, administered during 36-hour stay in respiration chamber with 3-day run-in period of similar diet at home
comparison: 10% of energy from casein diet (10En% casein diet): 10% protein, 35% fat, and 55% carbohydrate of energy, isoenergetic according to subject-specific energy requirements
outcomes_primary: Not explicitly distinguished as primary
outcomes_secondary: Not explicitly distinguished as secondary; measured outcomes included: 24-hour total energy expenditure, sleeping metabolic rate, substrate oxidation, substrate balance (protein balance, fat balance, carbohydrate balance), appetite scores (satiety)
extraction_notes: Randomized crossover design with 24 subjects (12 men, 12 women). Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract. Casein was the only protein source in both diets.

title: Viscosity of oat bran-enriched beverages influences gastrointestinal hormonal responses in healthy humans.
population: Healthy, normal-weight participants
intervention: Low-viscosity oat bran beverage (300 mL, 1250 kJ; carbohydrates 57.9 g, protein 7.8 g, fat 3.3 g, fiber 10.2 g) with viscosity reduced by beta-glucanase treatment, consumed after 12-hour fast
comparison: High-viscosity oat bran beverage (300 mL, 1250 kJ; identical chemical composition) consumed after 12-hour fast
outcomes_primary: Sensations of appetite and satiety; gastrointestinal hormone responses (plasma glucose, insulin, cholecystokinin, glucagon-like peptide 1, peptide YY, ghrelin)
outcomes_secondary: Gastric emptying measured by paracetamol absorption
extraction_notes: Crossover randomized design. Primary vs secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract; categorization based on study objectives stated. Blood sampling timepoints: before and 15, 30, 45, 60, 90, 120, and 180 min after beverage consumption.

title: Beneficial effects of once-daily liraglutide, a human glucagon-like peptide-1 analogue, on cardiovascular risk biomarkers in patients with Type 2 diabetes.
journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association
population: Patients with Type 2 diabetes
intervention: Once-daily liraglutide, a human glucagon-like peptide-1 analogue
comparison: Not explicitly stated in available text
outcomes_primary: Cardiovascular risk biomarkers
outcomes_secondary: Not explicitly stated in available text
extraction_notes: Only title and competing interests information available; abstract text not provided. Dose, route, frequency details, specific comparator groups, and specific outcome definitions cannot be extracted from the available text.

title: Safety, tolerability, pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetics of albiglutide, a long-acting glucagon-like peptide-1 mimetic, in healthy subjects.
population: Healthy non-diabetic volunteers, aged 18-60 years, body mass index 19.9-35.0 kg/m²
intervention: Albiglutide subcutaneous injection, escalating doses administered on days 1 and 8: cohort 1 (0.25 + 1 mg), cohort 2 (3 + 6 mg), cohort 3 (16 + 24 mg), cohort 4 (48 + 60 mg), cohort 5 (80 + 104 mg)
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Pharmacokinetics: area under the plasma drug concentration versus time curve (AUC(0-7 days)), maximum plasma drug concentration (Cmax), terminal elimination half-life (T1/2), time to maximum observed plasma drug concentration (Tmax); dose proportionality
outcomes_secondary: Safety and tolerability: incidence and severity of adverse events; Pharmacodynamics: glucose weighted mean AUC, fructosamine levels
extraction_notes: Phase of clinical development not explicitly stated. Primary versus secondary outcome distinction not explicitly specified in abstract; classification based on stated study aims.

title: Exenatide exhibits dose-dependent effects on glycemic control over 12 weeks in Japanese patients with suboptimally controlled type 2 diabetes.
population: Japanese patients with type 2 diabetes suboptimally controlled despite therapeutic doses of sulfonylurea (SU), SU plus biguanide, or SU plus thiazolidinedione
intervention: Exenatide 2.5 microg, 5 microg, or 10 microg administered subcutaneously twice daily (BID) for 12 weeks; patients assigned to 10 microg received 5 microg BID for the first 4 weeks with dose escalated to 10 microg BID for the final 8 weeks
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Change in hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) from baseline to endpoint
outcomes_secondary: Proportion of patients achieving HbA1c <7% at endpoint; change in fasting plasma glucose from baseline to endpoint; treatment-emergent adverse events including hypoglycemia, nausea, anorexia, decreased appetite, and diarrhea
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in the abstract; classification based on presentation order and emphasis

title: One-year treatment with exenatide improves beta-cell function, compared with insulin glargine, in metformin-treated type 2 diabetic patients: a randomized, controlled trial.
population: Metformin-treated patients with type 2 diabetes, age 30-75 years, A1C 6.5-9.5%, BMI 25-40 kg/m2, metformin treatment at stable dose for at least 2 months, no other blood glucose-lowering agents within 3 months before screening
intervention: Exenatide initiated at 5 μg twice daily subcutaneous injection 15 min before breakfast and dinner for 4 weeks, then increased to 10 μg twice daily, titrated to maximum 20 μg three times daily or maximum tolerated dose based on A1C targets, for 52 weeks, in addition to ongoing metformin
comparison: Insulin glargine starting at 10 IU once daily subcutaneous injection at bedtime, titrated based on fasting self-monitored blood glucose to achieve fasting levels 4.5-5.5 mmol/l, for 52 weeks, in addition to ongoing metformin
outcomes_primary: Treatment effect on β-cell function measured by ratio of week 52 combined glucose- and arginine-stimulated C-peptide secretion during hyperglycemic clamp
outcomes_secondary: First-phase and second-phase glucose-stimulated C-peptide secretion, arginine-stimulated C-peptide secretion (AIRarg), A1C, fasting plasma glucose, body weight, insulin sensitivity (M value during euglycemic-hyperinsulinemic clamp), β-cell function measures after 4-week off-drug period, adverse events including hypoglycemia and gastrointestinal events
extraction_notes: Primary outcome explicitly stated in statistical analysis section. Off-drug follow-up period of 4 weeks (for clamp measures) and 12 weeks (for A1C and body weight) included in study design.

title: Efficacy and safety of biphasic insulin aspart 70/30 versus exenatide in subjects with type 2 diabetes failing to achieve glycemic control with metformin and a sulfonylurea.
population: Adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus for more than 6 months, aged 18-80 years, HbA1c ≥8%, insulin naive, not achieving glycemic targets with metformin and sulfonylurea combination therapy
intervention: Biphasic insulin aspart 70/30 (BIAsp 30) administered either once daily (QD: 12 U before supper) or twice daily (BID: 12 U divided equally between pre-breakfast and pre-supper) for 24 weeks
comparison: Exenatide 5 micrograms BID for 4 weeks followed by 10 micrograms BID thereafter for 24 weeks
outcomes_primary: HbA1c
outcomes_secondary: Fasting plasma glucose (FPG), adverse events, hypoglycemic episodes (major, minor, symptoms only), weight change, proportion of subjects achieving HbA1c <7% and ≤6.5%
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in the abstract; outcomes listed are based on efficacy and safety assessments described. Three-arm trial with 1:1:1 randomization.

title: GLP-1 regulates gastroduodenal motility involving cholinergic pathways.
population: Healthy volunteers studied during interdigestive period followed by duodenal perfusion of a mixed liquid meal
intervention: Exendin(9-39) intravenous infusion; Atropine intravenous infusion; Exendin(9-39) + atropine intravenous infusion
comparison: Saline intravenous infusion (placebo)
extraction_notes: Sample size is 10 healthy volunteers. Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract. Outcomes assessed included: antro-pyloro-duodenal motility, fundic motility, proximal stomach compliance determined by isobaric distensions, proximal gastric volume, pyloric tone, duodenal contractility, antral waves, gastric volume accommodation, postprandial antral inhibition, gastric compliance, glycaemia, plasma glucagon concentrations, insulin concentrations, and GLP-1 secretion. Drug doses, frequencies, and durations not specified. Mixed liquid meal was 250 kcal.

title: Effect of the artificial sweetener, sucralose, on gastric emptying and incretin hormone release in healthy subjects.
journal: American journal of physiology. Gastrointestinal and liver physiology
population: Healthy human subjects, n=7
intervention: Intragastric infusion of sucralose: 1) 80 mg sucralose in 500 ml normal saline (~300 mosmol/l, 0.4 mM), or 2) 800 mg sucralose in 500 ml normal saline (~300 mosmol/l, 4 mM), labeled with 150 mg 13C-acetate
comparison: 1) 50 g sucrose in water to total volume of 500 ml (~290 mosmol/l) labeled with 150 mg 13C-acetate; 2) 500 ml normal saline (~300 mosmol/l) labeled with 150 mg 13C-acetate
outcomes_primary: Blood glucose, plasma levels of insulin, GLP-1 (glucagon-like peptide-1), and GIP (glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide), gastric emptying measured by breath test (t50)
extraction_notes: Crossover design implied but not explicitly stated. Primary vs secondary outcomes not distinguished in the abstract; all outcomes listed as primary.

title: The acute effects of a lunch containing capsaicin on energy and substrate utilisation, hormones, and satiety.
population: Healthy subjects aged 18-60 years with BMI 20-30 kg/m2, non-smokers, not using medication, at most moderate alcohol users (less than 10 units per week)
intervention: Lunch supplemented with 1,030 mg red pepper equivalent to 80,000 Scoville Heat Units (SHU) of capsaicin (Cayenne, Solaray), providing 35% of individual daily energy requirements with macronutrient composition of 60% carbohydrates, 10% protein, 30% fat
comparison: Control lunch without capsaicin, matched for energy content (35% of individual daily energy requirements) and macronutrient composition (60% carbohydrates, 10% protein, 30% fat)
outcomes_primary: Gut-derived hormone concentrations (GLP-1, ghrelin, PYY) measured at baseline and 45, 60, 120, and 180 minutes after lunch
outcomes_secondary: Energy expenditure and diet-induced thermogenesis measured by ventilated hood system for 210 minutes post-lunch; substrate oxidation (protein, carbohydrate, fat oxidation); respiratory quotient; appetite profile (satiety and hunger) measured by 100-mm visual analogue scales at 0, 30, 60, 90, 120, 150, 180, and 240 minutes
extraction_notes: Single-blind randomized crossover design with at least 1 week washout. Study conducted at lunch in postprandial state rather than at breakfast. Primary vs secondary outcomes not explicitly designated in the text; categorization based on stated study aims.

title: The addition of monosodium glutamate and inosine monophosphate-5 to high-protein meals: effects on satiety, and energy and macronutrient intakes.
population: Healthy men and women (10 men and 12 women)
intervention: High-protein meal with 0.6% monosodium glutamate (MSG) and 0.25% inosine monophosphate-5 (IMP-5); High-protein meal with 0.6% MSG only
comparison: Water (control); High-protein meal with no additives; Sham-fed meal (oral stimulation only)
outcomes_primary: Energy intake at a buffet (second course)
outcomes_secondary: Appetite perceptions; Plasma concentrations of glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1), glucose, and insulin
extraction_notes: Crossover design with random order administration. Study examined fed and orally stimulated states. Specific participant age range and health status not stated in abstract.

title: Efficacy and safety of the human glucagon-like peptide-1 analog liraglutide in combination with metformin and thiazolidinedione in patients with type 2 diabetes (LEAD-4 Met+TZD).
population: Adults aged 18-80 years with type 2 diabetes, A1C 7-11% (previous oral antidiabetes drug monotherapy ≥3 months) or 7-10% (previous combination OAD therapy ≥3 months), BMI ≤45 kg/m², excluding those who used insulin during the previous 3 months (except short-term treatment)
intervention: Liraglutide 1.2 mg or 1.8 mg once daily subcutaneously (initiated at 0.6 mg, titrated weekly) in combination with metformin 1000 mg twice daily and rosiglitazone 4 mg twice daily for 26 weeks
comparison: Liraglutide placebo subcutaneously once daily in combination with metformin 1000 mg twice daily and rosiglitazone 4 mg twice daily
outcomes_primary: Change in A1C from randomization to end of study (26 weeks)
outcomes_secondary: Change in body weight; fasting plasma glucose; seven-point plasma glucose profiles; β-cell function based on fasting insulin, fasting C-peptide, and fasting proinsulin-to-insulin ratio; HOMA for β-cell function (HOMA-B) and insulin resistance (HOMA-IR); lipids; proportion of subjects achieving A1C targets (<7% ADA target; ≤6.5% AACE/IDF target); systolic and diastolic blood pressure; adverse events; hypoglycemic episodes
extraction_notes: 1:1:1 randomization across three groups (liraglutide 1.2 mg, liraglutide 1.8 mg, placebo). All groups received background metformin and rosiglitazone. 6-9 week run-in period before randomization.

title: Liraglutide, a once-daily human GLP-1 analogue, added to a sulphonylurea over 26 weeks produces greater improvements in glycaemic and weight control compared with adding rosiglitazone or placebo in subjects with Type 2 diabetes (LEAD-1 SU).
journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association
population: Adults aged 18-80 years with Type 2 diabetes treated with oral glucose-lowering agents for ≥3 months; HbA1c 7.0-11.0% (previous monotherapy) or 7.0-10.0% (previous combination therapy); BMI ≤45.0 kg/m²; excluded if insulin use within 3 months, impaired liver or renal function, uncontrolled hypertension (≥180/100 mmHg), cancer, or use of drugs apart from oral glucose-lowering agents likely to affect glucose concentrations
intervention: Liraglutide 0.6 mg/day, 1.2 mg/day, or 1.8 mg/day subcutaneous injection once daily, added to glimepiride 2-4 mg/day orally, for 26 weeks; liraglutide up-titrated weekly in 0.6 mg increments until allocated dose reached
comparison: Rosiglitazone 4 mg/day orally added to glimepiride 2-4 mg/day; Placebo added to glimepiride 2-4 mg/day (glimepiride monotherapy)
outcomes_primary: Change from baseline HbA1c after 26 weeks of treatment
outcomes_secondary: Percentage of subjects reaching HbA1c targets (<7.0%, ≤6.5%); percentage reaching fasting plasma glucose target (5.0 to ≤7.2 mmol/l); percentage reaching postprandial plasma glucose target (<10.0 mmol/l); changes in body weight; changes in fasting plasma glucose; changes in mean postprandial plasma glucose; indices of pancreatic B-cell function (proinsulin:insulin ratio, HOMA-B); HOMA-insulin resistance; blood pressure; safety variables including hypoglycaemic episodes, liraglutide antibodies, tolerability (gastrointestinal complaints), pulse, adverse events, vital signs, ECG, biochemical and haematology measures including calcitonin
extraction_notes: Study was double-blind, double-dummy, randomized, active-control, five-armed parallel trial; stratification based on previous oral glucose-lowering mono:combination therapies (30:70%)

title: Sex differences in energy homeostatis following a diet relatively high in protein exchanged with carbohydrate, assessed in a respiration chamber in humans.
population: Healthy males, BMI 22.5±1.6 kg/m², age 25±3.5 years
intervention: High protein (HP) diet: 30% protein, 40% carbohydrate, 30% fat, fed in energy balance in a respiration chamber
comparison: Adequate protein (AP) diet: 10% protein, 60% carbohydrate, 30% fat, fed in energy balance in a respiration chamber
outcomes_secondary: 24-hour energy expenditure, sleeping energy expenditure, protein balance, fat balance, 24-hour respiratory quotient (RQ), satiety (AUC), hunger (AUC), plasma GLP-1 concentrations
extraction_notes: Primary outcomes not explicitly distinguished from secondary outcomes in abstract. Study also includes comparison with previous outcomes in women from a separate study. Sample size n=10. Randomized cross-over design.

title: Fat oxidation during exercise and satiety during recovery are increased following a low-glycemic index breakfast in sedentary women.
population: Healthy sedentary women
intervention: Low-glycemic index (LGI) breakfast consumed 3 hours before 60 minutes of walking exercise
comparison: High-glycemic index (HGI) breakfast consumed 3 hours before 60 minutes of walking exercise
outcomes_primary: Substrate utilization (fat oxidation) during rest and walking exercise
outcomes_secondary: Plasma glucose response, serum insulin response, metabolic responses to standard lunch, appetite/satiety responses following lunch
extraction_notes: Crossover design with 8 participants completing 2 trials. Primary outcome not explicitly designated; assumed based on study focus. Specific exercise intensity not defined beyond 'low intensity' and 'walking for 60 min'.

title: The glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide and glucose-stimulated insulin response to exercise training and diet in obesity.
journal: American journal of physiology. Endocrinology and metabolism
population: Older adults (66.8 ± 1.5 years), obese (34.4 ± 1.7 kg/m2) with impaired glucose tolerance
intervention: 12-week exercise training intervention (5 days/week, 60 min/day, 75% VO2 max) combined with hypocaloric diet (EX-HYPO group, n=9)
comparison: 12-week exercise training intervention (5 days/week, 60 min/day, 75% VO2 max) combined with eucaloric diet (EX group, n=10)
outcomes_secondary: GIP response to glucose; plasma PYY3-36 response; insulin response; glucose response during 3-hour 75-g oral glucose tolerance test; VO2 max; weight loss
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in the abstract; all outcomes listed as secondary. Small sample sizes (n=10 and n=9). Study appears to be a non-randomized intervention study rather than an RCT.

title: Dose-dependent satiating effect of whey relative to casein or soy.
population: Healthy subjects with BMI 23.9 kg/m2, age 22 years
intervention: Whey-protein breakfast custards at either 10 En% (normal) or 25 En% (high) protein with 55% carbohydrate and 35% or 20% fat respectively

title: Pharmacology and tolerability of a single dose of exenatide in adolescent patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus being treated with metformin: a randomized, placebo-controlled, single-blind, dose-escalation, crossover study.

title: Effect of rimonabant and metformin on glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide and glucagon-like peptide-1 in obese women with polycystic ovary syndrome.

extraction_notes: Abstract text not available; extraction based solely on title. Drug doses, routes, frequencies, durations, specific outcome definitions, and distinction between primary/secondary outcomes cannot be determined from title alone.

title: Adding liraglutide to oral antidiabetic drug monotherapy: efficacy and weight benefits.

title: Liraglutide once a day versus exenatide twice a day for type 2 diabetes: a 26-week randomised, parallel-group, multinational, open-label trial (LEAD-6).

outcomes_primary: Change in glycosylated haemoglobin (HbA1c)

title: Efficacy of a continuous GLP-1 infusion compared with a structured insulin infusion protocol to reach normoglycemia in nonfasted type 2 diabetic patients: a clinical pilot trial.
population: Clinically stable type 2 diabetic patients with self-measured fasting glucose levels >150 mg/dl; treated with oral antidiabetic drugs; excluded: New York Heart Association class III or IV heart failure, uncontrolled hypertension, impaired kidney function (creatinine >3 mg/dl), or acute infection

outcomes_secondary: Plasma glucose after 2 hours; plasma glucose after 4 hours; maximum glycemia; number of hypoglycemic episodes
extraction_notes: Prospective open randomized crossover trial design with 7±3 days washout between treatments; small sample size (n=8); blood glucose measurements performed every 30 min or at symptoms of hypoglycemia

title: Effects of the phases of the menstrual cycle on gastric emptying, glycemia, plasma GLP-1 and insulin, and energy intake in healthy lean women.

outcomes_secondary: Blood glucose concentrations, plasma GLP-1 concentrations, plasma insulin concentrations, plasma cholecystokinin (CCK) concentrations, hunger ratings, energy intake at buffet meal, reproducibility of measurements within follicular phase

Each participant was studied on three occasions (twice during follicular phase, once during luteal phase). The study also assessed reproducibility by comparing two visits within the follicular phase.

title: Improved treatment satisfaction and weight-related quality of life with exenatide once weekly or twice daily.

population: Adults with Type 2 diabetes managed with diet and exercise and/or oral glucose-lowering medications

outcomes_primary: Change in glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c) at 30 weeks
outcomes_secondary: Diabetes Treatment Satisfaction Questionnaire status version (DTSQ-s) total score and individual items; Impact of Weight on Quality of Life-Lite (IWQOL-Lite) total score and domain scores (physical function, self-esteem, sexual life, public distress, work); fasting plasma glucose; weight; adverse events
extraction_notes: Open-label study design. The PRO measures (DTSQ-s and IWQOL-Lite) appear to be secondary outcomes while HbA1c was the primary endpoint. All subjects in the BID arm were switched to QW at week 30, so there was no parallel comparison group through week 52.

title: Potential of albiglutide, a long-acting GLP-1 receptor agonist, in type 2 diabetes: a randomized controlled trial exploring weekly, biweekly, and monthly dosing.
population: Adults aged 18-75 years with type 2 diabetes diagnosed ≥3 months before screening, inadequately controlled with diet and exercise (drug naïve) or metformin monotherapy (stable for >3 months), BMI 20-40 kg/m², A1C 7-10%. intervention: Albiglutide subcutaneous injection in multiple dosing regimens: weekly (4 mg, 15 mg, or 30 mg), biweekly/every 2 weeks (15 mg, 30 mg, or 50 mg), or monthly (50 mg or 100 mg) for 16 weeks, followed by 11-week washout period
comparison: Double-blind placebo (matched to albiglutide arms); open-label exenatide 5 μg twice daily for 4 weeks followed by 10 μg twice daily for 12 weeks (metformin-treated subjects only)
outcomes_primary: Change from baseline A1C at week 16 versus placebo across different doses within each schedule
outcomes_secondary: Fasting plasma glucose (FPG), fasting fructosamine, C-peptide, glucagon, insulin, lipid profiles, β-cell function (homeostasis model assessment), body weight, blood pressure, proportion achieving A1C <7.0%, adverse events including gastrointestinal events (nausea, vomiting), injection site reactions, hypoglycemia, immunogenicity (anti-albiglutide antibodies), pharmacokinetics
extraction_notes: Phase II dose-finding study with 10 treatment arms. Exenatide was administered open-label as active reference only in metformin-treated subjects, and no formal statistical comparisons versus exenatide were conducted. Only subjects on metformin monotherapy were eligible for exenatide arm.

title: Food form and portion size affect postprandial appetite sensations and hormonal responses in healthy, nonobese, older adults.
population: Healthy, non-obese older adults aged 65 years or older with BMI between 20 and 29 kg/m2; not dieting with no weight change greater than 2 kg in past six months; non-smoking; non-diabetic; clinically normal blood profiles including normal liver and kidney function, normal complete blood count, and fasting blood glucose less than 110 mg/dL; maintained free-living sedentary lifestyle
intervention: Beverage form test meal (meal-replacement shake) provided as either 12.5% or 25% of estimated daily energy need, consumed within 15 minutes along with 88.7 mL water
comparison: Solid form test meal (meal-replacement nutrition bar) matched for energy content and macronutrient composition, provided as either 12.5% or 25% of estimated daily energy need
outcomes_primary: Appetite sensations (hunger, fullness, desire to eat) measured using 13-point numerical rating scale; hormonal responses including plasma glucose, insulin, total ghrelin, cholecystokinin (CCK), and glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) concentrations measured over 4-hour postprandial period
extraction_notes: Semi-randomized partial crossover design with food form as within-subject factor and portion size as between-subject factor; 25 subjects received 25% portion size and 18 different subjects received 12.5% portion size; primary versus secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in the text

title: Four-month treatment with GLP-2 significantly increases hip BMD: a randomized, placebo-controlled, dose-ranging study in postmenopausal women with low BMD.

comparison: Saline control injection (placebo)
outcomes_primary: Bone mineral density (BMD) at total hip
outcomes_secondary: Biochemical markers of bone turnover (serum CTX for bone resorption, serum osteocalcin for bone formation), safety and tolerability, tachyphylaxis, antibodies against GLP-2
extraction_notes: Primary vs secondary outcome distinction not explicitly stated in abstract; outcomes categorized based on study objectives described. Route of administration (subcutaneous) inferred from 'injection' but not explicitly stated.

title: Improvement in glucose metabolism after bariatric surgery: comparison of laparoscopic Roux-en-Y gastric bypass and laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy: a prospective randomized trial.
population: Patients undergoing bariatric surgery, mostly nondiabetic
intervention: Laparoscopic Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (LRYGB)
comparison: Laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy (LSG)
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly designated. Outcomes measured include fasting and meal-stimulated insulin, glucose, glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1), PYY, and ghrelin concentrations; body weight; body mass index; excess BMI loss. Evaluations performed before surgery, 1 week after, and 3 months after surgery. Sample size: 13 patients randomized to LRYGB, 14 patients to LSG. Trial registration: NCT00356213.

title: Exenatide versus insulin glargine: a cost-effectiveness evaluation in patients with Type 2 diabetes in Switzerland.
journal: International journal of clinical pharmacology and therapeutics
population: Individuals with Type 2 diabetes inadequately controlled with combination oral agents in the Swiss setting
intervention: Exenatide as add-on treatment to oral therapy
comparison: Insulin glargine as add-on treatment to oral therapy
outcomes_primary: Long-term clinical outcomes (diabetes-related complications, life expectancy), economic outcomes (direct medical costs), quality-adjusted life expectancy, cost-effectiveness (incremental cost-effectiveness ratio)
extraction_notes: This is a cost-effectiveness modeling study based on data from a 26-week randomized clinical trial. Primary vs secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished. Treatment doses, routes, and frequencies not specified in the abstract.

title: Differential effect of PYY1-36 and PYY3-36 on gastric emptying in man.
population: Healthy adults
intervention: Intravenous infusion of PYY1-36 (0.8 pmol kg(-1) min(-1)) or PYY3-36 (0.8 pmol kg(-1) min(-1)) with a radio-labelled omelette
comparison: Intravenous infusion of saline with a radio-labelled omelette
outcomes_primary: Gastric emptying measured by scintigraphy (half-emptying time, retention at 120 min)
outcomes_secondary: Appetite ratings measured by Visual Analogue Scale (VAS), plasma concentrations of insulin, glucose, GLP-1, and PYY
extraction_notes: Study described as single-blinded, randomized design with eight participants studied at separate occasions (crossover design implied). Sample size is small (n=8). Primary vs secondary outcome distinction not explicitly stated in abstract.

title: Adaptation of colonic fermentation and glucagon-like peptide-1 secretion with increased wheat fibre intake for 1 year in hyperinsulinaemic human subjects.
population: Hyperinsulinaemic human subjects with fasting plasma insulin ≥40 pmol/l
intervention: High-wheat fibre cereal providing 24 g fibre/d daily for 1 year
comparison: Low-fibre cereal daily for 1 year
outcomes_primary: Time-course of effects on plasma acetate, butyrate and glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) concentrations over 1 year, measured during 8-hour metabolic profiles performed every 3 months
outcomes_secondary: Body weight
extraction_notes: Study described as randomized by computer. Sample size: 20 assigned per group with 6 dropouts each, leaving 14 included per group. Primary objective explicitly stated in abstract.

title: Liraglutide vs insulin glargine and placebo in combination with metformin and sulfonylurea therapy in type 2 diabetes mellitus (LEAD-5 met+SU): a randomised controlled trial.
population: Adults aged 18-80 years with type 2 diabetes mellitus treated with oral glucose-lowering drugs for at least 3 months, HbA1c 7.5-10% if on monotherapy or 7-10% if on combination therapy, BMI ≤45 kg/m2.
