intervention: Liraglutide 1.8 mg once daily subcutaneous injection (dose escalation from 0.6 mg with weekly increments of 0.6 mg over 2 weeks) in combination with metformin 1 g twice daily and glimepiride 4 mg once daily for 26 weeks
comparison: 1) Liraglutide placebo once daily subcutaneous injection (volume-matched) in combination with metformin 1 g twice daily and glimepiride 4 mg once daily; 2) Open-label insulin glargine once daily subcutaneous injection (self-titrated targeting fasting plasma glucose ≤5.5 mmol/l) in combination with metformin 1 g twice daily and glimepiride 4 mg once daily
outcomes_primary: Change in HbA1c from baseline after 26 weeks of treatment
outcomes_secondary: Change in bodyweight, waist circumference, fasting plasma glucose, eight-point plasma glucose profiles, beta cell function (proinsulin to C-peptide ratio), blood pressure, proportion achieving HbA1c targets (ADA <7%, AACE ≤6.5%), hypoglycaemic episodes, adverse events, liraglutide antibodies
extraction_notes: Randomisation ratio was 2:1:2 for liraglutide:placebo:insulin glargine. Insulin glargine arm was open-label while liraglutide and placebo arms were blinded. Study conducted at 107 sites in 17 countries with 581 randomised patients.

title: Safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, and pharmacodynamics of exenatide once weekly in Japanese patients with type 2 diabetes.
population: Japanese patients with type 2 diabetes suboptimally controlled by diet and exercise alone or combined with biguanide, sulfonylurea, thiazolidinedione, or combinations of these agents
intervention: Exenatide once weekly (QW) 0.8 mg or 2.0 mg subcutaneous injection for 10 weeks
comparison: Placebo once weekly subcutaneous injection
outcomes_primary: Safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics (steady-state plasma exenatide concentrations), and pharmacodynamics
outcomes_secondary: HbA1c change from baseline to Week 10, fasting plasma glucose change from baseline to Week 10, 2-hour postprandial plasma glucose excursions, adverse events, injection site reactions, hypoglycemia
extraction_notes: The abstract does not clearly distinguish between primary and secondary outcomes; all outcomes listed appear to be co-primary based on study objectives. Sample size is small (n=30 randomized in 1:1:1 ratio).

title: A high-fat vs. a moderate-fat meal in obese boys: nutrient balance, appetite, and gastrointestinal hormone changes.

extraction_notes: Small sample size (n=10). Crossover design implied but not explicitly stated. Primary vs secondary outcome distinction not explicitly defined in abstract.

title: Orally administered glucagon-like peptide-1 affects glucose homeostasis following an oral glucose tolerance test in healthy male subjects.

comparison: Controls (not further specified)

Outcomes measured include plasma GLP-1 concentrations, basal insulin release, glucose levels, and postprandial glucose peak timing. Control group not explicitly defined (unclear if placebo or no treatment).

title: Absence of QTc prolongation in a thorough QT study with subcutaneous liraglutide, a once-daily human GLP-1 analog for treatment of type 2 diabetes.

title: Gut microbiota fermentation of prebiotics increases satietogenic and incretin gut peptide production with consequences for appetite sensation and glucose response after a meal.

extraction_notes: Small sample size (n=10 total). Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in the abstract; all outcomes listed under primary. Meal tolerance tests used to assess multiple outcomes.

title: Effects of exenatide alone and in combination with daclizumab on beta-cell function in long-standing type 1 diabetes.

outcomes_secondary: Weight change, total daily insulin dose, preprandial insulin doses, A1C, hypoglycemia episodes (glucose <55 mg/dl), gastric emptying (acetaminophen absorption), glucagon levels, GLP-1 levels, T-cell reactivity to diabetes-related antigens
extraction_notes: Open-label crossover trial design. Sample size based on detecting 50% increase in C-peptide levels with exenatide. 20 patients enrolled but only 16 randomized after optimization period; 14 completed the study.

title: Teduglutide, a novel mucosally active analog of glucagon-like peptide-2 (GLP-2) for the treatment of moderate to severe Crohn's disease.

outcomes_primary: Percentage of subjects with clinical response, defined as decrease in Crohn's Disease Activity Index (CDAI) score to <150 or decrease of >100 points
outcomes_secondary: Remission rates, plasma citrulline levels, adverse events

title: Role of fat hydrolysis in regulating glucagon-like Peptide-1 secretion.

comparison: Study 1: Intraduodenal fat infusion without orlistat, vehicle; Study 2: Intraduodenal vehicle; Study 3: Intraduodenal sodium oleate without dexloxiglumide, intraduodenal vehicle plus intravenous saline (placebo)
outcomes_primary: GLP-1 concentrations
outcomes_secondary: CCK release (plasma CCK concentrations)
extraction_notes: Three consecutive randomized double-blind crossover studies with different sample sizes: Study 1 (n=12), Study 2 (n=12), Study 3 (n=10). Total 34 subjects but unclear if this represents unique individuals or overlapping participants. Doses and infusion durations not specified in abstract.

title: Improvement in peripheral glucose uptake after gastric bypass surgery is observed only after substantial weight loss has occurred and correlates with the magnitude of weight lost.
journal: Journal of gastrointestinal surgery : official journal of the Society for Surgery of the Alimentary Tract
population: Morbidly obese nondiabetic patients aged 21-65 years, BMI >40 or >35 kg/m2 with high-risk comorbidities, meeting National Institute of Health and UCSF Bariatric Surgery Program criteria for bariatric surgery, documented BMI >35 kg/m2 for more than 5 years, excluding those with previous weight loss surgery, previous esophageal/gastric/pancreatic/adrenal/small bowel/large bowel/thyroid/central nervous system operations, thyroid/liver/pancreatic/adrenal/hypothalamic/pituitary/ovarian/chronic renal disease, diagnosis of type 2 diabetes mellitus, or use of insulin or oral diabetes medications

Primary outcome not explicitly stated but peripheral glucose uptake appears to be the main focus. Six-month follow-up data included subjects from both original groups who underwent RYGB.

title: The effect of exenatide on lisinopril pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetics in patients with hypertension.

comparison: Placebo twice daily coadministered with lisinopril
outcomes_primary: Baseline-adjusted 24-hour mean systolic blood pressure; Baseline-adjusted 24-hour mean diastolic blood pressure
outcomes_secondary: Steady state plasma lisinopril concentration-time profiles including time to maximum concentration (tmax,ss), maximum concentration (Cmax,ss), and area under the concentration-time profile (AUCtau,ss) over 24-hour steady-state dosing interval
extraction_notes: Double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, 2-period, 2-sequence crossover design with at least 2 days washout period between treatments. Duration of each treatment period not explicitly stated.

title: Effects of meal size and composition on incretin, alpha-cell, and beta-cell responses.
population: Subjects with type 2 diabetes mellitus and healthy volunteers
intervention: Three standardized meals: small carbohydrate-rich meal, large carbohydrate-rich meal, and fat-rich meal administered as 4-hour meal tolerance tests

outcomes_secondary: Postprandial glucose response, insulin response, C-peptide response, glucagon response, GLP-1 response, GIP response, model-based and non-model-based estimates of beta-cell function, incremental areas under the curve for glucose, insulin, C-peptide, glucagon, GLP-1, and GIP
extraction_notes: Primary outcomes not explicitly distinguished from secondary outcomes in the abstract. Sample size: 18 subjects with type 2 diabetes mellitus and 6 healthy volunteers. Randomized crossover design.

title: Effects of liraglutide in the treatment of obesity: a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled study.

title: Safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of albiglutide, a long-acting GLP-1-receptor agonist, in Japanese subjects with type 2 diabetes mellitus.

intervention: Albiglutide administered subcutaneously in four dose/dose schedules: 15 mg weekly, 30 mg weekly, 50 mg biweekly, and 100 mg monthly over a 4-week treatment period

title: A simulation of the comparative long-term effectiveness of liraglutide and glimepiride monotherapies in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus.

outcomes_secondary: Nonfatal renal events; nonfatal ocular events; neuropathies leading to first or recurrent amputation; average cumulative cost per patient

title: Eating slowly increases the postprandial response of the anorexigenic gut hormones, peptide YY and glucagon-like peptide-1.

title: Endogenous glucagon-like peptide-1 slows gastric emptying in healthy subjects, attenuating postprandial glycemia.

population: Healthy fasted subjects

title: The effect of glucagon-like peptide-2 on arterial blood flow and cardiac parameters.
population: Healthy volunteers
intervention: Glucagon-like peptide-2 (GLP-2) 450 nmol subcutaneous injection, single dose
comparison: Isotonic saline (placebo) subcutaneous injection

title: Adding liraglutide to oral antidiabetic drug therapy: onset of treatment effects over time.
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes from three phase 3 trials; patients underwent run-in and titration period with metformin (LEAD-2), glimepiride (LEAD-1), or metformin plus rosiglitazone (LEAD-4)
intervention: Liraglutide 1.2 mg or 1.8 mg once-daily in combination with oral antidiabetic drugs (metformin, glimepiride, or metformin plus rosiglitazone)
comparison: Active comparator and/or placebo (specific comparators not detailed in abstract)
outcomes_primary: Not explicitly specified as primary

extraction_notes: Pooled analysis of three phase 3 trials (LEAD-1, LEAD-2, LEAD-4). Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished. Only 1.2 mg and 1.8 mg liraglutide doses included in this analysis (0.6 mg excluded). Specific active comparators not named in abstract.

title: Pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic properties of taspoglutide, a once-weekly, human GLP-1 analogue, after single-dose administration in patients with Type 2 diabetes.
journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association
population: Patients with Type 2 diabetes inadequately controlled with metformin (≤2 g/day)
intervention: Taspoglutide, single subcutaneous injection at 1 mg, 8 mg, or 30 mg doses

Baseline characteristics (mean age 56±7 years; mean BMI 30.4±3.0 kg/m²) are descriptive statistics, not eligibility criteria. Primary vs secondary outcome distinction not explicitly stated in abstract.

title: Exenatide compared with long-acting insulin to achieve glycaemic control with minimal weight gain in patients with type 2 diabetes: results of the Helping Evaluate Exenatide in patients with diabetes compared with Long-Acting insulin (HEELA) study.
population: Adults with type 2 diabetes, BMI >27 kg/m2, inadequate glycaemic control (HbA1c 7.5-10.0%) despite stable doses of two or three oral antidiabetes drugs (metformin, sulphonylurea, thiazolidinedione) for at least 3 months, with at least one cardiovascular risk factor (previous cardiovascular event, peripheral vascular disease, or abnormal risk factor: LDL >3.0 mmol/l, HDL <1.0 mmol/l men or <1.3 mmol/l women, triglyceride >1.7 mmol/l, systolic BP >130 mmHg, diastolic BP >80 mmHg, or increased waist circumference). Exclusions: history of malignancy, Class III or IV heart disease, uncontrolled hypertension (systolic BP ≥180 mmHg or diastolic BP ≥105 mmHg), renal transplantation or dialysis, chronic renal impairment (serum creatinine ≥135 μmol/l males or ≥110 μmol/l females), liver disease (ALT >3× upper limit of normal)

outcomes_secondary: Change in HbA1c from baseline; change in body weight from baseline; change in waist circumference; change in fasting serum glucose; change in lipid profile (total cholesterol, HDL cholesterol, LDL cholesterol, triglycerides); change in blood pressure (systolic and diastolic); proportion achieving fasting serum glucose ≤5.6 mmol/l; treatment-emergent adverse events; hypoglycaemic episodes (overall, nocturnal, severe)
extraction_notes: Post hoc analysis using composite endpoint of HbA1c ≤7.0% with weight gain ≤1 kg was also reported. Open-label study design. Primary endpoint HbA1c threshold of 7.4% was based on UK audit standards current at time of study design rather than optimal glycaemic control.

title: Weight loss with liraglutide, a once-daily human glucagon-like peptide-1 analogue for type 2 diabetes treatment as monotherapy or added to metformin, is primarily as a result of a reduction in fat tissue.

intervention: Liraglutide 1.8 mg/day, 1.2 mg/day, or 0.6 mg/day; in LEAD-2 combined with metformin 1.5-2 g/day; in LEAD-3 as monotherapy (1.8 mg or 1.2 mg/day)
comparison: LEAD-2: placebo combined with metformin, glimepiride 4 mg/day combined with metformin 1.5-2 g/day; LEAD-3: glimepiride 8 mg/day monotherapy
outcomes_primary: Not explicitly specified

extraction_notes: Primary outcome not explicitly distinguished from secondary outcomes. This abstract reports on body composition sub-analyses from two separate trials (LEAD-2: 26 weeks; LEAD-3: 52 weeks). Randomized, double-blind, parallel-group design.

title: Regulation of energy balance during long-term physical inactivity induced by bed rest with and without exercise training.

population: Lean women
intervention: Combined aerobic/resistive exercise training concomitant to 60-day bed rest
comparison: Strict 60-day bed rest without exercise training (control group)
outcomes_secondary: Body composition, spontaneous energy intake, hunger, total energy expenditure (TEE), fasting gut hormones
extraction_notes: Primary outcomes not explicitly distinguished from secondary outcomes in abstract. Sample size was 16 women total (n=8 per group). Study described as using bed-rest model rather than randomized controlled trial terminology.

title: Cardiovascular and metabolic effects of 48-h glucagon-like peptide-1 infusion in compensated chronic patients with heart failure.

population: Patients without diabetes with compensated congestive heart failure due to ischemic heart disease, ejection fraction approximately 30%, New York Heart Association class II and III
intervention: GLP-1 (glucagon-like peptide-1) infusion at 0.7 pmol/kg/min for 48 hours
comparison: Placebo infusion for 48 hours
outcomes_primary: Left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), diastolic function, tissue Doppler regional myocardial function
outcomes_secondary: Exercise testing, noninvasive cardiac output, brain natriuretic peptide (BNP), blood pressure, heart rate, metabolic parameters (insulin, glucose levels), body weight, hypoglycemic events
extraction_notes: Randomized double-blind crossover design. Primary vs secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract; categorization based on emphasis in text. 20 patients enrolled but only 15 completed the protocol.

title: Actions of prolonged ghrelin infusion on gastrointestinal transit and glucose homeostasis in humans.
population: Healthy male volunteers

comparison: Intravenous saline infusion for 360 minutes
outcomes_primary: Gastric emptying rate, gastric half-emptying time
outcomes_secondary: Orocecal transit, colonic transit, postprandial plasma concentrations of glucose, postprandial plasma concentrations of insulin, postprandial plasma concentrations of glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1), postprandial plasma concentrations of peptide YY, insulinogenic index, in vitro gastrointestinal muscle contractility
extraction_notes: Study design appears to be a crossover trial with 12 participants but this is not explicitly stated. Primary vs secondary outcome distinction not explicitly defined in abstract; categorization based on study aim emphasis.

title: Appetite suppression through smelling of dark chocolate correlates with changes in ghrelin in young women.
population: Twelve female residents with BMI between 18 and 25 kg/m²
intervention: Smelling dark chocolate (85% cocoa) or eating 30 g dark chocolate (85% cocoa, 12.5 g sugar per 100g product) via melt-and-swallow method
comparison: Control group (no eating or smelling)
outcomes_primary: Relationship between appetite (scored on visual analogue scale) and levels of gastrointestinal hormones (ghrelin, insulin, GLP-1, CCK, glucose)
extraction_notes: Crossover design for eating session (all 12 participated), but only randomization for second session (smell vs control, n=6 each). Duration of intervention sessions was 60 minutes. Primary outcome not explicitly designated; inferred from study objective.

title: Effects of exenatide plus rosiglitazone on beta-cell function and insulin sensitivity in subjects with type 2 diabetes on metformin.
population: Adults aged 18-75 years with type 2 diabetes, BMI 25-40 kg/m2, stable body weight for at least 6 months, A1C 6.8-10.0%, on stable metformin dose for at least 6 weeks, no treatment with other antidiabetic medications, absence of islet cell autoantibodies
intervention: Exenatide 5 μg subcutaneous injection twice daily for first month then 10 μg twice daily thereafter, plus rosiglitazone 2 mg twice daily for first month then 4 mg twice daily thereafter, added to continued metformin regimen for 20 weeks

outcomes_primary: Glucose-potentiated arginine-stimulated incremental insulin area under the curve (ASI-iAUC) during hyperglycemic clamp test

extraction_notes: Open-label study design. 73 of 137 participants underwent clamp procedures. Primary endpoint explicitly stated as ASI-iAUC; secondary endpoint stated as glucose AUC during meal challenge. Study powered to detect differences between EXE+ROSI and ROSI groups.

title: Effect of exenatide on heart rate and blood pressure in subjects with type 2 diabetes mellitus: a double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomized pilot study.
population: Adults aged 18 to 75 years with type 2 diabetes mellitus on stable metformin (for 30 days) and/or thiazolidinedione (for 120 days), body mass index >25 and <40 kg/m2, hemoglobin A1c between 6.5 and 9.5%, stable body weight (≤10% variation for 3 months), stable antihypertensive regimens for at least 6 weeks. intervention: Exenatide 5 μg subcutaneous injection twice daily (BID) for 4 weeks, followed by 10 μg BID for 8 weeks (total 12 weeks), administered within 60 minutes before morning and evening meals
comparison: Placebo subcutaneous injection BID for 12 weeks
outcomes_primary: Change from baseline in mean 24-hour heart rate at Week 12
outcomes_secondary: Hourly heart rate; change from baseline in 24-hour, daytime, and nighttime heart rate, systolic blood pressure, and diastolic blood pressure; rate pressure product; mean arterial pressure; hemoglobin A1c; body weight
extraction_notes: Per-protocol population was pre-defined for primary analysis; intent-to-treat population used for secondary analyses. Background metformin and/or thiazolidinedione and antihypertensive medications remained constant throughout the study.

title: The fermentable fibre inulin increases postprandial serum short-chain fatty acids and reduces free-fatty acids and ghrelin in healthy subjects.

Study design: randomized, single-blind, crossover. Sample size n=12. Duration of observation: 6 hours with standard lunch served at 4 hours after test drink.

title: A psyllium fiber-enriched meal strongly attenuates postprandial gastrointestinal peptide release in healthy young adults.

outcomes_secondary: Hunger and satiety ratings
extraction_notes: Single-blind, randomized, cross-over design with n=16. Primary outcomes not explicitly distinguished from secondary outcomes in abstract; classification based on emphasis in methods description.

title: Exenatide versus glibenclamide in patients with diabetes.

comparison: Glibenclamide 2.5 mg three times a day titrated to 5 mg three times a day
outcomes_secondary: Body weight, body mass index (BMI), glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c), fasting plasma glucose (FPG), postprandial plasma glucose (PPG), fasting plasma insulin (FPI), homeostasis model assessment insulin resistance (HOMA-IR) index, homeostasis model assessment beta-cell function (HOMA-beta) index, plasma proinsulin (PPr), PPr/FPI ratio, resistin, retinol binding protein-4 (RBP-4), high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (Hs-CRP)

title: Addition of metformin to exogenous glucagon-like peptide-1 results in increased serum glucagon-like peptide-1 concentrations and greater glucose lowering in type 2 diabetes mellitus.

extraction_notes: Randomized crossover design with all subjects receiving all 3 treatments. Glucose was raised to 15 mmol/L by rapid IV infusion at 15 minutes post-treatment as part of protocol. Primary vs secondary outcome distinction not explicitly stated in abstract.

title: Do the actions of glucagon-like peptide-1 on gastric emptying, appetite, and food intake involve release of amylin in humans?

outcomes_secondary: Appetite (measured using visual analog scales); food intake during subsequent ad libitum meal at 240 minutes; postprandial glucagon responses
extraction_notes: Placebo-controlled, randomized, single-blinded, crossover study design. Specific doses of GLP-1, amylin, and pramlintide infusions not stated in abstract. Sample size: 11 T1DM patients and 12 healthy controls.

title: Efficacy and safety of the once-daily human GLP-1 analogue, liraglutide, vs glibenclamide monotherapy in Japanese patients with type 2 diabetes.

outcomes_primary: HbA1C at 24 weeks

title: Improvement of postprandial endothelial function after a single dose of exenatide in individuals with impaired glucose tolerance and recent-onset type 2 diabetes.

outcomes_primary: Postprandial endothelial function measured by reactive-hyperemia peripheral arterial tonometry (PAT) index at 210 min after meal ingestion, adjusted for baseline
outcomes_secondary: Postprandial glucose concentrations, postprandial insulin concentrations, postprandial triglyceride concentrations (measured at 120 and 240 min)

title: DURATION-1: exenatide once weekly produces sustained glycemic control and weight loss over 52 weeks.

extraction_notes: Open-label trial design. Inclusion and exclusion criteria were reported in a previous publication (reference 17) and not detailed in this abstract/full text. The 22-week assessment phase lacked a separate comparator arm as all patients received exenatide QW.

title: Effects of exogenous glucagon-like peptide-1 on gastric emptying and glucose absorption in the critically ill: relationship to glycemia.

outcomes_primary: Gastric emptying coefficient (calculated from exhaled 13CO2), blood glucose concentration, serum 3-O-methyl-glucose concentration (index of glucose absorption)
outcomes_secondary: Plasma insulin concentration, plasma glucagon concentration, insulin/glucose ratio
extraction_notes: Crossover design with patients studied on consecutive days. Sample size was 25 patients. Primary vs secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract; classification based on study objectives stated.

title: Switching to once-daily liraglutide from twice-daily exenatide further improves glycemic control in patients with type 2 diabetes using oral agents.
population: Adults with type 2 diabetes inadequately controlled (A1C 7–11%) with maximally tolerated stable doses of metformin, sulfonylurea, or both for ≥3 months

title: Effects of exenatide and lifestyle modification on body weight and glucose tolerance in obese subjects with and without pre-diabetes.

outcomes_secondary: Change in glucose concentrations, change in lipid concentrations, change in A1C, change in blood pressure, change in physical activity, change in food intake, glucose tolerance normalization

title: The role of adjunctive exenatide therapy in pediatric type 1 diabetes.

title: Further improvement in postprandial glucose control with addition of exenatide or sitagliptin to combination therapy with insulin glargine and metformin: a proof-of-concept study.
population: Men or women aged 35–70 years with type 2 diabetes for >6 months and <10 years, treated with stable dose of metformin with or without sulfonylureas or with long- or intermediate-acting insulin (insulin glargine, insulin detemir, or NPH insulin) with or without stable dose of metformin for at least 3 months; BMI 21.0–39.9 kg/m2; A1C ≥7.0% and ≤10.0%; stable antihypertensive or lipid-lowering therapy for at least 3 months if applicable

title: Twelve weeks treatment with the DPP-4 inhibitor, sitagliptin, prevents degradation of peptide YY and improves glucose and non-glucose induced insulin secretion in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus.
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus on metformin therapy
