title: Liraglutide, a once-daily human glucagon-like peptide 1 analogue, provides sustained improvements in glycaemic control and weight for 2 years as monotherapy compared with glimepiride in patients with type 2 diabetes.
population: Adults aged 18-80 years with type 2 diabetes, body mass index ≤45 kg/m², screening HbA1c 7-11% (53-97 mmol/mol) on diet/exercise or 7-10% (53-86 mmol/mol) on oral antidiabetic drug monotherapy
intervention: Liraglutide 1.2 mg once daily subcutaneous injection or liraglutide 1.8 mg once daily subcutaneous injection for 104 weeks (52-week double-blind period followed by 52-week open-label extension)
comparison: Glimepiride 8 mg oral once daily for 104 weeks
outcomes_primary: Change in HbA1c from baseline to week 52 (primary endpoint of original trial); change in HbA1c from baseline to week 104 (key extension efficacy variable)
outcomes_secondary: Body weight, waist circumference, fasting plasma glucose, mean postprandial plasma glucose from eight-point self-measured plasma glucose profiles, systolic blood pressure, HOMA-B (homeostasis model assessment of β-cell function), HOMA-IR (homeostasis model assessment of insulin resistance), pro-insulin to insulin ratio, fasting glucagon, fasting insulin, fasting C-peptide, proportion reaching HbA1c targets (<7% and ≤6.5%), adverse events, hypoglycaemia (minor defined as self-treated plasma glucose <3.1 mmol/l), calcitonin levels, nausea frequency
extraction_notes: Study was a phase 3 trial with initial 52-week randomized double-blind double-dummy period followed by 52-week open-label extension. Randomization ratio was 1:1:1. Participants were withdrawn for 'ineffective therapy' if FPG exceeded specified thresholds.

title: GLP-1 and calcitonin concentration in humans: lack of evidence of calcitonin release from sequential screening in over 5000 subjects with type 2 diabetes or nondiabetic obese subjects treated with the human GLP-1 analog, liraglutide.
journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
population: Subjects with type 2 diabetes mellitus or nondiabetic obese subjects without medullary thyroid carcinoma or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma
intervention: Liraglutide (GLP-1 receptor agonist), dose not specified, for up to 2 years
comparison: Control therapy (not further specified)
outcomes_primary: Unstimulated serum calcitonin concentrations measured at 3-month intervals
outcomes_secondary: Proportion of subjects with calcitonin levels above clinically relevant cutoff of 20 ng/liter
extraction_notes: Liraglutide dose, route, and frequency not specified in abstract. Nature of control therapy not specified. Study described as a series of trials rather than a single trial. Sample size over 5000 subjects across multiple trials.

title: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist treatment prevents glucocorticoid-induced glucose intolerance and islet-cell dysfunction in humans.
population: Healthy men aged 18-35 years, BMI 22.0-28.0 kg/m2, normoglycemia defined as fasting plasma glucose <5.6 mmol/L and 2-hour glucose <7.8 mmol/L after 75g oral glucose tolerance test. Exclusion criteria: presence of any disease, use of any medication, first-degree relative with type 2 diabetes, smoking, shift work, history of glucocorticoid use, recent changes in weight or physical activity.
intervention: 80 mg oral prednisolone once daily for 2 consecutive days plus intravenous exenatide infusion (40 ng/min for 30 minutes then 20 ng/min for remainder of test) (PRED+EXE)
comparison: 1) 80 mg oral prednisolone once daily for 2 consecutive days plus intravenous saline infusion (PRED+SAL); 2) Oral placebo-prednisolone once daily for 2 consecutive days plus intravenous saline infusion (PLB+SAL)
outcomes_primary: 4-hour glucose area under the curve (AUCG) during standardized meal challenge test
outcomes_secondary: First-phase and second-phase C-peptide incremental area under the curve (iAUCCP) during hyperglycemic clamp; arginine-stimulated C-peptide secretion (ASI-iAUCCP) during hyperglycemic clamp; insulin sensitivity (M-value from hyperinsulinemic-euglycemic clamp); disposition index; glucagon secretion; gastric emptying (acetaminophen AUC); Matsuda whole-body insulin sensitivity index
extraction_notes: Randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind, crossover study design. Three 2-day treatment blocks separated by at least 4 weeks. Small sample size (n=8). Intravenous exenatide administration used rather than subcutaneous injection.

title: Effect of ginger on gastric motility and symptoms of functional dyspepsia.
population: Patients with functional dyspepsia
intervention: Ginger 1.2 g total (three capsules), oral administration, single dose, followed after 1 hour by 500 mL low-nutrient soup
comparison: Placebo (three capsules), followed after 1 hour by 500 mL low-nutrient soup
outcomes_primary: Gastric half-emptying time calculated from change in antral area measured by ultrasound
outcomes_secondary: Antral area; fundus area and diameter; frequency of antral contractions measured by ultrasound; gastrointestinal sensations and appetite scored using visual analog questionnaires; plasma concentrations of glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1), motilin, and ghrelin
extraction_notes: Randomized double-blind crossover design with same patients studied twice. Small sample size (n=11). Primary outcome not explicitly designated; gastric emptying appears to be the main outcome of interest.

title: Treatment with liraglutide--a once-daily GLP-1 analog--does not reduce the bioavailability of ethinyl estradiol/levonorgestrel taken as an oral combination contraceptive drug.
population: Postmenopausal healthy women
intervention: Liraglutide, once-daily human GLP-1 analog, with single dose of oral contraceptive (ethinyl estradiol/levonorgestrel)
comparison: Placebo with single dose of oral contraceptive (ethinyl estradiol/levonorgestrel)
outcomes_primary: Pharmacokinetics of ethinyl estradiol and levonorgestrel including area under the curve (AUC) and maximum concentration (Cmax)
extraction_notes: Study is a pharmacokinetic drug-drug interaction study in healthy postmenopausal women, not a therapeutic efficacy trial in type 2 diabetes patients. Primary vs secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract.

title: Effects of oral ingestion of sucralose on gut hormone response and appetite in healthy normal-weight subjects.
population: Healthy normal-weight subjects, fasted state, n=8
intervention: Oral ingestion of sucralose (0.083% w/v) in 50 ml water
comparison: Water (50 ml); glucose-polymer matched for sweetness with sucralose addition (50% w/v maltodextrin + 0.083% sucralose); modified sham-feeding protocol of sucralose (0.083% w/v, oral stimulation only)
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract. Outcomes measured included: plasma GLP-1, plasma PYY, plasma insulin, plasma glucose, appetite ratings, and energy intake at buffet meal at 120 min. Study design: randomised, single-blinded, crossover study with 4 study days in random order. Measurements taken at regular time points for 120 min.

title: A 5-week study of the pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of LY2189265, a novel, long-acting glucagon-like peptide-1 analogue, in patients with type 2 diabetes.
population: Subjects with type 2 diabetes mellitus controlled with diet and exercise alone or with a single oral antidiabetic medication
intervention: LY2189265 (a novel, long-acting glucagon-like peptide-1 analogue) administered once weekly at doses of 0.05, 0.3, 1, 3, 5 or 8 mg for 5 weeks (five once-weekly doses)
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Pharmacokinetics of LY2189265; effects on glucose, insulin and C-peptide concentrations during fasting and following standard test meals
outcomes_secondary: HbA1c; glucagon; body weight; gastric emptying; safety parameters
extraction_notes: Study described as subject- and investigator-blind but route of administration not explicitly stated. Subjects on metformin or thiazolidinediones continued therapy as background treatment. Primary vs secondary outcome distinction not explicitly stated in abstract.

title: LY2189265, a long-acting glucagon-like peptide-1 analogue, showed a dose-dependent effect on insulin secretion in healthy subjects.
population: Healthy subjects
intervention: LY2189265 (LY), a long-acting glucagon-like peptide-1 analogue, single subcutaneous injections at escalating doses ranging from 0.1 to 12 mg
comparison: Placebo
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished. Outcomes assessed included: safety parameters (adverse events, gastrointestinal symptoms, pulse rate, blood pressure), pharmacokinetic parameters (half-life, Cmax over 14 days), pharmacodynamic parameters (glucose and insulin concentrations measured during step-glucose infusion on day 3 and oral glucose tolerance test on day 5), and immunogenicity (antibody development). This was a phase 1, three-period, crossover, double-blind, placebo-controlled study with approximately six subjects randomized to each dose level.

title: The effects of LY2189265, a long-acting glucagon-like peptide-1 analogue, in a randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind study of overweight/obese patients with type 2 diabetes: the EGO study.
population: Overweight/obese patients with type 2 diabetes failing oral antihyperglycaemic medications (OAMs), receiving two OAMs
intervention: LY2189265 (GLP-1 IgG4-Fc fusion protein) once-weekly subcutaneous injection in three regimens: LY 0.5/1.0 (0.5 mg for 4 weeks then 1.0 mg for 12 weeks); LY 1.0/1.0 (1.0 mg for 16 weeks); LY 1.0/2.0 (1.0 mg for 4 weeks then 2.0 mg for 12 weeks)
comparison: Placebo once-weekly subcutaneous injection
outcomes_primary: Change in glycosylated haemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) at week 16
outcomes_secondary: Fasting blood glucose, postprandial blood glucose, body weight change, adverse events (nausea, diarrhoea, abdominal distension), hypoglycaemia episodes, cardiovascular events, blood pressure
extraction_notes: Primary outcome not explicitly distinguished from secondary outcomes in abstract; classification inferred from presentation order. Study duration 16 weeks.

title: Exogenous glucagon-like peptide-1 attenuates the glycaemic response to postpyloric nutrient infusion in critically ill patients with type-2 diabetes.
population: Critically ill adult patients with pre-existing type-2 diabetes, mechanically ventilated, admitted to intensive care unit, aged greater than 17 years, likely to remain mechanically ventilated for more than 48 hours. Exclusion criteria: pregnancy, contraindication to enteral feeding or post-pyloric catheter insertion, acute pancreatitis, previous surgery on the oesophagus, stomach or duodenum.
intervention: Intravenous infusion of synthetic GLP-1-(7-36) amide (glucagon-like peptide-1) at 1.2 pmol/kg/minute, infused at 1 ml/minute for 270 minutes, with intraduodenal liquid nutrient (Ensure) infusion at 1 kcal/minute from t=30 to t=270 minutes via naso-enteric catheter
comparison: Intravenous infusion of placebo (4% albumin) at 1 ml/minute for 270 minutes, with identical intraduodenal liquid nutrient infusion
outcomes_primary: Glycaemic response to small intestinal nutrient infusion (blood glucose area under curve from t=30 to t=270 minutes)
outcomes_secondary: Peak glycaemic excursion, blood glucose at predefined timepoints (t=0, t=30, t=270 minutes), proportion of patients maintaining blood glucose at less than 10 mmol/l, serum insulin concentrations, serum C-peptide concentrations, plasma glucagon concentrations, serum non-esterified fatty acids
extraction_notes: Randomised double-blind crossover design with patients studied over two consecutive days receiving both interventions. Sample size n=11. Study terminated prematurely in some patients if blood glucose exceeded 15 mmol/l.

title: Exenatide - pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, safety and tolerability in patients ≥ 75 years of age with Type 2 diabetes.
journal: International journal of clinical pharmacology and therapeutics
population: Elderly patients aged ≥75 years with Type 2 diabetes compared to control patients aged ≥45 to ≤65 years with Type 2 diabetes
intervention: Single subcutaneous doses of exenatide 5 μg and exenatide 10 μg administered before a standardized breakfast
comparison: Placebo; control age group (≥45 to ≤65 years)
outcomes_primary: Pharmacokinetics (plasma exenatide maximum concentration, exposure, apparent clearance)
outcomes_secondary: Pharmacodynamics (postprandial serum glucose excursions); safety; tolerability; hypoglycemia; serious adverse events
extraction_notes: Crossover study design with two sequences. Integrated pharmacokinetic analysis also included data from six other clinical pharmacology studies (139 controls ≤65 y; 28 elderly patients >65 y). Primary vs secondary outcome distinction not explicitly stated in abstract.

title: Weight-related quality of life, health utility, psychological well-being, and satisfaction with exenatide once weekly compared with sitagliptin or pioglitazone after 26 weeks of treatment.
population: Male and nonpregnant female patients, at least 18 years of age, with type 2 diabetes, treated with a stable regimen of metformin monotherapy for a minimum of 2 months prior to screening, A1C 7.1–11.0%, BMI 25–45 kg/m2
intervention: Exenatide 2 mg subcutaneous injection once weekly (self-administered) plus placebo oral capsule each morning, on background of metformin, for 26 weeks
comparison: Sitagliptin 100 mg oral capsule each morning plus placebo subcutaneous injection once weekly; Pioglitazone 45 mg oral capsule each morning plus placebo subcutaneous injection once weekly; both on background of metformin for 26 weeks
outcomes_primary: Change in weight-related quality of life (IWQOL-Lite total and domain scores), health utility (EQ-5D index and visual analog scores), psychological well-being (PGWB global and dimension scores), diabetes treatment satisfaction (DTSQ-s total scores and perceived frequency of hyperglycemia/hypoglycemia)
extraction_notes: Primary clinical outcomes (A1C, fasting plasma glucose, weight, adverse events) were reported elsewhere and are not the focus of this PRO-focused analysis. No explicit distinction made between primary and secondary PRO outcomes in this article.

title: Staggered meal consumption facilitates appetite control without affecting postprandial energy intake.
population: Healthy participants, n=38, age 24 ± 6 years, BMI 25.0 ± 3.1 kg/m²
intervention: Staggered meal consumption: 4-course lunch (40% of daily energy requirements) consumed over 2 hours with 3 within-meal pauses
comparison: Nonstaggered meal consumption: 4-course lunch (40% of daily energy requirements) consumed in 0.5 hours
outcomes_secondary: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) concentrations, peptide tyrosine-tyrosine (PYY3-36) concentrations, ghrelin concentrations, appetite ratings (satiety, hunger), food reward measures (liking, wanting), ad libitum energy intake
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in the abstract. Study uses randomized cross-over design. All participants received both conditions.

title: The pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, and tolerability of liraglutide, a once-daily human GLP-1 analogue, after multiple subcutaneous administration in healthy Chinese male subjects.
population: Healthy Chinese male subjects
intervention: Liraglutide 0.6 mg, 1.2 mg, or 1.8 mg once daily by subcutaneous injection for 21 consecutive days, with dose escalation starting at 0.6 mg for 1 week and increasing in weekly steps of 0.6 mg to predefined dose targets
comparison: Placebo (randomized 3:1 within each dose group)
outcomes_primary: Pharmacokinetics (AUC(0-24h), C(max), C(trough) at steady state, t(max), t(1/2))
outcomes_secondary: Pharmacodynamics (plasma glucose levels, serum insulin levels), tolerability, safety, adverse events
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract; classification based on typical pharmacokinetic study hierarchy. Total sample size was 37 subjects across all dose groups.

title: The possible protective role of glucagon-like peptide 1 on endothelium during the meal and evidence for an "endothelial resistance" to glucagon-like peptide 1 in diabetes.
population: Type 2 diabetic patients (n=16) and matched healthy control subjects (n=12). Diabetic patients: no retinopathy, nephropathy, or neuropathy; 10 on diet alone, 6 on metformin discontinued at least 4 weeks before study; 5 with hypertension treated with ACE inhibitor (withheld on study days); none receiving statin or antioxidant supplementation.
intervention: GLP-1 (7-36) amide infusion at 0.4 pmol/kg/min during hyperglycemic clamp. Diabetic patients also received 2 months of intensive insulin treatment to improve glycemic control, after which clamp studies were repeated.
comparison: Placebo infusion during hyperglycemic clamp; standard meal test; oral glucose tolerance test (75g glucose in 300mL water)
outcomes_primary: Flow-mediated vasodilation (FMD) as measure of endothelial function
outcomes_secondary: Plasma nitrotyrosine (marker of oxidative stress); plasma 8-iso prostaglandin F2α (8-iso-PGF2a, marker of oxidative stress); glycemia; insulin; GLP-1 (active 7-36) plasma levels; endothelium-independent vasodilation (nitroglycerin response)
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly designated in text; classification based on study focus. Crossover design with randomized order of interventions. Sample size based on previous studies, not power calculation described.

title: Effect of exenatide on inflammatory and oxidative stress markers in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus.
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus with inadequate glucose control, suboptimally controlled with metformin and/or sulfonylurea
intervention: Exenatide 5 μg twice daily for 4 weeks followed by 10 μg twice daily for 12 weeks
comparison: Placebo
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract. Outcomes measured included: glycosylated hemoglobin (HbA1c), seven-point glucose profile, daily mean glucose, glycemic excursion, body weight, body mass index (BMI), 8-iso-prostaglandin F2α (PGF2α), monocyte chemoattractant protein-1 (MCP-1), and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP). Sample size was 23 patients total (12 in exenatide group, 11 in placebo group).

title: Exenatide twice daily versus premixed insulin aspart 70/30 in metformin-treated patients with type 2 diabetes: a randomized 26-week study on glycemic control and hypoglycemia.
population: Metformin-treated adults with type 2 diabetes, A1C 6.5–10.0%, conducted at 68 sites in Germany
intervention: Exenatide twice daily (BID): 5 μg for 4 weeks, then 10 μg, for 26 weeks, with metformin continued unchanged
comparison: Premixed insulin aspart 70/30 BID (PIA), titrated to glucose targets of 5.0–7.2 mmol/L (fasting) and <10 mmol/L (2 h postprandial) after each main meal, with metformin continued unchanged
outcomes_primary: Noninferiority of exenatide BID versus PIA for A1C control; superiority of exenatide BID versus PIA for hypoglycemia (blood glucose ≤3.9 mmol/L or severe episode requiring assistance of another person)
outcomes_secondary: Body weight change; proportion of patients reaching A1C <7.0% without weight gain and without hypoglycemic episodes (composite end point, post hoc); adverse events
extraction_notes: Open-label study design. Randomization stratified by baseline A1C (≤8.0 or >8.0%). Hierarchical testing procedure used. Sulfonylurea treatment was excluded. Composite end point was analyzed post hoc.

title: Comparative effects of glucose and xylose on blood pressure, gastric emptying and incretin hormones in healthy older subjects.
population: Healthy older subjects aged 65-75 years
intervention: 300 ml drink containing 50 g d-xylose, single oral administration
comparison: 300 ml drink containing 50 g glucose; 300 ml water alone
outcomes_primary: Blood pressure (measured by DINAMAP)
outcomes_secondary: Gastric emptying (measured by three-dimensional ultrasound); blood glucose; serum insulin; glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1); glucose-dependent insulinotropic peptide (GIP)
extraction_notes: Small sample size (n=8). Double-blind, randomised crossover design. Primary outcome not explicitly distinguished from secondary outcomes in abstract.

title: DURATION-5: exenatide once weekly resulted in greater improvements in glycemic control compared with exenatide twice daily in patients with type 2 diabetes.
journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes, drug naïve or previously treated with one or multiple oral antidiabetic medications
intervention: Exenatide once weekly (ExQW) 2 mg for 24 weeks
comparison: Exenatide twice daily (ExBID) 5 μg for 4 weeks followed by ExBID 10 μg for 20 weeks
outcomes_primary: Change in HbA1c from baseline to week 24
outcomes_secondary: Fasting plasma glucose, body weight, safety and tolerability (adverse events including nausea, injection-site reactions, hypoglycemia)
extraction_notes: Open-label study design. Secondary outcomes not explicitly labeled as such but inferred from main outcome measure designation and results reporting structure.

title: Liraglutide improves treatment satisfaction in people with Type 2 diabetes compared with sitagliptin, each as an add on to metformin.
journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association
population: People with Type 2 diabetes on metformin
intervention: Liraglutide 1.2 mg or 1.8 mg once daily, injected with a pen, added to metformin ≥1500 mg daily
comparison: Sitagliptin 100 mg oral once daily, added to metformin ≥1500 mg daily
outcomes_primary: Treatment satisfaction measured by Diabetes Treatment Satisfaction Questionnaire (DTSQ) at baseline and 26 weeks, including overall treatment satisfaction score (calculated by adding satisfaction scores for current treatment, convenience, flexibility, understanding, recommend, and continue)
outcomes_secondary: Perceived frequency of hyperglycaemia, perceived frequency of hypoglycaemia
extraction_notes: This was a patient-reported outcomes substudy of a larger 26-week randomized open-label trial. The main study outcomes (HbA1c reduction, weight loss) are mentioned but the primary focus of this substudy was DTSQ assessment. Substudy sample sizes: liraglutide 1.8 mg n=171, liraglutide 1.2 mg n=164, sitagliptin n=170.

title: GIP does not potentiate the antidiabetic effects of GLP-1 in hyperglycemic patients with type 2 diabetes.
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes with fasting hyperglycemia; 12 patients (9 men, 3 women); age 61 ± 10 years; BMI 30.0 ± 3.7 kg/m²; HbA1c 7.3 ± 1.5%; antidiabetic medications discontinued 1 day before each experiment
intervention: Intravenous infusion of GLP-1(7-36)-amide (1.2 pmol·kg⁻¹·min⁻¹) plus GIP (4 pmol·kg⁻¹·min⁻¹) administered over 360 minutes after overnight fast
comparison: Placebo (0.9% NaCl with 1% human serum albumin); GLP-1(7-36)-amide alone (1.2 pmol·kg⁻¹·min⁻¹); GIP alone (4 pmol·kg⁻¹·min⁻¹); all administered intravenously over 360 minutes in randomized order with at least 1 day wash-out between experiments
outcomes_primary: Capillary blood glucose concentrations; plasma insulin concentrations; plasma C-peptide concentrations; insulin secretion rates (determined by deconvolution analysis)
outcomes_secondary: Plasma glucagon concentrations; plasma free fatty acids (FFA) concentrations; plasma GIP concentrations (total and intact); plasma GLP-1 concentrations (total and intact); metabolic clearance rates for GLP-1 and GIP
extraction_notes: Crossover design with 4 treatment conditions. Primary vs secondary outcomes not explicitly designated in the abstract or methods; outcomes listed are those measured. Study focused on determining whether GIP potentiates GLP-1 effects rather than superiority of a specific treatment.

title: The once-daily human glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) analog liraglutide improves postprandial glucose levels in type 2 diabetes patients.
population: Adults with type 2 diabetes, aged 18-70 years, body mass index 18.5-40 kg/m², HbA1c 7.0%-9.5%
intervention: Once-daily liraglutide subcutaneous injection at doses of 0.6 mg, 1.2 mg, and 1.8 mg for 3 weeks
comparison: Placebo (once-daily for 3 weeks)
outcomes_primary: Postprandial plasma glucose levels, fasting plasma glucose levels
outcomes_secondary: Postprandial insulin levels, fasting insulin levels, gastric emptying (assessed by paracetamol/acetaminophen concentrations)
extraction_notes: Crossover trial design with 3-4 week washout period between treatment periods. Small sample size (n=18). Primary versus secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract.

title: An oral lipid challenge and acute intake of caffeinated coffee additively decrease glucose tolerance in healthy men.
population: Young, healthy males
intervention: Oral fat tolerance test (OFTT: 1 g lipid/kg body weight) followed 5 hours later by caffeinated coffee (5 mg/kg)
comparison: Water control, decaffeinated coffee, OFTT with water, OFTT with decaffeinated coffee
outcomes_primary: Glucose tolerance measured by oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT) at 6 hours
outcomes_secondary: Glucagon-like peptide-1 active (GLP-1a) response, glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) response
extraction_notes: Randomized cross-over design with 5 trial conditions. Sample size is 10 participants. Primary outcome not explicitly designated; determined based on study goals stated in abstract.

title: One year of liraglutide treatment offers sustained and more effective glycaemic control and weight reduction compared with sitagliptin, both in combination with metformin, in patients with type 2 diabetes: a randomised, parallel-group, open-label trial.
population: Adults with type 2 diabetes previously treated with metformin monotherapy (≥1500 mg/day) for a minimum of 3 months with suboptimal glycaemic control (HbA1c 7.5-10%)
intervention: Liraglutide 1.2 mg/day subcutaneous injection or liraglutide 1.8 mg/day subcutaneous injection, added to existing metformin therapy, for 52 weeks (26-week main phase plus 26-week extension)
comparison: Sitagliptin 100 mg/day orally, added to existing metformin therapy
outcomes_primary: Change in HbA1c from baseline to week 52
outcomes_secondary: Change in fasting plasma glucose; change in body weight; proportion of participants achieving HbA1c <7% or ≤6.5%; proportion of participants reaching composite end-point of HbA1c <7.0% with no weight gain and no confirmed major or minor hypoglycaemia; fasting C-peptide; fasting pro-insulin:insulin ratio; HOMA-B (beta-cell function); HOMA-IR (insulin resistance); change in waist circumference; Diabetes Treatment Satisfaction Questionnaire scores; incidence of adverse events; incidence of hypoglycaemia
extraction_notes: Open-label trial design. Primary outcome not explicitly designated but HbA1c change was the main efficacy comparison used for superiority testing.

title: Dose response of subcutaneous GLP-1 infusion in patients with type 2 diabetes.
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes
intervention: Recombinant glucagon-like peptide-1 (7-36) amide (rGLP-1) administered by continuous subcutaneous infusion (CSCI) at doses of 1.25, 2.5, 5.0, or 8.5 pmol/kg/min for 7 days
comparison: Placebo by continuous subcutaneous infusion for 7 days
outcomes_primary: Fasting serum glucose; postprandial serum glucose; 11-hour serum glucose profile (area under the curve)
outcomes_secondary: Fasting C-peptide; hormone profiles; safety outcomes including hypoglycemia
extraction_notes: Study design is double-blind, parallel, placebo-controlled. Primary vs secondary outcome distinction not explicitly stated in abstract; outcomes listed based on apparent emphasis in methods and results.

title: Patient-reported outcomes are superior in patients with Type 2 diabetes treated with liraglutide as compared with exenatide, when added to metformin, sulphonylurea or both: results from a randomized, open-label study.
journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association
population: Adults aged 18-80 years with Type 2 diabetes receiving stable regimen of metformin, sulphonylurea or both for at least 3 months, HbA1c 7.0-11.0% (53-97 mmol/mol), BMI ≤45 kg/m2, no previous treatment with insulin, exenatide or liraglutide
intervention: Liraglutide 1.8 mg subcutaneous once daily (escalated from 0.6 mg starting dose in weekly 0.6 mg increments) added to existing metformin and/or sulphonylurea regimen for 26 weeks, followed by 14-week extension phase
comparison: Exenatide 10 μg subcutaneous twice daily (escalated from 5 μg twice daily after 4 weeks) added to existing metformin and/or sulphonylurea regimen for 26 weeks
outcomes_primary: Not explicitly specified; treatment satisfaction measured by Diabetes Treatment Satisfaction Questionnaire status (DTSQs) and change (DTSQc) versions
outcomes_secondary: Individual DTSQ items (current treatment, convenience, flexibility, understanding, recommend, continue); perceived frequency of hyperglycaemia and hypoglycaemia
extraction_notes: Primary outcome not explicitly designated in text. Open-label design. Patient-reported outcomes assessed in subset of 379 patients (82%) from 8 of 15 participating countries due to availability of linguistically validated questionnaires.

title: Gastric emptying, incretin hormone secretion, and postprandial glycemia in cystic fibrosis--effects of pancreatic enzyme supplementation.
journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
population: Nondiabetic cystic fibrosis patients with exocrine pancreatic insufficiency; healthy subjects of similar age and body mass index served as controls
intervention: Radiolabeled mashed potato meal with four capsules of Creon Forte (100,000 IU lipase)
comparison: Radiolabeled mashed potato meal with placebo capsules (within CF patients); healthy subjects consuming meal without pancreatic enzymes
outcomes_primary: Gastric emptying measured using scintigraphy; blood glucose concentration; plasma glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) concentration; plasma glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) concentration; plasma glucagon concentration
extraction_notes: Small sample size (5 CF patients, 6 healthy subjects). Abstract does not distinguish between primary and secondary outcomes. Crossover design with CF patients receiving both intervention and placebo on separate days.

title: Effects of small intestinal glucose load on blood pressure, splanchnic blood flow, glycemia, and GLP-1 release in healthy older subjects.
journal: American journal of physiology. Regulatory, integrative and comparative physiology
population: Healthy older subjects aged 65-76 years
intervention: Intraduodenal infusion of glucose at rates of 1, 2, or 3 kcal/min (G1, G2, G3) for 60 minutes via nasoduodenal catheter
comparison: Intraduodenal infusion of saline (0.9%) for 60 minutes
outcomes_primary: Blood pressure (systolic and diastolic), superior mesenteric artery flow, GLP-1 release, noradrenaline levels
extraction_notes: Study design is double-blind, randomized, with four separate occasions per subject. Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract.

title: Slowly and rapidly digested fat emulsions are equally satiating but their triglycerides are differentially absorbed and metabolized in humans.
population: Healthy men and women with BMI approximately 25 kg/m², age approximately 59 years
intervention: Fat emulsions (350 mL preload containing 30 g fat) stabilized by sodium caseinate/monoglyceride (CasMag) with either liquid oil or liquid oil/solid fat mixture (30% solid fat)
comparison: Fat emulsions stabilized by egg lecithin (control) or sodium sterol lactylate; In second experiment: ¹³C-labeled mixed TG incorporated into CasMag emulsion versus control emulsion
outcomes_primary: Postprandial plasma triglyceride (TG) concentrations
outcomes_secondary: Plasma cholecystokinin (CCK) concentrations; plasma glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) concentrations; plasma peptide YY (PYY) concentrations; food intake at test meal 3 hours after preload; ¹³C breath test for TG absorption and metabolism (second experiment)
extraction_notes: Crossover design with randomized, double-blind methodology. Two separate experiments described: main study (n=20) and subset study with ¹³C-labeled TG (n=8). Primary outcome not explicitly designated; inferred from study aim.

title: Rapid tachyphylaxis of the glucagon-like peptide 1-induced deceleration of gastric emptying in humans.
population: Healthy male volunteers, 25 ± 4 years old, BMI 24.6 ± 4.7 kg/m2, with normal oral glucose tolerance according to World Health Organization criteria, no family history of diabetes, no personal history of gastrointestinal disorders
intervention: Intravenous infusion of synthetic GLP-1 [7-36 amide] at 0.8 pmol/kg/min, starting 30 minutes before first meal and continuing for 510 minutes (total 8.5 hours), with two liquid mixed meals (50g sucrose plus amino acids in 400mL) administered intragastrically at time 0 and 240 minutes
comparison: Placebo (0.9% NaCl with 1% human serum albumin) intravenous infusion from -30 to 480 minutes, with identical liquid mixed meal protocol
outcomes_primary: Gastric emptying velocity measured using double-sampling dye dilution technique with phenol red
outcomes_secondary: Plasma glucose concentrations, insulin concentrations, C-peptide concentrations, pancreatic glucagon concentrations, GIP (gastric inhibitory polypeptide) concentrations, pancreatic polypeptide (PP) concentrations as marker of vagal activation
extraction_notes: Crossover design with random order, 1-4 weeks washout between experiments. Sample size is small (n=9). Primary outcome not explicitly designated; gastric emptying appears to be the main outcome based on study objectives.

title: DURATION-2: efficacy and safety of switching from maximum daily sitagliptin or pioglitazone to once-weekly exenatide.
journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association
population: Male and non-pregnant female patients, at least 18 years of age, with Type 2 diabetes mellitus, otherwise healthy, treated with a stable regimen of metformin for a minimum of 2 months prior to screening, HbA1c 7.1-11.0% (54-97 mmol/mol), BMI 25-45 kg/m2
intervention: Exenatide once-weekly 2 mg subcutaneous injection (self-administered) plus metformin background therapy
comparison: Sitagliptin 100 mg once daily in the morning plus placebo once-weekly injection; Pioglitazone 45 mg once daily in the morning plus placebo once-weekly injection. In open-label phase: all patients switched to exenatide once-weekly, comparing continued exenatide once-weekly treatment versus switching from sitagliptin or pioglitazone to exenatide once-weekly
outcomes_primary: Change from baseline to weeks 26 and 52 in HbA1c; change from week 26 to week 52 in HbA1c
outcomes_secondary: Proportion of patients achieving HbA1c targets of <7.0% (<53 mmol/mol) and ≤6.5% (≤48 mmol/mol); change in fasting plasma glucose (target ≤7 mmol/l); body weight; fasting lipids; fasting insulin; systolic and diastolic blood pressure; cardiovascular risk markers (urinary albumin/creatinine ratio, B-type natriuretic peptide, high-sensitivity C-reactive protein, plasminogen activator inhibitor-1); safety and tolerability including treatment-emergent adverse events, hypoglycaemia (major and minor)
extraction_notes: This is an extension study (open-label phase) of DURATION-2 trial. The initial 26-week phase was double-blind, double-dummy; the subsequent 26-week open-label phase is the focus of this report. Primary and secondary outcome distinction not explicitly stated in text; outcomes listed are described collectively as 'study endpoints'.

title: Almond ingestion at mealtime reduces postprandial glycemia and chronic ingestion reduces hemoglobin A(1c) in individuals with well-controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus.
population: Adults including individuals with well-controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus and healthy individuals without diabetes
intervention: One serving of almonds (28 g) consumed with a standardized test meal (bagel, juice, and butter); for pilot study: 1 serving of almonds 5 days per week for 12 weeks
comparison: Same standardized test meal without almonds; for pilot study: comparison group without almond ingestion
outcomes_primary: Postprandial glycemia
outcomes_secondary: Postprandial insulinemia, plasma glucagon-like peptide-1 at 30 minutes postmeal, hemoglobin A1c (pilot study), fasting glucose concentrations (pilot study)
extraction_notes: Study contains two components: a randomized crossover trial for acute effects and a small pilot study for chronic effects. Pilot study had 6-7 subjects per group. Washout period of at least 1 week between crossover occasions.

title: Cardioprotection against ischaemia induced by dobutamine stress using glucagon-like peptide-1 in patients with coronary artery disease.
population: Patients with coronary artery disease and good left ventricular function awaiting revascularisation
intervention: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) infused intravenously at 1.2 pmol/kg/min starting 30 min before dobutamine stress echocardiography
comparison: Control (dobutamine stress echocardiography without GLP-1 infusion)
outcomes_primary: Global and regional wall left ventricular function assessed using tissue Doppler imaging at rest, peak stress and 30 min into recovery
extraction_notes: Randomised crossover design with 14 patients. No secondary outcomes explicitly defined. Primary outcome measures included ejection fraction, mitral annular systolic velocity, and regional wall function assessed by velocity, strain and strain rate.

title: Breakfast consumption affects appetite, energy intake, and the metabolic and endocrine responses to foods consumed later in the day in male habitual breakfast eaters.
population: Male habitual breakfast eaters of healthy body weight who reported regularly consuming breakfast
intervention: Standardized breakfast (10% daily energy requirement; 14% protein, 14% fat, 72% carbohydrate) followed by a 1050-kJ liquid preload 150 min later
comparison: No breakfast followed by a 1050-kJ liquid preload 150 min later
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract. Outcomes measured included: blood glucose response to preload, serum insulin response to preload, plasma FFA response, plasma glucagon-like peptide 1 response, plasma peptide Y response, subjective appetite ratings (desire to eat, fullness, hunger), and energy intake at lunchtime test meal. Small sample size (n=12). Randomized crossover design.

title: A pilot study to assess whether glucagon-like peptide-1 protects the heart from ischemic dysfunction and attenuates stunning after coronary balloon occlusion in humans.
population: Patients with normal left ventricular function and single-vessel coronary disease within the left anterior descending artery undergoing elective percutaneous coronary intervention
intervention: GLP-1(7-36) amide infusion at 1.2 pmol/kg per minute, administered immediately after the first balloon occlusion
comparison: Saline infusion
outcomes_primary: Left ventricular systolic and diastolic function recovery after balloon occlusion, measured by pressure-volume loops using conductance catheter (dP/dt max)
outcomes_secondary: Left ventricular dysfunction after second balloon occlusion, cumulative left ventricular dysfunction on subsequent occlusion
extraction_notes: This is described as a pilot study. Duration of GLP-1 infusion not explicitly stated. Primary versus secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract.

title: Four weeks of treatment with liraglutide reduces insulin dose without loss of glycemic control in type 1 diabetic patients with and without residual beta-cell function.
population: Type 1 diabetic patients aged 18-50 years, BMI 18-27 kg/m2, Caucasian descent, diagnosed between ages 5-40 years, with completed remission period, no known late diabetes complications (except microalbuminuria), no use of medication known to affect glucose metabolism, no symptoms of autonomic neuropathy, HbA1c ≤8.5%. Patients stratified by residual β-cell function: C-peptide positive (stimulated C-peptide ≥0.06 nmol/L) and C-peptide negative (stimulated C-peptide <0.03 nmol/L)
intervention: Liraglutide 0.6 mg subcutaneous daily for first week, then 1.2 mg daily for remaining 3 weeks, plus insulin (with initial fast-acting insulin dose decreased by 50% and long-acting insulin by 0-20% at liraglutide initiation, then titrated to target blood glucose 5-7 mmol/L)
comparison: Insulin monotherapy alone (C-peptide negative patients only)
outcomes_primary: Change in mean insulin dose
outcomes_secondary: Changes in 24-hour glucose profiles, glycemic control (HbA1c), mean blood glucose, body weight, time spent with blood glucose <3.9 mmol/L (hypoglycemia), time spent with blood glucose >10 mmol/L (hyperglycemia), time spent with blood glucose 3.9-10 mmol/L (normoglycemia), fasting blood glucose, peak postprandial blood glucose, β-cell function (stimulated C-peptide), time to hypoglycemia during exercise test, rate of plasma glucose fall during exercise, glucagon response
extraction_notes: Non-blinded study due to unavailable placebo pen devices. C-peptide positive patients were not randomized - all received liraglutide plus insulin. Only C-peptide negative patients were randomized to liraglutide plus insulin versus insulin alone. Sample size calculation specified 9 patients per group to detect 30% change in insulin dose.

title: Glutamine reduces postprandial glycemia and augments the glucagon-like peptide-1 response in type 2 diabetes patients.
population: Type 2 diabetes patients with HbA1c ≤7.1% (6.5±0.6%), diabetes duration <5 years (2.4±1.2 years), treated with lifestyle alone or metformin therapy. Exclusion criteria: treatment with oral hypoglycemic agents other than metformin, ethanol intake >40 g/d, liver or kidney disease, weight change >2 kg in preceding 6 months, use of weight loss medications, previous bowel surgery, documented malabsorption.
intervention: 30 g L-glutamine (Gln-30) consumed orally in 300 mL ice-cold water over 2 min immediately prior to meal; 15 g L-glutamine (Gln-15) consumed orally in 300 mL ice-cold water over 2 min immediately prior to meal; 100 mg sitagliptin plus 15 g L-glutamine (SIT+Gln-15) with sitagliptin administered orally 25 min prior to meal and glutamine immediately prior to meal; single dose administration with low-fat meal (963 kJ: 37 g carbohydrate, 1.3 g fat, 16 g protein)
comparison: Water control; 100 mg sitagliptin alone (SIT) administered orally 25 min prior to meal with 50 mL water
outcomes_primary: Postprandial glycemic response (blood glucose AUC at 0-60 min, 60-180 min, and 0-180 min)
outcomes_secondary: Circulating insulin concentration, C-peptide concentration, glucagon concentration, total GLP-1 concentration, active GLP-1 concentration, insulin:glucose ratio, C-peptide:glucose ratio, insulin:glucagon ratio, satiety assessed by visual analogue scale, adverse effects
extraction_notes: Randomized cross-over design with 5 separate study visits separated by 1-2 weeks. Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in the text; classification based on study aims stated in introduction. Single-dose acute study design.

title: Effects of exenatide twice daily versus sitagliptin on 24-h glucose, glucoregulatory and hormonal measures: a randomized, double-blind, crossover study.
population: Adults aged 18-70 years with type 2 diabetes, BMI 25-45 kg/m2, stable body weight for at least 3 months, HbA1c 7-11%, fasting glucose <280 mg/dl, on stable dose of metformin for at least 60 days or thiazolidinedione for at least 120 days. Exclusions: females of childbearing potential, treatment with insulin, exenatide or any GLP-1 receptor agonist, sulphonylureas, drugs affecting gastrointestinal motility, weight loss drugs, corticosteroids, α-glucosidase inhibitors, history of organ transplant, liver or renal disease, fasting triglycerides >400 mg/dl, blood pressure >165/90 mm Hg
intervention: Exenatide 5 µg subcutaneous twice daily for 1 week then 10 µg subcutaneous twice daily for additional 3 weeks (total 4 weeks), plus oral placebo capsule once daily in the morning, in addition to prestudy medication(s)
comparison: Sitagliptin 100 mg oral capsule once daily in the morning for 4 weeks, plus subcutaneous placebo injections twice daily, in addition to prestudy medication(s). Crossover design: subjects received one treatment for 4 weeks then switched to alternative treatment for 4 weeks
outcomes_primary: Time-averaged glucose during 24-hour inpatient visits (calculated from 36 glucose measurements over 24 hours)
outcomes_secondary: Fasting glucose; 2-hour postprandial glucose; difference between minimum and maximum glucose concentrations during 24 hours; area under the curve of glucose above 7.8 mmol/l and above 11 mmol/l; proportion of time during 24 hours with glucose 3.9-7.8 mmol/l; homeostasis model assessment of β-cell function (HOMA-B); postprandial insulin concentrations; postprandial intact GLP-1 concentrations; postprandial glucagon concentrations; 24-hour caloric intake; weight change; hypoglycaemic events (minor and major); adverse events
extraction_notes: 8-week double-blind randomized crossover single-centre study. No washout period between treatments. Sample size: 86 randomized, 83 received study drug. HbA1c measured only at baseline due to short study duration.

title: Effects of a single dose of exenatide on appetite, gut hormones, and glucose homeostasis in adults with Prader-Willi syndrome.
journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
population: Adults with Prader-Willi syndrome (PWS) compared with obese controls (OBESE), matched for gender, age, body mass index, and central/total body fat
intervention: Single subcutaneous injection of exenatide 10 μg
comparison: Placebo (single-blinded, crossover design)
outcomes_primary: Glucose, insulin, C-peptide, glucagon, peptide YY (total)/PYY (3-36), glucagon-like peptide-1, and ghrelin (total) measured fasting and postprandially; appetite and satiety assessed by visual analog scales; energy expenditure measured by indirect calorimetry
outcomes_secondary: Side effects screened during and for 24 hours after the meal
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract; outcomes listed under 'Main Outcome Measures' were categorized as primary. Sample size was small (8 PWS and 11 OBESE patients). Study described as a pilot study.

title: Exenatide or glimepiride added to metformin on metabolic control and on insulin resistance in type 2 diabetic patients.
population: Type 2 diabetic patients with uncontrolled diabetes mellitus, intolerant to metformin at highest dosages (2500-3000 mg/day)
intervention: Exenatide 5 μg twice a day, titrated after 1 month to 10 μg twice a day, for 12 months
comparison: Glimepiride 1 mg three times a day, titrated after 1 month to 2 mg three times a day, for 12 months
outcomes_secondary: Body weight, body mass index (BMI), HbA1c, glycemic control, fasting plasma insulin, homeostasis model assessment insulin resistance index (HOMA-IR), adiponectin, tumor necrosis factor-α, high sensitivity-C reactive protein
extraction_notes: Primary outcome not explicitly distinguished from secondary outcomes in the abstract. All outcomes listed as secondary. Study design described as randomized, single-blind, controlled. Sample size: 111 patients. Background therapy: metformin (patients continued on metformin but were intolerant to highest dosages).

title: Effects of combined exenatide and pioglitazone therapy on hepatic fat content in type 2 diabetes.
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes on diet and/or metformin
intervention: Combined therapy with pioglitazone 45 mg/day orally and exenatide 10 µg subcutaneously twice daily for 12 months
comparison: Pioglitazone 45 mg/day alone for 12 months
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract. Outcomes assessed included hepatic fat content (measured by magnetic resonance spectroscopy), plasma adiponectin levels, fasting plasma glucose, fasting free fatty acid, HbA1c, plasma triglyceride concentration, body weight, and hepatic injury biomarkers (AST, ALT). Small sample size (n=21 total, n=10 pioglitazone alone, n=11 combined therapy).

title: Effect of the dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitor sitagliptin in older adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus.
journal: Journal of the American Geriatrics Society
population: Older adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus
intervention: Sitagliptin (dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitor); dose, route, frequency, and duration not specified in available text
comparison: Not specified in available text
outcomes_primary: Not specified in available text
outcomes_secondary: Not specified in available text
extraction_notes: Abstract text not available; extraction based solely on title. Dose, comparator, and outcome definitions cannot be determined from title alone.

title: The effects of L-arabinose on intestinal sucrase activity: dose-response studies in vitro and in humans.
journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
population: 15 healthy men
intervention: Sucrose beverages (75 g in 300 mL) supplemented with l-arabinose at 1.3%, 2.7%, and 4% by weight, tested at breakfast
comparison: Sucrose beverage (75 g in 300 mL) supplemented with 0% l-arabinose (placebo)
outcomes_secondary: Glucose, insulin, C-peptide, incretin hormones (glucagon-like peptide-1, glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide), triacylglycerol measured under fasting conditions and for 3 hours postprandially; postprandial appetite sensations; energy intake at lunch
extraction_notes: Randomized, double-blind, crossover study design. Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract. Study also included in vitro component using Caco-2 cells which is outside human clinical trial scope.

title: Effects of oligofructose on appetite profile, glucagon-like peptide 1 and peptide YY3-36 concentrations and energy intake.
population: Healthy subjects, men and women, aged approximately 28 years, BMI approximately 24.8 kg/m²
intervention: Oligofructose 16 g daily orally for 13 days; Oligofructose 10 g daily orally for 13 days
comparison: Placebo (maltodextrin) 16 g daily for 13 days
outcomes_primary: Energy intake; appetite profile
outcomes_secondary: Active glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1) concentrations; peptide YY3-36 (PYY) concentrations; area under the curve for GLP-1 and PYY
extraction_notes: Randomised double-blind crossover study design with 2-week washout period between treatments. Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract; categorization based on emphasis in text.

title: Gastric bypass reduces fat intake and preference.
journal: American journal of physiology. Regulatory, integrative and comparative physiology
population: Two populations studied: (1) Patients with morbid obesity who underwent gastric bypass surgery (human trial setting), (2) Rats undergoing experimental gastric bypass surgery
intervention: Roux-en-Y gastric bypass surgery
comparison: Human study: vertical-banded gastroplasty; Rat study: sham-operated controls
outcomes_primary: Proportion of dietary fat intake; total fat and caloric intake; preference for high-fat food (Intralipid concentrations in two-bottle preference tests)
outcomes_secondary: Standard low-fat chow consumption; appetitive and consummatory behavior in brief access test; glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) levels; conditioned taste aversion following oral gavage of corn oil after saccharin ingestion
extraction_notes: Mixed study design combining human clinical data (6 years post-surgery) with experimental rat model. Primary outcomes not explicitly designated as such in abstract; categorization based on emphasis in text.

title: Structure modification of a milk protein-based model food affects postprandial intestinal peptide release and fullness in healthy young men.
population: Healthy males (n=8)
intervention: Casein protein cross-linked with transglutaminase (Cas-TG, rigid gel) - milk protein-based model food
comparison: Whey protein (Wh, low-viscous liquid); Casein (Cas, high-viscous liquid) - isoenergetic and isovolumic test products
outcomes_secondary: Plasma glucose; Insulin; Cholecystokinin (CCK); Glucagon-like peptide 1; Peptide YY; Appetite/fullness assessment
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract; all outcomes listed as secondary. Crossover design implied by 'randomised order' consumption of all three products by same participants. Follow-up period was 4 hours post-consumption.

title: The effect of the once-daily human glucagon-like peptide 1 analog liraglutide on the pharmacokinetics of acetaminophen.
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes
intervention: Liraglutide 1.8 mg once daily, administered until steady state, followed by a single dose of acetaminophen 1 g administered at the time of liraglutide Cmax
comparison: Placebo (two-period crossover design)
outcomes_primary: Area under the curve (AUC)(0-∞) and AUC(0-480 min) of acetaminophen; equivalence defined as 90% CI for the ratio fully contained within 0.80 to 1.25
outcomes_secondary: Acetaminophen Cmax (maximum concentration); acetaminophen tmax (time to maximum concentration)
extraction_notes: Crossover design with subjects serving as their own controls. Primary outcome appears to be bioequivalence assessment based on acetaminophen AUC. Study population baseline characteristics were provided but not explicit eligibility criteria.

title: Changes in gut hormone and glucose concentrations in relation to hunger and fullness.
journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
population: Healthy subjects, age 24 ± 6 years, BMI 25.1 ± 3.1 kg/m²
intervention: 4-course lunch consumed over 2 hours
comparison: 4-course lunch consumed over 0.5 hours
outcomes_primary: Within-subject relations between visual analog scale (VAS) hunger and fullness ratings and concentrations of glucagon-like peptide 1, peptide tyrosine-tyrosine, ghrelin, glucose, and insulin; synchronization and time lags between appetite ratings and hormone/glucose concentrations
extraction_notes: Randomized crossover design with n=38 subjects. Study started in 2007 and was not registered as a clinical trial. Primary outcomes not explicitly labeled but derived from stated objectives. No secondary outcomes explicitly defined.

title: Flaxseed dietary fibers suppress postprandial lipemia and appetite sensation in young men.
journal: Nutrition, metabolism, and cardiovascular diseases : NMCD
population: Young men, healthy, after overnight fast
intervention: High-mucilage dose (HM) meal: 3.4 g/MJ dietary fiber from flaxseed; Low-mucilage dose (LM) meal: 2.4 g/MJ dietary fiber from flaxseed; Whole flaxseed (WF) meal: 2.4 g/MJ dietary fiber from whole flaxseeds
comparison: Control meal (C): 1.4 g/MJ dietary fiber
outcomes_primary: Postprandial lipemia (triacylglycerols), subjective appetite sensation (satiety, fullness) assessed using visual analogue scales
outcomes_secondary: Appetite-regulating hormones (ghrelin, CCK, GLP-1), insulin, glycemia, ad libitum energy intake
extraction_notes: Sample size n=18. Double-blind randomized crossover design. Iso-caloric meals tested. Test day duration was 7 hours. Primary outcomes not explicitly labeled as such; classification based on study aims.

title: Effects of a long-acting GLP-1 mimetic (PF-04603629) on pulse rate and diastolic blood pressure in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus.
population: Subjects with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM)
intervention: PF-04603629 (exendin-transferrin fusion protein, a long-acting GLP-1 mimetic), single dose, dose range 1-70 mg
comparison: Placebo
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract. Outcomes assessed included: safety, pharmacodynamics, glucose area under the curve following mixed meal test, treatment-related adverse events (gastrointestinal including nausea and vomiting), pulse rate, and diastolic blood pressure. The abstract does not specify which outcomes were designated as primary versus secondary.

title: Effects of short-term therapy with glibenclamide and repaglinide on incretin hormones and oxidative damage associated with postprandial hyperglycaemia in people with type 2 diabetes mellitus.
population: Adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus suboptimally treated with metformin, HbA1c between 7.5 and 10.5%, free from cardiovascular and renal disease
intervention: Repaglinide for eight weeks
comparison: Glibenclamide for eight weeks
outcomes_secondary: Glucose, insulin, C-peptide, glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1), glucose-dependent insulinotropic peptide (GIP), total antioxidant status, F2-isoprostane, interleukin-6, cell adhesion molecules measured during oral glucose load; areas under the curve at 45, 60 and 120 minutes; HbA1c; fasting glucose; 2-hour glucose
extraction_notes: Primary outcomes not explicitly distinguished from secondary outcomes in abstract. Sample size was 27 subjects.

title: Safety, tolerability and sustained weight loss over 2 years with the once-daily human GLP-1 analog, liraglutide.
population: Adults aged 18–65 years with stable weight, body mass index 30–40 kg/m², fasting plasma glucose <7 mmol/l (126 mg/dl), without type 1 or 2 diabetes mellitus, drug-induced obesity, use of weight-lowering pharmacotherapy or participation in weight-control study within preceding 3 months, surgical obesity treatment, or major medical conditions; recruited from 19 research sites in 8 European countries
intervention: Once-daily subcutaneous liraglutide at doses of 1.2 mg, 1.8 mg, 2.4 mg, or 3.0 mg by evening injection, starting at 0.6 mg per day and increasing weekly during 4-week dose escalation period; after 1 year, liraglutide/placebo recipients switched to liraglutide 2.4 mg, then to 3.0 mg between weeks 70–96; combined with diet (500 kcal deficit per day, approximately 30% energy from fat, 20% from protein, 50% from carbohydrates) and exercise counseling throughout 2-year treatment period
comparison: Placebo (matching injection volumes in identical 3 ml cartridges administered by evening subcutaneous injection); open-label orlistat 120 mg capsules three times daily with each main meal
outcomes_primary: At 20-week trial: weight change from randomization. At 1 year: weight loss from randomization. At 2-year extension: safety and tolerability of liraglutide
outcomes_secondary: At 2-year extension: efficacy for sustaining weight loss. Additional efficacy endpoints: proportion losing >5% or >10% of randomization weight, changes in waist circumference, blood pressure, prevalence of prediabetes and metabolic syndrome, glycemic parameters, fasting lipids, cardiovascular biomarkers, body composition (by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry and abdominal CT in subgroup), and quality of life
extraction_notes: Complex study design: 20-week double-blind RCT with 2-year extension; sponsor unblinded at 20 weeks, participants/investigators unblinded at 1 year; orlistat arm was open-label throughout; placebo arm terminated at 1 year

title: Effects of exenatide on measures of β-cell function after 3 years in metformin-treated patients with type 2 diabetes.
population: Metformin-treated patients with type 2 diabetes, aged 30-75 years, HbA1c 6.5-9.5%, BMI 25-40 kg/m2, metformin treatment at stable dose for at least 2 months, no other blood glucose-lowering agents within 3 months prior to screening
intervention: Exenatide initiated at 5 µg twice daily (b.i.d.) injected 15 min before breakfast and dinner for 4 weeks, then increased to 10 µg b.i.d., titrated up to maximum 20 µg three times daily (t.i.d.) or maximum tolerated dose based on HbA1c levels, for 168 weeks (3 years), in addition to ongoing metformin treatment
comparison: Insulin glargine starting at 10 IU once daily at bedtime, titrated according to fasting self-monitored blood glucose levels (<5.6 mmol/L) using treat-to-target algorithm, for 168 weeks (3 years), in addition to ongoing metformin treatment
outcomes_primary: Treatment effect on β-cell function measured as first-phase glucose-stimulated C-peptide secretion adjusted for M value (disposition index)
outcomes_secondary: HbA1c, fasting plasma glucose, body weight, insulin sensitivity (M value from euglycemic hyperinsulinemic clamp), second-phase glucose-stimulated C-peptide secretion, arginine-stimulated C-peptide secretion, adverse events including gastrointestinal events and hypoglycemia
extraction_notes: Extension study of an original 1-year trial. Original randomization: 69 patients; 46 entered extension phase; 36 completed 3-year treatment period (EXE n=16, GLAR n=20). β-cell function assessed after 4-week off-drug period following treatment.

title: Exenatide reduces reperfusion injury in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction.
population: Patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) and Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction (TIMI) flow 0/1 treated with primary percutaneous coronary intervention (pPCI)
intervention: Exenatide administered intravenously, commenced 15 minutes before intervention and maintained for 6 hours after the procedure
comparison: Placebo (saline) administered intravenously with same timing
outcomes_primary: Salvage index calculated from myocardial area at risk (AAR) measured in the acute phase and final infarct size measured 90 ± 21 days after pPCI by cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR)
outcomes_secondary: Infarct size in relation to AAR; absolute infarct size; left ventricular function; 30-day clinical events; adverse effects
extraction_notes: Exenatide dose not specified in abstract

title: Postprandial glucose, insulin and glucagon-like peptide 1 responses to sucrose ingested with berries in healthy subjects.
population: Healthy subjects, n=12
intervention: Berry meal: purée (150 g) made of bilberries, blackcurrants, cranberries and strawberries with 35 g sucrose
comparison: Control meal: same amount of sucrose and available carbohydrates in water
outcomes_primary: Postprandial glucose concentrations (capillary and venous plasma), serum insulin concentrations, glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1) responses, measured at baseline and at 15, 30, 45, 60, 90 and 120 min after meal ingestion
outcomes_secondary: Maximum increases of capillary and venous glucose and insulin concentrations, glycaemic profile
extraction_notes: Study design: randomised, single-blind, placebo-controlled crossover study. Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract; classification based on reporting emphasis.

title: Intraduodenal administration of intact pea protein effectively reduces food intake in both lean and obese male subjects.
population: Healthy male subjects, 10 lean (BMI 18-25 kg/m2) and 10 obese (BMI >30 kg/m2), with no diabetes, no gastrointestinal diseases, and no medical treatment
intervention: Pea protein solution (250 mg/kg bodyweight in 0.4 ml/kg bodyweight of water) administered intraduodenally via naso-duodenal tube over 30 minutes, or orally consumed within 5 minutes
comparison: Placebo (0.4 ml/kg bodyweight of water) administered either intraduodenally or orally
outcomes_primary: Food intake at ad libitum meal (Lasagne Bolognese) assessed 120 minutes after intervention
outcomes_secondary: Appetite profile (Visual Analogue Scale questionnaire measuring feelings of hunger, fullness, satiety, thirst, desire to eat); plasma GLP-1 concentrations; plasma CCK concentrations; plasma PYY concentrations; plasma total Ghrelin levels; well-being questionnaire (headache, nausea, stomach-ache, diarrhea, other symptoms)
extraction_notes: Single-blind, randomized controlled crossover design with 4 test days separated by 1 week. Only male subjects included to avoid hormonal fluctuations. Primary outcome not explicitly designated as such but food intake appears to be main outcome of interest.

title: Exenatide decreases hepatic fibroblast growth factor 21 resistance in non-alcoholic fatty liver disease in a mouse model of obesity and in a randomised controlled trial.
population: Type 2 diabetes mellitus patients aged 30-70 years with stable body weight for at least 3 months, fasting plasma glucose 7.0-14.5 mmol/l, on diet and/or metformin therapy, with alanine aminotransferase or aspartate aminotransferase not greater than 2.5 times upper limit of normal; patients who had received insulin, sulfonylureas, sitagliptin, exenatide or thiazolidinedione within previous 3 months were excluded
intervention: Pioglitazone 45 mg/day orally plus exenatide 10 μg subcutaneously twice daily for 12 months (preceded by 2-week titration period with pioglitazone 30 mg/day and exenatide 5 μg twice daily)
comparison: Pioglitazone 45 mg/day orally alone for 12 months (preceded by 2-week titration period with pioglitazone 30 mg/day)
outcomes_primary: Fasting plasma FGF21 levels
outcomes_secondary: Hepatic fat content measured by magnetic resonance spectroscopy; body weight
extraction_notes: Open-label parallel study design. Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly designated in abstract; outcomes listed based on main reported measurements. Study also included a separate animal (DIO mouse) experiment which is not extracted here as per focus on human RCT. n=24 randomised, n=21 completed.

title: A thorough QT study to evaluate the effects of singledose exenatide 10 μg on cardiac repolarization in healthy subjects.
journal: International journal of clinical pharmacology and therapeutics
population: Healthy subjects who passed an initial tolerability screening (receiving subcutaneous exenatide 10 μg daily for 3 consecutive days)
intervention: Exenatide 10 μg subcutaneous injection, single dose
comparison: Placebo; Moxifloxacin 400 mg orally (positive control)
outcomes_primary: QT interval change from predose using Fridericia's correction (ΔQTcF) and individual correction (ΔQTcI); difference from placebo in QTc change
outcomes_secondary: Relationship between QTc interval and plasma exenatide concentrations; relationship between QTc interval and plasma glucose concentrations; relationship between QTc interval and plasma insulin concentrations
extraction_notes: This is a thorough QT study designed to evaluate cardiac repolarization effects rather than therapeutic efficacy. Double-dummy, double-blinded design. Washout periods of approximately 5 days between treatment periods.

title: Pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, safety, and tolerability of JNJ-38431055, a novel GPR119 receptor agonist and potential antidiabetes agent, in healthy male subjects.
population: Healthy male volunteers
intervention: JNJ-38431055, single oral doses ranging from 2.5-800 mg, administered as oral suspension formulation
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics (systemic exposure, terminal elimination half-life), pharmacodynamics
outcomes_secondary: Plasma glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1) concentrations, glucose-dependent insulinotropic peptide (GIP) concentrations, peptide YY (PYY) concentrations, glucose excursion, insulin secretion, insulin secretion rate (ISR) during graded glucose infusion
extraction_notes: Study conducted in healthy volunteers rather than diabetic patients. Multiple studies appear to be described (single dose studies and a graded glucose infusion study). Primary vs secondary outcome distinction not explicitly stated in abstract.

title: Changes in postprandial gut hormones after metabolic surgery: a comparison of gastric bypass and sleeve gastrectomy.
journal: Surgery for obesity and related diseases : official journal of the American Society for Bariatric Surgery
population: Patients undergoing metabolic surgery for type 2 diabetes mellitus; participants from a previous randomized trial comparing laparoscopic gastric bypass and laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy
intervention: Laparoscopic gastric bypass (GB)
comparison: Laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy (SG)
outcomes_secondary: Glucose homeostasis; mixed meal test results; postprandial gut hormone levels (acyl ghrelin, des-acyl ghrelin, cholecystokinin, resistin, obestatin, gastric inhibitory peptide, glucagon-like peptide-1, leptin); T2DM remission; body weight; waist circumference; glucose levels; hemoglobin A1c; insulin resistance
extraction_notes: Primary outcomes not explicitly distinguished from secondary outcomes in abstract. Study is a prospective follow-up of patients from a previous randomized trial at 2 years post-surgery. Sample size was 16 per group initially with 13 per group completing gut hormone evaluation.

title: The gut hormones PYY 3-36 and GLP-1 7-36 amide reduce food intake and modulate brain activity in appetite centers in humans.
population: Healthy right-handed subjects, age 21-36 years, body mass index 18.3-25.1 kg/m2. Exclusion criteria: smoking, substance abuse, eating disorders, regular medication (except oral contraceptives), pregnancy, medical or psychiatric illness.

comparison: 90-minute saline infusion in fasted state (control); 90-minute saline infusion after standard 2500 kJ breakfast (fed state)

extraction_notes: Single-blinded randomized crossover design with 5 intervention visits plus 1 acclimatization visit. 16 subjects recruited, 15 completed analysis due to one exclusion for excessive head movement.

title: Effects of variations in duodenal glucose load on glycaemic, insulin, and incretin responses in type 2 diabetes.
journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association
population: Males with well-controlled Type 2 diabetes, managed by diet alone
intervention: Intraduodenal glucose infusions at 1 kcal/min (G1), 2 kcal/min (G2), and 4 kcal/min (G4) for 120 minutes
comparison: Saline control; healthy controls (separate comparison group)
outcomes_primary: Blood glucose responses, plasma insulin responses, plasma GLP-1 responses, plasma GIP responses
extraction_notes: This is a physiological study with single-blind randomized crossover design. Sample size is small (n=8). Healthy controls were compared but appear to be from separate/existing data rather than concurrently randomized. Primary vs secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract.

title: Exenatide exerts a potent antiinflammatory effect.

population: Patients with type 2 diabetes; 24 patients randomized
intervention: Exenatide 10 μg twice daily subcutaneous injection for 12 weeks; single dose acute study with exenatide 5 μg

outcomes_secondary: Fasting blood glucose, glycosylated hemoglobin (HbA1c), free fatty acids, body weight, plasma concentrations of monocyte chemoattractant protein-1, matrix metalloproteinase-9, serum amyloid A, and IL-6
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in the abstract; classification based on stated study objective (antiinflammatory effect). Baseline characteristics (age, BMI, HbA1c) reported but not explicitly stated as inclusion criteria.

title: Short-term exenatide treatment leads to significant weight loss in a subset of obese women without diabetes.
population: Obese women without diabetes aged 18-70 years with BMI 28-40 kg/m2. Subjects had stable weight within 6 months of screening.
intervention: Exenatide 5 μg subcutaneous injection twice daily (before breakfast and supper) for 2 weeks, then increased to 10 μg twice daily, for a total treatment period of 16 weeks. No lifestyle intervention.

outcomes_primary: Change in body weight (kg) and BMI (kg/m2)
outcomes_secondary: Waist circumference, body composition (bioelectrical impedance analysis), blood pressure, heart rate, lipid panels, leptin, adiponectin, glycemic status (75-g 2-h oral glucose tolerance test), insulin, resting energy expenditure, physical activity (accelerometer), sleep parameters (sleep monitor), hunger/satiety/nausea ratings (visual analog scale)
extraction_notes: Crossover design study (35 weeks total: two 16-week treatment periods separated by 3-week washout). Study enrolled only women, limiting generalizability. 24% of population had prediabetes at enrollment.

title: Effects of vildagliptin on postprandial markers of bone resorption and calcium homeostasis in recently diagnosed, well-controlled type 2 diabetes patients.
population: Drug-naïve patients with type 2 diabetes, recently diagnosed, well-controlled/mild hyperglycemia
intervention: Vildagliptin 100 mg once daily for 1 year
comparison: Placebo for 1 year
outcomes_primary: Postprandial serum concentrations of cross-linked C-terminal telopeptide (s-CTx)
outcomes_secondary: Fasting serum alkaline phosphatase, serum calcium, serum phosphate
extraction_notes: Single-center, double-blind, randomized clinical trial. Primary outcome not explicitly labeled but s-CTx appears to be the main endpoint based on study aim. 50 weeks treatment duration mentioned in methods though 1 year stated elsewhere.

title: Comparisons of the effects of 12-week administration of miglitol and voglibose on the responses of plasma incretins after a mixed meal in Japanese type 2 diabetic patients.
population: Japanese type 2 diabetic patients
intervention: Miglitol (alpha-glucosidase inhibitor absorbed in the intestine), 12-week administration
comparison: Voglibose (alpha-glucosidase inhibitor not absorbed), 12-week administration
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract. Outcomes measured include: plasma glucose, serum insulin, total GIP, active GLP-1, and body weight during 2-hour meal tolerance test. Sample sizes: miglitol group n=26, voglibose group n=24. Dose, route, and frequency of both drugs not specified.

title: Effect of additional treatment with EXenatide in patients with an Acute Myocardial Infarction (EXAMI): study protocol for a randomized controlled trial.
population: Patients with acute ST elevation myocardial infarction successfully treated with primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI)

comparison: Placebo infusion on top of standard treatment
outcomes_primary: Myocardial infarct size as a percentage of the area at risk, measured by MRI (area at risk measured using T2-weighted images at 3-7 days; infarct size measured using delayed contrast enhancement at 4 months)
outcomes_secondary: Left ventricular volumes, mass and ejection fraction; segmental wall thickening; microvascular obstruction; area at risk; global and regional cardiac function by echocardiography; tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion (TAPSE); diastolic left ventricular function; major cardiovascular events (death, myocardial re-infarction, coronary artery bypass grafting, repeat PCI); cardiac arrhythmias; heart failure; repeat coronary angiography; stroke; hospital admission; TIMI frame count; TIMI blush grade
extraction_notes: This is a study protocol publication, not a completed trial report. Standard treatment includes aspirin, heparin, clopidogrel, aggressive lipid-lowering treatment, ACE inhibitor or ARB, and beta-blocker. Total planned enrollment is 108 patients.

title: Exenatide as a weight-loss therapy in extreme pediatric obesity: a randomized, controlled pilot study.
population: Children and adolescents aged 8-19 years with extreme obesity (BMI ≥1.2 times the 95th percentile or BMI ≥35 kg/m2); exclusion criteria: diabetes mellitus (type 1 or 2), use of weight-loss medication within 3 months of screening, initiation of new drug therapy within 30 days of screening, BMI ≥55 kg/m2, history of bariatric surgery, obesity from established genetic cause or known syndrome (e.g., Prader-Willi)
