comparison: Clinically-offered lifestyle modification alone (control phase) for 3 months
outcomes_primary: Body mass index (BMI)
outcomes_secondary: Body fat percentage, blood pressure, lipids, oral glucose tolerance (OGTT), fasting glucose, fasting insulin, insulin sensitivity (WBISI/Matsuda index), beta cell function, adipokines (adiponectin, leptin), plasma biomarkers of inflammation (CRP, IL-6, TNF-α), oxidized LDL, markers of endothelial activation (VCAM-1, vWF), endothelial function (reactive hyperemic index)
extraction_notes: Open-label crossover design with no washout period; enrolled age range was 9-16 years (narrower than inclusion criteria of 8-19 years); lifestyle modification content varied by center

title: Effect of bile acid sequestrants on glucose metabolism, hepatic de novo lipogenesis, and cholesterol and bile acid kinetics in type 2 diabetes: a randomised controlled study.
population: Adults with type 2 diabetes, HbA1c 6.7-10.0% (50-86 mmol/mol), fasting glucose <16.7 mmol/l, fasting triacylglycerols <3.9 mmol/l, LDL-cholesterol >1.55 mmol/l, treated with diet and exercise, sulfonylurea, metformin or a combination thereof
intervention: Colesevelam 3.75 g/day for 12 weeks
comparison: Placebo for 12 weeks
outcomes_primary: Change from baseline in glucose kinetics
outcomes_secondary: Fasting and postprandial glucose pathways, lipid pathways, bile acid pathways measured using stable isotope techniques; plasma glucose, insulin, total GLP-1, total GIP, glucagon, and FGF-19 concentrations during fasting and following meal tolerance test; hepatic de novo lipogenesis; cholesterol synthesis; bile acid synthesis; HOMA-beta cell function; HOMA-insulin resistance
extraction_notes: Study conducted at three clinical sites in the USA

title: Preventive effects of exenatide on endothelial dysfunction induced by ischemia-reperfusion injury via KATP channels.
population: Healthy volunteers (n=20)
intervention: Subcutaneous exenatide 10 μg administered 30 minutes before ischemia-reperfusion injury protocol (15 minutes of ischemia at the level of the brachial artery followed by 15 minutes of reperfusion)
comparison: Placebo (double-blind, crossover design with 7-day washout period); Separate protocol: glibenclamide (glyburide) 5 mg pretreatment prior to exenatide (n=7)
outcomes_primary: Endothelium-dependent flow-mediated dilatation (FMD) of the radial artery measured before and after ischemia-reperfusion injury
outcomes_secondary: Pre-IR radial artery diameter; baseline radial artery diameter after IR injury
extraction_notes: Crossover design study. The glibenclamide arm (n=7) appears to be a separate mechanistic protocol rather than part of the main crossover study. Specific volunteer characteristics (age, sex, health status details) not provided in abstract.

title: Dosing rationale for liraglutide in type 2 diabetes mellitus: a pharmacometric assessment.
population: Adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus
intervention: Liraglutide (GLP-1 receptor agonist) as adjunct treatment to diet and exercise
comparison: Not explicitly stated
outcomes_primary: Not explicitly stated
outcomes_secondary: Fasting plasma glucose, hemoglobin A1c, calcitonin levels (assessed in exposure-response analyses)
extraction_notes: This is a pharmacometric assessment/regulatory review article rather than a clinical trial. No specific doses, comparators, or primary/secondary outcome designations are provided. The outcomes listed are parameters examined in exposure-response analyses rather than formally defined trial endpoints.

title: Efficacy and safety of exenatide once weekly versus metformin, pioglitazone, and sitagliptin used as monotherapy in drug-naive patients with type 2 diabetes (DURATION-4): a 26-week double-blind study.
population: Adults with type 2 diabetes, drug-naive (not treated with any antihyperglycemic drug for >7 days within 3 months of screening), HbA1c 7.1–11.0%, BMI 23–45 kg/m2, history of stable weight, suboptimally treated with diet and exercise alone
intervention: Exenatide once weekly (EQW) 2.0 mg subcutaneous injection + oral placebo, administered weekly for 26 weeks
comparison: Metformin 2,000 mg/day (up to 2,500 mg/day) oral + subcutaneous placebo; Pioglitazone 45 mg/day oral + subcutaneous placebo; Sitagliptin 100 mg/day oral + subcutaneous placebo. All comparators administered for 26 weeks with weekly placebo injections and daily oral medication.
outcomes_primary: Change in HbA1c from baseline at 26 weeks
outcomes_secondary: Proportion of patients achieving HbA1c <7.0% and ≤6.5%; change in fasting serum glucose; seven-point self-monitoring of blood glucose (SMBG); change in body weight; serum lipids; homeostasis model assessment of pancreatic β-cell function (HOMA-B) and insulin sensitivity (HOMA-S); safety and tolerability including adverse events, clinical laboratory assessments, vital signs, hypoglycemia (minor and major), and antibodies to exenatide; patient-reported outcomes including Impact of Weight on Quality of Life Questionnaire-Lite (IWQOL-Lite), Binge Eating Scale (BES), Diabetes Treatment Satisfaction Questionnaire (DTSQ), and EuroQol-5 dimensions (EQ-5D)
extraction_notes: Study was double-blind with 26-week treatment period and 10-week safety follow-up. Metformin and pioglitazone doses were titrated up to target/maximum-tolerated doses. Randomization stratified by country across 22 countries.

title: The role of the stomach in the control of appetite and the secretion of satiation peptides.
journal: American journal of physiology. Endocrinology and metabolism
population: Healthy subjects
intervention: Rapid intragastric load of glucose or mixed liquid meal
comparison: Continuous intraduodenal infusion of glucose or mixed liquid meal (3 kcal/min)
outcomes_primary: Appetite; plasma levels of glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1), peptide YY (PYY), and ghrelin
extraction_notes: This appears to be a physiological study rather than a clinical trial. Sample size not reported. Study design (randomization, blinding, crossover) not specified in abstract. Primary vs secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished.

title: Comparative effects of variations in duodenal glucose load on glycemic, insulinemic, and incretin responses in healthy young and older subjects.
journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
population: Healthy young subjects (age approximately 22 years) and healthy older subjects (age approximately 69 years), with equal male and female distribution in each group
intervention: Intraduodenal infusions of glucose at 1, 2, or 3 kcal/min for 60 minutes
comparison: Saline intraduodenal infusion for 60 minutes; comparison between young and older subject groups
outcomes_primary: Blood glucose, serum insulin, plasma incretin hormones (glucagon-like peptide-1 and glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide)
outcomes_secondary: Insulin resistance (homeostatic model assessment), β-cell function corrected for insulin sensitivity
extraction_notes: This is a mechanistic/physiological study rather than a traditional therapeutic intervention trial. Primary vs secondary outcome distinction not explicitly stated in abstract; categorization based on direct measurements vs calculated indices.

title: Effects of intravenous exenatide in type 2 diabetic patients with congestive heart failure: a double-blind, randomised controlled clinical trial of efficacy and safety.
population: Male and female patients aged 18-80 years with type 2 diabetes and congestive heart failure (ejection fraction ≤35% and New York Heart Association functional class III or IV)
intervention: Intravenous exenatide 0.12 pmol/kg/min infusion for 6 hours
comparison: Placebo intravenous infusion for 6 hours
outcomes_primary: Increase in cardiac index (CI) of ≥20% or decrease in pulmonary capillary wedge pressure (PCWP) of ≥20%
outcomes_secondary: Tolerability and safety of exenatide infusion
extraction_notes: Crossover trial design with 18-hour washout period. Although eligibility included male and female patients aged 18-80, only 20 male patients participated in the trial.

title: Satiety scores and satiety hormone response after sucrose-sweetened soft drink compared with isocaloric semi-skimmed milk and with non-caloric soft drink: a controlled trial.
population: Obese individuals
intervention: 500 ml of sugar-sweetened soft drink (regular cola: 900 kJ)
comparison: 500 ml semi-skimmed milk (950 kJ); 500 ml aspartame-sweetened soft drink (diet cola: 7.5 kJ); 500 ml water
outcomes_primary: Subjective appetite scores (fullness, hunger); appetite-regulating hormone concentrations (ghrelin, GLP-1, GIP) measured at baseline and continuously 4 hours post intake
outcomes_secondary: Ad libitum energy intake measured 4 hours after intake of test drinks; total energy intake (ad libitum energy intake plus energy intake from the drink)
extraction_notes: Crossover trial design with each subject receiving all four beverages. Primary vs secondary outcome distinction not explicitly stated in abstract; classification based on measurement timing and study objectives.

title: Beverage consumption, appetite, and energy intake: what did you expect?
journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
population: Healthy adults
intervention: Oral liquid preload with cognitive manipulation to perceive as gastric liquid (oral liquid/perceived gastric liquid) or oral liquid preload with cognitive manipulation to perceive as gastric solid (oral liquid/perceived gastric solid), or oral solid preload with cognitive manipulation to perceive as gastric liquid (oral solid/perceived gastric liquid) - all preloads designed to present a liquid gastric challenge, energy- and macronutrient-matched
comparison: Oral solid preload with cognitive manipulation to perceive as gastric solid (oral solid/perceived gastric solid) - all preloads designed to present a liquid gastric challenge, energy- and macronutrient-matched; 4-arm crossover design comparing all conditions
outcomes_primary: Appetite (hunger and fullness sensations), gastric-emptying time, orocecal transit time, endocrine responses (insulin, glucagon-like peptide 1, ghrelin), total energy intake
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract. This is a mechanistic crossover study examining cognitive and sensory contributions to postingestive responses rather than a traditional therapeutic trial. Sample size: 52 participants.

title: Addition of liraglutide in patients with Type 2 diabetes well controlled on metformin monotherapy improves several markers of vascular function.
journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association
population: Patients with Type 2 diabetes, age 30-65 years, pretreated with metformin on a stable dosage, HbA1c < 53 mmol/mol (7.0%)
intervention: Addition of liraglutide to metformin monotherapy, 1.2 mg for 6 weeks then 1.8 mg for 12 weeks
comparison: Continued metformin monotherapy alone
outcomes_primary: Laboratory markers characterizing vascular and endothelial function (asymmetric dimethylarginine, E-selectin, plasminogen activator inhibitor 1, intact proinsulin, high-sensitivity C-reactive protein, monocyte chemotactic protein 1, vascular cell adhesion molecule), retinal microvascular endothelial function (microvascular response to flicker light), arterial stiffness
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in the abstract; all outcomes listed as primary. HbA1c also measured but appears to be a glycemic control measure rather than a primary vascular outcome.

title: Impaired incretin-induced amplification of insulin secretion after glucose homeostatic dysregulation in healthy subjects.
journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
population: Healthy Caucasian males without risk factors for type 2 diabetes

comparison: Pre-intervention (before 12-day dysregulation period) vs post-intervention; within each period: hyperglycemic clamps with infusion of GIP vs GLP-1 vs saline (placebo) at physiological doses
outcomes_primary: Insulinotropic effect of GIP and GLP-1 compared with placebo measured using hyperglycemic clamps
outcomes_secondary: Insulin resistance assessed by homeostatic model assessment (HOMA); glucose tolerance assessed by area under curve for plasma glucose during 75-g oral glucose tolerance test
extraction_notes: Study design is a before-after intervention study in healthy subjects rather than a traditional RCT. Sample size is small (n=10). The incretin hormone infusions (GIP, GLP-1, saline) appear to be administered within-subject but timing/crossover details not fully specified in abstract.

title: Investigation of the haemodynamic effects of exenatide in healthy male subjects.
population: Healthy male volunteers
intervention: Single 10 µg subcutaneous injection of exenatide
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Haemodynamic measurements including heart rate, cardiac output, total peripheral resistance, blood pressure (measured using Finometer, venous occlusion plethysmography and Doppler ultrasound)
outcomes_secondary: Urine sodium:creatinine excretion ratio
extraction_notes: Study design is double-blind, randomized, crossover. Measurement period was 2 hours after dosing. Primary vs secondary outcome distinction not explicitly stated in abstract; categorization based on emphasis in methods description.

title: Effects of JNJ-38431055, a novel GPR119 receptor agonist, in randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled studies in subjects with type 2 diabetes.
population: Male and female subjects aged 25-60 years with type 2 diabetes mellitus diagnosed 6 months to 10 years before screening, mean body mass index between 22 and 39.9 kg/m2
intervention: JNJ-38431055 100 mg single dose, JNJ-38431055 500 mg single dose, or JNJ-38431055 500 mg once daily for 14 consecutive days
comparison: Placebo; sitagliptin 100 mg single dose (positive control, single-dose study only)
outcomes_primary: Stimulated plasma glucose, insulin, C-peptide and incretin concentrations
extraction_notes: Two separate experiments involving 25 and 32 subjects respectively. Primary/secondary outcome distinction not explicitly specified; all listed outcomes described as pre-specified. Pharmacokinetics, safety and tolerability also assessed but not clearly designated as primary or secondary outcomes.

title: Pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, and tolerability of a generic formulation of exenatide: a randomized, open-label, single- and multiple-dose study in healthy Chinese volunteers.
population: Healthy Chinese volunteers, 24 subjects
intervention: Exenatide (generic formulation) 5 μg or 10 μg subcutaneous injection; single dose followed by twice daily dosing on days 2-4 and once on day 5
comparison: 5 μg versus 10 μg dose groups (dose-escalating design); no placebo or active comparator
outcomes_primary: Pharmacokinetic parameters (Cmax, AUC0-t, AUC0-∞, tmax, t1/2)
outcomes_secondary: Pharmacodynamics (serum glucose concentrations); tolerability assessed by physical examination, vital signs, laboratory analysis, and subject interview; effect of gender on pharmacokinetics
extraction_notes: Open-label study design; randomization method not specified; primary vs secondary outcome distinction not explicitly stated in abstract

title: Anorexigenic effects of miglitol in concert with the alterations of gut hormone secretion and gastric emptying in healthy subjects.
journal: Hormone and metabolic research = Hormon- und Stoffwechselforschung = Hormones et metabolisme
population: Healthy volunteers
intervention: Miglitol 50 mg administered before test meal; separate cohort received miglitol 50 mg three times daily for 1 week
comparison: No miglitol (control condition in crossover design)
outcomes_primary: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) levels, peptide YY (PYY) levels, ghrelin levels, appetite scores using visual analogue scales (VAS)
outcomes_secondary: Gastric emptying rate (GER) measured using breath 13CO2 appearance
extraction_notes: Sample size was 20 subjects total, with subgroups of 10 for GER measurement and 12 for one-week administration. Randomized open-label crossover design. Primary vs secondary outcome distinction not explicitly stated in abstract.

title: The effect of exenatide and erythromycin on postprandial symptoms and their relation to gastric functions.
population: Healthy volunteers
intervention: Exenatide (dose, route, frequency, and duration not specified)
comparison: Placebo; Erythromycin
outcomes_primary: Postprandial symptoms; Gastric volumes (fasting and postprandial) measured by 3-dimensional single photon emission computed tomography
outcomes_secondary: Electrogastrography (EGG) rhythm; Ratio of postprandial over fasting gastric volume
extraction_notes: Three-way cross-over design with 1-week intervals between treatments. Doses, routes, and frequencies for exenatide and erythromycin not specified in abstract. Sample size is 10 subjects. Primary versus secondary outcome designation not explicitly stated.

title: Metabolic and hormonal changes after laparoscopic Roux-en-Y gastric bypass and sleeve gastrectomy: a randomized, prospective trial.
population: Non-diabetic morbidly obese patients undergoing bariatric surgery; subgroup of Swiss Multicenter Bypass or Sleeve Study (SM-BOSS)
intervention: Laparoscopic Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (LRYGB) with small gastric pouch, 25-mm circular pouch-jejunostomy to 150-cm antecolic Roux limb, and 50-cm biliopancreatic limb exclusion
comparison: Laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy (LSG) performed along a 35-F bougie from angle of His to approximately 3-4 cm orally to pylorus
outcomes_primary: Not explicitly specified as primary; metabolic and hormonal changes including glucose homeostasis (HOMA index, fasting glucose, fasting insulin) and gut hormone profiles (cholecystokinin, ghrelin, GLP-1, PYY)
outcomes_secondary: Weight loss, BMI reduction, excessive BMI loss (EBMIL)
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in the text. Study is a subgroup analysis of the ongoing SM-BOSS trial (NCT00356213). Follow-up assessments at 1 week, 3 months, and 12 months after surgery.

title: Safety and efficacy of once-weekly exenatide compared with insulin glargine titrated to target in patients with type 2 diabetes over 84 weeks.
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes failing to maintain sufficient glycemic control using metformin alone or in combination with sulfonylurea
intervention: Exenatide once weekly (EQW) 2 mg subcutaneous injection added to existing oral blood glucose-lowering regimen
comparison: Insulin glargine (IG) once daily, starting at 10 IU/day and titrated to target fasting glucose 4.0-5.5 mmol/L using the INITIATE dosing algorithm, added to existing oral blood glucose-lowering regimen
outcomes_primary: Change in A1C from baseline to study treatment end point
outcomes_secondary: Time to failure to maintain glycemic control (defined as time from randomization to first visit after week 18 when A1C was ≥7.0%); proportions of patients achieving A1C <7.0% and ≤6.5%; change in body weight; fasting serum glucose; self-monitored blood glucose; fasting serum lipids; urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio; high-sensitivity C-reactive protein; homeostasis model assessment of β-cell function; waist and hip circumference; adverse events; hypoglycemia incidence
extraction_notes: This is an 84-week extension study of a previously reported 26-week phase 3 trial. Open-label design. Data collected after treatment regimen changes at 48 weeks or after were excluded from analyses.

title: A randomized non-inferiority study comparing the addition of exenatide twice daily to sitagliptin or switching from sitagliptin to exenatide twice daily in patients with type 2 diabetes experiencing inadequate glycaemic control on metformin and sitagliptin.
journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association

intervention: Exenatide twice daily plus placebo and metformin (SWITCH group) - switching from sitagliptin to exenatide
comparison: Exenatide twice daily plus sitagliptin and metformin (ADD group) - adding exenatide to existing sitagliptin therapy
outcomes_primary: Change in HbA1c from baseline to week 20, assessed for non-inferiority with 0.4% margin
outcomes_secondary: Proportion of patients reaching HbA1c target <7.0% (<53 mmol/mol); fasting serum glucose; daily mean postprandial self-monitored blood glucose; incidence of nausea and vomiting
extraction_notes: Study duration was 20 weeks. Exenatide dose not explicitly specified. Both groups continued metformin throughout. Non-inferiority design with SWITCH as the intervention being tested against ADD as the reference.

title: Effects of diet soda on gut hormones in youths with diabetes.
population: Youths aged 12-25 years with type 1 diabetes (n=9), type 2 diabetes (n=10), or healthy controls (n=25). Type 2 diabetes subjects were all overweight or obese (BMI >85th centile for age, or >25 kg/m2 after age 20 years) and lacked classic family history suggestive of monogenic diabetes.
intervention: 240 mL cola-flavored caffeine-free diet soda (Diet Rite Cola containing sucralose and acesulfame-K) consumed 10 minutes before a 75-g oral glucose load

outcomes_primary: GLP-1 area under the curve (AUC) measured over 180 minutes
outcomes_secondary: Glucose AUC, C-peptide AUC, glucose-dependent insulinotropic peptide (GIP) AUC, peptide Tyr-Tyr (PYY) AUC measured over 180 minutes
extraction_notes: Primary outcome not explicitly designated; GLP-1 appears to be the main focus based on study objectives. This is a cross-over study so all participants received both interventions. Some GLP-1 data from 22 of 25 healthy subjects previously reported in another publication.

title: Metabolic effects of short-term GLP-1 treatment in insulin resistant heart failure patients.
journal: Experimental and clinical endocrinology & diabetes : official journal, German Society of Endocrinology [and] German Diabetes Association
population: Non-diabetic heart failure patients with ischemic heart disease (IHD) and insulin resistance
intervention: 48-hour GLP-1 infusion
comparison: 48-hour placebo infusion
extraction_notes: Cross-over study design. Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract. Outcomes measured included: plasma glucose levels, glucose tolerance (OGTT), whole body protein turnover, muscle wasting, circulating levels of insulin, glucagon, free fatty acids, and insulin sensitivity. Methods used included hyperinsulinemic clamp, indirect calorimetry, forearm methods, and tracer methods.

title: Effect of exenatide on the pharmacokinetics of a combination oral contraceptive in healthy women: an open-label, randomised, crossover trial.
population: Healthy pre-menopausal females, 18 to 45 years old, BMI 19 to 35 kg/m2, taking an oral contraceptive prior to study entry, no diabetes mellitus, no implanted contraceptives for 6 months or injectable contraceptives for 12 months prior to study
intervention: Exenatide administered subcutaneously 15 minutes prior to morning and evening meals at 5 μg BID on Days 1 through 4, increased to 10 μg BID on Days 5 through 22, with combination oral contraceptive (ethinyl estradiol 30 μg, levonorgestrel 150 μg) administered either 1 hour before exenatide or 30 minutes after exenatide
comparison: Oral contraceptive alone (ethinyl estradiol 30 μg, levonorgestrel 150 μg)
outcomes_primary: Multiple-dose pharmacokinetics of ethinyl estradiol and levonorgestrel when administered 1 hour before and 30 minutes after exenatide dose, including AUC0-τ,ss and Cmax,ss on Day 22
outcomes_secondary: Single-dose pharmacokinetics (AUC0-∞ and Cmax on Day 8), Tmax, trough concentrations at 24 hours post-dose following single and multiple doses, safety assessments including adverse events, physical examination, vital signs, body weight, clinical laboratory tests, and 12-lead electrocardiogram
extraction_notes: Open-label, 3-period, 3-sequence, randomised crossover design. Primary objective explicitly stated as multiple-dose PK evaluation; single-dose PK appears secondary but both were pre-specified statistical analyses.

title: Efficacy and safety of the once-daily GLP-1 receptor agonist lixisenatide in monotherapy: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in patients with type 2 diabetes (GetGoal-Mono).
population: Male and female patients aged 20–85 years with type 2 diabetes mellitus not currently receiving glucose-lowering therapy, with HbA1c ≥7.0% and ≤10.0%. intervention: Lixisenatide subcutaneous injection once daily within 1 hour before breakfast for 12 weeks, administered as either: (1) 2-step dose increase regimen: 10 μg for 1 week, 15 μg for 1 week, then 20 μg maintenance dose; or (2) 1-step dose increase regimen: 10 μg for 2 weeks, then 20 μg maintenance dose.

title: Exenatide twice daily versus glimepiride for prevention of glycaemic deterioration in patients with type 2 diabetes with metformin failure (EUREXA): an open-label, randomised controlled trial.

title: Exenatide at therapeutic and supratherapeutic concentrations does not prolong the QTc interval in healthy subjects.

title: A randomized, open-label, multicenter, 4-week study to evaluate the tolerability and pharmacokinetics of ITCA 650 in patients with type 2 diabetes.

outcomes_primary: Not explicitly specified as primary; tolerability, pharmacodynamics, and pharmacokinetics of ITCA 650
outcomes_secondary: Not explicitly specified; measured outcomes included fasting plasma glucose, 2-hour postprandial glucose, glucose AUC, HbA1c, insulin, weight, exenatide plasma levels, anti-exenatide antibodies, adverse events
extraction_notes: Open-label study with no placebo or active comparator; primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract; this appears to be a phase 1/2 dose-finding study focused on tolerability and pharmacokinetics

title: Mechanisms of glucose lowering of dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitor sitagliptin when used alone or with metformin in type 2 diabetes: a double-tracer study.
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus, age 47 ± 3 years, BMI 33.5 ± 2.0 kg/m², HbA1c 8.8 ± 1.2%, fasting plasma glucose 165 ± 12 mg/dL, diabetes duration 1.5 ± 0.5 years, controlled by diet or stable dose of sulfonylurea or metformin for ≥6 months, in good health as determined by medical history, physical exam, routine laboratory analysis, and electrocardiogram

outcomes_secondary: Fasting plasma glucose, mean post-meal tolerance test plasma glucose, fasting and post-meal plasma insulin, C-peptide, insulin secretory rate (ISR), fasting and post-meal plasma glucagon, bioactive GLP-1 concentration, bioactive GIP concentration, splanchnic glucose uptake, indices of insulin secretion (ΔI/ΔG, ΔISR/ΔG), β-cell function indices, Matsuda index of insulin sensitivity, hepatic insulin sensitivity

title: Quality of life in patients with short bowel syndrome treated with the new glucagon-like peptide-2 analogue teduglutide--analyses from a randomised, placebo-controlled study.

comparison: Placebo

title: Independent and combined effects of eating rate and energy density on energy intake, appetite, and gut hormones.

comparison: Four conditions compared in crossover design: FR-HED, FR-LED, SR-HED, SR-LED

title: Efficacy and safety over 26 weeks of an oral treatment strategy including sitagliptin compared with an injectable treatment strategy with liraglutide in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus inadequately controlled on metformin: a randomised clinical trial.
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus aged 18-79 years, on stable metformin monotherapy ≥1,500 mg/day for ≥12 weeks, with HbA1c ≥7.0% (53 mmol/mol) and ≤11.0% (97 mmol/mol), fasting fingerstick glucose <15 mmol/l (<270 mg/dl) at randomisation, capable of using Victoza pen injection device, women agreed to remain abstinent or use acceptable birth control

outcomes_primary: HbA1c change from baseline at week 26 (non-inferiority assessment with margin of 0.4%)
outcomes_secondary: Hypoglycaemia, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, abdominal pain, overall tolerability
extraction_notes: Open-label study; secondary outcomes inferred from safety reporting - not explicitly designated as secondary outcomes in abstract; all patients continued background metformin therapy

title: Effect of vildagliptin on glucose and insulin concentrations during a 24-hour period in type 2 diabetes patients with different ranges of baseline hemoglobin A1c levels.
population: Drug-naive adult volunteers with type 2 diabetes and overweight or obesity, fasting glucose values between 7.2 and 13.3 mmol/L, stratified by baseline HbA1c: Group A (HbA1c 7.0-8.4%) and Group B (HbA1c 8.5-10.0%)

title: Efficacy and safety of lixisenatide once daily versus placebo in type 2 diabetes insufficiently controlled on pioglitazone (GetGoal-P).
population: Adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus insufficiently controlled on pioglitazone with or without metformin

comparison: Placebo

outcomes_secondary: Proportion of patients achieving HbA1c <7%; fasting plasma glucose; body weight; treatment-emergent adverse events; serious treatment-emergent adverse events; symptomatic hypoglycaemia
extraction_notes: Study design included 24-week main treatment period and ≥52-week variable extension period. Randomization ratio was 2:1 (lixisenatide:placebo). Specific inclusion criteria thresholds for 'insufficiently controlled' not defined in abstract.

title: Adding once-daily lixisenatide for type 2 diabetes inadequately controlled by established basal insulin: a 24-week, randomized, placebo-controlled comparison (GetGoal-L).
population: Adults with type 2 diabetes diagnosed ≥1 year, using basal insulin regimen for ≥3 months with stable dose (±20%) ≥30 units/day for ≥2 months before screening, HbA1c 7-10%, with or without metformin (stable dose ≥1.5 g/day for ≥3 months if used). intervention: Lixisenatide 20 μg subcutaneously once daily within 1 hour before morning meal for 24 weeks, with two-step dose-increase regimen (10 μg for 1 week, 15 μg for 1 week, then 20 μg if tolerated), added to established basal insulin therapy with or without metformin
comparison: Matching placebo subcutaneously once daily within 1 hour before morning meal for 24 weeks, added to established basal insulin therapy with or without metformin
outcomes_primary: Change in HbA1c from randomization to week 24
outcomes_secondary: Percentage of patients attaining HbA1c <7.0% or ≤6.5%; change from baseline in FPG, body weight, seven-point self-measurement of plasma-referenced glucose (SMPG), 2-hour postprandial glucose (PPG) after standardized meal, glucose excursion; daily basal insulin dosage; percentage of participants requiring rescue therapy; safety (adverse events, symptomatic hypoglycemia, clinical laboratory data)
extraction_notes: Randomization was 2:1 (lixisenatide:placebo). Basal insulin dosage was to remain relatively stable (±20%) throughout the study except for reductions in response to hypoglycemia or initial 20% reduction if HbA1c ≤7.5% at screening.

title: Randomized trial of continuous subcutaneous delivery of exenatide by ITCA 650 versus twice-daily exenatide injections in metformin-treated type 2 diabetes.
population: Men and women aged 18–70 years with type 2 diabetes mellitus diagnosed ≥6 months, on stable dose of metformin for ≥3 months, HbA1c ≥7% and ≤10%, fasting plasma glucose <240 mg/dL, BMI ≤40 kg/m2, stable body weight for 3 months prior to study entry. Excluded: previous treatment with exenatide, thiazolidinediones, sulfonylureas, dipeptidyl peptidase-IV inhibitors, or acarbose; insulin within 3 months of screening; type 1 diabetes; overt diabetes complications; fasting triglyceride level >500 mg/dL
intervention: ITCA 650 (continuous subcutaneous miniature osmotic pump delivery system of exenatide). Stage I: 20 or 40 μg/day for 12 weeks. Stage II: rerandomized to 20, 40, 60, or 80 μg/day for additional 12 weeks (20→20, 20→60, 40→40, or 40→80 μg/day regimens)
comparison: Twice-daily exenatide injections (Ex-BID): 5 μg twice daily for 4 weeks titrated to 10 μg twice daily for 8 weeks during Stage I. In Stage II, Ex-BID subjects were switched to ITCA 650 40 μg/day or 60 μg/day
outcomes_primary: Change from baseline in HbA1c at week 12 (end of Stage I) and week 24 (end of Stage II)
outcomes_secondary: Change from baseline in fasting plasma glucose; change from baseline in body weight; proportion of subjects achieving HbA1c ≤7%; safety assessments including adverse events, clinical laboratory measurements, electrocardiograms, vital signs, physical examinations, and anti-exenatide antibodies
extraction_notes: Open-label study design. Stage II had no true control arm as Ex-BID subjects were switched to ITCA 650. Primary endpoint explicitly stated in statistical analysis section.

title: Thirty days of resveratrol supplementation does not affect postprandial incretin hormone responses, but suppresses postprandial glucagon in obese subjects.

population: Obese men (BMI 32 ± 1 kg/m²), age 52 ± 2 years, fasting plasma glucose 5.5 ± 0.1 mmol/l
intervention: Resveratrol (Resvida®) 150 mg/day oral dietary supplement for 30 days
comparison: Placebo for 30 days
outcomes_primary: Postprandial plasma responses of incretin hormones (glucagon-like peptide-1 and glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide) and glucagon, measured as fasting plasma concentrations and area under curve values following a standardized meal test
extraction_notes: Randomized, double-blind, crossover design with 4-week washout period. Sample size is 10 subjects. Primary vs secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract.

title: Effects of lixisenatide once daily on gastric emptying in type 2 diabetes--relationship to postprandial glycemia.
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) receiving ≤2 oral antidiabetic drugs

outcomes_primary: Postprandial glucose (PPG) after three standardized meals (breakfast, lunch, and dinner); gastric emptying of standardized breakfast measured by 13C-octanoic acid breath test (50% emptying time)
outcomes_secondary: Relationship between postprandial glucose area under the curve after breakfast and gastric emptying
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in the abstract; outcomes listed based on stated objectives

title: High protein intake stimulates postprandial GLP1 and PYY release.
population: Healthy volunteers, weight stable, no medication use, no medical illnesses or food allergies, BMI range 19.8-27.5 kg/m²
intervention: High protein breakfast providing 60% energy from protein, 20% from fat, 20% from carbohydrate, calculated to provide 20% of daily energy requirements
comparison: High carbohydrate breakfast (60% carbohydrate, 20% protein, 20% fat) and high fat breakfast (60% fat, 20% carbohydrate, 20% protein), all isocaloric and isovolaemic
outcomes_primary: Postprandial gut hormone response (total ghrelin, PYY, GLP-1 levels) measured half-hourly for 4 hours; energy intake at subsequent ad libitum meal
outcomes_secondary: Hunger and fullness scores assessed by visual analogue scales; plasma glucose and insulin concentrations
extraction_notes: Randomized three-way crossover design with 8 participants. Study occasions separated by at least 1 week. Primary outcomes not explicitly designated as primary vs secondary in abstract.

title: Liraglutide suppresses postprandial triglyceride and apolipoprotein B48 elevations after a fat-rich meal in patients with type 2 diabetes: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, cross-over trial.
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus, aged 18-75 years, BMI 18.5-40 kg/m², n=20

comparison: Placebo (once-daily subcutaneous injection) for 3 weeks
outcomes_primary: Postprandial triglyceride AUC(0-8h) after a standardized fat-rich meal
outcomes_secondary: Apolipoprotein B48 AUC(0-8h), non-esterified fatty acids, glycaemic responses (glucose, glucagon AUC(0-8h) and Cmax), gastric emptying rate assessed by paracetamol absorption (liquid phase) and 13C-octanoate breath test (solid phase), low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, total cholesterol
extraction_notes: Cross-over trial design. Liraglutide dose was escalated weekly from 0.6 to 1.8 mg.

title: Calcium co-ingestion augments postprandial glucose-dependent insulinotropic peptide(1-42), glucagon-like peptide-1 and insulin concentrations in humans.
population: Healthy males
intervention: High-calcium meal: 15 mg/kg body mass calcium content
comparison: Control meal: 3 mg/kg body mass calcium content (energy- and macronutrient-matched)
outcomes_primary: Circulating concentrations of GIP(1-42), GLP-1 and insulin over 180-min postprandial period
outcomes_secondary: Subjective appetite sensations assessed by visual analogue scales; rates of energy expenditure and substrate (lipid and carbohydrate) oxidation estimated using indirect calorimetry
extraction_notes: Sample size is 10 participants. Double-blind, randomized, crossover design. Primary outcomes not explicitly distinguished from secondary outcomes in abstract.

title: Rationale and design of the glycemia reduction approaches in diabetes: a comparative effectiveness study (GRADE).
population: Adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus, age ≥30 years at time of diagnosis, diabetes duration <5 years, treated with metformin (1,000-2,000 mg/day), baseline hemoglobin A1C 6.8-8.5% (51-69 mmol/mol), no other glucose-lowering medications

comparison: Four-arm parallel comparison: glimepiride vs sitagliptin vs liraglutide vs insulin glargine, all added to metformin background therapy
outcomes_primary: Time to primary metabolic failure defined as A1C ≥7% (53 mmol/mol), subsequently confirmed at the next quarterly visit, while being treated at maximum tolerable doses of both metformin and the assigned medication
outcomes_secondary: Time to secondary metabolic failure (confirmed A1C >7.5% requiring addition of basal insulin); time to tertiary metabolic failure (confirmed A1C >7.5% requiring intensive basal/bolus insulin therapy); cumulative incidence of microalbuminuria; cardiovascular disease risk factors; major cardiovascular events; adverse effects; tolerability; quality of life; cost-effectiveness; hypoglycemia; weight change; measures of insulin secretion and sensitivity; peripheral neuropathy; estimated glomerular filtration rate; mortality; hospital admissions; cognitive function; cancer
extraction_notes: This is a protocol/design paper describing a planned randomized controlled trial. The study is unmasked (open-label) for practical reasons. Target enrollment is 5,000 subjects across 37 U.S. centers with anticipated mean follow-up of 4.8 years (range 4-7 years).

title: Efficacy and safety of lixisenatide once daily versus exenatide twice daily in type 2 diabetes inadequately controlled on metformin: a 24-week, randomized, open-label, active-controlled study (GetGoal-X).
population: Adults aged 21-84 years with type 2 diabetes inadequately controlled on metformin (≥1.5 g/day) with HbA1c 7-10%. Exclusion criteria: use of oral or injectable glucose-lowering agents other than metformin within 3 months before screening; FPG at screening >13.9 mmol/L (250 mg/dL); history of unexplained pancreatitis, chronic pancreatitis, pancreatectomy, stomach/gastric surgery, or inflammatory bowel disease; history of metabolic acidosis including diabetic ketoacidosis within 1 year before screening; history within previous 6 months of myocardial infarction, stroke, or heart failure requiring hospitalization; clinically relevant history of gastrointestinal disease with prolonged nausea and vomiting during previous 6 months.
intervention: Lixisenatide subcutaneous injection once daily (within 1 hour before morning meal), titrated from 10 μg once daily for 1 week, then 15 μg once daily for 1 week, then 20 μg once daily maintenance dose, for 24 weeks
comparison: Exenatide subcutaneous injection twice daily (before morning and evening meals), titrated from 5 μg twice daily for 4 weeks, then 10 μg twice daily maintenance dose, for 24 weeks
outcomes_primary: Absolute change in HbA1c from baseline to week 24, with noninferiority assessment (predefined noninferiority margin of 0.4% for upper limit of 95% CI)
outcomes_secondary: Percentage of participants attaining HbA1c <7.0% or ≤6.5% at week 24; change in fasting plasma glucose from baseline to week 24; change in body weight from baseline to week 24. Safety outcomes: treatment-emergent adverse events, symptomatic hypoglycemia (defined as symptoms consistent with hypoglycemia with blood glucose <3.3 mmol/L or prompt recovery with carbohydrate/glucagon/IV glucose), severe hypoglycemia (requiring assistance of another person with plasma glucose <2.0 mmol/L or prompt recovery with IV glucose/glucagon/oral carbohydrate administered by third party), gastrointestinal tolerability assessed by Patient Assessment of Upper Gastrointestinal Disorders–Quality of Life (PAGI-QOL) questionnaire
extraction_notes: Open-label study design. Participants stratified by screening HbA1c (<8%, ≥8%) and BMI (<30 kg/m², ≥30 kg/m²). No predefined formal statistical tests were performed for secondary efficacy endpoints.

title: Characterisation of oral and i.v. glucose handling in truncally vagotomised subjects with pyloroplasty.
population: Adults with truncal vagotomy and pyloroplasty (n=16, including 7 with prior surgery for uncomplicated duodenal ulcer and 9 with prior cardia resection for oesophageal cancer) and matched healthy controls without family history of diabetes (n=10). Inclusion criteria: informed consent, normal haemoglobin. Exclusion criteria: BMI above 30 kg/m2, diabetes, inflammatory bowel disease, gut resection (except appendectomy), kidney or liver disease, medication that could not be paused for 12 hours.
intervention: 50g oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT) with DPP4 inhibition using vildagliptin 50mg orally administered 12 hours and 1 hour before the OGTT
comparison: 50g oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT) without DPP4 inhibition; isoglycaemic intravenous glucose infusion (IIGI) copying the plasma glucose profile from the OGTT without DPP4 inhibition; comparison between vagotomised subjects and matched healthy controls
outcomes_primary: Gastrointestinal-mediated glucose disposal (GIGD); incretin effect calculated from beta cell secretory responses to oral and isoglycaemic intravenous glucose
outcomes_secondary: Plasma glucose concentrations; intact and total GLP1 concentrations; intact GIP concentrations; insulin secretion; C-peptide concentrations; insulin secretion rates (ISR); glucagon concentrations; beta cell glucose sensitivity; insulinogenic index; disposition index; gastric emptying (assessed by plasma paracetamol); pancreatic polypeptide response to sham-feeding
extraction_notes: This is a mechanistic physiological study in vagotomised subjects rather than a traditional therapeutic RCT. The study uses a crossover design where each participant underwent 4 experimental days. No formal sample size calculation or primary outcome designation provided in the text.

title: Effect of laparoscopic Roux-en-Y gastric bypass surgery on type 2 diabetes mellitus with hypertension: a randomized controlled trial.
population: Obese adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and hypertension
intervention: Laparoscopic Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (RYGB) surgery
comparison: Usual care alone (group A); Usual care plus Exenatide therapy (group B)
outcomes_primary: Diabetes remission; requirement of antihypertensive drugs
outcomes_secondary: Body mass index; hemoglobin A1c; homeostasis model assessment of insulin resistance; lipids; high sensitivity C-reactive protein; tumor necrosis factor-α; high molecular weight adiponectin; left ventricular mass index; cardiac structure and function
extraction_notes: Primary vs secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract; classification based on emphasis in results presentation. Exenatide dose, route, frequency not specified. Duration of follow-up is 12 months.

title: Effects of short-term sitagliptin treatment on immune parameters in healthy individuals, a randomized placebo-controlled study.
population: Healthy volunteers
intervention: Sitagliptin daily for 28 days
comparison: Placebo daily for 28 days
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract. Outcomes measured included: percentage of leucocyte subsets within peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs), plasma chemokine/cytokine levels, cytokines released by stimulation of PBMCs with lipopolysaccharide (LPS) or anti-CD3, and percentage of cells expressing CD26. Abstract does not specify which were designated as primary versus secondary.

title: Exenatide and the treatment of patients with Parkinson's disease.
population: Patients with moderate Parkinson's disease
intervention: Subcutaneous exenatide injection for 12 months
comparison: Control group (no exenatide treatment)
outcomes_primary: Movement Disorders Society Unified Parkinson's Disease Rating Scale (MDS-UPDRS) assessed after overnight withdrawal of conventional PD medication using blinded video assessment at baseline, 6 months, 12 months, and after 2-month washout period (14 months)
outcomes_secondary: Several nonmotor tests including cognitive measures
extraction_notes: Single-blind trial design with blinded video assessment. Specific nonmotor tests not named in abstract. Secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished from primary outcomes.

title: Hyperglycemia associated with pasireotide: results from a mechanistic study in healthy volunteers.
journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
population: Healthy male volunteers
intervention: Pasireotide 600 μg subcutaneously twice a day for 7 days; Pasireotide 900 μg subcutaneously twice a day for 7 days; Pasireotide 1200 μg subcutaneously twice a day for 7 days (discontinued due to gastrointestinal adverse events)

outcomes_primary: Effect of pasireotide on insulin secretion; effect on hepatic insulin sensitivity; effect on peripheral insulin sensitivity
outcomes_secondary: Effects of pasireotide on oral glucose absorption
extraction_notes: This is a mechanistic study in healthy volunteers, not a disease population. The 1200 μg arm was discontinued during the study. Study design is open-label without placebo control - comparisons are within-subject (baseline vs treatment end) and between dose groups.

title: Variation in inflammatory markers and glycemic parameters after 12 months of exenatide plus metformin treatment compared with metformin alone: a randomized placebo-controlled trial.
population: White treatment-naive adults with type 2 diabetes and glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) level higher than 7.5%
intervention: Exenatide 5 μg twice daily for the first 4 weeks, then 10 μg twice daily thereafter, plus metformin, for 12 months (following an open-label run-in period of 8 ± 2 months with metformin)

outcomes_secondary: Body mass index, HbA1c, fasting plasma glucose, postprandial plasma glucose, fasting plasma insulin (FPI), homeostasis model assessment insulin resistance index (HOMA-IR), homeostasis model assessment β-cell function index (HOMA-β), fasting plasma proinsulin (FPPr), proinsulin-to-fasting plasma insulin ratio (Pr:FPI ratio), C-peptide, glucagon, vaspin, chemerin, resistin, insulin sensitivity and insulin secretion assessed by combined euglycemic hyperinsulinemic and hyperglycemic clamp with subsequent arginine stimulation
extraction_notes: Primary versus secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract; all outcomes listed under secondary. Run-in period with metformin preceded randomization.

title: One-year sustained glycemic control and weight reduction in type 2 diabetes after addition of liraglutide to metformin followed by insulin detemir according to HbA1c target.
journal: Journal of diabetes and its complications

intervention: Add-on insulin detemir to metformin plus liraglutide 1.8mg for 52 weeks (open-label)
comparison: Continuation of metformin plus liraglutide 1.8mg without detemir for 52 weeks; observational group of patients with HbA1c <7.0% after run-in continuing unchanged treatment for 52 weeks
outcomes_primary: HbA1c change over 52 weeks
outcomes_secondary: Proportion achieving HbA1c <7.0% at 52 weeks; weight change; major hypoglycemia; minor hypoglycemia rate
extraction_notes: Primary outcome not explicitly labeled as such; outcomes inferred from results presentation. Sulfonylurea was discontinued during run-in phase. Randomization was 1:1.

title: Efficacy, safety, and tolerability of exenatide once weekly in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus: an integrated analysis of the DURATION trials.
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus
intervention: Exenatide once weekly (EQW), an extended-release formulation, administered for 24 to 30 weeks
comparison: Comparator-controlled (specific comparators from individual DURATION trials pooled in this analysis not specified in abstract)
outcomes_primary: Not explicitly specified as primary in abstract
outcomes_secondary: Not explicitly specified as secondary in abstract; outcomes assessed include: change from baseline in HbA1c levels, fasting blood glucose levels, body weight, blood pressure (systolic and diastolic), fasting lipid levels (total cholesterol, LDL cholesterol, triglycerides), safety and tolerability (treatment-emergent adverse events including gastrointestinal and injection-site events, hypoglycemic events)
extraction_notes: This is a post hoc pooled analysis of 6 DURATION trials; the abstract does not distinguish primary from secondary outcomes; specific comparators from individual trials are not detailed in the pooled analysis abstract; ITT population n=1379, completer population n=1195

title: Efficacy and tolerability of exenatide once weekly versus sitagliptin in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus: a retrospective analysis of pooled clinical trial data.
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus on background therapies of diet and exercise and/or metformin
intervention: Exenatide once weekly (EQW) for 26 weeks
comparison: Sitagliptin (sita) for 26 weeks
outcomes_primary: HbA1c change from baseline, fasting blood glucose (FBG) change from baseline
outcomes_secondary: Achievement of goal HbA1c levels, body weight change, cholesterol levels, cardiovascular risk factors, adverse events (nausea, diarrhea), incidence of minor hypoglycemic events
extraction_notes: This is a post hoc retrospective analysis of pooled data from 2 randomized, double-blind, comparator-controlled clinical trials. Primary vs secondary outcome distinction not explicitly stated in abstract.

title: A new endoscopically implantable device (SatiSphere) for treatment of obesity--efficacy, safety, and metabolic effects on glucose, insulin, and GLP-1 levels.

intervention: SatiSphere endoluminal mechanical device - endoscopically implantable nitinol wire with pigtail ends and mesh spheres, placed in duodenum and gastric antrum, with scheduled device removal after 3 months

outcomes_primary: Body weight loss; excess weight loss
outcomes_secondary: Safety (device migration, adverse events); glucose levels following mixed-meal test; insulin levels following mixed-meal test; glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1) levels following mixed-meal test
extraction_notes: Trial was terminated early due to device migration issues. Metabolic outcomes (glucose, insulin, GLP-1) measured in a subgroup only (n=7). Randomization ratio was 2:1 (device:control). Specific inclusion/exclusion criteria not stated in abstract.

title: Pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic interaction of vildagliptin and voglibose in Japanese patients with Type 2 diabetes.

intervention: 50 mg vildagliptin twice daily co-administered with 0.2 mg voglibose three times daily for 3 days

outcomes_primary: Pharmacokinetic interaction: plasma vildagliptin exposure (AUCτ,ss and Cmax,ss); Pharmacodynamic interaction: DPP-4 inhibition, active GLP-1 plasma concentration, plasma glucose levels
extraction_notes: Open-label, randomized, 3-treatment, 3-period, 6-way crossover design. Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract. Tolerability mentioned but not specified as formal outcome.

title: Effects of chenodeoxycholic acid on the secretion of gut peptides and fibroblast growth factors in healthy humans.

intervention: Intraduodenal infusions (2.0 mL/min for 180 minutes) of chenodeoxycholic acid (CDCA) at 5 mmol/L or 15 mmol/L, either alone or with sodium oleate (fatty acid)

title: Impact of early versus late enteral nutrition on cell mediated immunity and its relationship with glucagon like peptide-1 in intensive care unit patients: a prospective study.
population: Patients aged 40-70 years admitted to neurology ICU with acute thromboembolic cerebrovascular event within first 24 hours of symptom onset, with NIH stroke scores between 12 and 16. intervention: Early enteral feeding within first 24 hours of admission via nasogastric tube using commercially available enteral nutrition liquid (JEVITY), starting at 10 ml/h for first 6 hours, then 20 ml/h for following 12 hours, then 30 ml/h thereafter. title: Exercise training during normobaric hypoxic confinement does not alter hormonal appetite regulation.

outcomes_secondary: Hypoglycemia episodes (plasma glucose ≤3.9 mmol/L)

title: Impact of sitagliptin on carotid intima-media thickness in patients with coronary artery disease and impaired glucose tolerance or mild diabetes mellitus.

intervention: Exenatide 5 μg subcutaneous twice daily increased to 10 μg twice daily after 1 month for 6 months; or Sitagliptin 100 mg orally each morning for 6 months

title: Effects of the once-weekly glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist dulaglutide on ambulatory blood pressure and heart rate in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus.

title: Monotherapy with the once weekly GLP-1 receptor agonist dulaglutide for 12 weeks in Japanese patients with type 2 diabetes: dose-dependent effects on glycaemic control in a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled study.

title: Adding liraglutide to the backbone therapy of biguanide in patients with coronary artery disease and newly diagnosed type-2 diabetes (the AddHope2 study): a randomised controlled study protocol.

title: Effects of sitagliptin therapy on markers of low-grade inflammation and cell adhesion molecules in patients with type 2 diabetes.

title: Comparison of insulin glargine and liraglutide added to oral agents in patients with poorly controlled type 2 diabetes.
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes treated with metformin ± sulphonylurea, with glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c) levels of 7.5-12%

comparison: Liraglutide, escalated to 1.8 mg daily, for 24 weeks
outcomes_primary: Percentage of people reaching HbA1c <7%
outcomes_secondary: HbA1c reduction, fasting plasma glucose, weight change, symptomatic hypoglycaemia, gastrointestinal treatment-emergent adverse events, withdrawal due to adverse events
extraction_notes: Open-label trial design. Trial was powered to detect superiority of glargine over liraglutide.

title: The effect of eating speed at breakfast on appetite hormone responses and daily food consumption.
journal: Journal of investigative medicine : the official publication of the American Federation for Clinical Research
population: Healthy participants; 68% men; age 25.9 (8.1) years; body mass index 25.0 (3.2) kg/m²
intervention: Slow eating speed at breakfast: consuming breakfast over 30 minutes
comparison: Fast eating speed at breakfast: consuming breakfast over 10 minutes
outcomes_primary: Postprandial gut hormone responses (ghrelin, glucagon-like peptide-1, peptide YY); subjective appetite measures (hunger, fullness, desire to eat) assessed using visual analog scales

extraction_notes: Randomized crossover design with 2 separate days; blood samples collected at fasting and 3 hours postprandially; the same breakfast was consumed in both conditions; sample size was 25 participants

title: Postprandial glucose, insulin and incretin responses to different carbohydrate tolerance tests.
population: 240 participants across different glucose tolerance groups (normal glucose tolerance and type 2 diabetes mellitus)
intervention: 75 g oral glucose (monosaccharide, liquid state)
comparison: 100 g standard noodle (polysaccharide, containing 75 g carbohydrates equivalently)
outcomes_primary: Postprandial plasma glucose, insulin, and active glucagon-like peptide-1 (AGLP-1) responses
outcomes_secondary: C-peptide, glucagon, incremental area under curve above baseline from 0 to 120 min of insulin (iAUC(0-120 min)-INS), incremental area under curve of AGLP-1 (iAUC(0-120 min)-AGLP-1), ratio of iAUC(0-120 min)-INS/iAUC(0-120 min)-AGLP-1
extraction_notes: Open-label, randomized, two-way crossover design with 5-7 day washout period. Primary vs secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract.

title: Efficacy and tolerability of albiglutide versus placebo or pioglitazone over 1 year in people with type 2 diabetes currently taking metformin and glimepiride: HARMONY 5.
population: Adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus currently taking metformin (>1500 mg/day) and glimepiride (4 mg/day, standardized before randomization)
