comparison: Placebo; Pioglitazone 30 mg/day orally with allowed blinded uptitration to 45 mg/day if needed
outcomes_primary: Change in glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c) at 52 weeks
outcomes_secondary: Fasting plasma glucose; confirmed hypoglycaemia; weight change; serious adverse events; injection site reactions
extraction_notes: Study design is 156-week total duration but primary results reported at 52 weeks. Route of administration for albiglutide not explicitly stated but implied (injection site reactions mentioned). Secondary outcomes not explicitly labeled as such in abstract.

title: The protective effect of the Mediterranean diet on endothelial resistance to GLP-1 in type 2 diabetes: a preliminary report.
population: Type 2 diabetic patients (n=24); inclusion criteria: no retinopathy, nephropathy, or neuropathy; all taking metformin; none on statins or antioxidant supplements; non-smokers; no high alcohol consumption; no participation in weight-reduction programs or nutritional interventions in previous 6 months
intervention: Mediterranean diet (MedDiet) enriched in monounsaturated fatty acids with 50 mL (4 tablespoons) extra virgin olive oil per day (approximately 1L/week) for 12 weeks
comparison: Control low-fat diet for 12 weeks (reduced all types of fat, emphasized lean meats, low-fat dairy products, cereals, potatoes, pasta, rice, fruits and vegetables; discouraged olive oil use, nuts, fatty meats, sausages, and fatty fish)
outcomes_primary: Not explicitly designated as primary; outcomes measured included: plasma antioxidant capacity (FRAP and TRAP), endothelial function (flow mediated dilatation/FMD of brachial artery), nitrotyrosine, 8-iso-PGF2a, IL-6, ICAM-1 levels; effect of GLP-1 during hyperglycemic clamp on these parameters; insulin secretion during hyperglycemic clamp with GLP-1
outcomes_secondary: Not explicitly designated; additional measures included glycemia, insulin, GLP-1 (active 7-36) levels, endothelium-independent vasodilation (response to nitroglycerin)
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly differentiated in the text; study described as preliminary report; randomized trial with two groups of 12 subjects each; outcomes assessed at baseline and after 3 months; hyperglycemic clamps performed with and without GLP-1 infusion at 0.4 pmol/kg/min

title: Liraglutide promotes natriuresis but does not increase circulating levels of atrial natriuretic peptide in hypertensive subjects with type 2 diabetes.
population: Hypertensive subjects with type 2 diabetes, overweight and obese
intervention: Liraglutide, starting at 0.6 mg single dose then titrated to 1.8 mg daily for 21 days
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Within-subject change from baseline in plasma atrial natriuretic peptide (ANP)
outcomes_secondary: Plasma Nt-proBNP, office blood pressure, heart rate at baseline and over 4 hours following single dose and after 21 days, 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure and heart rate monitoring, 24-hour urinary sodium excretion, body weight, HbA1c, cholesterol
extraction_notes: Primary outcome not explicitly designated; inferred from study objective focus on ANP. Crossover design with double-blinding.

title: Study protocol of a randomised controlled trial comparing perioperative intravenous insulin, GIK or GLP-1 treatment in diabetes-PILGRIM trial.
population: Adults aged 18-75 years with known type 2 diabetes mellitus for >3 months, treated with oral glucose lowering tablets or moderate dose insulin (<1 IU/kg body weight daily), scheduled for elective non-cardiac surgery. Exclusions: oral corticosteroid use, treatment with long-acting GLP-1 agonist or DPP-4 inhibitor, day-care surgery, planned ICU stay postoperatively, planned bowel surgery, history of chronic or idiopathic acute pancreatitis, impaired liver function (ALAT ≥2.5 times upper normal limit), impaired renal function (serum creatinine ≥133 μmol/L males, ≥115 μmol/L females), pregnant/breastfeeding females, known allergy to trial products
intervention: Three arms: (1) Glucose-insulin-potassium infusion (GIK): 500ml glucose 5% with 10 mmol potassium chloride and calculated insulin dose, infused at 83 ml/hr starting 30 minutes before surgery; (2) Insulin bolus regimen (BR): intravenous sliding-scale insulin boluses according to treatment algorithm; (3) Liraglutide (LG): 0.6 mg subcutaneously at 17:00 day before surgery, then 1.2 mg subcutaneously on morning of surgery. All arms: capillary glucose measured every 60 minutes with additional insulin boluses per algorithm if needed. Target glucose range 6-8 mmol/L. Treatment continued up to 4 hours postoperatively
comparison: Three-arm parallel comparison: GIK infusion vs insulin bolus regimen vs liraglutide pre-treatment
outcomes_primary: Difference in median serum glucose between the three study arms at 1 hour postoperatively
outcomes_secondary: Difference in median serum glucose at 4 hours and 1 day postoperatively; amount of insulin administered; occurrence of major complications (composite: death, re-admission, unplanned ICU admission, re-operation, deep wound infection, pneumonia, sepsis/bacteremia, myocardial infarction, cerebrovascular event, deep venous thrombosis, pulmonary embolus, stent thrombosis, bleeding, respiratory failure, renal failure); minor complications (composite: cystitis/UTI, superficial wound infection/wound leakage, pancreatitis, ileus, delirium, length of hospital stay); diabetes-related complications (hypoglycemia requiring assistance, diabetic ketoacidosis requiring admission, unplanned medical appointments, medication changes); perioperative area under the curve outside target range; hypoglycemia (<4.0 mmol/L mild, <2.3 mmol/L severe); hypokalemia (<3.5 mmol/L); hyperkalemia (>5.0 mmol/L); glucose variability (mean absolute glucose change)
extraction_notes: This is a study protocol, not completed trial results. Open-label design. Multicentre trial. Stratified randomization for insulin use.

title: Initial combination therapy with metformin, pioglitazone and exenatide is more effective than sequential add-on therapy in subjects with new-onset diabetes. Results from the Efficacy and Durability of Initial Combination Therapy for Type 2 Diabetes (EDICT): a randomized trial.
population: Drug-naïve adults aged 30-75 years with recently diagnosed type 2 diabetes mellitus (<2 years duration) according to ADA criteria, BMI 24-50 kg/m2, negative glutamic acid decarboxylase antibodies, normal liver function/serum chemistries, stable body weight (±3 pounds within preceding year), negative pregnancy tests. Exclusion criteria: haematocrit <34%, medications known to affect glucose metabolism, previous treatment with any antidiabetic agent, diabetic proliferative retinopathy, albumin excretion >300 mg/day, major organ system disease
intervention: Triple combination therapy: metformin starting at 1000 mg/day increased to 2000 mg/day at 1 month, pioglitazone starting at 15 mg/day increased to 30 mg/day at 1 month (and to 45 mg if HbA1c >6.5% at 3 months), exenatide starting at 5 μg twice daily before breakfast and supper increased to 10 μg twice daily at 1 month
comparison: Conventional sequential add-on therapy: metformin starting at 1000 mg/day increased to 2000 mg/day if FPG >6.1 mmol/l at 1 month, then glipizide added at 5 mg/day and escalated to 10 mg then 20 mg if FPG >6.1 mmol/l or HbA1c >6.5%, then glargine insulin starting at 10 units before breakfast escalated weekly by 1-5 units up to 60 units/day to maintain FPG <6.1 mmol/l
outcomes_primary: HbA1c difference between triple therapy and conventional therapy groups
outcomes_secondary: Percentage of participants achieving HbA1c <6.5% and <7.0%; decrease in fasting plasma glucose; decrease in postprandial plasma glucose; change in body weight; rate of hypoglycaemic events; treatment failure (HbA1c >6.5% on two consecutive visits despite maximum therapy); lipid profile changes; blood pressure changes; adverse events
extraction_notes: Open-label single-centre randomized controlled trial. This is an interim analysis with mean follow-up of 18.5 months from a planned 3-year study. Treatment goal was HbA1c <6.5%.

title: Evaluation of exenatide versus insulin glargine for the impact on endothelial functions and cardiovascular risk markers.
population: Insulin and incretin-naive patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus, body mass index 25-45 kg/m², receiving metformin for at least two months
intervention: Exenatide for 26 weeks
comparison: Insulin glargine for 26 weeks
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract. Outcomes measured included: endothelial functions (by ultrasonography), cardiovascular risk markers including high sensitivity-C-reactive protein, endothelin-1, fibrinogen, monocyte chemoattractant protein-1, leptin, plasminogen activator inhibitor type 1 (by serum ELISA), flow mediated dilatation, endothelium independent vascular responses, total body fat mass (by bioimpedance), and body weight.

title: Quantitative gastrointestinal and psychological traits associated with obesity and response to weight-loss therapy.
population: Adults aged 18 years or older with body mass index >18 kg/m2, including normal weight (BMI 18-24.9 kg/m2), overweight (BMI 25-29.9 kg/m2), obesity class I (BMI 30-34.9 kg/m2), or obesity class II/III (BMI ≥35 kg/m2). For the randomized controlled trial: obese adults with BMI 30-40 kg/m2. Exclusion criteria: positive history of any systemic disease, concurrent treatment for gastrointestinal motility disorders, psychological disorders (eating disorder, anxiety, depression), or weight loss medications.
intervention: Extended-release phentermine-topiramate: 3.75 mg phentermine and 23 mg topiramate for the first 5 days, then 7.5 mg phentermine and 46 mg topiramate for the next 10 days, for a total of 15 days of combination treatment (oral administration)
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Weight loss; gastric emptying of solids and liquids; satiation measured by nutrient drink test (volume to fullness and maximum tolerated volume); satiety measured by caloric intake at ad-libitum buffet meal; fasting and postprandial gastric volume
outcomes_secondary: Gastrointestinal hormones (ghrelin, cholecystokinin, GLP-1, PYY); association of quantitative traits with response to weight-loss therapy; latent dimensions identified by principal component analysis
extraction_notes: This is a multi-component study including a prospective observational cohort study (n=328), analysis of historical data (n=181), and a proof-of-concept randomized placebo-controlled trial (n=24). The primary outcomes listed reflect both the observational and interventional components. The trial duration was 15 days (2 weeks).

title: Effects of targeted delivery of propionate to the human colon on appetite regulation, body weight maintenance and adiposity in overweight adults.
population: Men and women aged 40-65 years with body mass index of 25-40 kg/m2. Excluded: clinically significant illness including type 1 or type 2 diabetes, medication known to affect appetite and/or body weight, weight loss of 3 kg or greater in preceding 2 months, smoking, substance abuse, psychiatric illness, abnormalities on physical examination, electrocardiography or screening blood tests, pregnant or breast feeding women.
intervention: 10 g/day inulin-propionate ester supplementation mixed into normal diet once daily for 24 weeks
comparison: 10 g/day inulin-control supplementation mixed into normal diet once daily for 24 weeks
outcomes_primary: Changes in body weight; food intake
outcomes_secondary: Change in adipose tissue distribution; intra-abdominal adipose tissue; intrahepatocellular lipid content; plasma PYY and GLP-1 concentrations; postprandial glucose and insulin response; body composition by MRI and MRS; subjective appetite ratings by visual analogue scales; cardiovascular and diabetes risk factors including triglycerides, total cholesterol, LDL cholesterol, HDL cholesterol, HbA1c, C reactive protein, liver function tests, blood pressure
extraction_notes: This publication describes multiple studies: in vitro experiments, acute crossover study (n=20), and long-term 24-week parallel RCT (n=60). PICO extraction focused on the long-term 24-week randomized controlled trial as the primary clinical study. The acute study had energy intake as primary outcome with gut hormone release as secondary outcome.

title: LX4211 therapy reduces postprandial glucose levels in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus and renal impairment despite low urinary glucose excretion.
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus and renal impairment with estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) <60 mL/min/1.73 m²
intervention: LX4211 400 mg orally for 7 days
comparison: Placebo for 7 days
outcomes_primary: Change from baseline to day 7 in postprandial glucose (PPG) levels
outcomes_secondary: Changes in fasting plasma glucose levels; glucagon-like peptide 1 levels; urinary glucose excretion (UGE); blood pressure
extraction_notes: Route of administration not explicitly stated but assumed oral based on context. Subgroup analyses by eGFR strata (<45 and 45-59 mL/min/1.73 m²) were reported.

title: Effect of exogenous intravenous administrations of GLP-1 and/or GIP on circulating pro-atrial natriuretic peptide in subjects with different stages of glucose tolerance.
population: Subjects with different stages of glucose tolerance
intervention: Exogenous intravenous administration of GLP-1 and/or GIP
comparison: Not explicitly stated
outcomes_primary: Circulating pro-atrial natriuretic peptide levels
outcomes_secondary: Not explicitly stated
extraction_notes: Abstract text not available; extraction based solely on title. Specific doses, frequencies, durations, and comparator groups not stated. Primary/secondary outcome designation not confirmed.

title: Postprandial effects of polydextrose on satiety hormone responses and subjective feelings of appetite in obese participants.
population: Non-diabetic obese adults aged 20-55 years with BMI 30-37 kg/m2, consuming a moderately low fiber diet (typical fiber intake less than 19 g/day for men and 17 g/day for women). Exclusion criteria: critical illness, inflammatory bowel disease, celiac disease, GI tract malignancy, pregnancy, cardiovascular or metabolic diseases, use of lipid lowering medication affecting serum triglyceride concentrations, anti-obesity drugs, dietary supplements with high fiber content, regular use of fiber supplements/bran/seeds, regular abundant use of non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, familial hyperlipidemia.
intervention: High-fat meal (4293 kJ, 36% from fat consisting of hamburger, french fries, and carbonated drink) supplemented with 15 g polydextrose (Litesse Ultra, DuPont) incorporated into the carbonated drink, consumed once in acute postprandial setting
comparison: High-fat meal (4293 kJ, 36% from fat consisting of hamburger, french fries, and carbonated drink) with placebo carbonated drink containing no additional ingredients
outcomes_primary: Postprandial changes in serum triglycerides (primary outcome of the overall study)
outcomes_secondary: Postprandial plasma concentrations of satiety-related gastrointestinal peptides (ghrelin, cholecystokinin, glucagon-like peptide 1, peptide YY); postprandial plasma concentrations of short chain fatty acids and lactic acid; subjective feelings of appetite (hunger, satisfaction, desire to eat) assessed using 100 mm visual analogue scales expressed as incremental areas under the curve during satiation and satiety periods
extraction_notes: This was an acute, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial with 10-day washout. The outcomes reported in this article are described as secondary outcomes; primary outcome (serum triglycerides) stated as unpublished observations. Sample size (n=18) was calculated based on the primary triglyceride outcome.

title: Fasting gut hormone levels change with modest weight loss in obese adolescents.
population: Obese adolescents aged 10-17 years with body mass index (BMI) > 90th centile; subset of participants from the 'Eat Smart Study'
intervention: Structured reduced carbohydrate dietary intervention for 12 weeks; or structured low-fat dietary intervention for 12 weeks
comparison: Wait-listed control group
outcomes_primary: Fasting gut hormone levels including glucose, insulin, leptin, adiponectin, total amylin, acylated ghrelin, active glucagon-like peptide-1, glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP), pancreatic polypeptide (PP), and total peptide tyrosine-tyrosine
outcomes_secondary: Pre- and postprandial subjective sensations of appetite assessed using visual analogue scales; BMI z-score; homeostatic model of assessment-insulin resistance (HOMA-IR)
extraction_notes: Study is a sub-study of the 'Eat Smart Study'. Two intervention groups (reduced carbohydrate and low-fat) were analyzed together against control for main comparisons. Primary vs secondary outcome distinction not explicitly stated in abstract.

title: Comparable liraglutide pharmacokinetics in pediatric and adult populations with type 2 diabetes: a population pharmacokinetic analysis.
population: Pediatric subjects aged 10-17 years with type 2 diabetes, HbA1c 6.5-11%, fasting plasma glucose 6.1-13.3 mmol/L (110-240 mg/dL), BMI >85th percentile for age and gender, treated with diet and exercise alone or in combination with stable dose of metformin for at least 4 weeks before screening; excluded if impaired renal function (serum creatinine greater than upper reference range for age). Adult subjects with type 2 diabetes from two comparator trials (Trial 2: HbA1c 6.5-10%, BMI 18.5-40 kg/m2, creatinine clearance ≥60 mL/min; Trial 3: HbA1c 7-9.5%, serum creatinine <1.5 mg/dL for males and <1.3 mg/dL for females)
intervention: Liraglutide subcutaneous injection, once daily, dose escalated weekly starting at 0.3 mg/day to 0.6, 0.9, 1.2, and 1.8 mg/day over 5 weeks based on tolerability and fasting plasma glucose
comparison: Placebo (in pediatric trial); adult subjects with type 2 diabetes receiving liraglutide 1.8 mg once daily at steady-state (from Trials 2 and 3)
outcomes_primary: Population pharmacokinetic parameters: apparent clearance (CL/F), apparent volume of distribution (Vd/F), area under the plasma-concentration time curve from 0-24 hours (AUC24), dose proportionality assessment
outcomes_secondary: Effect of covariates (body weight, gender, age category) on liraglutide exposure; comparison of pharmacokinetic profiles between pediatric and adult populations
extraction_notes: This is a population pharmacokinetic analysis comparing pediatric and adult data, not a traditional efficacy trial. The pediatric trial was randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, but this analysis focuses on pharmacokinetic modeling rather than clinical efficacy outcomes. Only 13 pediatric subjects contributed pharmacokinetic data. Adult trial data were from two separate published trials used as comparators.

title: Effects of glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide on gastric emptying, glycaemia and insulinaemia during critical illness: a prospective, double blind, randomised, crossover study.
population: Critically ill patients without known diabetes, with blood glucose concentration >7.1 mmol/l when fasting and/or >10 mmol/l during enteral feeding, mechanically ventilated via tracheal tube with expected ventilation for at least 48 hours, with arterial catheter in situ. Exclusions: pregnancy, anaemia (haemoglobin <80 g/l), age <18 years, contraindication to enteral feeding, previous surgery on small intestine or gastrointestinal surgery during current hospital admission.
intervention: Intravenous glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) 4 pmol/kg/minute, administered via central venous catheter at 1 ml/minute using infusion pump, from T=-60 to T=300 minutes (360 minutes total infusion duration). At T=0, 100 ml liquid nutrient meal (2 kcal/ml) administered via nasogastric tube.
comparison: Placebo (0.9% saline) administered intravenously via central venous catheter at 1 ml/minute using infusion pump, from T=-60 to T=300 minutes. At T=0, 100 ml liquid nutrient meal (2 kcal/ml) administered via nasogastric tube.
outcomes_primary: Blood glucose concentrations (area under concentration curve from T=-60 to T=300 minutes)
outcomes_secondary: Glucose absorption (serum 3-O-methylglucose concentrations, AUC), gastric emptying (scintigraphy measuring intragastric retention and 13C-octanoic breath test measuring gastric emptying coefficient), serum insulin concentrations (AUC), serum glucagon concentrations (incremental AUC), plasma GIP concentrations
extraction_notes: Primary outcome not explicitly labeled as primary in the text but identified based on sample size calculation targeting postprandial glycaemia. Crossover design with patients studied on two consecutive days.

title: An enriched, cereal-based bread affects appetite ratings and glycemic, insulinemic, and gastrointestinal hormone responses in healthy adults in a randomized, controlled trial.
population: Healthy adults aged 19-32 years with body mass index of 19.2-28.5
intervention: Cereal-based bread containing wheat, oat, and spelt flours with 22% dried fruits (figs, apricots, raisins, and prunes), enriched with fiber (7% from wheat cross-linked maltodextrins and pea) and protein (10-11% from wheat gluten and hydrolyzed wheat proteins), consumed 2 times with 1-week wash-out period
comparison: Control bread consisting of white bread with margarine and jam (matched for energy density, fat, and sugar content), consumed 2 times with 1-week wash-out period
outcomes_primary: Appetite ratings measured using standardized visual analogue scales (prospective consumption, satiety, hunger)
outcomes_secondary: Postprandial glucose response, insulin response, gastrointestinal hormone responses (ghrelin, glucagon-like peptide 1, gastric inhibitory polypeptide, pancreatic polypeptide) measured as areas under the curve over 4 hours; subsequent ad libitum energy intake at 4 hours
extraction_notes: Primary versus secondary outcome distinction not explicitly stated in abstract; crossover design with each volunteer receiving both interventions

title: Association among weight change, glycemic control, and markers of cardiovascular risk with exenatide once weekly: a pooled analysis of patients with type 2 diabetes.
population: Adults at least 16 years of age with type 2 diabetes mellitus, A1C 7.1% to 11.0%, stable body weight for 3-6 months prior to enrollment, and body mass index 23 to 45 kg/m2
intervention: Exenatide once weekly (2 mg subcutaneous injection), with or without oral glucose-lowering medications
comparison: Patients were distributed into quartiles based on body weight change from baseline (Quartile 1: greatest weight loss; Quartile 4: least weight loss or weight gain); this was a pooled analysis without a separate comparator arm
outcomes_primary: Not explicitly stated as primary outcome; glycemic parameters (A1C, fasting plasma glucose) and cardiovascular risk markers (systolic blood pressure, diastolic blood pressure, heart rate, HDL-C, LDL-C, total cholesterol, triglycerides) were evaluated
outcomes_secondary: Liver enzymes (alanine aminotransferase, aspartate aminotransferase), adverse events, incidence of severe and non-severe hypoglycemia
extraction_notes: This is a pooled analysis of 8 randomized controlled trials (24-30 weeks duration) rather than a single RCT. Primary and secondary outcomes were not explicitly distinguished in the methods. The analysis examined associations between weight change quartiles and clinical outcomes rather than comparing exenatide to a control group.

title: LEADER 2: baseline calcitonin in 9340 people with type 2 diabetes enrolled in the Liraglutide Effect and Action in Diabetes: Evaluation of cardiovascular outcome Results (LEADER) trial: preliminary observations.
population: Adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus at high risk of cardiovascular disease (with or without existing cardiovascular disease), drug-naïve or treated with one or more antihyperglycaemic drugs including basal and premix insulins, baseline serum calcitonin ≤50 ng/l. Exclusion criteria: baseline calcitonin >50 ng/l (initially >100 ng/l), personal or family history of multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2 or familial medullary thyroid carcinoma.
intervention: Liraglutide once daily (dose not specified in abstract), followed for up to 5 years
comparison: Placebo once daily
outcomes_primary: Cardiovascular outcomes (specific primary endpoint not defined in this preliminary report)
outcomes_secondary: Serum calcitonin concentrations measured at baseline and annually thereafter
extraction_notes: This is a preliminary baseline report of the ongoing LEADER trial, focusing on baseline calcitonin measurements rather than primary trial outcomes. Liraglutide dose not specified in the text. The primary cardiovascular outcome is referenced but not explicitly defined in this preliminary publication.

title: Plant-rich mixed meals based on Palaeolithic diet principles have a dramatic impact on incretin, peptide YY and satiety response, but show little effect on glucose and insulin homeostasis: an acute-effects randomised study.
population: Healthy subjects
intervention: Palaeolithic-type meals (PAL 1 and PAL 2) comprising fish and a variety of plants, selected to be rich in fibre and phyto-nutrients. PAL1 contained more protein and energy; PAL2 matched for energy, protein, fat and carbohydrates with reference meal
comparison: Reference meal based on WHO guidelines (REF), matched with PAL2 for energy, protein, fat and carbohydrates
outcomes_secondary: Plasma glucose concentration over 180 min; plasma insulin concentration over 180 min; glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) concentration over 180 min; glucose-dependent insulinotropic peptide (GIP) concentration over 180 min; peptide YY (PYY) concentration over 180 min; satiation assessed using electronic visual analogue scale (EVAS) scores; positive incremental AUC over 120 min for glucose and insulin
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract. Sample size not reported. Randomised cross-over trial design with three meals given on separate occasions.

title: The effects of TNF-α on GLP-1-stimulated plasma glucose kinetics.
journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
population: Healthy males, aged 24 ± 3 years, body mass index 22.9 ± 1.3 kg/m²
intervention: Recombinant human TNF-α infusion (1000 ng/m² · h) from t = 0-6 hours, combined with GLP-1 infusion (0.5 pmol/kg · min from t = 2 hours, increased to 1.2 pmol/kg · min from t = 4-6 hours), with plasma glucose clamped at 5 mmol/L via variable rate 20% dextrose infusion
comparison: Saline (0.9%) infusion from t = 0-6 hours, combined with same GLP-1 infusion protocol and glucose clamp; crossover design with trials 7-14 days apart
outcomes_primary: Endogenous glucose production (EGP) measured by [6,6-²H₂]glucose isotope tracer dilution method
outcomes_secondary: Plasma glucagon, plasma insulin, C-peptide, plasma TNF-α, IL-6, body temperature, plasma GLP-1
extraction_notes: Crossover trial design with participants serving as their own controls. Sample size of 12 participants. Secondary outcomes not explicitly labeled as such but measured throughout the study.

title: A randomized controlled trial of liraglutide versus insulin detemir plus sitagliptin: Effective switch from intensive insulin therapy to the once-daily injection in patients with well-controlled type 2 diabetes.
population: Japanese patients with type 2 diabetes treated with a basal-bolus insulin regimen whose diabetes had been controlled well or moderately (glycated hemoglobin [HbA1c] ≤ 7.3%)
intervention: Liraglutide, once daily
comparison: Insulin detemir plus sitagliptin
outcomes_primary: HbA1c change from baseline to 24 weeks
outcomes_secondary: Diabetes Treatment Satisfaction Questionnaire overall satisfaction score
extraction_notes: Liraglutide dose not specified in abstract. Route and frequency for detemir plus sitagliptin not specified. Duration of follow-up was 24 weeks.

title: Liraglutide pharmacokinetics and dose-exposure response in Asian subjects with Type 2 diabetes from China, India and South Korea.
population: Asian subjects with Type 2 diabetes mellitus from China, India and South Korea
intervention: Liraglutide 0.6 mg, 1.2 mg, or 1.8 mg once daily for 16 weeks
comparison: Active control (double-dummy design); specific comparator not stated in abstract
outcomes_primary: Liraglutide population pharmacokinetics (exposure measured as area under the curve), exposure-response relationship
outcomes_secondary: Effects on glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c), effects on body weight
extraction_notes: This is a pharmacokinetic/exposure-response analysis of a previously published trial. The specific active comparator drug is not named in the abstract. Primary outcomes appear to be PK-focused rather than clinical efficacy endpoints.

title: Effects of two dietary fibers as part of ready-to-eat cereal (RTEC) breakfasts on perceived appetite and gut hormones in overweight women.
population: Overweight women, 18-29 years of age, BMI 25.0-29.9 kg/m2, regular consumers of breakfast cereal, tested during luteal phase of menstrual cycle. Exclusions: recent weight loss >4.1 kg within 4 weeks, history of cancer, renal, hepatic, endocrine (including diabetes mellitus), pulmonary, biliary, gastrointestinal, pancreatic, or neurologic disorders, use of weight loss drugs, weight-reducing surgery, diagnosed eating disorder, pregnancy or planning pregnancy
intervention: High-fiber ready-to-eat cereals (RTEC): (1) HF-AXOS: 100g RTEC containing 15g enzyme-hydrolyzed arabinoxylan from wheat plus 4g base cereal fiber (19g total fiber, ~345 kcal), consumed with 2% milk diluted with water (500g total breakfast weight); (2) HF-FLAX: 100g RTEC containing 15g intact arabinoxylan from flax plus 4g base cereal fiber (19g total fiber, ~347 kcal), consumed with 2% milk diluted with water (500g total breakfast weight). Single meal consumption after 9-13 hour overnight fast
comparison: Trial 1: Low-fiber RTEC (LF): 100g RTEC with 4g fiber, 461 kcal. Trial 2: Low-fiber RTEC (LF): 100g RTEC with 4g fiber, 461 kcal; Low-fiber isocaloric RTEC (LF-iso): 70g RTEC with 3g fiber, 341 kcal (energy-matched to high-fiber RTECs). All consumed with 2% milk diluted with water (500g total breakfast weight)
outcomes_primary: Perceived appetite assessed by visual analogue scale (VAS, 100mm) for desire to eat, hunger, fullness, and prospective consumption at multiple time points from pre-breakfast to 270 minutes; net incremental area under the curve (niAUC) for appetite ratings at 2h and 4h
outcomes_secondary: Ad libitum lunch energy intake at 240 minutes post-breakfast; plasma hormone concentrations (active ghrelin, active GLP-1, total PYY, insulin) and glucose at baseline and multiple postprandial time points (15, 30, 45, 60, 90, 120, 180, 240 minutes) with niAUC at 2h and 4h (Trial 2 only); gastrointestinal tolerability (cramping, flatulence, gas/bloating, loose stools, nausea) on 6-point scale

title: Preserved Insulin Secretory Capacity and Weight Loss Are the Predominant Predictors of Glycemic Control in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes Randomized to Roux-en-Y Gastric Bypass.
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus; BMI 30-39.9 kg/m2; HbA1c ≥8% (64 mmol/mol) or ≤14% (130 mmol/mol); C-peptide >1 ng/mL 90 min after a standardized meal challenge
intervention: Lifestyle modification and intensive medical management (LS/IMM) in conjunction with Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (RYGB)
comparison: Lifestyle modification and intensive medical management (LS/IMM) alone
outcomes_primary: Changes in incretins (GLP-1, GLP-2, GIP), insulin sensitivity (HOMA-IR, Matsuda index), and insulin secretion at 1 year after randomization
outcomes_secondary: HbA1c, fasting glucose, glucose area under the curve, weight loss, glucagon levels, insulin clearance, metabolic clearance rate of insulin, insulin secretion rate, C-peptide index, insulinogenic index, oral disposition index, β-cell glucose sensitivity, adiponectin
extraction_notes: This is an ancillary study to the Diabetes Surgery Study (DSS). Sample size is 68 patients (n=34 per group) from two of five study sites that recruited 120 participants total in the main trial. Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly labeled as such in the abstract; classification based on stated study objectives.

title: Polyphenol-rich diets improve glucose metabolism in people at high cardiometabolic risk: a controlled randomised intervention trial.
population: Individuals with high waist circumference and at least one more component of the metabolic syndrome, recruited at the obesity outpatient clinic
intervention: Isoenergetic diet rich in polyphenols, or diet rich in long chain n-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids (LCn3) of marine origin, or diet rich in both LCn3 and polyphenols, for 8 weeks
comparison: Control diet low in LCn3 and polyphenols
outcomes_primary: Plasma glucose, insulin and glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1) concentrations during 3-hour OGTT and test meal
outcomes_secondary: Indices of insulin sensitivity and beta cell function, early insulin secretion, oral glucose insulin sensitivity (OGIS), GLP-1 total postprandial AUC
extraction_notes: 2x2 factorial design with 4 groups. Primary vs secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract. Total 86 participants randomized, 77 analysed.

title: Safety and efficacy of once-weekly dulaglutide versus sitagliptin after 2 years in metformin-treated patients with type 2 diabetes (AWARD-5): a randomized, phase III study.
population: Adults aged 18-75 years with type 2 diabetes (≥6 months duration), HbA1c ≥7.0% (≥53.0 mmol/mol) and ≤9.5% (≤80.3 mmol/mol) on metformin monotherapy or combination therapy, or HbA1c >8.0% (>63.9 mmol/mol) and ≤9.5% (≤80.3 mmol/mol) on diet and exercise alone, body mass index 25-40 kg/m2, treated with metformin monotherapy (minimum dose ≥1500 mg/day) for ≥6 weeks before randomization
intervention: Dulaglutide 1.5 mg or 0.75 mg subcutaneous injection once weekly for 104 weeks
comparison: Sitagliptin 100 mg orally for 104 weeks; Placebo for 26 weeks (replaced with sitagliptin after 26 weeks)
outcomes_primary: Change in glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c) concentration from baseline
outcomes_secondary: Percentage of participants achieving HbA1c target <7.0% (<53.0 mmol/mol) and ≤6.5% (≤47.5 mmol/mol); body weight change; fasting plasma glucose; fasting insulin; HOMA2-%β (β-cell function); HOMA2-%S (insulin sensitivity); lipids; adverse events; hypoglycaemic episodes; vital signs; ECG results; laboratory variables; pancreatic safety (pancreatic enzyme levels, adjudicated pancreatitis events); thyroid safety (calcitonin measurements); cardiovascular safety (adjudicated cardiovascular events); immunogenicity (antidrug antibodies)
extraction_notes: Randomization ratio was 2:2:2:1 for dulaglutide 1.5 mg, dulaglutide 0.75 mg, sitagliptin, and placebo. Metformin was continued as background therapy during the treatment period. Study had adaptive seamless design with initial dose-finding portion.

title: Rationale, design, and baseline characteristics in Evaluation of LIXisenatide in Acute Coronary Syndrome, a long-term cardiovascular end point trial of lixisenatide versus placebo.
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and a recent acute coronary syndrome (ACS) event
intervention: Lixisenatide (glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonist); dose, route, frequency, and duration not specified in abstract
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Composite of time to cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, or hospitalization for unstable angina
outcomes_secondary: Not explicitly specified in abstract; safety outcomes systematically collected include hypoglycemia, pancreatitis, and malignancy
extraction_notes: This is a trial design/baseline characteristics paper, not a results paper. Intervention dosing details not provided in abstract. Secondary efficacy outcomes not explicitly listed.

title: One-year efficacy and safety of a fixed combination of insulin degludec and liraglutide in patients with type 2 diabetes: results of a 26-week extension to a 26-week main trial.
population: Insulin-naïve adults (≥18 years) with type 2 diabetes inadequately controlled on metformin ± pioglitazone who completed the 26-week main DUAL I trial and continued into the extension phase
intervention: IDegLira (fixed combination of insulin degludec 100 U/ml plus liraglutide 3.6 mg/ml), administered subcutaneously once daily, starting at 10 dose steps (10 U insulin degludec plus 0.36 mg liraglutide), titrated twice weekly in 2 dose step increments to fasting glucose target of 4.0-5.0 mmol/l, maximum 50 dose steps (50 U insulin degludec and 1.8 mg liraglutide)
comparison: 1) Insulin degludec 100 U/ml subcutaneously once daily, starting at 10 U, titrated twice weekly to fasting glucose target of 4.0-5.0 mmol/l with no maximum dose limit; 2) Liraglutide 6 mg/ml subcutaneously once daily, starting at 0.6 mg/day, increased by 0.6 mg weekly to maximum 1.8 mg/day
outcomes_primary: Change from baseline in HbA1c concentration at 26 weeks (main trial primary endpoint)
outcomes_secondary: Change from baseline in HbA1c concentration at 52 weeks; percentage of patients reaching HbA1c targets of <7% and ≤6.5%; change from baseline in laboratory-measured fasting plasma glucose; change from baseline in body weight; insulin dose at end of trial; nine-point self-monitored blood glucose profiles; confirmed hypoglycaemic episodes; confirmed nocturnal hypoglycaemic episodes; adverse events; serious adverse events
extraction_notes: This is a 26-week extension of the DUAL I trial (total 52 weeks). Randomization ratio was 2:1:1 (IDegLira:insulin degludec:liraglutide). Open-label design. The primary endpoint stated was for the main 26-week trial; the extension focused on 52-week secondary endpoints. Post hoc analyses by BMI category were also performed.

title: Preserved pharmacokinetic exposure and distinct glycemic effects of insulin degludec and liraglutide in IDegLira, a fixed-ratio combination therapy.
population: Healthy subjects (for pharmacokinetic crossover study); subjects with type 2 diabetes (for phase 3 treat-to-target study)
intervention: IDegLira (insulin degludec/liraglutide fixed-ratio combination)
comparison: Insulin degludec (IDeg) alone; liraglutide alone
outcomes_primary: Pharmacokinetics (bioavailability) of IDegLira compared to monocomponents
outcomes_secondary: Dose proportionality; covariate effects on exposure; exposure-response relationship for change in glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c)
extraction_notes: Abstract describes two studies: a single-dose 4-period crossover pharmacokinetic study in healthy subjects and a phase 3 treat-to-target study in type 2 diabetes subjects. Specific doses, routes, frequencies, and durations not explicitly stated. Primary vs secondary outcome designation inferred from study design description.

title: Carbohydrate-rich breakfast attenuates glycaemic, insulinaemic and ghrelin response to ad libitum lunch relative to morning fasting in lean adults.
population: Healthy, lean men and women aged 22-56 years with BMI 18-25 kg/m2, classified as lean based on dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry-derived fat mass indices of ≤7.5 kg/m2 (men) and ≤11 kg/m2 (women), weight stable (±1 kg body mass within past 6 months), free of metabolic disorders, adhering to standard sleep-wake cycle (no shift workers)
intervention: Carbohydrate-rich breakfast (corn flakes, 2% fat milk, toasted white bread, margarine, fresh orange juice; 70% carbohydrate, 17% fat, 13% protein) provided in quantities containing 0.06 g carbohydrate per kcal of individual participant's measured daily RMR (resulting in 1963 kJ/469 kcal), consumed within 15 minutes, followed by ad libitum lunch 3 hours later
comparison: Extended morning fasting (overnight fast of ≥10 hours extended until ad libitum lunch at approximately ≥14.5 hours total fasting), followed by same ad libitum lunch 3 hours after matched rest period
outcomes_primary: Energy intake at ad libitum lunch and total daily energy intake
outcomes_secondary: Plasma glucose, serum insulin, plasma NEFA, plasma acylated and total ghrelin, plasma peptide tyrosine-tyrosine (PYY), plasma glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1), serum leptin concentrations; subjective appetite ratings (desire to eat, hunger, fullness, prospective consumption, composite appetite score) assessed via 100-mm visual analogue scales
extraction_notes: This is a randomised counterbalanced cross-over study. Primary and secondary outcomes were not explicitly designated in the text; classification based on study focus and discussion emphasis. Sample size was determined for a wider project rather than specifically for this investigation.

title: Once-weekly dulaglutide versus bedtime insulin glargine, both in combination with prandial insulin lispro, in patients with type 2 diabetes (AWARD-4): a randomised, open-label, phase 3, non-inferiority study.
population: Patients aged ≥18 years with type 2 diabetes inadequately controlled with conventional insulin treatment
intervention: Once-weekly dulaglutide 1.5 mg or dulaglutide 0.75 mg subcutaneous injection, in combination with prandial insulin lispro, for 52 weeks
comparison: Daily bedtime insulin glargine in combination with prandial insulin lispro
outcomes_primary: Change in glycated haemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) from baseline to week 26, with a 0.4% non-inferiority margin
extraction_notes: Secondary outcomes not explicitly stated in the abstract. Randomisation was stratified by country and metformin use. Open-label trial but participants and investigators were unaware of dulaglutide dose assignment.

title: Effects of a high-protein/low-carbohydrate versus a standard hypocaloric diet on adipocytokine levels and cardiovascular risk factors during 9 months, role of rs6923761 gene variant of glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor.
population: Obese subjects (211 participants), stratified by rs6923761 GLP-1 receptor gene variant genotype (GG wild type vs. GA/AA mutant type)
intervention: Diet HP (high protein/low carbohydrate hypocaloric diet) for 9 months
comparison: Diet S (standard hypocaloric diet) for 9 months
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly differentiated in abstract. Outcomes measured included: body mass index, weight, fat mass, waist circumference, systolic blood pressure, LDL cholesterol, total cholesterol, leptin levels, insulin levels, HOMA-R, and adipokine levels. Study design described as randomized allocation. Exact macronutrient compositions of diets not specified.

title: Short term monotherapy with GLP-1 receptor agonist liraglutide or PDE 4 inhibitor roflumilast is superior to metformin in weight loss in obese PCOS women: a pilot randomized study.
population: Obese women with PCOS diagnosed by ASRM-ESHRE Rotterdam criteria, type A phenotype (concomitant hyperandrogenemia, menses abnormalities, and PCO morphology), aged 18 years to menopause, BMI ≥30 kg/m2. Exclusion criteria: history of carcinoma or neuropsychiatric events, personal or familiar history of multiple endocrine neoplasia 2, significant cardiovascular, kidney or hepatic disease, use of medications known to affect reproductive or metabolic functions within 180 days prior to study entry
intervention: Liraglutide 1.2 mg subcutaneously once daily (initiated at 0.6 mg once daily, increased to 1.2 mg/day after 1 week) for 12 weeks; or Roflumilast 500 mcg orally once daily for 12 weeks
comparison: Metformin 1000 mg twice daily (initiated at 500 mg once daily, increased by 500 mg every 3 days up to 1000 mg BID) for 12 weeks
outcomes_primary: Change in measures of obesity (weight, BMI, waist circumference, visceral adipose tissue area)
outcomes_secondary: Hormonal changes (total testosterone, free testosterone, SHBG, free androgen index, androstenedione, DHEAS, LH, FSH); metabolic changes (fasting glucose, fasting insulin, HOMA-IR, glucose levels during OGTT); menstrual frequency; whole-body composition by DXA
extraction_notes: Open-label study design. All women received general lifestyle intervention advice at study entry. Three-arm trial with two intervention groups (liraglutide, roflumilast) compared to metformin.

title: Efficacy and Safety of Lixisenatide in Japanese Patients with Type 2 Diabetes Insufficiently Controlled with Basal Insulin±Sulfonylurea: A Subanalysis of the GetGoal-L-Asia Study.
journal: Hormone and metabolic research = Hormon- und Stoffwechselforschung = Hormones et metabolisme
population: Japanese patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus insufficiently controlled with basal insulin with or without sulfonylurea
intervention: Once-daily lixisenatide 20 μg as add-on to basal insulin with or without sulfonylurea
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Change from baseline in HbA1c
outcomes_secondary: Proportion of patients reaching HbA1c targets of <7% (53 mmol/mol) and ≤6.5% (48 mmol/mol); 2-hour postprandial plasma glucose; glucose excursion; fasting plasma glucose; body weight; adverse events including gastrointestinal adverse events; symptomatic hypoglycemia
extraction_notes: This is a subanalysis of 159 Japanese patients from the 24-week double-blind GetGoal-L-Asia study (NCT00866658). The distinction between primary and secondary outcomes is inferred based on explicit statement of primary endpoint; other outcomes listed as secondary.

title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonist Treatment Increases Bone Formation and Prevents Bone Loss in Weight-Reduced Obese Women.
journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
population: Healthy obese women with body mass index of 34 ± 0.5 kg/m², age 46 ± 2 years, who achieved 12% weight loss through low-calorie diet
intervention: GLP-1 receptor agonist liraglutide 1.2 mg/day for 52 weeks during weight maintenance phase; in case of weight gain, up to two meals per day could be replaced with a low-calorie-diet product
comparison: No liraglutide treatment during 52-week weight maintenance phase; in case of weight gain, up to two meals per day could be replaced with a low-calorie-diet product
outcomes_primary: Changes in bone mineral content (total, pelvic, and arm-leg BMC) and bone markers (C-terminal telopeptide of type 1 collagen [CTX-1] and N-terminal propeptide of type 1 procollagen [P1NP]) after 52-week weight maintenance
extraction_notes: Sample size is 37 participants total but allocation between groups not specified in abstract. Secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished from primary outcomes.

title: Effect of reducing portion size at a compulsory meal on later energy intake, gut hormones, and appetite in overweight adults.
population: Healthy adults aged 18-60 years with BMI ≥25 and <35 kg/m2 (overweight and obese). Exclusions: disordered eating (EAT-26 score ≥11), depressive symptoms (Zung Depression Scale score ≥70), smoking, excessive alcohol intake (women >14 units/week, men >21 units/week), weight change >4.5kg in last 3 months or actively trying to change weight, medical conditions/medications affecting appetite, inflammatory conditions, diabetes or fasting glucose ≥7mmol/l, pregnancy/breastfeeding/planning pregnancy, extreme exercise levels (>420 min/week moderate/vigorous activity), unable to eat test foods, irregular breakfast consumption (≤3/week)
intervention: Standardized breakfast with portion size reduced by 20% or 40% from control; control breakfast provided 25% of gender-specific estimated daily energy requirements (3310kJ for men, 2540kJ for women); 20% reduction (2650kJ men, 2030kJ women); 40% reduction (1990kJ men, 1520kJ women); breakfast consumed in entirety; macronutrient composition 35% fat, 18% protein, 47% carbohydrate
comparison: Control portion size breakfast providing 25% of gender-specific estimated daily energy requirements; randomised crossover design with all participants receiving all three conditions (control, 20% reduction, 40% reduction) on separate days at least 1 week apart
outcomes_primary: Energy intake at ad libitum lunch (240 minutes post-breakfast) and afternoon snack (360 minutes post-breakfast), and total daily energy intake measured by weighed diet diaries
outcomes_secondary: Postprandial gastrointestinal hormone concentrations (PYY3-36, GLP-1, GIP, glucose, insulin) measured at fasting and 30, 60, 120, 180, and 240 minutes in a subgroup of 20 participants; appetite ratings (hunger, fullness, desire to eat, prospective consumption) measured using visual analogue scales at 30-minute intervals until lunch then at specified intervals; perceived portion size ratings; associations between hormones, appetite ratings, and energy intake
extraction_notes: Primary outcomes not explicitly designated as such in abstract/text but inferred from study objectives. Blood sampling performed in subgroup of 20 participants only. Study visits conducted outside luteal phase for females.

title: Design of FLAT-SUGAR: Randomized Trial of Prandial Insulin Versus Prandial GLP-1 Receptor Agonist Together With Basal Insulin and Metformin for High-Risk Type 2 Diabetes.
population: People with insulin-requiring type 2 diabetes and high cardiovascular risk
intervention: Basal insulin with prandial GLP-1 receptor agonist (GLIPULIN regimen) plus metformin, seeking to maintain HbA1c levels between 6.7% and 7.3% (50-56 mmol/mol) for 6 months
comparison: Continued basal-bolus insulin (BBI), seeking to maintain HbA1c levels between 6.7% and 7.3% (50-56 mmol/mol) for 6 months
outcomes_primary: Glycemic variability assessed by continuous glucose monitoring
outcomes_secondary: HbA1c, weight, circulating markers of inflammation and cardiovascular risk, albuminuria, electrocardiographic patterns assessed by Holter monitoring
extraction_notes: This is a design/methods paper describing the FLAT-SUGAR trial protocol rather than reporting final results. Metformin mentioned in title but not explicitly described in abstract body regarding dosing details.

title: Intake of Lactobacillus reuteri improves incretin and insulin secretion in glucose-tolerant humans: a proof of concept.
population: Glucose-tolerant humans, including lean (age 49 ± 7 years, BMI 23.6 ± 1.7 kg/m²) and obese (age 51 ± 7 years, BMI 35.5 ± 4.9 kg/m²) participants
intervention: Lactobacillus reuteri SD5865, 10^10 colony forming units, twice daily (b.i.d.), oral ingestion, for 4 weeks
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Incretin effect, GLP-1 and GLP-2 secretion assessed by oral glucose tolerance and isoglycemic glucose infusion tests; peripheral insulin sensitivity and endogenous glucose production measured by euglycemic-hyperinsulinemic clamps with [6,6-²H2]glucose
outcomes_secondary: Muscle and hepatic lipid content assessed by ¹H-magnetic resonance spectroscopy; immune status, cytokines, and endotoxin; insulin and C-peptide secretion; body mass; ectopic fat content
extraction_notes: Primary vs secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract; classification inferred from study objectives. Sample size was 21 participants (11 lean, 10 obese).

title: Comparison of effects of sitagliptin and voglibose on left ventricular diastolic dysfunction in patients with type 2 diabetes: results of the 3D trial.
population: Outpatients aged 20-85 years with type 2 diabetes and left ventricular diastolic dysfunction (LV ejection fraction >50%, mitral annular early diastolic velocity (e') <8 cm/s or E/e' ratio >15) who had not achieved glycemic control targets with diet, exercise, sulfonylurea, metformin, or pioglitazone treatments. Exclusion criteria: patients treated with insulin, alpha-glucosidase inhibitor, or glinide; type 1 diabetes; HbA1c ≥9.0%; systolic blood pressure ≥160 mmHg; serum creatinine ≥1.5 mg/dL; myocardial infarction or stroke within previous 24 weeks; significant LV hypertrophy (LV wall thickness ≥13 mm); atrial fibrillation; significant valve diseases (moderately severe or greater)
intervention: Sitagliptin 50 mg/day orally for at least 24 weeks
comparison: Voglibose 0.6 mg/day orally for at least 24 weeks
outcomes_primary: Changes in e' velocity (mitral annular early diastolic velocity) and E/e' ratio (ratio of mitral inflow velocity to e' velocity) from baseline to 24 weeks
outcomes_secondary: Changes in HbA1c, GLP-1, GIP, C-peptide, CD34, lipid profile (total cholesterol, triglyceride, HDL-C), oxidative stress markers (MDA-LDL, urine 8-OHdG), inflammatory markers (hs-CRP, pentraxin-3), eGFR, and any adverse events
extraction_notes: Study was randomized, prospective, open-label, multicenter design. Stratified block randomization by age, HbA1c, e', and thiazolidinedione use. 100 patients enrolled, 80 completed follow-up (40 per group).

title: Efficacy and Safety of Once-Weekly Dulaglutide Versus Insulin Glargine in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes on Metformin and Glimepiride (AWARD-2).
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes on maximally tolerated doses of metformin and glimepiride
intervention: Dulaglutide 1.5 mg once weekly or dulaglutide 0.75 mg once weekly, combined with metformin and glimepiride
comparison: Insulin glargine daily, combined with metformin and glimepiride
outcomes_primary: HbA1c change from baseline at 52 weeks (noninferiority of dulaglutide 1.5 mg to glargine)
outcomes_secondary: Achievement of HbA1c targets <7.0%, body weight change, hypoglycemia rates (total and severe), pancreatic enzymes, gastrointestinal adverse events (nausea, diarrhea)
extraction_notes: Open-label study design; 78-week total study duration with primary endpoint at 52 weeks; glargine was administered without forced titration

title: Brain reward-system activation in response to anticipation and consumption of palatable food is altered by glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor activation in humans.
population: Obese subjects with type 2 diabetes, obese subjects with normoglycaemia, and lean subjects with normoglycaemia
intervention: Intravenous infusion of the GLP-1 receptor agonist exenatide during somatostatin pituitary-pancreatic clamps
comparison: Exenatide with prior GLP-1 receptor blockade by exendin-9-39; placebo
outcomes_primary: Brain responses to anticipation and receipt of chocolate milk versus a tasteless solution measured by functional MRI (fMRI)
outcomes_secondary: Food intake
extraction_notes: This was part of a larger study. Total n=48 across all three groups but distribution between groups not specified. Dose, frequency, and duration of exenatide infusion not provided. Crossover design implied (three fMRI sessions at separate visits) but not explicitly stated.

title: Treatment satisfaction in people with type 2 diabetes mellitus treated with once-weekly dulaglutide: data from the AWARD-1 and AWARD-3 clinical trials.
population: People with type 2 diabetes mellitus
intervention: Dulaglutide 1.5 mg once weekly and dulaglutide 0.75 mg once weekly (long-acting glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist)
comparison: AWARD-1 study: exenatide or placebo; AWARD-3 study: metformin
outcomes_primary: Not explicitly specified
outcomes_secondary: Treatment satisfaction measured by Diabetes Treatment Satisfaction Questionnaire status version (DTSQs) and change version (DTSQc); total treatment satisfaction score; perceived frequency of hyperglycaemia; perceived frequency of hypoglycaemia
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly differentiated in the abstract. Study duration was 52 weeks. This analysis includes data from two separate trials (AWARD-1 and AWARD-3). Exenatide dose, route, and frequency not specified.

title: Exenatide Regulates Cerebral Glucose Metabolism in Brain Areas Associated With Glucose Homeostasis and Reward System.
population: Male subjects with HbA1c of 5.7%, fasting glucose of 114 mg/dL, and 2-h glucose of 177 mg/dL
intervention: Exenatide 5 μg subcutaneous injection, single dose, administered 30 min before oral glucose tolerance test
comparison: Placebo subcutaneous injection
outcomes_primary: Cerebral glucose metabolic rate (CMRglu) measured by positron emission tomography after injection of [18F]2-fluoro-2-deoxy-d-glucose
outcomes_secondary: Rate of glucose absorption (RaO), rate of glucose disposal, plasma glucose, plasma insulin
extraction_notes: Study described as double-blind, randomized design. Sample size is 15 subjects. Population appears to be prediabetic based on glucose values but this is not explicitly stated as an inclusion criterion.

title: A Randomized, Controlled Trial of 3.0 mg of Liraglutide in Weight Management.
journal: The New England journal of medicine
population: Adults without type 2 diabetes with BMI ≥30, or BMI ≥27 with treated or untreated dyslipidemia or hypertension
intervention: Liraglutide 3.0 mg once-daily subcutaneous injection plus counseling on lifestyle modification for 56 weeks
comparison: Placebo subcutaneous injection plus counseling on lifestyle modification
outcomes_primary: Change in body weight; proportion of patients losing at least 5% of initial body weight; proportion of patients losing more than 10% of initial body weight
extraction_notes: Secondary outcomes not explicitly specified in abstract. Coprimary endpoints included three measures. Adverse events reported but not designated as formal outcomes.

title: The role of efferent cholinergic transmission for the insulinotropic and glucagonostatic effects of GLP-1.
journal: American journal of physiology. Regulatory, integrative and comparative physiology
population: Healthy male participants
intervention: Atropine infusion to block vagal cholinergic transmission, combined with GLP-1 infusion at low dose (0.3 pmol·kg−1·min−1) from t=45-95 min and higher dose (1 pmol·kg−1·min−1) from t=95-145 min, with plasma glucose clamped at 6 mmol/l starting at t=15 min
comparison: Saline infusion (instead of atropine) with same GLP-1 infusion protocol; Control experiments without GLP-1 infusions (atropine vs saline)
outcomes_primary: Insulinotropic effect of GLP-1 (measured by C-peptide levels); Glucagon secretion levels
outcomes_secondary: Heart rate; Pancreatic polypeptide levels; Glucose infusion rate required to maintain clamp; Plasma glucose levels after infusion suspension
extraction_notes: Randomized single-blinded crossover design with participants receiving both atropine and saline on separate occasions. Sample size n=10 for main study, n=5 for control experiments. Primary vs secondary outcomes not explicitly designated in abstract.

title: Mucosal glucagon-like peptide-1 and glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide cell numbers in the super-obese human foregut after gastric bypass.
journal: Surgery for obesity and related diseases : official journal of the American Society for Bariatric Surgery
population: Super-obese nondiabetic patients undergoing laparoscopic Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (RYGB) with body mass index >50 kg/m²
intervention: Laparoscopic Roux-en-Y gastric bypass with biliopancreatic limb of 200 cm (BP200)
comparison: Laparoscopic Roux-en-Y gastric bypass with biliopancreatic limb of 60 cm (BP60)
outcomes_secondary: Mucosal height; density of hormone-producing cell populations (GLP-1, GIP, PYY, ghrelin, cholecystokinin, neurotensin, secretin, serotonin, histamine, somatostatin); mRNA expression of gut hormones measured with real-time polymerase chain reaction; villi length
extraction_notes: Primary outcomes not explicitly distinguished from secondary outcomes in abstract. Sample size is 18 patients. Study is a randomized trial (NCT 01514799). Biopsies obtained intraoperatively and at 12 months via endoscopy.

title: Effects of wheat bran extract rich in arabinoxylan oligosaccharides and resistant starch on overnight glucose tolerance and markers of gut fermentation in healthy young adults.
population: Healthy young adults
intervention: Evening bread products: (1) White wheat flour bread supplemented with AXOS and resistant starch (WWB + AXOS + RS), (2) White wheat flour bread with increased content of AXOS (WWB + hiAXOS), (3) White wheat flour bread with increased content of resistant starch (WWB + hiRS)
comparison: Reference white wheat flour bread (WWB)
outcomes_primary: Glucose tolerance at subsequent standardized breakfast measured over 3 hours
outcomes_secondary: Insulin, nonesterified fatty acids, glucagon-like peptide (GLP)-1, GLP-2, breath hydrogen concentration, short chain fatty acids (SCFA), insulin sensitivity index, subjective appetite ratings using visual analog scales
extraction_notes: Randomized cross-over study design. Specific doses of AXOS and RS not provided in abstract. Sample size not specified. Duration of study/washout period not specified.

title: The 2-monoacylglycerol moiety of dietary fat appears to be responsible for the fat-induced release of GLP-1 in humans.
journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
population: Healthy white men, mean age 24 years, BMI 22 kg/m²
intervention: 200 g carrots + 13.15 g C8-dietary oil (1,3-dioctanoyl-2-oleoyl glycerol), single meal; 200 g carrots + 19 g olive oil, single meal; 200 g carrots + 6.53 g tributyrin, single meal; all lipids totaled 0.0216 mol
comparison: 200 g carrots alone (control meal); crossover comparison between tributyrin, C8-dietary oil, olive oil, and carrots alone
outcomes_primary: Incremental areas under the curve for total GLP-1, GIP, and cholecystokinin (CCK) in plasma
outcomes_secondary: Peptide YY (PYY) and neurotensin responses
extraction_notes: Sample size n=12. Single-blinded randomized crossover design with 4 meals on 4 different days. Study compared different lipid sources to understand mechanism of fat-induced incretin hormone release.

title: GSK2374697, a long duration glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist, reduces postprandial circulating endogenous total GLP-1 and peptide YY in healthy subjects.
population: Healthy subjects in two cohorts: one normal/overweight and one obese
intervention: GSK2374697 2 mg administered subcutaneously on days 1, 4 and 7
comparison: Placebo administered subcutaneously on days 1, 4 and 7
outcomes_primary: Weighted mean area under the curve (0-4 h) of postprandial endogenous total GLP-1; Weighted mean area under the curve (0-4 h) of postprandial peptide YY (PYY)
extraction_notes: Sample sizes differ between cohorts: normal/overweight cohort had n=8 active and n=4 placebo; obese cohort had n=8 active and n=2 placebo. Primary vs secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract.

title: Once-weekly glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist dulaglutide is non-inferior to once-daily liraglutide and superior to placebo in Japanese patients with type 2 diabetes: a 26-week randomized phase III study.
population: Japanese patients with type 2 diabetes; male or female; aged ≥20 years; OAM-naïve (diet and exercise only) or discontinued from oral antidiabetic medication monotherapy (excluding thiazolidinedione); body mass index 18.5–35.0 kg/m2; HbA1c 7.0–10.0% at randomization. Key exclusion criteria: type 1 diabetes, previous GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment, treatment with more than half of the sulphonylurea maximum dose at screening, current insulin or thiazolidinedione use, chronic systemic glucocorticoid use, or gastric emptying abnormality.
intervention: Dulaglutide 0.75 mg subcutaneous injection once weekly, initiated at full dose
comparison: 1) Placebo subcutaneous injection once weekly; 2) Liraglutide 0.9 mg subcutaneous injection once daily (uptitrated from 0.3 mg/day during week 1 to 0.6 mg/day during week 2 and 0.9 mg/day starting at week 3)
outcomes_primary: Change from baseline in glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c) at 26 weeks
outcomes_secondary: Non-inferiority and superiority of dulaglutide compared with liraglutide on HbA1c change from baseline; proportion of patients achieving HbA1c targets (<7.0% or ≤6.5%); change in fasting serum glucose from baseline; change in seven-point self-monitored blood glucose profiles from baseline; change in body weight from baseline; safety assessments including adverse events, vital signs (pulse rate and blood pressure), ECGs, laboratory variables, hypoglycaemia, and dulaglutide antidrug antibodies
extraction_notes: Trial design was double-blind for dulaglutide and placebo but open-label for liraglutide comparator. Randomization ratio was 4:2:1 (dulaglutide:liraglutide:placebo). 26-week primary endpoint is presented; study continued for 52 weeks total.

title: Efficacy and safety of liraglutide versus placebo added to basal insulin analogues (with or without metformin) in patients with type 2 diabetes: a randomized, placebo-controlled trial.

population: Adolescents aged 12-19 years with severe obesity (BMI ≥1.2 times the 95th percentile or BMI-SDS >2.3).
