intervention: Exenatide 5 mcg subcutaneously twice daily for 1 month, followed by exenatide 10 mcg subcutaneously twice daily for 2 additional months, plus lifestyle modification therapy (dietary and physical activity counseling)
comparison: Placebo (with identical delivery devices) plus lifestyle modification therapy; or lifestyle modification alone (control phase in crossover design)
outcomes_primary: Percent change in BMI from baseline at 3 months
outcomes_secondary: Predictors of BMI reduction including: baseline BMI, BMI percent change at 1 month, incidence of nausea/vomiting, baseline appetite and satiety measures (assessed via Child Eating Behavior Questionnaire subscales), sex, age, frequency of gastrointestinal symptoms
extraction_notes: Pooled analysis of two near-identical clinical trials (one open-label crossover, one double-blind placebo-controlled). Study focused on identifying predictors of treatment response rather than primary efficacy assessment. CEBQ data available only from first study (n=22). Analysis described as secondary and hypothesis-generating.

title: Patient-reported outcome results in patients with type 2 diabetes treated with once-weekly dulaglutide: data from the AWARD phase III clinical trial programme.
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes
intervention: Dulaglutide 1.5 mg and 0.75 mg, once-weekly administration
comparison: Insulin glargine, exenatide, metformin
outcomes_primary: Not explicitly specified
outcomes_secondary: Impact of Weight on Self-Perception (IW-SP), Impact of Weight on Ability to Perform Physical Activities of Daily Living (APPADL), Impact of Weight on Quality of Life-Lite, EQ-5D, Diabetes Treatment Satisfaction Questionnaire (DTSQ), Diabetes Symptom Checklist-Revised, Adult Low Blood Sugar Survey
extraction_notes: This is a pooled analysis of patient-reported outcomes from the AWARD clinical trial programme (multiple studies). Primary versus secondary outcome distinction not specified in abstract; all listed measures appear to be PRO instruments analyzed across one or more AWARD studies.

title: Subgroup analysis of phase 3 studies of dulaglutide in Japanese patients with type 2 diabetes.
population: Japanese patients with type 2 diabetes; subgroups defined by sex (male, female), age (<65, ≥65 years), body weight (<70, ≥70 kg), body mass index (<25, ≥25 kg/m²), duration of diabetes (<7, ≥7 years), HbA1c (≤8.5, >8.5%), use of concomitant sulfonylurea (yes, no), and use of concomitant biguanide (yes, no)
intervention: Dulaglutide 0.75 mg once weekly for up to 26 weeks
comparison: Post hoc subgroup analysis pooling data from three phase 3 trials; original comparators not specified in abstract
outcomes_primary: Not explicitly specified as primary in abstract
outcomes_secondary: Not explicitly specified as secondary in abstract; efficacy measures: change from baseline in HbA1c, change from baseline in body weight, percentage of patients achieving HbA1c <7.0%; safety measures: incidence of hypoglycemia, incidence of nausea, change from baseline in seated pulse rate
extraction_notes: This is a post hoc pooled subgroup analysis of three phase 3 trials (one open-label randomized, one double-blind and open-label randomized, one open-label nonrandomized). Original comparator arms from parent trials not described. Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly labeled as such.

title: Meal sequence and glucose excursion, gastric emptying and incretin secretion in type 2 diabetes: a randomised, controlled crossover, exploratory trial.
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes (n=12) and healthy volunteers (n=10), aged 30-75 years, HbA1c 9.0% (75 mmol/mol) or less, BMI 35 kg/m2 or less. Exclusion criteria: type 1 diabetes, gastrointestinal tract disease including gastroparesis, history of gastrointestinal operation, cardiac disease, pulmonary disease, pancreatic disease, liver disease, renal disease, alcohol or drug abuse, glucose-lowering medication, diabetogenic medication, malignancy, pregnancy, or allergy to mackerel.
intervention: Fish before rice (FR): 920 kJ boiled mackerel consumed first, followed by 1004 kJ steamed rice 15 minutes later. Meat before rice (MR): 920 kJ grilled beef consumed first, followed by 1004 kJ steamed rice 15 minutes later.
comparison: Rice before fish (RF): 1004 kJ steamed rice consumed first, followed by 920 kJ boiled mackerel 15 minutes later.
outcomes_primary: Postprandial glucose excursion (AUC glucose), glucose variability (SD glucose)
outcomes_secondary: Gastric emptying rate (Time50% by 13C-acetate breath test), GLP-1 secretion (AUC GLP-1), GIP secretion (AUC GIP), insulin secretion (AUC insulin), C-peptide levels (AUC C-peptide), glucagon secretion (AUC glucagon)
extraction_notes: This was a single-center, randomized controlled crossover exploratory trial conducted in Japan. Participants, those performing measurements, and outcome assessors were not blinded. The study did not explicitly designate primary vs secondary outcomes; classification based on stated objectives.

title: L-rhamnose as a source of colonic propionate inhibits insulin secretion but does not influence measures of appetite or food intake.
population: Healthy unrestrained eaters
intervention: L-rhamnose 25.5 g/d alongside standardized breakfast and lunch, following a 6-day run-in period
comparison: Inulin 22.4 g/d; No supplement (control)
outcomes_secondary: Postprandial qualitative appetite; Breath hydrogen; Plasma glucose; Plasma insulin; Plasma triglycerides; Plasma non-esterified fatty acids; Ad libitum meal intake (quantitative appetite); Meal desire; Desire to eat sweet
extraction_notes: Primary outcomes not explicitly distinguished from secondary outcomes in the abstract. Study design: single-blind randomized crossover. Sample size n=13. Outcomes assessed over 420 minutes postprandially.

title: Capsaicin-induced satiety is associated with gastrointestinal distress but not with the release of satiety hormones.
journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
population: Healthy volunteers; 13 participants (7 women), mean age 21.5 years, BMI 22.8 kg/m²
intervention: Intraduodenal infusion of 1.5 mg pure capsaicin administered via nasoduodenal catheter over 30 minutes
comparison: Placebo (physiologic saline) intraduodenal infusion
outcomes_primary: Hunger, satiety, and gastrointestinal symptoms measured by visual analog scale scores; plasma concentrations of GLP-1 and PYY
outcomes_secondary: Gallbladder volumes measured using real-time ultrasonography
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract; all outcomes listed appear to be of equal importance in the study design. Population characteristics include baseline statistics that may not be strict eligibility criteria.

title: Effects of exenatide and liraglutide on 24-hour glucose fluctuations in type 2 diabetes.
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes inadequately controlled by sulfonylureas
intervention: Add-on exenatide 10 μg/day twice daily
comparison: Add-on liraglutide 0.3-0.9 mg/day once daily
outcomes_primary: Daily blood glucose fluctuations assessed by mean amplitude of glycemic excursion (MAGE) and standard deviation (SD) via 24-hour continuous subcutaneous glucose monitoring
outcomes_secondary: Mean blood glucose levels at specific time points (3 hours after breakfast, 3 hours after dinner, between 0000h and 0600h)
extraction_notes: Open-label trial design. Primary vs secondary outcome distinction not explicitly stated in abstract; outcomes listed based on apparent focus of the study.

title: Efficacy and safety of liraglutide 3.0 mg for weight management are similar across races: subgroup analysis across the SCALE and phase II randomized trials.
population: Adults with body mass index (BMI) ≥27 kg/m2 with at least one comorbidity, or BMI ≥30 kg/m2; men and women; racial subgroups including white, black/African-American, Asian, and other
intervention: Liraglutide 3.0 mg once-daily subcutaneous injection, starting at 0.6 mg with weekly 0.6 mg increments to 3.0 mg, as adjunct to reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity; treatment duration 32-56 weeks depending on trial
comparison: Placebo (matching once-daily subcutaneous injection) as adjunct to reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity
outcomes_primary: Mean relative and absolute weight loss from baseline to end of treatment; categorical weight loss (≥5%, >10%, >15% of baseline body weight)
outcomes_secondary: Cardiovascular risk markers (including HbA1c, fasting plasma glucose, systolic blood pressure); glycaemic control variables in participants with T2DM and in those with prediabetes or normoglycaemia; health-related quality of life (IWQoL-Lite questionnaire, SF-36); safety outcomes including overall adverse events, serious adverse events, events leading to discontinuation, gastrointestinal disorders, resting pulse
extraction_notes: Post hoc pooled analysis of data from five randomized controlled trials (four SCALE phase IIIa trials and one phase II trial). The analysis was exploratory and trials were not designed or powered for racial subgroup comparisons. Primary versus secondary outcome distinction not explicitly stated in text; categorization inferred from presentation order and emphasis.

title: Effect of meal composition on postprandial glucagon-like peptide-1, insulin, glucagon, C-peptide, and glucose responses in overweight/obese subjects.
population: Overweight/obese participants without type 2 diabetes
intervention: High protein (HP) meal containing 31.9% energy from protein
comparison: High monounsaturated fat (HMF) meal containing 35.2% fat and 20.7% monounsaturated fat; both meals contained the same energy and carbohydrate content
outcomes_primary: GLP-1 response (active GLP-1 and total GLP-1)
outcomes_secondary: Insulin, glucagon, C-peptide, glucose responses, insulin sensitivity (Matsuda index), appetite ratings
extraction_notes: Crossover design with meals consumed in random order. Sample size n=24. Primary outcome not explicitly designated; GLP-1 response inferred as primary based on stated purpose.

title: Jejunal feeding is followed by a greater rise in plasma cholecystokinin, peptide YY, glucagon-like peptide 1, and glucagon-like peptide 2 concentrations compared with gastric feeding in vivo in humans: a randomized trial.
journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
population: Healthy young men
intervention: Continuous enteral nutrition containing noncoagulating proteins for 12 hours via nasojejunal tube placed 30-40 cm distal to the ligament of Treitz
comparison: Continuous enteral nutrition containing noncoagulating proteins for 12 hours via nasogastric tube
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract. Outcomes measured include: postprandial rise in plasma glucose concentrations, plasma amino acid concentrations, plasma insulin concentrations, plasma cholecystokinin concentrations, plasma peptide YY concentrations, plasma glucagon-like peptide 1 concentrations, plasma glucagon-like peptide 2 concentrations, plasma ghrelin concentrations, and incremental AUC for gastrointestinal hormones. Sample size n=12. Randomized crossover design.

title: A Protein Preload Enhances the Glucose-Lowering Efficacy of Vildagliptin in Type 2 Diabetes.
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes treated with metformin
intervention: Vildagliptin 50 mg (administered on evening before and morning of study day) combined with whey protein preload (25 g whey protein drink given 60 minutes after vildagliptin dose, 30 minutes before meal)
comparison: Four treatment conditions: 1) Placebo with control flavoring (PLBO/CTRL), 2) Placebo with whey protein preload (PLBO/WHEY), 3) Vildagliptin with control flavoring (VILD/CTRL), 4) Vildagliptin with whey protein preload (VILD/WHEY)
outcomes_primary: Not explicitly specified as primary
outcomes_secondary: Not explicitly specified as secondary; measured outcomes included: plasma glucose, postprandial peak glycemia, area under the curve for glucose, plasma insulin, plasma glucagon, plasma incretin hormones (total and intact GLP-1 and GIP), gastric emptying
extraction_notes: Crossover design study with 22 patients studied on four occasions. Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly designated in abstract. The 13C-octanoate-labeled mashed potato meal was used to evaluate gastric emptying.

title: Effects of endogenous GLP-1 and GIP on glucose tolerance after Roux-en-Y gastric bypass surgery.
journal: American journal of physiology. Endocrinology and metabolism
population: Glucose-tolerant patients after Roux-en-Y gastric bypass surgery
intervention: Oral sitagliptin (DPP-4 inhibitor), exendin-(9-39) intravenous infusion (GLP-1 receptor antagonist), or combined exendin-(9-39) plus sitagliptin, administered with standard mixed-meal tests
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Glucose tolerance, β-cell function
outcomes_secondary: Postprandial glucagon secretion, concentrations of intact GLP-1 and GIP
extraction_notes: Small sample size (n=12). Study described as randomized placebo-controlled 4-day crossover design. Specific doses, frequencies, and durations of interventions not provided in abstract. Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished.

title: Protein-Enriched Liquid Preloads Varying in Macronutrient Content Modulate Appetite and Appetite-Regulating Hormones in Healthy Adults.
population: Healthy adults, mean age 27 ± 5 years, body mass index 24.3 ± 1.6 kg/m²
intervention: Protein-enriched liquid preloads with varying macronutrient composition: 9%, 24%, or 40% of energy from protein combined with carbohydrate-to-fat ratios of 0.4, 2, or 3.6; isovolumetric (670 mL) and isoenergetic (2100 kJ) liquid preloads matched for energy density and sensory properties, consumed as breakfast
comparison: Within-subjects comparison of 7 different liquid preloads varying in protein content (low-protein 9%, medium-protein 24%, high-protein 40%) and carbohydrate-to-fat ratios (0.4, 2, 3.6)
outcomes_primary: Appetite ratings, energy intake at ad libitum lunch test meal served 3.5 hours after breakfast
outcomes_secondary: Biomarkers of satiety including glucose, insulin, glucagon-like peptide 1, and ghrelin; prospective consumption; fullness ratings
extraction_notes: Randomized within-subjects 2-level factorial design with 36 participants; 7 preload conditions total but exact combinations not fully specified; baseline statistics for age and BMI reported but unclear if these were strict inclusion criteria

title: A 24-week study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of once-weekly dulaglutide added on to glimepiride in type 2 diabetes (AWARD-8).
population: Adult men and women aged ≥18 years with type 2 diabetes, BMI ≤45 kg/m², HbA1c ≥7.5% and ≤9.5% (≥58 and ≤80 mmol/mol), on stable dose of sulphonylurea at least 50% of maximum dose for at least 3 months. Exclusions: treatment with other antihyperglycaemic medications within 3 months, history of pancreatitis, signs or symptoms of liver disease, impaired renal function (eGFR <30 ml/min/1.73 m²), elevated serum calcitonin (≥20 ng/L), recent history of severe hypoglycaemia.
intervention: Dulaglutide 1.5 mg once weekly, subcutaneous injection, initiated at full 1.5 mg dose, added to glimepiride, for 24 weeks
comparison: Matching placebo once weekly, subcutaneous injection, added to glimepiride
outcomes_primary: Change in HbA1c from baseline at 24 weeks
outcomes_secondary: Percentage of patients achieving HbA1c <7.0% (<53 mmol/mol); change from baseline in fasting serum glucose; change from baseline in body weight; percentage of patients achieving HbA1c ≤6.5% (48 mmol/mol); seven-point self-monitored plasma glucose profiles; safety assessments including adverse events, serious adverse events, hypoglycaemia, vital signs, ECGs, antidrug antibodies, pancreatic events, cardiovascular events
extraction_notes: Randomization ratio was 4:1 (dulaglutide:placebo). N=300 randomized (240 dulaglutide, 60 placebo). Phase IIIb study. During lead-in, participants either continued prestudy glimepiride or switched from other SU to equivalent glimepiride dose.

title: Circulating adiponectin levels in type 2 diabetes mellitus patients with or without non-alcoholic fatty liver disease: Results of a small, open-label, randomized controlled intervention trial in a subgroup receiving short-term exenatide.
population: Type 2 diabetes mellitus patients with abnormal aminotransferases, subgroup assessed for eligibility criteria (n=110)
intervention: 6-month exenatide supplementation on glargine insulin
comparison: Intense, self-regulated, insulin therapy alone
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract. Outcomes measured include circulating adiponectin levels, weight loss, HbA1c, and C-reactive protein. Study described as small, open-label, randomized controlled intervention trial. Randomization described as 'blindly randomized' but also labeled 'open-label' which is contradictory. A separate non-randomized group (group A, n=17) underwent liver biopsy for NAFLD assessment.

title: Liraglutide is effective and well tolerated in combination with an oral antidiabetic drug in Japanese patients with type 2 diabetes: A randomized, 52-week, open-label, parallel-group trial.
population: Male and female Japanese patients aged ≥20 years with type 2 diabetes for at least 6 months, HbA1c levels of 7.0–10.0%, body mass index <40.0 kg/m2, receiving OAD monotherapy (glinide, metformin, α-glucosidase inhibitor or thiazolidinedione) with inadequate glycemic control. Exclusions included use of GLP-1 receptor agonist, DPP-4 inhibitor or insulin within past 12 weeks, personal history of non-familial medullary thyroid carcinoma, family or personal history of multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2 or familial medullary thyroid carcinoma, malignant tumor, history of chronic pancreatitis or idiopathic acute pancreatitis, calcitonin ≥160 pg/mL, recurrent severe hypoglycemia, hypoglycemia unawareness, or hospitalization for diabetic ketoacidosis during previous 6 months
intervention: Liraglutide 0.9 mg/day subcutaneous injection once daily (starting dose 0.3 mg/day, escalated to 0.6 mg/day after 1 week, then to 0.9 mg/day after a further week) in combination with pretrial OAD (glinide, metformin, α-glucosidase inhibitor or thiazolidinedione) for 52 weeks
comparison: Pretrial OAD in combination with an additional OAD with a different mechanism of action (DPP-4 inhibitor, SU, glinide, metformin, α-glucosidase inhibitor or thiazolidinedione) for 52 weeks
outcomes_primary: Incidence of adverse events during 52 weeks
outcomes_secondary: Number of hypoglycemic episodes during 52 weeks; changes from baseline in vital signs (blood pressure and pulse rate); change from baseline in HbA1c; change from baseline in fasting plasma glucose; patients achieving target HbA1c <7.0%; change from baseline in bodyweight; change from baseline in β-cell function (HOMA-B, proinsulin:insulin ratio, proinsulin:C-peptide ratio); seven-point self-measured plasma glucose profiles (change from baseline in mean plasma glucose and mean prandial plasma glucose increment)
extraction_notes: Open-label study design. Randomization was 2:1 ratio (liraglutide:additional OAD). The additional OAD type, dosage and administration were chosen by the investigator within approved labeling, resulting in heterogeneous comparator group.

title: Comparison of short-term energy intake and appetite responses to active and seated video gaming, in 8-11-year-old boys.
population: 8-11-year-old boys
intervention: 90-minute active video gaming with ad libitum food and drinks provided
comparison: 90-minute seated video gaming with ad libitum food and drinks provided
outcomes_primary: Energy intake during gaming sessions
outcomes_secondary: Blood glucose; plasma glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-17-36); subjective appetite (hunger, prospective food consumption, fullness); energy intake at post-gaming test meal 1 hour later; relative energy intake; estimated energy expenditure
extraction_notes: Crossover randomised design. Primary outcome not explicitly distinguished from secondary outcomes in abstract; classification based on emphasis in text. Sample size n=22.

title: Efficacy and tolerability of exenatide twice daily and exenatide once weekly in Asian versus White patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus: A pooled analysis.
population: Asian and White patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), race was self-identified
intervention: Exenatide 10μg twice daily (BID) for 12-30 weeks or exenatide 2mg once weekly (QW) for 24-30 weeks
comparison: Asian versus White patients (within each exenatide formulation group)
extraction_notes: This is a post-hoc pooled analysis of exenatide clinical development program trials. Primary and secondary outcomes were not explicitly distinguished in the abstract. Outcomes assessed included glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c), fasting glucose (FG), body weight, post-prandial glucose (PPG), PPG excursions, and adverse events. No placebo or active comparator drug group mentioned - comparison is between racial groups receiving the same treatment.

title: The insulinotropic effect of pulsatile compared with continuous intravenous delivery of GLP-1.
population: Healthy individuals aged 18-35 years
intervention: Pulsatile intravenous infusion of GLP-1 (3.6 pmol/kg bolus every 6 minutes) with placebo continuous infusion at 1 ml/min
comparison: Continuous intravenous infusion of GLP-1 (0.6 pmol kg-1 min-1 at 1 ml/min) with 1 ml placebo bolus every 6 minutes; Placebo (placebo at 1 ml/min and 1 ml placebo bolus every 6 minutes)
outcomes_primary: Insulinotropic response (insulin secretion)
outcomes_secondary: Dextrose requirement during hyperglycaemic clamp; plasma glucagon concentrations; venous blood glucose concentrations
extraction_notes: Primary outcome not explicitly labeled but implied from study aims. Study used hyperglycaemic clamp to maintain blood glucose at 9 mmol/l between 45 and 120 minutes.

title: GLP-1 receptors exist in the parietal cortex, hypothalamus and medulla of human brains and the GLP-1 analogue liraglutide alters brain activity related to highly desirable food cues in individuals with diabetes: a crossover, randomised, placebo-controlled trial.
population: Adults with type 2 diabetes (defined as fasting plasma glucose > 6.94 mmol/l and/or HbA1c > 6.5% or 47.5 mmol/mol), currently being treated with lifestyle changes or metformin
intervention: Liraglutide subcutaneous injection, dose escalation: 0.6 mg daily for 7 days, 1.2 mg daily for 7 days, 1.8 mg daily for 3 days (total 17 days treatment)
comparison: Placebo (identical dosing schedule, 17 days total)
outcomes_primary: Neural responses to food cues measured by functional MRI (fMRI) brain activation
outcomes_secondary: Expression of GLP-1 receptors in human brain tissue (hypothalamus, medulla oblongata, parietal cortex) via immunohistochemistry; metabolic changes (fasting blood glucose, HbA1c, fructosamine, lipid profiles); anthropometric measurements (weight, BMI, waist circumference, fat mass); resting metabolic rate; energy intake; subjective ratings of hunger, appetite, and nausea via visual analogue scale; neurocognitive testing (CANTAB device)
extraction_notes: Study includes two components: Study 1 is immunohistochemistry on 22 autopsy brain samples (separate from RCT); Study 2 is the crossover RCT with 21 enrolled, 18 analyzed. Crossover design with minimum 3-week washout period between arms.

title: Exposure-response analyses of liraglutide 3.0 mg for weight management.
population: Adults with obesity (BMI ≥30 kg/m2) or overweight with weight-related comorbidities; Trial 1: obese (BMI ≥30 kg/m2) or overweight adults (BMI 27-29.9 kg/m2) with treated or untreated hypertension and/or dyslipidaemia; Trial 2: obese or overweight (BMI ≥27 kg/m2) adults with type 2 diabetes (HbA1c 7.0-10.0%) treated with diet and exercise alone or with up to three of metformin, sulphonylurea and/or thiazolidinedione; Trial 3: obese adults (BMI ≥30.0 and ≤40.0 kg/m2)
intervention: Liraglutide subcutaneous injection at doses of 1.2 mg, 1.8 mg, 2.4 mg, or 3.0 mg daily as adjunct to diet and exercise; Trial 1: 56 weeks duration; Trial 2: 56 weeks duration; Trial 3: 20 weeks duration
comparison: Placebo (Trials 1, 2, 3); Orlistat 120 mg three times daily (Trial 3 only)
outcomes_primary: Exposure-response relationship for body weight change from baseline; proportion of individuals achieving ≥5% and >10% weight loss
outcomes_secondary: Exposure-response relationship for HbA1c change from baseline (in individuals with type 2 diabetes); safety outcomes including nausea, vomiting, documented symptomatic hypoglycaemia, resting pulse, serum calcitonin, gallbladder adverse events, acute pancreatitis, malignant neoplasms, malignant breast neoplasms, benign colorectal neoplasms
extraction_notes: This is a pooled exposure-response analysis from one phase II and two phase IIIa trials (n=4372 total). Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly designated; outcomes listed based on analysis content. Different trial durations (20 weeks vs 56 weeks).

title: Phase III Study on Efficacy and Safety of Triple Combination (Exenatide/Metformin/Biphasic Insulin Aspart) Therapy for Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.
population: Patients with poorly controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus
intervention: Normal-dose triple combination therapy: exenatide 2 μg twice daily, biphasic insulin aspart 30 (BIA30) 0.2 U·kg·d twice daily, and metformin 0.05 g twice daily for 48 weeks
comparison: Low-dose triple combination therapy: exenatide 0.5 μg twice daily, biphasic insulin aspart 30 (BIA30) 0.05 U·kg·d twice daily, and metformin 0.01 g twice daily for 48 weeks
outcomes_primary: Hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) levels
outcomes_secondary: Weight change; insulin sensitivity; adiponectin levels; C-reactive protein levels; tumor necrosis factor-α levels; resistin levels; adverse effects
extraction_notes: No explicit distinction between primary and secondary outcomes stated in abstract; outcomes categorized based on presentation order. No placebo or standard care comparator - both arms received triple combination therapy at different doses.

title: Effects of liraglutide on no-reflow in patients with acute ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction.
population: Patients with acute ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI)
intervention: Liraglutide 1.8 mg administered 30 minutes before PCI
comparison: Placebo administered 30 minutes before PCI
outcomes_primary: Prevalence of no-reflow after PCI
outcomes_secondary: Serum high-sensitivity C-reactive protein levels at 6-hour reperfusion; incidence of major adverse cardiovascular events during 3-month follow-up
extraction_notes: Randomization was 1:1; 284 patients enrolled but only 210 were randomized, suggesting some exclusions not detailed in abstract

title: LEADER-4: blood pressure control in patients with type 2 diabetes and high cardiovascular risk: baseline data from the LEADER randomized trial.
population: Adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus aged at least 50 years with concomitant cardiovascular disease, cerebrovascular disease, peripheral vascular disease, chronic renal failure, or chronic heart failure; or aged at least 60 years with one or more cardiovascular risk factors (microalbuminuria or proteinuria, hypertension, left ventricular hypertrophy, left ventricular dysfunction, or ankle-brachial index less than 0.9); baseline HbA1c at least 7.0%; exclusion criteria included type 1 diabetes, calcitonin at least 50 ng/l, use of GLP-1 receptor agonists, DPP-4 inhibitors, or specified insulin preparations within 3 months prior to screening
intervention: Liraglutide (GLP-1 receptor agonist) for at least 3.5 years and up to 5 years (dose not specified in abstract)
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Incidence of cardiovascular events defined as cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or nonfatal stroke
extraction_notes: This paper reports baseline data only from the LEADER trial (NCT01179048), not trial results. The primary analysis focuses on blood pressure control at baseline prior to randomization. Liraglutide dose not specified in the abstract or main text. Secondary outcomes for the main LEADER trial not specified in this publication.

title: Difference in postprandial GLP-1 response despite similar glucose kinetics after consumption of wheat breads with different particle size in healthy men.
population: Healthy men, age 24 ± 0.6 years, BMI 22 ± 0.2 kg/m2. Exclusion criteria: use of medication, blood donation or use of antibiotics in the past three months, gastrointestinal surgery or dysfunction, inflammatory diseases, and diabetes mellitus.
intervention: Kernel bread (KB): 137g portion providing 50g available carbohydrates, made with 85% broken wheat kernels substituted for flour, consumed with 10g light margarine, 2 slices lean ham, and 250mL tap water within 20 minutes. Single administration in crossover design with at least 1 week washout between study days.
comparison: Control bread (CB): 138g portion providing 50g available carbohydrates, made from wheat flour combined with wheat bran (same dietary fiber content as KB), consumed with 10g light margarine, 2 slices lean ham, and 250mL tap water within 20 minutes.
outcomes_primary: Postprandial glucose kinetics including rate of appearance of exogenous glucose (RaE), endogenous glucose production (EGP), and glucose clearance rate (GCR); postprandial plasma glucose concentrations.
outcomes_secondary: Postprandial plasma concentrations of insulin, glucagon, incretins (GIP, GLP-1), cholecystokinin (CCK), and bile acids; 13CO2 excretion in breath; incremental areas under the curve (iAUC) at 0-2h and 0-6h; subjective appetite ratings (VAS); discomfort ratings; meal liking ratings.
extraction_notes: This study is part of a larger 4-treatment crossover study but only 2 treatments are reported here. Sample size is small (n=10) and insufficient to detect differences in subjective appetite measures as noted by authors. Primary outcome was not explicitly stated; categorization based on study objectives described in introduction.

title: Ghrelin, GLP-1, and leptin responses during exposure to moderate hypoxia.
journal: Applied physiology, nutrition, and metabolism = Physiologie appliquee, nutrition et metabolisme
population: Healthy males, age approximately 21 years
intervention: Rest trial in moderate hypoxia (FiO2 = 15.0%) for 7 hours in an environmental chamber, with standard meals provided at 1 hour (745 kcal) and 4 hours (731 kcal) after initiating exposure
comparison: Rest trial in normoxia (FiO2 = 20.9%) for 7 hours in an environmental chamber, with identical meal timing and composition
outcomes_secondary: Plasma active ghrelin concentrations; area under the curve for plasma active ghrelin concentrations over 7 hours; glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1) concentrations; leptin concentrations; subjective appetite scores including hunger and fullness
extraction_notes: Small sample size (n=8). Primary vs secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract. This appears to be a mechanistic/physiological study rather than a clinical trial.

title: LEADER 5: prevalence and cardiometabolic impact of obesity in cardiovascular high-risk patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus: baseline global data from the LEADER trial.
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus at high cardiovascular risk enrolled in LEADER trial from 32 countries: (1) aged ≥50 years with prior cardiovascular disease (CVD), cerebrovascular disease, peripheral vascular disease, chronic renal failure, or chronic heart failure; (2) aged ≥60 years with one or more CV risk factors including microalbuminuria or proteinuria, hypertension and left ventricular hypertrophy, left ventricular dysfunction, or ankle-brachial index <0.9
intervention: Liraglutide up to 1.8 mg daily (glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist)
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Cardiovascular safety of liraglutide (primary outcome of main LEADER trial); this sub-study (LEADER 5) analyzed baseline cross-sectional data for: prevalence of overweight and obesity; relationship between cardiometabolic risk factors and anthropometric measures (BMI and waist circumference); treatment intensity in relation to BMI and waist circumference categories
outcomes_secondary: Not explicitly defined for this baseline analysis sub-study
extraction_notes: This publication (LEADER 5) reports baseline cross-sectional data only from the LEADER trial, not longitudinal outcomes. The PICO elements reflect the main LEADER trial design, but this specific analysis focuses on observational associations at baseline rather than intervention effects.

title: Flaked sorghum biscuits increase postprandial GLP-1 and GIP levels and extend subjective satiety in healthy subjects.
population: Healthy subjects; 40 participants in main trial, subset of 20 subjects for plasma measurements
intervention: Whole grain sorghum flaked biscuits (white, red, or brown sorghum varieties), 50 grams consumed after 12-hour fast
comparison: Wheat control biscuits, 50 grams
outcomes_primary: Subjective satiety measured at 8 time-points over four hours
outcomes_secondary: Plasma glucose, insulin, gastric inhibitory peptide (GIP), glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1), peptide-tyrosine-tyrosine (PYY), ghrelin; energy intake at subsequent meal
extraction_notes: Study design is randomized cross-over trial. Primary vs secondary outcomes not explicitly designated in abstract; categorization based on description emphasis. Subjects tested on four occasions corresponding to four treatment meals.

title: Pharmacokinetic and Pharmacodynamic Effects of Multiple-dose Administration of Omarigliptin, a Once-weekly Dipeptidyl Peptidase-4 Inhibitor, in Obese Participants With and Without Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.
population: Obese participants with and without type 2 diabetes mellitus, aged 45 to 65 years, body mass index ≥30 and ≤40 kg/m², including obese but otherwise healthy subjects (panel A) and obese patients with T2DM who were treatment naive with hemoglobin A1c ≥6.5% and ≤10.0% (panel B)

title: Exenatide decreases liver fat content and epicardial adipose tissue in patients with obesity and type 2 diabetes: a prospective randomized clinical trial using magnetic resonance imaging and spectroscopy.

intervention: Exenatide for 26 weeks
comparison: Reference treatment according to French guidelines
outcomes_primary: Epicardial adipose tissue (EAT), myocardial triglyceride content (MTGC), hepatic triglyceride content (HTGC), and pancreatic triglyceride content (PTGC) assessed with 3T magnetic resonance imaging and proton magnetic resonance spectroscopy 45 min after a standardized meal
outcomes_secondary: HbA1c, body weight, homeostatic model assessment of insulin resistance index, adiponectin, fructosamine
extraction_notes: Primary vs secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract; outcomes listed based on study aim and methods. Reference treatment not specifically defined beyond 'according to French guidelines'.

title: The Effects of a Hypocaloric Diet on Diet-Induced Thermogenesis and Blood Hormone Response in Healthy Male Adults: A Pilot Study.
journal: Journal of nutritional science and vitaminology
population: Healthy male adults
intervention: Extremely hypocaloric meal (200 kcal) and moderately hypocaloric meal (400 kcal)
comparison: Normocaloric meal (800 kcal)
outcomes_primary: Diet-induced thermogenesis (DIT); postprandial blood hormone responses including pancreatic peptide, ghrelin, insulin, amylin, glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP), and glucagon-like peptide type-1 (GLP-1)
outcomes_secondary: Thermogenic efficiency (DIT per energy intake); postprandial energy expenditure
extraction_notes: Pilot study with crossover design; sample size of 10 participants; measurement duration differed between conditions (4 hours for hypocaloric meals vs 6 hours for normocaloric meal); primary vs secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract

title: Insulin resistance, postprandial GLP-1 and adaptive immunity are the main predictors of NAFLD in a homogeneous population at high cardiovascular risk.
journal: Nutrition, metabolism, and cardiovascular diseases : NMCD
population: Individuals with high waist circumference and at least one more criterion for metabolic syndrome; 70 participants at high cardio-metabolic risk
intervention: Nutritional intervention (specific details not provided in abstract)
comparison: Not explicitly stated
outcomes_primary: Liver fat content evaluated by hepatic/renal echo intensity ratio (H/R)
outcomes_secondary: Dietary habits (7-day dietary record); insulin sensitivity and β-cell function (fasting and OGTT-derived indices); fasting and postprandial plasma GLP-1; lipoproteins; plasma inflammatory markers
extraction_notes: This appears to be a cross-sectional baseline analysis from a nutritional intervention study (NCT01154478). The abstract focuses on baseline correlations rather than intervention effects. Specific details of the nutritional intervention are not provided. The comparison group is not explicitly defined.

title: Comparative evaluation of the therapeutic effect of metformin monotherapy with metformin and acupuncture combined therapy on weight loss and insulin sensitivity in diabetic patients.
population: Adults aged 20-65 years with type 2 diabetes mellitus diagnosed per American Diabetes Association criteria, overweight with BMI ≥25, using metformin monotherapy (500 mg one/two/three times per day). Exclusions: nephrotic syndrome, edema, renal failure, heart failure (NYHA III-IV), implanted pacemaker, liver dysfunction, HbA1c >9%, pregnant or nursing mothers, receiving insulin therapy, receiving other therapy or dosage changes during study period, endocrine abnormalities (thyroid disease, polycystic ovarian syndrome), receiving weight loss supplements/anti-depressants/hormonal medicine in last 3 months, homeostasis disorders or systemic diseases
intervention: Metformin monotherapy plus electro-acupuncture (EA) and auricular acupuncture (Aa). EA at 10 body acupoints (Zhongwan REN 12, Tianshu ST 25, Zusanli ST 36, Sanyinjiao SP 6, Shuifen REN 9, Hegu LI 4, Daheng SP 15, Shuidao ST 28, Quchi LI 11, Qihai REN 6) and 6 ear acupoints (Sanjiao, Jidian, Wei, Shenmen, Neifenmi, Pi). EA using Hwato SDZ-II machine, frequency 15 Hz/10 mA, for 30 minutes. Copper needles 0.25 mm × 0.40 mm inserted to muscle layer with de-qi sensation. Treatment 10 times every other day for 3 weeks total duration
comparison: Metformin monotherapy plus sham electro-acupuncture and sham auricular acupuncture. Sham EA: needles inserted 0.3 cm laterally from abdominal acupoints and 0.5 cm up and 0.5 cm laterally from other acupoints, superficial needling, electric lines connected but EA machine switched off during 30-minute treatment. Sham Aa: sticky layers without seeds
outcomes_primary: HOMA index (homeostasis model assessment for insulin resistance)
outcomes_secondary: Body weight, BMI, fasting blood sugar (FBS), fasting insulin (FINS), IL-6, TNF-α, CRP, leptin, adiponectin, GLP-1, resistin, serotonin, free fatty acids (FFAs), triglyceride (TG), LDL cholesterol, HDL cholesterol, ceramides
extraction_notes: Study described as randomized double-blind (subject and assessor) placebo-controlled trial. Sample size calculation based on HOMA index as primary outcome. Blood collected at baseline, fifth treatment, and end of study. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT02438540

title: Increased colonic propionate reduces anticipatory reward responses in the human striatum to high-energy foods.
journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
population: Healthy men aged 18-65 years with BMI 20-35 kg/m². Exclusion criteria: weight change >3 kg in previous 3 months, chronic illness or gastrointestinal disorder, history of drug or alcohol abuse in previous 2 years, use of antibiotics or medications likely to interfere with energy homeostasis in previous 3 months, claustrophobia, contraindications for MRI scanning, daily smoking, gluten or lactose intolerance, vegan or vegetarian diet, or depression (Beck Depression Inventory II score >10)
intervention: Inulin-propionate ester (IPE) 10 g, single dose, consumed orally with breakfast (chocolate milkshake and snack bar)
comparison: Control inulin 10 g, single dose, consumed orally with breakfast (chocolate milkshake and snack bar)
outcomes_primary: Blood oxygen level-dependent (BOLD) signal measured by fMRI in a priori brain regions involved in reward processing (caudate, nucleus accumbens, amygdala, anterior insula, and orbitofrontal cortex) during food picture evaluation task
outcomes_secondary: Ad libitum energy intake at test meal; subjective food appeal ratings during fMRI task; reaction time to rate food pictures; plasma peptide YY (PYY) concentrations; plasma glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1) concentrations; plasma glucose concentrations; serum insulin concentrations; serum short-chain fatty acid concentrations; breath hydrogen concentrations; composite appetite visual analog scale ratings
extraction_notes: Randomized, placebo-controlled, single-blind, crossover design. 20 participants enrolled; 18 had analyzable fMRI data (2 excluded for poor task compliance); 15 had analyzable energy intake data (5 excluded for consuming all presented food). Study visits separated by ≥6 days.

title: Combination therapy with liraglutide and insulin in Japanese patients with type 2 diabetes: A 36-week, randomized, double-blind, parallel-group trial.
population: Japanese adults aged ≥20 years with type 2 diabetes for ≥6 months, HbA1c 7.5–11.0% (59–97 mmol/mol), BMI <45.0 kg/m2, on stable insulin therapy (basal, premixed, or basal-bolus regimen) with daily dose ≥10 U for ≥12 weeks before screening, in addition to diet and exercise
intervention: Liraglutide 0.9 mg/day subcutaneous injection once daily (starting dose 0.3 mg/day, increased to 0.6 mg/day after 1 week, then to 0.9 mg/day after a further week) added to existing insulin therapy; insulin dose fixed for first 16 weeks, then titrated based on self-measured plasma glucose for remaining 20 weeks
comparison: Placebo subcutaneous injection once daily added to existing insulin therapy; insulin dose fixed for first 16 weeks, then titrated based on self-measured plasma glucose for remaining 20 weeks
outcomes_primary: Change in HbA1c from baseline after 16 weeks
outcomes_secondary: Change from baseline in HbA1c at 36 weeks; change from baseline in fasting plasma glucose at 16 and 36 weeks; proportion of patients achieving HbA1c <7.0% (<53 mmol/mol) and ≤6.5% (≤48 mmol/mol) at 16 and 36 weeks; proportion achieving HbA1c targets without weight gain; proportion achieving HbA1c targets with no severe/minor hypoglycemia during last 4 weeks; change from baseline in insulin dose at 36 weeks; change from baseline in bodyweight at 16 and 36 weeks; seven-point self-measured plasma glucose profiles; number of adverse events; number of hypoglycemic episodes; change from baseline in blood pressure and pulse
extraction_notes: Trial duration was 36 weeks total. Randomization was 1:1 (n=127 liraglutide, n=130 placebo). The liraglutide dose of 0.9 mg/day is the approved dose in Japan, lower than the 1.2-1.8 mg/day used in international studies.

title: Adjuvant Liraglutide and Insulin Versus Insulin Monotherapy in the Closed-Loop System in Type 1 Diabetes: A Randomized Open-Labeled Crossover Design Trial.
journal: Journal of diabetes science and technology
population: Patients with type 1 diabetes
intervention: Adjuvant subcutaneous liraglutide 1.2 mg once daily plus insulin using the closed-loop system
comparison: Insulin monotherapy using the closed-loop system
outcomes_primary: Blood glucose levels, postprandial blood glucose profiles
outcomes_secondary: Insulin concentrations, glucagon concentrations, area under the curve for postprandial blood glucose levels, area under the curve for glucagon, incidence of hypoglycemia, tolerability
extraction_notes: Open-label crossover design trial. Primary versus secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in the abstract; classification inferred from emphasis in text.

title: Combination of soya protein and polydextrose reduces energy intake and glycaemic response via modulation of gastric emptying rate, ghrelin and glucagon-like peptide-1 in Chinese.
population: Healthy, normotensive, lean Chinese men aged 21-40 years
intervention: High-protein soyabean curd with polydextrose preload; Low-protein soyabean curd with polydextrose preload
comparison: High-protein soyabean curd alone; Low-protein soyabean curd alone (four different soyabean curd preloads with or without polydextrose)
outcomes_primary: Energy intake at subsequent meal
outcomes_secondary: Glycaemic response; gastric emptying rate; ghrelin levels; glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) levels; gut hormone responses
extraction_notes: Study design is repeated-measure, randomised, cross-over. Sample size n=27. Specific doses of soya protein and polydextrose not provided in abstract. Duration of intervention/washout periods not specified.

title: Liraglutide 3.0 mg for Weight Management: A Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis.
population: Overweight or obese adults (BMI ≥27 kg/m² with weight-related comorbidities or BMI ≥30 kg/m²), with or without type 2 diabetes mellitus, aged 18 years and older
intervention: Liraglutide subcutaneous injection once daily, initiated at 0.6 mg/day with weekly 0.6 mg increments up to maximum 3.0 mg daily
comparison: Placebo (in Trials 1 and 2); Liraglutide 1.8 mg once daily (in Trial 2); Orlistat 120 mg thrice daily (in Trial 3, dose-finding study)
outcomes_primary: Population pharmacokinetic parameters including apparent clearance (CL/F), apparent volume (V/F), area under the curve (AUC), and dose proportionality of liraglutide exposure
outcomes_secondary: Effect of covariates on liraglutide exposure (body weight, sex, age, race, ethnicity, glycaemic status, injection site, renal function)
extraction_notes: This is a population pharmacokinetic analysis rather than a traditional efficacy RCT. Primary and secondary outcomes are pharmacokinetic parameters rather than clinical endpoints. Data were pooled from multiple trials (SCALE Obesity and Prediabetes, SCALE Diabetes, and a phase II dose-finding trial).

title: Mycoprotein reduces energy intake and postprandial insulin release without altering glucagon-like peptide-1 and peptide tyrosine-tyrosine concentrations in healthy overweight and obese adults: a randomised-controlled trial.
population: Overweight and obese volunteers aged 18–65 years with BMI 25–32 kg/m2, otherwise healthy (no medication or chronic disease), no history of eating behaviour disorder, non-smokers, no history of alcoholism or substance abuse within past 12 months, not pregnant or breast-feeding
intervention: Test meal (350g risotto) containing mycoprotein at low (44g), medium (88g), or high (132g) contents, consumed within 15 minutes following 12-hour overnight fast
comparison: Isoenergetic chicken meals matched for protein content at equivalent levels (low: 22g chicken, medium: 44g chicken, high: 66g chicken)
outcomes_primary: Energy intake at ad libitum meal served 3 hours after test meal consumption
outcomes_secondary: 24-hour energy intake; appetite ratings (hunger, nausea, desire to eat, prospective food intake, fullness) measured by visual analogue scales; serum glucose and insulin concentrations; plasma peptide tyrosine-tyrosine (PYY) and glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) concentrations; insulin sensitivity indices (Matsuda Index, Insulinogenic Index, Disposition Index); gastric emptying rate by paracetamol method; resting energy expenditure; substrate oxidation; urinary and plasma metabolic profiles by 1H NMR spectroscopy-based metabonomics analysis
extraction_notes: Two-part study design (Part A: n=36 for energy intake and hormones; Part B: n=14 for gastric emptying and energy expenditure). Single-blinded design. Meals were not matched for fibre content.

title: Improvements in health-related quality of life with liraglutide 3.0 mg compared with placebo in weight management.
population: Adults aged 18 years or older with obesity (BMI ≥30 kg/m²) or overweight (BMI ≥27 kg/m²) with treated or untreated hypertension or dyslipidaemia; patients with type 2 diabetes were excluded; patients with prediabetes were permitted to enrol
intervention: Once-daily subcutaneous liraglutide 3.0 mg, initiated at 0.6 mg/day and escalated in weekly increments of 0.6 mg until target dose of 3.0 mg, as adjunct to 500 kcal/day deficit diet and 150 min/week exercise programme, for 56 weeks
comparison: Placebo (once-daily subcutaneous injection), with same dose escalation schedule and same lifestyle intervention (500 kcal/day deficit diet and 150 min/week exercise programme)
outcomes_primary: Health-related quality of life assessed using Impact of Weight on Quality of Life-Lite (IWQOL-Lite) total score and subscales (physical function, self-esteem, sexual life, public distress, work), and Short-Form 36 version 2 (SF-36v2) physical component summary (PCS) and mental component summary (MCS) scores and eight subscales, measured at baseline, 28 weeks, and 56 weeks
outcomes_secondary: Meaningful change in HRQoL scores (defined by published algorithms with severity-dependent cut-offs for IWQOL-Lite and fixed thresholds for SF-36); changes in HRQoL by categories of weight change
extraction_notes: This is an exploratory analysis of HRQoL from the SCALE Obesity and Prediabetes trial; HRQoL was not the primary endpoint of the original trial. Randomization ratio was 2:1 (liraglutide:placebo). HRQoL assessments were conducted in 14 of 27 countries (~82% of participants).

title: Effect of two bakery products on short-term food intake and gut-hormones in young adults: a pilot study.
journal: International journal of food sciences and nutrition
population: University students, young adults aged approximately 18-20 years
intervention: Whole grain bread consumed as mid-morning cereal-based snack
comparison: Conventional bread consumed as mid-morning cereal-based snack
outcomes_primary: Satiety perception, energy intake during testing day, postprandial response of peptide YY
outcomes_secondary: Gut-hormones (including peptide YY), Visual Analogue Scale scores for satiation
extraction_notes: Pilot study with small sample size (n=11). Primary vs secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract. Crossover design. Specific dosing/amount of bread not specified.

title: Glucose Variability in a 26-Week Randomized Comparison of Mealtime Treatment With Rapid-Acting Insulin Versus GLP-1 Agonist in Participants With Type 2 Diabetes at High Cardiovascular Risk.
population: Participants with insulin-requiring type 2 diabetes and high cardiovascular risk
intervention: Exenatide dosing before the two largest meals plus metformin and basal insulin (GLIPULIN group)
comparison: Continuation of rapid-acting insulin analogs plus metformin and basal insulin (basal-bolus insulin, BBI group)
outcomes_primary: Change in glucose coefficients of variation (CV) by continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) from baseline to 26 weeks
outcomes_secondary: Other glycemic variability indices by CGM, hypoglycemia, weight, cardiometabolic risk markers, cardiac arrhythmias during electrocardiographic monitoring
extraction_notes: Run-in period on metformin and basal-bolus insulin preceded randomization. Exenatide dose not specified in abstract.

title: Addition of Liraglutide to Insulin in Patients With Type 1 Diabetes: A Randomized Placebo-Controlled Clinical Trial of 12 Weeks.
population: Overweight and obese patients with type 1 diabetes
intervention: Liraglutide 0.6 mg, 1.2 mg, or 1.8 mg daily added to insulin for 12 weeks
comparison: Placebo added to insulin
outcomes_primary: Glycemia (average blood glucose, HbA1c), body weight, insulin dose
outcomes_secondary: Glycemic variability, postprandial plasma glucagon concentration, gastrointestinal adverse events, percent time spent in hypoglycemia (<55 mg/dL, 3.05 mmol/L)
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract; outcomes listed based on stated study objectives and reported measures. Exact BMI criteria for overweight/obese not specified.

title: Once-daily delayed-release metformin lowers plasma glucose and enhances fasting and postprandial GLP-1 and PYY: results from two randomised trials.
population: Male or female adults aged 19-70 years with BMI 25-40 kg/m2 and type 2 diabetes mellitus treated with diet and exercise or with metformin and/or dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitor (medications withheld for at least 14 days prior to randomisation)
intervention: Study 1: Delayed-release metformin (Metformin DR) 500 mg twice-daily or 1,000 mg twice-daily administered with meals for 5 days. Study 2: Metformin DR 1,000 mg once-daily in the morning, 1,000 mg once-daily in the evening, or 500 mg twice-daily for 6-7 days
comparison: Study 1: Immediate-release metformin (Metformin IR) 1,000 mg twice-daily administered with meals for 5 days. Study 2: Three Metformin DR dosing regimens compared against each other (once-daily am vs once-daily pm vs twice-daily)
outcomes_primary: Study 1: Plasma metformin bioavailability (AUC, Cmax), fasting plasma glucose, postprandial plasma glucose AUC, plasma GLP-1 and PYY concentrations. Study 2: Plasma metformin bioavailability (AUC0-24), plasma glucose over 24 hours, fasting plasma glucose
outcomes_secondary: Safety and tolerability assessed through adverse events, concomitant medication use, clinical laboratory values, and vital signs; urinary metformin excretion (Study 2)
extraction_notes: Two separate crossover studies reported together. Study 1 was blinded; Study 2 was non-blinded. Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly designated in the text; categorisation based on study objectives described.

title: Prandial Options to Advance Basal Insulin Glargine Therapy: Testing Lixisenatide Plus Basal Insulin Versus Insulin Glulisine Either as Basal-Plus or Basal-Bolus in Type 2 Diabetes: The GetGoal Duo-2 Trial.
population: Overweight patients with type 2 diabetes inadequately controlled on basal insulin glargine with or without 1-3 oral antidiabetic agents (OADs); HbA1c ≥7 to ≤9% (≥53 to ≤75 mmol/mol) after 12 weeks of glargine optimization
intervention: Lixisenatide once daily added to insulin glargine, with or without metformin
comparison: Insulin glulisine once daily (basal-plus) added to glargine, with or without metformin; Insulin glulisine thrice daily (basal-bolus) added to glargine, with or without metformin
outcomes_primary: 1) HbA1c reduction with lixisenatide versus glulisine once daily (noninferiority); 2a) HbA1c reduction for lixisenatide versus glulisine thrice daily (noninferiority); 2b) Body weight change for lixisenatide versus glulisine thrice daily (superiority)
outcomes_secondary: Fasting plasma glucose; postprandial plasma glucose; composite efficacy/safety end points; adverse events; symptomatic hypoglycemia
extraction_notes: OADs other than metformin were stopped at the start of optimization phase. Duration of treatment was 26 weeks.

title: Baseline factors associated with glycaemic response to treatment with once-weekly dulaglutide in patients with type 2 diabetes.
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes receiving dulaglutide in six phase III studies (AWARD clinical trial programme)
intervention: Once-weekly dulaglutide
comparison: Not specified (pooled analysis of dulaglutide-treated patients only)
outcomes_primary: Change in glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c) after 26 weeks of treatment
outcomes_secondary: Baseline factors associated with HbA1c reduction including: HbA1c, age, fasting serum glucose (FSG), fasting serum insulin (FSI), estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR)
extraction_notes: This is a pooled post-hoc analysis of dulaglutide-treated patients from six phase III AWARD trials; no comparator arm was included in this specific analysis. Dose of dulaglutide not specified. Abstract appears truncated.

title: Efficacy of lixisenatide in patients with type 2 diabetes: A post hoc analysis of patients with diverse β-cell function in the GetGoal-M and GetGoal-S trials.
journal: Journal of diabetes and its complications
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes from the Phase 3 GetGoal-M and GetGoal-S clinical trials, stratified into quartiles by baseline β-cell function as measured by the secretory units of islet in transplantation (SUIT) index
intervention: Lixisenatide 20μg once daily
comparison: Not applicable (post hoc analysis of lixisenatide-treated patients only, stratified by baseline β-cell function quartiles)
outcomes_primary: Not explicitly stated
outcomes_secondary: Not explicitly stated; outcomes assessed included glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c), postprandial plasma glucose (PPG), postprandial glucagon, insulinogenic index, and severe symptomatic hypoglycemic events
extraction_notes: This is a post hoc analysis of patients randomized to lixisenatide only; placebo arm from original trials not included in this analysis. Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly designated in abstract. Original trials were GetGoal-M and GetGoal-S Phase 3 trials.

title: Effect of Adding Liraglutide vs Placebo to a High-Dose lnsulin Regimen in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
population: Patients with uncontrolled type 2 diabetes (glycated hemoglobin level 7.5%-11.0%) using more than 1.5 U/kg/d of insulin
intervention: Subcutaneous injection of liraglutide 1.8 mg/d for 6 months
comparison: Matching placebo subcutaneous injection for 6 months
outcomes_primary: Change in glycated hemoglobin level
outcomes_secondary: Changes in weight, hypoglycemia rate, insulin dosage, quality-of-life measures (glycemia control perception, satisfaction with insulin treatment, willingness to continue insulin use)

title: Continuous glucose monitoring in patients with type 2 diabetes treated with glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist dulaglutide in combination with prandial insulin lispro: an AWARD-4 substudy.
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes previously treated with conventional insulin regimen; substudy of AWARD-4 trial participants who were inserted with continuous glucose monitoring device
intervention: Dulaglutide 1.5 mg or dulaglutide 0.75 mg in combination with prandial insulin lispro
comparison: Insulin glargine in combination with prandial insulin lispro
outcomes_primary: Percentage time spent with CGM glucose values in the 3.9-7.8 mmol/L range at 26 weeks
outcomes_secondary: Mean 24-hour glucose; percentage time in target glucose ranges; percentage time in 3.9-10.0 mmol/L range; hyperglycaemia; hypoglycaemia (percentage time with glucose values ≤3.9 mmol/L); glucose variability indices including overall within-patient standard deviation
extraction_notes: This is a substudy of AWARD-4 trial using CGM. CGM sessions were completed at weeks 0, 13, 26 and 52. The substudy included 144 patients from the main trial of 884 patients.

title: Pharmacokinetic Properties of Liraglutide as Adjunct to Insulin in Subjects with Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus.
population: Adults aged 18-64 years with clinical diagnosis of type 1 diabetes mellitus for ≥12 months, treated with multiple daily insulin injections or continuous subcutaneous insulin infusion for ≥12 months, body mass index 20.0-28.0 kg/m2, body weight ≥52 kg, glycated hemoglobin ≤9.5%. Exclusion criteria: use of liraglutide or exenatide within 3 months before randomization, recurrent severe hypoglycemia (more than one episode within past 12 months), hypoglycemia unawareness, severe autonomic neuropathy.
intervention: Liraglutide 0.6 mg, 1.2 mg, or 1.8 mg administered subcutaneously once daily in the evening as adjunct to insulin for 4 weeks. Liraglutide initiated at 0.6 mg/day with weekly dose escalations of 0.6 mg until target dose reached.
comparison: Placebo in equivalent volume administered subcutaneously once daily in the evening as adjunct to insulin for 4 weeks (crossover design with 2-3 week washout period between treatment periods).
outcomes_primary: Pharmacokinetic endpoints derived from liraglutide steady-state concentration-time curves: area under the curve (AUC), maximum serum concentration (Cmax), time to Cmax (tmax), terminal half-life (t½), clearance (CL/F), volume of distribution (Vz/F), minimum liraglutide concentration in dosing interval (Ctrough).
outcomes_secondary: Dose proportionality assessment of liraglutide AUC and Cmax; comparison of dose-normalized liraglutide AUC with data from previous trials in healthy volunteers and subjects with type 2 diabetes.
extraction_notes: This is a clinical pharmacology/pharmacokinetic trial with crossover design. Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly labeled as such; categorization based on stated objectives. Counter-regulatory response to hypoglycemia and other clinical outcomes were reported in a separate publication (Pieber et al.).

title: Short-term administration of the GLP-1 analog liraglutide decreases circulating leptin and increases GIP levels and these changes are associated with alterations in CNS responses to food cues: A randomized, placebo-controlled, crossover study.
population: Men and women with type 2 diabetes mellitus (defined as fasting plasma glucose > 125 mg/dL and/or HbA1c > 6.5%), treated with metformin or lifestyle modification (diet and exercise); patients receiving other treatments were excluded
intervention: Liraglutide subcutaneous injection, escalating doses: 0.6 mg daily for 7 days, then 1.2 mg daily for 7 days, then 1.8 mg daily for 3 days (total 17 days)
comparison: Placebo (identical administration schedule in crossover design with 3-week to 3-month washout period)
outcomes_primary: Fasting levels of circulating hormones important to energy homeostasis (leptin, ghrelin, PYY, GIP, GLP-1, adiponectin, irisin, amylin, FGF-21, pancreatic polypeptide); fMRI BOLD responses to food cues (highly desirable vs. less desirable food images contrast)
outcomes_secondary: Anthropometric measures (body weight, waist circumference, DEXA body composition); resting metabolic rate; visual analog scale ratings; fasting serum glucose, lipid panel (total cholesterol, triglycerides, HDL, LDL), amylase, lipase, fructosamine; caloric intake
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in the text; classification based on stated objectives. Study designed to assess effects before body weight changed (17 days duration).

title: Efficacy and Safety of LixiLan, a Titratable Fixed-Ratio Combination of Lixisenatide and Insulin Glargine, Versus Insulin Glargine in Type 2 Diabetes Inadequately Controlled on Metformin Monotherapy: The LixiLan Proof-of-Concept Randomized Trial.
population: Insulin-naïve adults with type 2 diabetes inadequately controlled on metformin monotherapy
intervention: LixiLan, a fixed-ratio titratable combination of 2 units insulin glargine (Gla-100) and 1 μg lixisenatide, administered once daily via a single pen, starting at 10 units/5 μg and titrated based on fasting plasma glucose levels, for 24 weeks, while continuing metformin
comparison: Insulin glargine (Gla-100) once daily, starting at 10 units and titrated based on fasting plasma glucose levels, for 24 weeks, while continuing metformin
outcomes_primary: Change in HbA1c from baseline to week 24, tested for noninferiority (upper bound of 95% CI ≤0.4%) and if met, statistical superiority
outcomes_secondary: Body weight changes, hypoglycemia incidence, 2-hour postmeal plasma glucose, proportion achieving HbA1c <7.0% (<53 mmol/mol), safety including gastrointestinal adverse events (nausea, vomiting)
extraction_notes: Baseline characteristics (mean age 57 years, diabetes duration 6-7 years, BMI 32 kg/m2) appear to describe the study population but are not explicitly stated as inclusion criteria

title: Extra virgin olive oil improves post-prandial glycemic and lipid profile in patients with impaired fasting glucose.
population: Patients with impaired fasting glucose (IFG); n=30
intervention: Meal containing 10 g of extra virgin olive oil (EVOO)
comparison: Meal without EVOO (cross-over design)
outcomes_primary: Post-prandial glucose, insulin, Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP1), dipeptidyl-peptidase-4 (DPP4) activity measured at baseline, 60 min and 120 min after lunch
outcomes_secondary: Post-prandial triglycerides, total cholesterol, HDL-cholesterol, Apo B-48 measured at baseline, 60 min and 120 min after lunch
extraction_notes: Cross-over design study. Primary vs secondary outcome distinction not explicitly stated in abstract; categorization based on study aims describing glycemic outcomes first, then lipid profile. No washout period duration specified.

title: Liraglutide and Cardiovascular Outcomes in Type 2 Diabetes.
journal: The New England journal of medicine
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus and high cardiovascular risk; glycated hemoglobin level ≥7.0%; either drug-naive or treated with one or more oral antihyperglycemic agents or insulin (human neutral protamine Hagedorn, long-acting analogue, or premixed) or combination; age ≥50 years with at least one cardiovascular coexisting condition (coronary heart disease, cerebrovascular disease, peripheral vascular disease, chronic kidney disease stage 3 or greater, or chronic heart failure NYHA class II or III) OR age ≥60 years with at least one cardiovascular risk factor (microalbuminuria or proteinuria, hypertension and left ventricular hypertrophy, left ventricular systolic or diastolic dysfunction, or ankle-brachial index <0.9). Exclusion criteria: type 1 diabetes; use of GLP-1 receptor agonists, DPP-4 inhibitors, pramlintide, or rapid-acting insulin; familial or personal history of multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2 or medullary thyroid cancer; acute coronary or cerebrovascular event within 14 days before screening
intervention: Liraglutide 1.8 mg (or maximum tolerated dose) once daily as subcutaneous injection, in addition to standard care; 2-week placebo run-in phase before randomization; minimum 42 months treatment with maximum 60 months plus 30 days follow-up
comparison: Matching placebo once daily as subcutaneous injection, in addition to standard care
outcomes_primary: Primary composite outcome: first occurrence of death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction (including silent), or nonfatal stroke (time-to-event analysis)
outcomes_secondary: Prespecified exploratory outcomes: expanded composite cardiovascular outcome (death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, coronary revascularization, or hospitalization for unstable angina pectoris or heart failure); death from any cause; composite renal and retinal microvascular outcome (nephropathy defined as new onset of macroalbuminuria or doubling of serum creatinine level and eGFR ≤45 ml/min/1.73m², need for continuous renal-replacement therapy, or death from renal disease; retinopathy defined as need for retinal photocoagulation or treatment with intravitreal agents, vitreous hemorrhage, or onset of diabetes-related blindness); neoplasms; pancreatitis; glycated hemoglobin level; weight; systolic and diastolic blood pressure; heart rate
extraction_notes: No adjustments for multiplicity were performed for prespecified exploratory outcomes. Randomization stratified by eGFR at screening (<30 or ≥30 ml/min/1.73m²). Trial was double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter (410 sites, 32 countries)

title: Feedback suppression of meal-induced glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) secretion mediated through elevations in intact GLP-1 caused by dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibition: a randomized, prospective comparison of sitagliptin and vildagliptin treatment.
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes; 12 on diet/exercise regimen, 12 on metformin treatment
intervention: Vildagliptin 50 mg twice daily (100 mg/day) for 7-9 days; Sitagliptin 100 mg once daily for those on diet or 50 mg twice daily for those on metformin (100 mg/day) for 7-9 days
comparison: Placebo twice daily
outcomes_primary: Incretin hormone responses (intact GLP-1, total GLP-1, glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide concentrations); L-cell feedback inhibition

extraction_notes: Pragmatic, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, event-driven trial. Coprimary hypotheses were noninferiority for safety and superiority for efficacy. Stratified by history of cardiovascular disease. No upper age limit specified.

title: Semaglutide Added to Basal Insulin in Type 2 Diabetes (SUSTAIN 5): A Randomized, Controlled Trial.

intervention: Weekly subcutaneous injection of dulaglutide 1.5 mg
comparison: Placebo (weekly subcutaneous injection)
outcomes_primary: First occurrence of the composite endpoint of non-fatal myocardial infarction, non-fatal stroke, or death from cardiovascular causes (including unknown causes)
extraction_notes: Secondary outcomes not specified in abstract. The abstract text appears truncated in the FINDINGS and BACKGROUND sections (ending with 'HbA' and 'A' respectively), potentially missing additional details.

title: Efficacy and safety of oral semaglutide in patients with type 2 diabetes and moderate renal impairment (PIONEER 5): a placebo-controlled, randomised, phase 3a trial.
population: Adults aged 18 years and older with type 2 diabetes and moderate renal impairment (estimated glomerular filtration rate of 30-59 mL/min per 1.73 m²)
intervention: Oral semaglutide
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Change in HbA1c at 26 weeks
extraction_notes: Dose, frequency, and duration of oral semaglutide not specified in abstract. Secondary outcomes not explicitly listed. Abstract text appears truncated in methods and findings sections.

title: Durability of insulin degludec plus liraglutide versus insulin glargine U100 as initial injectable therapy in type 2 diabetes (DUAL VIII): a multicentre, open-label, phase 3b, randomised controlled trial.
population: Insulin-naive patients aged 18 years and older with type 2 diabetes and HbA1c inadequately controlled on oral antidiabetic drugs, eligible for basal insulin intensification
intervention: Insulin degludec plus liraglutide (IDegLira)
comparison: Insulin glargine 100 units/mL (IGlar U100)
outcomes_primary: Time to treatment intensification (defined as reaching the treatment intensification criterion during 104 weeks)
extraction_notes: Trial duration was 104 weeks. Open-label design. Specific doses, routes, and frequencies for IDegLira and IGlar U100 not provided in abstract. Secondary outcomes not explicitly listed in abstract. Visit schedule designed to mirror routine clinical practice.

title: Efficacy and safety of oral semaglutide with flexible dose adjustment versus sitagliptin in type 2 diabetes (PIONEER 7): a multicentre, open-label, randomised, phase 3a trial.
population: Adults aged 18 years or older (19 years or older in South Korea) with type 2 diabetes diagnosed at least 90 days before screening
intervention: Oral semaglutide with flexible dose adjustment
comparison: Sitagliptin 100 mg
outcomes_primary: Not explicitly stated in abstract
outcomes_secondary: Not explicitly stated in abstract

Primary and secondary outcome definitions not explicitly stated, though glycaemic control (HbA1c) and weight loss are mentioned as efficacy measures. Trial duration was 52 weeks. Open-label design.

title: Locally delivered GLP-1 analogues liraglutide and exenatide enhance microvascular perfusion in individuals with and without type 2 diabetes.
population: Study 1: Three groups - lean individuals (BMI ≤25.0 kg/m2), obese individuals (BMI ≥30.0 kg/m2), and individuals with type 2 diabetes on stable medication (minimum 3 months) or diet control only; n=21 per group. Exclusion criteria for lean/obese groups: diabetes, cardiovascular disease, Raynaud's disease, current antihypertensive or lipid-lowering therapies. Exclusion criteria for type 2 diabetes group: insulin or sulfonylurea treatment, known CVD, proliferative retinopathy, advanced nephropathy (macroalbuminuria), uncontrolled diabetes (HbA1c >8.5%/69 mmol/mol), previous GLP-1 analogue or DPP-4 inhibitor treatment. Study 2: Healthy lean individuals (BMI ≤25 kg/m2), >18 years, without diabetes, hypertension or CVD; n=16.
intervention: Study 1: Intradermal microinjection of liraglutide (0.06 mg, 10 μl) and exenatide (0.5 μg, 10 μl) into forearm dermis. Study 2: Intradermal microinjection of liraglutide (0.06 mg, 10 μl) with or without pretreatment with exendin-(9,39) (70 nmol/l, 10 μl) GLP-1 receptor blocker.
comparison: Study 1: Saline (0.9% NaCl, 154 mmol/l) as injection trauma control; acetylcholine (1%, 10 mg/ml) as positive endothelial function control. Study 2: Saline followed by saline (microinjection trauma control); exendin-(9,39) followed by saline; saline followed by liraglutide.
outcomes_primary: Stabilised response (mean skin perfusion between 7.5 and 10 minutes post microinjection) and total response (AUC normalized for baseline perfusion) measured by laser Doppler perfusion imaging.
outcomes_secondary: Comparison of perfusion responses between participant groups (lean, obese, type 2 diabetes); effect of GLP-1 receptor blockade on liraglutide response; in vitro assessment of nitrate levels and eNOS phosphorylation in human microvascular endothelial cells.
extraction_notes: This is a complex study with two separate clinical studies (Study 1 and Study 2) plus an in vitro component. Both clinical studies used randomised, controlled, double-blind designs. One-tenth of the lowest treatment dose was used for local delivery to avoid systemic effects.

title: Improved treatment satisfaction in patients with type 2 diabetes treated with once-weekly semaglutide in the SUSTAIN trials.
population: Adults aged ≥18 years with type 2 diabetes inadequately controlled (HbA1c 7.0–10.5%) on oral glucose-lowering therapy or basal insulin; key exclusion criteria included estimated glomerular filtration rate <30-60 mL/min/1.73 m² (varied by trial), acute coronary or cerebrovascular event <90 days before randomization, or severe chronic heart failure (New York Heart Association class IV)
intervention: Once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide 0.5 mg or 1.0 mg with fixed dose-escalation (0.25 mg for 4 weeks, then 0.5 mg; for 1.0 mg dose: 0.25 mg for 4 weeks, 0.5 mg for 4 weeks, then 1.0 mg) added to background oral glucose-lowering therapy or basal insulin for 30-56 weeks
comparison: Sitagliptin 100 mg for 56 weeks (SUSTAIN 2); exenatide extended release 2.0 mg for 56 weeks (SUSTAIN 3); insulin glargine for 30 weeks (SUSTAIN 4); placebo for 30 weeks (SUSTAIN 5); dulaglutide 0.75 mg or 1.5 mg for 40 weeks (SUSTAIN 7)
outcomes_primary: Change in HbA1c from baseline to end of treatment
outcomes_secondary: Change in body weight from baseline to end of treatment; Diabetes Treatment Satisfaction Questionnaire (DTSQs) overall treatment satisfaction score (range 0-36); perceived hyperglycaemia; perceived hypoglycaemia; other efficacy, safety and tolerability variables
extraction_notes: This is a post-hoc pooled analysis of SUSTAIN 2-5 and 7 trials focused on treatment satisfaction (DTSQs) as a patient-reported outcome; DTSQs was not the primary endpoint of the original trials; SUSTAIN 1 and 6 were excluded from this analysis

title: Olfactory Dysfunction Mediates Adiposity in Cognitive Impairment of Type 2 Diabetes: Insights From Clinical and Functional Neuroimaging Studies.
population: Obese and nonobese people with type 2 diabetes, and healthy control subjects matched for age, sex, and education. For the treatment arm: obese individuals with type 2 diabetes with inadequate glycemic control on metformin monotherapy.
intervention: Glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonist (GLP-1Ra) treatment for 3 months (added to existing metformin monotherapy)
comparison: Nonobese people with type 2 diabetes; healthy control subjects; pre-treatment baseline (within-subject comparison for GLP-1Ra treatment arm)
outcomes_primary: Cognitive function (general cognition, Montreal Cognitive Assessment score, episodic memory, processing speed), olfactory function (olfactory threshold scores, olfactory test total score), odor-induced brain activation (hippocampal activation, parahippocampus activation), functional connectivity (seed-based functional connectivity with insula)
outcomes_secondary: Metabolic changes, neuroimaging changes
extraction_notes: This study has both a cross-sectional observational component and a pre-post intervention component. The GLP-1Ra treatment arm appears to lack a parallel control group (single-arm pre-post design). Specific GLP-1Ra drug name, dose, and route not specified in abstract. Primary vs secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished.

title: Influence of subliminal intragastric fatty acid infusion on subjective and physiological responses to positive emotion induction in healthy women: A randomized trial.
population: Fasting healthy women
intervention: Intragastric infusion of 2.5 g lauric acid combined with positive or neutral emotion induction for 30 min
comparison: Intragastric infusion of saline combined with positive or neutral emotion induction for 30 min
outcomes_secondary: Appetite-related sensations; subjective emotional state; gastrointestinal hormones (CCK, GLP1, PYY, plasma octanoylated ghrelin); heart rate variability including vagal tone (root mean square of successive differences, RMSSD) and sympathovagal balance (low frequency to high frequency ratio, LF/HF)
extraction_notes: Primary outcomes not explicitly distinguished from secondary outcomes in abstract. Sample size is 12 participants. Study used a crossover design with 4 separate visits. Outcomes measured at baseline and every 10 min after infusion; heart rate variability measured at baseline and at t=20-30 min.

title: Differential effects of a 40-hour fast and bile acid supplementation on human GLP-1 and FGF19 responses.
journal: American journal of physiology. Endocrinology and metabolism
