intervention: 40-hour fast; glycine-conjugated deoxycholic acid (gDCA) administered with meal
comparison: Crossover design (specific comparator conditions not explicitly stated in abstract)
outcomes_primary: Postprandial bile acid response in plasma; relation to insulin, GLP-1, and FGF19
extraction_notes: Abstract appears truncated. Two separate observational randomized crossover studies mentioned but full design details not provided. Specific doses, routes, frequencies, and durations of interventions not stated. Primary vs secondary outcome designation not explicitly specified.

title: EFFICACY AND SAFETY OF IGLARLIXI IN HISPANICS AND NON-HISPANIC WHITES WITH TYPE 2 DIABETES.
journal: Endocrine practice : official journal of the American College of Endocrinology and the American Association of Clinical Endocrinologists
population: Hispanics and non-Hispanic Whites with type 2 diabetes
intervention: iGlarLixi (insulin glargine/lixisenatide fixed-ratio combination)
comparison: Not specified in available text
outcomes_primary: Not specified in available text
outcomes_secondary: Not specified in available text
extraction_notes: No abstract text available. Only title information used for extraction. Drug name iGlarLixi identified from title but dose, route, frequency, and duration not specified. Comparator groups not specified. Primary and secondary outcomes not specified. This appears to be a subgroup analysis by ethnicity.

title: Continuous subcutaneous insulin infusion combined with liraglutide reduced glycemic variability and oxidative stress in type 2 diabetes mellitus: a study based on the flash glucose monitoring system.
population: Hospitalized newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) patients
intervention: Continuous subcutaneous insulin infusion (CSII) combined with liraglutide for 2 weeks
comparison: Continuous subcutaneous insulin infusion (CSII) alone
outcomes_primary: Glycemic control measures: mean blood glucose concentration (MBG), estimated hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c); Glycemic variability (GV) indices: standard deviation of mean glucose (SD), coefficient of variation (CV), interquartile range (IQR), mean amplitude of glycemic excursions (MAGE), largest amplitude of glycemic excursions (LAGE), mean of daily difference (MODD)
outcomes_secondary: Oxidative stress biomarkers: 4-hydroxynonenal (4-HNE) and 8-hydroxydeoxyguanosine (8-OHdG)
extraction_notes: Liraglutide dose not specified. Primary vs secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract; classification based on study aims and presentation order. All outcomes assessed using flash glucose monitoring (FGM) system over 2 weeks.

title: Effect of Oral Nutritional Supplements with Sucromalt and Isomaltulose versus Standard Formula on Glycaemic Index, Entero-Insular Axis Peptides and Subjective Appetite in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes: A Randomised Cross-Over Study.
population: Adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus over 50 years old, BMI 18.5-35 kg/m², managed with diet/physical activity and/or metformin monotherapy only. Excluded: type 1 diabetes, diabetic ketoacidosis, thyroid disorders, congestive heart failure, gastric/kidney/hepatic diseases, myocardial infarction, stroke, insulin or sulfonylurea therapy, antibiotic or corticosteroid therapy, end-stage organ failure, organ transplantation, coagulation/bleeding disorders, chronic infectious diseases (tuberculosis, hepatitis B/C, HIV)
intervention: Oral nutritional supplement with sucromalt (Glucerna SR) containing slow-digesting carbohydrates including resistant maltodextrin and sucromalt, administered as standardized portion with 25g carbohydrates; Oral nutritional supplement with isomaltulose (Diasip) containing lactose, isomaltulose, and resistant starch, administered as standardized portion with 25g carbohydrates
comparison: Standard non-diabetes-specific oral nutritional supplement (Ensure) administered as standardized portion with 25g carbohydrates; Reference food: 25g anhydrous glucose dissolved in 250mL plain water
outcomes_primary: Glycaemic index (GI), glycaemic load (GL), glucose area under the curve (AUC0-180 min)
outcomes_secondary: Insulin AUC0-180 min, glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) AUC0-180 min, glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1) AUC0-180 min, subjective appetite ratings measured by visual analogue scale (hunger, desire to eat, prospective food consumption, fullness) AUC0-180 min
extraction_notes: Randomised double-blind cross-over design with 8 consumption tests per participant (2 for glucose reference, 2 for each of 3 supplements) with 1-week washout between tests. Appetite assessed on separate days from GI determination. Primary outcome not explicitly labeled but glycaemic response stated as primary outcome in sample size calculation.

title: The role of Glucagon-Like Peptide 1 Loading on periprocedural myocardial infarction During elective PCI (GOLD-PCI study): A randomized, placebo-controlled trial.
population: Patients undergoing elective percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), stratified for diabetes mellitus
intervention: Intravenous infusion of GLP-1 (glucagon-like peptide 1) at 1.2 pmol/kg/min administered before and during the procedure
comparison: Matched 0.9% saline placebo intravenous infusion
outcomes_primary: Periprocedural myocardial infarction (PMI) defined as cardiac troponin I (cTnI) rise ≥5× upper limit of normal (280 ng/L) at 6 hours
outcomes_secondary: Cardiac troponin I (cTnI) rise; major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCE) at 12 months
extraction_notes: Randomization was 1:1 with stratification for diabetes mellitus. Study was double-blind.

title: Longer-term liraglutide administration at the highest dose approved for obesity increases reward-related orbitofrontal cortex activation in response to food cues: Implications for plateauing weight loss in response to anti-obesity therapies.
population: Men and women with obesity (BMI ≥30 kg/m2), excluded if taking anti-obesity or anti-diabetes medications (aside from metformin) within 3 months, history of bariatric surgery, body weight changes in preceding 3 months, unable to have MRI, history of suicidality, taking psychiatric medications, or unable/unwilling to take study medication
intervention: Liraglutide subcutaneous injection with dose escalation over 5 weeks (0.6mg for 1 week, 1.2mg for 1 week, 1.8mg for 1 week, 2.4mg for 1 week, 3.0mg for 1 week)
comparison: Placebo (matching dose escalation schedule) in cross-over design with minimum 3 week wash-out period
outcomes_primary: Brain activations to food cues measured by fMRI (BOLD contrast responses to highly desirable food, less desirable food, and non-food control images)
outcomes_secondary: Body weight/BMI change, fasting glucose, cholesterol levels, neurocognitive testing (Stop-Signal Task, Intra-Extra Dimensional Set Shift, Verbal Recognition Memory, Spatial Span, Spatial Working Memory), visual analog scale ratings of hunger, satiety, food palatability, self-reported food intake
extraction_notes: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, cross-over trial. Primary outcome not explicitly labeled as such but neuroimaging was the main focus. Power calculation based on previous study referenced for brain activation outcomes.

title: Long-term efficacy and safety of combined insulin and glucagon-like peptide-1 therapy: Evidence from the LEADER trial.
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes, HbA1c >7% (>53 mmol/mol), at high risk of cardiovascular disease (aged ≥50 years with established cardiovascular disease or chronic kidney disease, or aged ≥60 years with ≥1 risk factor for cardiovascular disease), treated with oral glucose-lowering drugs, insulin (human neutral protamine Hagedorn, long-acting analog or premix insulin), combination therapy, or treatment-naïve at baseline. Exclusion criteria: use of GLP-1RAs, dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors, pramlintide, or rapid-acting insulin
intervention: Liraglutide up to 1.8 mg (as tolerated) subcutaneous injection, in addition to standard of care treatment, followed for minimum 3.5 years up to 5 years
comparison: Placebo in addition to standard of care treatment
outcomes_primary: Time to first occurrence of composite cardiovascular outcome comprising cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, or non-fatal stroke (MACE)
outcomes_secondary: HbA1c, body weight, systolic blood pressure, LDL-cholesterol, severe hypoglycaemia (hypoglycaemia requiring assistance of another person to administer carbohydrate, glucagon or other resuscitative actions), insulin initiation, basal insulin intensification, insulin discontinuation, insulin dose changes
extraction_notes: This is a post hoc subgroup analysis of the LEADER trial (NCT01179048). Subgroups analyzed by baseline insulin use: basal-only insulin, other insulin, no insulin. Insulin allocation was non-random as part of standard of care therapy.

title: A double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomised trial to assess the effect of liraglutide on ectopic fat accumulation in South Asian type 2 diabetes patients.
population: South Asian adults (individuals with two South Asian parents) with type 2 diabetes, aged 18-74 years, BMI ≥23 kg/m2, HbA1c ≥6.5% and ≤11.0%, with stable glucose-lowering medication (metformin, sulfonylurea derivatives, and/or insulin) for at least 3 months prior to participation. Exclusion criteria included use of other glucose-lowering therapy, renal disease, congestive heart failure NYHA class III-IV, uncontrolled hypertension (systolic BP >180 mmHg and/or diastolic BP >110 mmHg), acute coronary or cerebrovascular accident within 30 days prior to inclusion, or contraindication for contrast-enhanced MRI.
intervention: Liraglutide (Victoza) subcutaneous injection, starting dose 0.6 mg/day titrated over 2 weeks to maximum 1.8 mg/day (reduced if not tolerated), added to standard care, for 26 weeks
comparison: Placebo injection added to standard care for 26 weeks
outcomes_primary: Ectopic fat deposition measured by MRI (abdominal subcutaneous, visceral, epicardial, and paracardial adipose tissue volume) and proton magnetic resonance spectroscopy (myocardial and hepatic triglyceride content); HbA1c
outcomes_secondary: Body weight, BMI, waist circumference, hip circumference, waist-hip ratio, lean body mass, total cholesterol, HDL-cholesterol, LDL-cholesterol, triglycerides
extraction_notes: The primary outcome in the original sample size calculation was cardiac function, not the ectopic fat outcomes reported in this manuscript. Authors note that ectopic fat and HbA1c were secondary outcome measures for this analysis.

title: Hepatic triglyceride content does not affect circulating CETP: lessons from a liraglutide intervention trial and a population-based cohort.
population: Overweight and obese (BMI ≥ 25 kg/m²) patients with type 2 diabetes, aged 18-69 years, treated with metformin, with HbA1c ≥ 7.0% and ≤ 10.0% (53-86 mmol/mol), with stable glucose-lowering medication dosage for at least 3 months. Concomitant sulfonylurea derivatives and insulin were optional. Exclusion criteria: use of other glucose-lowering therapy, presence of renal, hepatic or cardiovascular disease, and contraindications for MRI.
intervention: Liraglutide (Victoza®) subcutaneous injection, starting dose 0.6 mg per day titrated over two weeks to maximum dose of 1.8 mg per day if tolerated, for 26 weeks, added to standard care according to current clinical guidelines
comparison: Placebo injection added to standard care according to current clinical guidelines for 26 weeks
outcomes_primary: Effect of liraglutide on cardiac function (reported elsewhere as primary outcome of MAGNA VICTORIA study)
outcomes_secondary: Hepatic triglyceride content measured by proton magnetic resonance spectroscopy; circulating CETP concentration measured by ELISA; body weight; BMI; total cholesterol; HDL-cholesterol; LDL-cholesterol; triglycerides; glucose; HbA1c; AST; ALT; association between hepatic triglyceride content and plasma CETP concentration
extraction_notes: This manuscript reports secondary and other endpoints of the MAGNA VICTORIA trial; primary outcome (cardiac function) reported elsewhere. The study also includes cross-sectional analysis of NEO cohort (n=1,611) which is a separate observational component, not the RCT. Sample size: 50 randomized (24 liraglutide, 26 placebo), 49 analyzed.

title: Development of a delayed-release nutrient for appetite control in adults with obesity and type 2 diabetes and initial clinical testing in a single dose randomized controlled trial.
population: Adults aged 18-65 years with body mass index >27 kg/m2 and type 2 diabetes with duration <10 years, using only lifestyle modification, metformin, sulfonylureas, thiazolidinedione, or SGLT2 inhibitors for diabetes management. Exclusions: known foregut pathology or prior foregut surgery, previous surgical treatment for obesity, history of pancreatitis, use of insulin, DPP4 inhibitors or GLP-1 analog inhibitors in previous 3 months, diet attempts using herbal supplements or over the counter medications in past 1 month, allergy to dairy products or lactose intolerance.
intervention: Single dose of delayed-release nutrient (DRN): 50 g (200 kcal) of coated nutrient pellets containing sucrose spheres and whole milk powder with ethyl cellulose-alginate GRAS coating (Nutrateric), ingested with 235 mL diet tonic water
comparison: Unformulated nutrient (UN): same 50 g (200 kcal) of sucrose spheres and whole milk powder with equivalent amounts of uncoated dietary fiber cellulose and sodium alginate powders, mixed with 235 mL diet tonic water
outcomes_primary: Maximum concentration (Cmax) and area under the curve (AUC) of total GLP-1
outcomes_secondary: Cmax and AUC levels of C-peptide, insulin, and glucose; time of maximal concentration (Tmax) for all analytes; satiety measures (hunger, fullness, satisfaction, thoughts of food) assessed by visual analog scale; adverse effect scores (nausea, abdominal pain, perspiration, palpitations) assessed by visual analog scale
extraction_notes: Prospective randomized crossover trial with 1-4 weeks between study visits. Study visits were 3-hour meal tolerance tests. Sample size calculation based on projected effect size of 0.68 requiring 20 participants for 80% power.

title: Assessment of real-time and quantitative changes in renal hemodynamics in healthy overweight males: Contrast-enhanced ultrasonography vs para-aminohippuric acid clearance.
population: Healthy overweight males, aged 20-27 years, BMI 26-31 kg/m²
intervention: Renal contrast-enhanced ultrasonography (CEUS) assessment during administration of exenatide (GLP-1 receptor agonist) and L-NMMA (nitric oxide synthase inhibitor)
comparison: Placebo; para-aminohippuric acid (PAH) clearance for effective renal plasma flow measurement
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract. Study assessed renal hemodynamics including effective renal plasma flow and renal cortical microvascular blood flow. This was a prespecified exploratory analysis of a placebo-controlled cross-over study with n=10. Full intervention details (doses, duration) truncated in abstract.

title: Once-Weekly Efpeglenatide Dose-Range Effects on Glycemic Control and Body Weight in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes on Metformin or Drug Naive, Referenced to Liraglutide.
population: Patients with early type 2 diabetes, drug naive or on metformin monotherapy
intervention: Efpeglenatide once weekly at doses of 0.3, 1, 2, 3, or 4 mg subcutaneously
comparison: Placebo; open-label liraglutide 1.8 mg (exploratory reference)
outcomes_primary: HbA1c change from baseline
outcomes_secondary: Body weight change from baseline; safety and tolerability
extraction_notes: Abstract appears truncated - results and conclusions sections are incomplete. Study duration was 12 weeks. Approximately 90% of participants were on metformin monotherapy.

title: Effects of glepaglutide, a novel long-acting glucagon-like peptide-2 analogue, on markers of liver status in patients with short bowel syndrome: findings from a randomised phase 2 trial.
population: Adults with short bowel syndrome (SBS) associated intestinal insufficiency (II) or intestinal failure (IF), with malabsorption defined as faecal wet weight output ≥1500 g/day. Exclusions: carriers of Hepatitis B surface antigen or Hepatitis C antibodies, history of significant alcohol or drug abuse within one year prior to screening, positive HIV antibodies, history of cancer (unless disease-free for at least five years), history of colon cancer.
intervention: Glepaglutide (long-acting glucagon-like peptide-2 analogue) administered as daily subcutaneous injections at doses of 0.1 mg, 1 mg, or 10 mg for three weeks per treatment period
comparison: Two-period crossover design where patients received two of three different doses (0.1 mg, 1 mg, and 10 mg) of glepaglutide, with treatment periods separated by a wash-out period of four to eight weeks
outcomes_primary: Absolute change from baseline in faecal wet weight output measured over each treatment period
outcomes_secondary: Exploratory endpoints: changes in liver stiffness measured by transient elastography (TE) in kPa; controlled attenuation parameter (CAP) in dB/m; indocyanine green (ICG) elimination measured as plasma disappearance rate (PDR) and retention after 15 minutes (R15); serum soluble CD163 (sCD163); soluble mannose receptor (sMR); lipopolysaccharide binding protein (LBP); conventional liver tests including alkaline phosphatase (ALP), total bilirubin, international normalised ratio (INR), albumin, liver transaminases (ASAT and ALAT)
extraction_notes: This is a dose-finding phase 2 trial with crossover design where all arms receive glepaglutide at different doses - no placebo comparator. Primary endpoint (faecal wet weight) was reported in a previous publication; this paper focuses on exploratory liver-related endpoints. No formal sample size calculation was performed.

title: Liraglutide in combination with metformin may improve the atherogenic lipid profile and decrease C-reactive protein level in statin treated obese patients with coronary artery disease and newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes: A randomized trial.
population: Patients with stable coronary artery disease (CAD) and newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes (T2DM), obese, on statin therapy
intervention: Liraglutide combined with metformin for 12 weeks
comparison: Placebo combined with metformin for 12 weeks (cross-over design with ≥2-week wash-out period)
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract. Outcomes assessed included: lipoprotein density profiles (LDL subfractions separated by continuous density gradient ultracentrifugation, with LDL divided into five subfractions between 226 and 270 Å), plasma C-reactive protein (CRP), and tumor necrosis factor-α (measured by ELISA). Liraglutide dose not specified. 41 patients randomized, 28 completed all visits. One patient excluded from analysis due to statin dosage change.

title: Addition of low-dose liraglutide to insulin therapy is useful for glycaemic control during the peri-operative period: effect of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist therapy on glycaemic control in patients undergoing cardiac surgery (GLOLIA study).
journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association
population: People with Type 2 diabetes undergoing elective cardiac surgery
intervention: Insulin plus liraglutide 0.6 mg/day
comparison: Insulin alone
outcomes_primary: Average M values (proximity index of target glucose level) from day 1 to day 10
outcomes_secondary: Frequency of insulin dose modification; frequency of hypoglycaemia
extraction_notes: Sample size is 70 participants. Duration of outcome assessment was day 1 to day 10 post-operatively. Route of liraglutide administration not explicitly stated but typically subcutaneous.

title: Liraglutide treatment reduced interleukin-6 in adults with type 1 diabetes but did not improve established autonomic or polyneuropathy.
population: Adults aged over 18 years with type 1 diabetes for a minimum of 2 years, confirmed symmetrical polyneuropathy according to Toronto criteria, HbA1c ≥6.5% (>48 mmol/mol), stable hyperglycaemic medication for at least 3 months prior to study entrance, body mass index >22 kg/m2. Exclusions: type 2 diabetes, other neurological disorders than DSPN, estimated glomerular filtration rate <60 mL/min/1.73 m2, calcitonin >25 ng/L, HbA1c level <6.5%, use of GLP-1 agonists or DPP-4 inhibitors.
intervention: Liraglutide, titrated over 6 weeks to a dose of 1.2-1.8 mg/day depending on tolerability, continued for 26 weeks
comparison: Placebo (identical in appearance), titrated over 6 weeks, continued for 26 weeks
outcomes_primary: Change in latency of early brain evoked potentials (early precortical N20 latency of primary somatosensory evoked potentials elicited by electrical stimuli to the median nerve)
outcomes_secondary: Changes in proinflammatory cytokines (IL-1β, TNF-α, IL-6, IL-8, IL-10), specific macrophage markers (sCD163, sCD206), cortical evoked potentials (subcortical N14, late cortical N60), autonomic function measures (24-hour heart rate variability indices, cardiac vagal tone, cardiac sensitivity to baroreflex, orthostatic blood pressure), peripheral neurophysiological testing (nerve conduction velocities, amplitudes, F-waves, thermal testing, monofilament testing). Tertiary outcomes: weight, HbA1c, heart rate, blood pressure, insulin utilization.
extraction_notes: Sample size calculation based on detecting 1.0 SD difference in N20 latency with 80% power. 39 patients completed the study (19 liraglutide, 20 placebo). Study was randomized, double-blinded, parallel-group, placebo-controlled. Duration of intervention was 26 weeks following 6-week titration period.

title: Glucagon-like peptide-2 mobilizes lipids from the intestine by a systemic nitric oxide-independent mechanism.
population: Healthy male volunteers
intervention: Teduglutide (glucagon-like peptide-2 analog) administered 7 hours after ingestion of a high-fat formula
comparison: NO synthase inhibitor L-NMMA; additional comparator groups not fully specified in abstract
outcomes_primary: Triglyceride concentrations in plasma, TG-rich lipoproteins, and chylomicrons; mesenteric blood flow; chylomicron secretion
extraction_notes: Abstract appears truncated with incomplete description of the three treatment arms in the methods section. Sample size is 10. Randomized, single-blind, cross-over design. Dose, route, frequency, and duration of interventions not specified in abstract.

title: IDegLira improves patient-reported outcomes while using a simple regimen with fewer injections and dose adjustments compared with basal-bolus therapy.
population: Adults ≥18 years with uncontrolled type 2 diabetes (HbA1c 53–86 mmol/mol [7.0%–10.0%]), BMI ≤40 kg/m2, receiving stable daily doses of 20–50 units of insulin glargine U100 and at least 1500 mg (or maximum tolerated dose) of metformin for more than 90 days prior to screening
intervention: IDegLira (insulin degludec/liraglutide fixed ratio combination) initiated at 16 U (16 U insulin degludec + 0.58 mg liraglutide), titrated twice weekly to fasting glucose target 4.0–5.0 mmol/L, once daily injection, plus continued metformin at pre-trial dose, for 26 weeks
comparison: Basal-bolus therapy: insulin glargine U100 continued at pre-trial dose titrated twice weekly to same fasting glucose target, plus insulin aspart initiated at 4 U/main meal titrated twice weekly to pre-prandial and bedtime SMBG target of 4.0–6.0 mmol/L (up to 4 boluses per day), plus continued metformin at pre-trial dose, for 26 weeks
outcomes_primary: Change from baseline in HbA1c at 26 weeks
outcomes_secondary: Number of injections per day; cumulative dose adjustments during 26 weeks; patient-reported outcomes including Treatment-Related Impact Measure for Diabetes (TRIM-D) domain and total scores; Short Form-36 Health Survey version 2 (SF-36v2) physical component summary and mental component summary scores; hypoglycaemia; body weight change
extraction_notes: This is a post hoc analysis of the DUAL VII trial. Primary outcome stated as HbA1c reduction non-inferiority from original trial; PRO outcomes were secondary/exploratory in this post hoc analysis. PRO analysis was not adjusted for multiplicity.

title: Effects of Nicotinamide Riboside on Endocrine Pancreatic Function and Incretin Hormones in Nondiabetic Men With Obesity.
journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
population: Nondiabetic males with obesity and insulin resistance
intervention: Nicotinamide riboside (NR) 1000 mg twice daily for 12 weeks
comparison: Placebo for 12 weeks
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract. title: Efficacy and Safety of 1:1 Fixed-Ratio Combination of Insulin Glargine and Lixisenatide Versus Lixisenatide in Japanese Patients With Type 2 Diabetes Inadequately Controlled on Oral Antidiabetic Drugs: The LixiLan JP-O1 Randomized Clinical Trial.

title: Effects of Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists, Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter-2 Inhibitors, and Their Combination on Endothelial Glycocalyx, Arterial Function, and Myocardial Work Index in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus After 12-Month Treatment.

title: Exenatide once weekly decreases urinary albumin excretion in patients with type 2 diabetes and elevated albuminuria: Pooled analysis of randomized active controlled clinical trials.

title: Dose-response, efficacy, and safety of oral semaglutide monotherapy in Japanese patients with type 2 diabetes (PIONEER 9): a 52-week, phase 2/3a, randomised, controlled trial.

title: Safety and efficacy of oral semaglutide versus dulaglutide in Japanese patients with type 2 diabetes (PIONEER 10): an open-label, randomised, active-controlled, phase 3a trial.

title: Comparison of the effects of twice-daily exenatide and insulin on carotid intima-media thickness in type 2 diabetes mellitus patients: a 52-week randomized, open-label, controlled trial.
population: Adults aged 20-75 years with type 2 diabetes mellitus diagnosed according to 1999 WHO criteria, with HbA1c between 7.5% and 11%, taking at least two oral hypoglycemic drugs at higher than 1/2 of maximum dose for at least 3 months. Exclusions: type 1 diabetes, >75% stenosis of any carotid artery segment, acute cardiovascular event within 30 days, planned cardiovascular/carotid/peripheral artery revascularization or cardiac valvular surgery, previous insulin or exenatide use >1 month, ALT or AST >2.5 times upper limit of normal, serum creatinine ≥133 µmol/L (males) or ≥106 µmol/L (females), history of pancreatitis, participation in another clinical trial within 3 months, positive urine hCG or inability to use contraception

outcomes_secondary: Change from baseline to week 52 in body weight, glycemic markers (HbA1c, fasting plasma glucose), lipid metabolism markers (total cholesterol, HDL-C, triglyceride, LDL-C), blood pressure (systolic and diastolic), C-reactive protein, fibrinogen, 8-hydroxydeoxyguanosine, irisin, brain natriuretic peptide
extraction_notes: Open-label trial design. Patients stratified by disease severity (HbA1c 7.5% vs 9%). Patients free to take hypoglycemic drugs except sulfonylureas and nateglinide.

title: Ileo-colonic delivery of conjugated bile acids improves glucose homeostasis via colonic GLP-1-producing enteroendocrine cells in human obesity and diabetes.

title: Effects of Liraglutide on Worsening Renal Function Among Patients With Heart Failure With Reduced Ejection Fraction: Insights From the FIGHT Trial.

comparison: Placebo

outcomes_secondary: Individual components of the primary endpoint (time to death, time to rehospitalization for acute HF, change in NT-proBNP); cardiac structure and function; 6-minute walk distance; quality of life measures; worsening renal function (WRF) defined as increase in SCr ≥ 0.3 mg/dl, or ≥ 25% decrease in eGFR, or increase in cystatin C ≥ 0.3 mg/L from baseline at 30-day, 90-day, and 180-day visits (post-hoc analysis)
extraction_notes: This is a post-hoc analysis of the FIGHT trial focusing on renal outcomes. Liraglutide dose, route, and frequency were not specified in the available text. WRF outcomes are from post-hoc analysis, not pre-specified primary/secondary outcomes of original trial.

title: iGlarLixi effectively reduces residual hyperglycaemia in patients with type 2 diabetes on basal insulin: A post hoc analysis from the LixiLan-L study.
population: Adults with type 2 diabetes with ≥1-year history of T2D, on basal insulin with or without oral antidiabetes drugs for ≥6 months before screening, HbA1c 7% to 10%, mean fasting self-measured plasma glucose ≤140 mg/dL, receiving insulin glargine 20 to 50 units daily after run-in period

outcomes_secondary: Proportion of patients achieving both HbA1c (<7.0%) and FPG (<140 mg/dL) targets; change from baseline in HbA1c; change from baseline in FPG; change from baseline in 2-hour postprandial glucose; change from baseline in body weight; insulin dose; proportion of patients with level 2 hypoglycaemia (glucose <54 mg/dL); proportion of patients with gastrointestinal adverse events
extraction_notes: This is a post hoc analysis of the LixiLan-L study (NCT02058160). The study was randomized and open-label. Primary outcome designation not explicitly stated in the text; outcomes listed are those analyzed in this post hoc analysis.

title: Cardiovascular Risk Reduction With Liraglutide: An Exploratory Mediation Analysis of the LEADER Trial.
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes, HbA1c ≥7% (≥53 mmol/mol), and high risk for cardiovascular disease (aged ≥50 years with established CVD or chronic kidney disease stage 3 or greater, or ≥60 years with at least one risk factor for CVD)

comparison: Placebo once daily by injection, in addition to standard-of-care treatment for type 2 diabetes and other cardiovascular risk factors
outcomes_primary: Time to first occurrence of major adverse cardiovascular event (MACE), defined as composite of cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or nonfatal stroke
outcomes_secondary: Individual components of the primary composite end point (cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke) and all-cause death; other variables assessed included HbA1c, body weight, waist circumference, fasting lipids, systolic blood pressure, diastolic blood pressure, pulse rate, biochemical and hematological parameters, calcitonin levels, anti-liraglutide antibodies, urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR), occurrence of hypoglycemia, adverse events, and concomitant medication use
extraction_notes: This is an exploratory mediation analysis of the LEADER trial (NCT01179048). The primary trial results were previously published; this analysis aimed to identify potential mediators of the cardiovascular benefit observed with liraglutide. The original LEADER trial design and endpoints are described, but this publication focuses on secondary mediation analyses.

title: The effect of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists liraglutide and semaglutide on cardiovascular and renal outcomes across baseline blood pressure categories: Analysis of the LEADER and SUSTAIN 6 trials.
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes (HbA1c ≥7.0%) and high cardiovascular risk, defined as: age ≥50 years with ≥1 co-existing cardiovascular condition (coronary heart disease, cerebrovascular disease, chronic kidney disease stage ≥3, or chronic NYHA class II or III heart failure) OR age ≥60 years with ≥1 cardiovascular risk factor (microalbuminuria or proteinuria, hypertension and left ventricular hypertrophy, left ventricular systolic or diastolic dysfunction, or ankle-brachial index <0.9)
intervention: LEADER trial: Liraglutide subcutaneous injection; SUSTAIN 6 trial: Semaglutide subcutaneous injection; follow-up up to 5 years in LEADER (median 3.8 years) and approximately 2 years in SUSTAIN 6 (median 2.1 years)
comparison: Placebo (in both LEADER and SUSTAIN 6 trials)
outcomes_primary: First occurrence of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE): composite of cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, or non-fatal stroke
outcomes_secondary: Composite renal outcome (new or worsening nephropathy): new-onset persistent macroalbuminuria, persistent doubling of serum creatinine level, need for continuous renal replacement therapy, or death from renal disease; Expanded MACE (primary MACE plus revascularization and hospitalization for heart failure or unstable angina); Hospitalization for heart failure; Cardiovascular death; All-cause mortality
extraction_notes: This is a post hoc analysis of two separate trials (LEADER n=9340; SUSTAIN 6 n=3297) evaluating cardiorenal effects across baseline blood pressure categories. Specific doses of liraglutide and semaglutide were not reported in this post hoc analysis manuscript.

title: Liraglutide accelerates colonic transit in people with type 1 diabetes and polyneuropathy: A randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial.

comparison: Placebo for 26 weeks
outcomes_primary: Regional transit times (gastric emptying, small-bowel transit time, large bowel transit time) and motility indexes assessed with a wireless motility capsule
outcomes_secondary: Gastrointestinal symptoms evaluated using the validated gastroparesis cardinal symptom index (including postprandial fullness, bloating)
extraction_notes: The abstract does not explicitly distinguish between primary and secondary outcomes; classification based on order of presentation and apparent emphasis

title: The GLP-1 receptor agonist lixisenatide reduces postprandial glucose in patients with diabetes secondary to total pancreatectomy: a randomised, placebo-controlled, double-blinded crossover trial.

outcomes_secondary: Peak glucose concentration, time to peak glucose, gastric emptying, postprandial glucagon responses, postprandial plasma C-peptide responses
extraction_notes: Dose, frequency, and duration of lixisenatide not specified in abstract. Study included both pancreatectomy patients and a healthy control group, both receiving lixisenatide vs placebo in crossover design.

title: Acute assessment of subjective appetite and implicated hormones after a hypnosis-induced hallucinated meal: a randomized cross-over pilot trial.

extraction_notes: Small pilot trial with only 8 participants. Abstract describes this as a 'highly selected group of individuals'. Primary outcome not explicitly labeled as such - designation inferred from study aim.

title: Consuming decaffeinated coffee with milk and sugar added before a high-glycaemic index meal improves postprandial glycaemic and insulinaemic responses in healthy adults.

intervention: Decaffeinated coffee with milk and sugar consumed before a high-glycaemic index meal; also tested: espresso, instant, boiled, and decaffeinated coffee (all with milk and sugar), and black coffees (espresso, instant, boiled, decaffeinated without milk and sugar)
comparison: Plain water

title: Liraglutide treatment in overweight and obese patients with type 1 diabetes: A 26-week randomized controlled trial; mechanisms of weight loss.
population: Adult overweight and obese patients with type 1 diabetes (T1DM) with no detectable C-peptide

outcomes_primary: Glycaemic control (glycated haemoglobin); adipose tissue metabolism
outcomes_secondary: Hypoglycaemia; time spent in normal glycaemia; time spent in hyperglycaemia; body weight; fat mass (including visceral fat); lean mass; systolic blood pressure; adipose tissue gene expression (adipose tissue triglyceride lipase, carnitine palmitoyl transferase-1, PPARα, PPARδ, uncoupling protein-2, type 2 iodothyronine deiodinase)
extraction_notes: Primary outcomes not explicitly distinguished from secondary outcomes in abstract; outcomes listed as primary are based on stated aims

title: Semaglutide 2.4 mg for the Treatment of Obesity: Key Elements of the STEP Trials 1 to 5.
population: Adults aged ≥18 years with obesity (BMI ≥30 kg/m2) or overweight (BMI ≥27 kg/m2) with weight-related complications (dyslipidemia, obstructive sleep apnea, hypertension, or cardiovascular disease), with history of at least one self-reported unsuccessful dietary effort to lose body weight. STEP 2 specifically includes adults with type 2 diabetes (HbA1c 7%-10%) diagnosed ≥180 days prior to screening with BMI ≥27 kg/m2. STEP 1, 3, 4, 5 exclude participants with type 2 diabetes. Exclusions include self-reported change in body weight >5 kg within 90 days before screening, history of type 1 diabetes, HbA1c ≥6.5% (for non-diabetes trials), or previous treatment with glucose-lowering agents or antiobesity medications within past 90 days.
intervention: Semaglutide 2.4 mg subcutaneously once weekly as adjunct to lifestyle intervention (500 kcal/day deficit diet and 150 min/week physical activity). STEP 3: semaglutide 2.4 mg with intensive behavioral therapy plus initial 8-week low-calorie diet followed by 60 weeks hypocaloric diet. STEP 4: 20-week run-in with semaglutide 2.4 mg then continued semaglutide 2.4 mg for 48 weeks. Dose escalated over 16-week titration period.
comparison: Placebo subcutaneously once weekly as adjunct to lifestyle intervention. STEP 2 also includes semaglutide 1.0 mg once weekly arm. All comparator groups receive same lifestyle intervention as intervention group.
outcomes_primary: Percentage change from baseline to end of treatment in body weight; proportion of participants achieving ≥5% weight loss from baseline at end of treatment (not applicable for STEP 4)
outcomes_secondary: Proportion of participants achieving ≥10% or ≥15% body weight reduction from baseline to end of treatment (not applicable for STEP 4); change from baseline to end of treatment in waist circumference (cm), systolic blood pressure (mmHg), and clinical outcome assessments including Short Form36v2 Health Survey, Impact of Weight on Quality of Life-Lite Clinical Trials Version
extraction_notes: This is a protocol/design paper for 5 phase 3 trials (STEP 1-5) with approximately 5,000 participants total. Results were not yet available at time of publication. Trial durations vary: STEP 1, 2, 3 are 68 weeks treatment; STEP 4 is 20-week run-in plus 48 weeks; STEP 5 is 2 years. Randomization ratios differ across trials (2:1, 1:1:1, 1:1).

title: Measures of adherence as predictors of early and total weight loss with intensive behavioral therapy for obesity combined with liraglutide 3.0 mg.
population: Adults aged 21-70 years with BMI of 30 to 55 kg/m2, without serious medical or psychological conditions (e.g., diabetes mellitus, recent cardiovascular disease, severe major depressive disorder) or contraindications to liraglutide use (e.g., history of medullary thyroid cancer)

comparison: IBT-alone: 52-week intensive behavioral therapy program without additional treatment (medication or meal replacement)
outcomes_primary: 52-week weight loss (percent change in weight from baseline to week 52)
outcomes_secondary: Early weight loss at week 6; weight change from weeks 24 to 52; associations between treatment adherence measures (visit attendance, dietary self-monitoring, medication adherence, meal replacement adherence) and weight loss outcomes
extraction_notes: This is a secondary analysis of a randomized trial focused on adherence predictors rather than efficacy comparison. Primary outcomes of the parent trial were previously reported. The study examined relationships between adherence behaviors and weight loss rather than between-group treatment differences.

title: Effects of Sustained Treatment With Lixisenatide on Gastric Emptying and Postprandial Glucose Metabolism in Type 2 Diabetes: A Randomized Controlled Trial.

extraction_notes: Study design was double-blind randomized parallel design. Primary vs secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract. Sample size was 30 patients total.

title: GIP and GLP-1 Potentiate Sulfonylurea-Induced Insulin Secretion in Hepatocyte Nuclear Factor 1α Mutation Carriers.
population: HNF1A mutation carriers (pathogenic HNF1A mutation verified by genetic testing, treated with diet, sulfonylurea monotherapy, or noninsulin treatments with or without sulfonylurea, aged ≥18 years) and matched control subjects without diabetes (fasting plasma glucose ≤6 mmol/L, HbA1c ≤6.1%, no family history of type 1 or type 2 diabetes, aged ≥18 years). outcomes_primary: Baseline-subtracted area under the curve (bsAUC) for C-peptide at 0-60 min, 60-120 min, and 0-120 min
outcomes_secondary: Insulin concentrations, insulin secretion rate (ISR), C-peptide/glucose ratio, insulin/glucose ratio, ISR/glucose ratio, glucagon concentrations, glucose infusion rate, arginine-induced C-peptide and glucagon secretion (peak, AUC120-125 min, iAUC120-125 min), plasma GIP and GLP-1 concentrations
extraction_notes: Crossover design with 6 experimental days per participant. Small sample size (n=10 per group). One study day excluded in each group due to protocol deviation. HNF1A mutation carriers were heterogeneous regarding diabetes status and treatment history.

title: Effect of short-acting exenatide administered three times daily on markers of cardiovascular disease in type 1 diabetes: A randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial.

extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract. Outcomes measured included: total fat mass, lean body mass, central and peripheral fat mass (assessed by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry), interleukin-2, interleukin-6, tumour necrosis factor-α, C-reactive protein, N-terminal prohormone of brain natriuretic peptide, 8-oxo-7,8-dihydroguanosine (RNA oxidation marker), and 8-oxo-7,8-dihydro-2'-deoxyguanosine (DNA oxidation marker). title: Pitfalls in the Detection of Insulinomas With Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Imaging.

comparison: No comparator intervention; comparison between PET/CT and SPECT/CT imaging modalities and between different readers
outcomes_primary: Detection and interpretation accuracy of GLP-1R imaging for insulinoma localization; identification of reading pitfalls including false-negative and false-positive readings

extraction_notes: This is a post hoc analysis of a prospective diagnostic accuracy study. Reference standard was surgery with histopathological confirmation and normalization of blood glucose levels. Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly labeled in abstract; categorized based on study aims.

title: Effects of L-Phenylalanine on Energy Intake and Glycaemia-Impacts on Appetite Perceptions, Gastrointestinal Hormones and Gastric Emptying in Healthy Males.
population: Healthy, normal-weight males, age 23 ± 1 years, BMI 21.7-22.6 kg/m2. Exclusion criteria: phenylketonuria, GI symptoms or history of GI disease or surgery, vegetarians, smokers, alcohol consumption >2 drinks on >5 days/week, use of medications affecting energy intake/appetite/GI function, high-performance athletes, lactose intolerance, consumption of protein supplements, unstable body weight (≥5% change over last 3 months), restrained eaters (score >12 on restrained eating component of 3-factor eating questionnaire)
intervention: L-phenylalanine administered intragastrically as suspension: 5g (Phe-5g) or 10g (Phe-10g) in 100mL volume, given as single bolus over 1 minute, 30 minutes before standardised buffet-meal (Part A) or mixed-nutrient drink (Part B)

title: Further improvement in glycemic control after switching from exenatide two times per day to exenatide once-weekly autoinjected suspension in patients with type 2 diabetes: 52-week results from the DURATION-NEO-1 study.

title: Efficacy and safety of exenatide as add-on therapy for patients with type 2 diabetes with an intensive insulin regimen: A randomized double-blind trial.

title: Efficacy and safety of once-weekly semaglutide versus once-daily sitagliptin as add-on to metformin in patients with type 2 diabetes in SUSTAIN China: A 30-week, double-blind, phase 3a, randomized trial.

title: Total cardiovascular or fatal events in people with type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular risk factors treated with dulaglutide in the REWIND trail: a post hoc analysis.

comparison: Matched placebo (weekly subcutaneous injection)

title: Appetite Control across the Lifecourse: The Acute Impact of Breakfast Drink Quantity and Protein Content. The Full4Health Project.
population: Normal weight and overweight/obese male and female participants across four age groups: children, adolescents, adults, and elderly (age range 7-77 years) recruited in Scotland and Greece. Exclusion criteria: smokers, morbid obesity (BMI ≥40 kg/m²), pregnancy, obesity of known endocrine origin, neurological disorders, medication known to influence appetite (including orlistat, oral antidiabetics, insulin, digoxin, anti-arrhythmics, sibutramine, antidepressants), self-reported fever/systemic infection, participation in medical or surgical weight loss program within 1 month, history of cerebrovascular disease, current major depressive disorder, history of cardiovascular disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, allergy to test drink components, and >6 hours of vigorous physical activity per week.
intervention: Four test drinks consumed for breakfast on four separate occasions (at least 4 days apart) in randomized order: (1) Normal-protein weight loss (NPWL): 15% energy from protein at 100% BMR × 0.25; (2) Normal-protein weight maintenance (NPMT): 15% energy from protein at 140% BMR × 0.25; (3) High-protein weight loss (HPWL): 30% energy from protein at 100% BMR × 0.25; (4) High-protein weight maintenance (HPMT): 30% energy from protein at 140% BMR × 0.25. Energy density: 130 kcal/100 mL. Drinks consumed immediately following baseline measures after overnight fast (10 hours).
comparison: Within-subject crossover comparison of four test drink conditions varying in protein composition (normal protein 15% vs high protein 30% of energy from protein) and quantity (weight loss 100% BMR vs weight maintenance 140% BMR). Between-subject comparisons across age groups (children, adolescents, adults, elderly), weight categories (normal weight vs overweight), genders (male vs female), and European sites (Aberdeen, Scotland vs Athens, Greece).
outcomes_primary: Ad libitum energy intake measured via 30-minute buffet-style test meal at 120 minutes post-drink consumption.
outcomes_secondary: Subjective appetite sensations assessed using visual analog scales (VASs) for adults/elderly or 9-point Likert scales for children/adolescents at 0, 30, 60, 90, and 120 minutes (hunger, fullness, prospective food consumption, composite appetite score). Test drink pleasantness and satisfaction ratings. Food reward measured by Leeds Food Preference Questionnaire (LFPQ) including fat bias and sweet bias scores for liking and wanting. Biomarkers of appetite (adults and elderly only): plasma concentrations of glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1), peptide YY (PYY), total ghrelin, and leptin. Glucose homeostasis markers: glucose, insulin, HOMA-IR, insulinogenic index (IGI), and insulin to glucose ratio (IGR).
extraction_notes: Double-blind randomized controlled crossover design. Blood samples collected from adults and elderly only, not from children or adolescents. Trial registered as NCT01597024.

title: Methods paper: Performance characteristics of novel assays for circulating levels of proglucagon-derived peptides and validation in a placebo controlled cross-over randomized clinical trial.

title: Dapagliflozin plus exenatide on patients with type 2 diabetes awaiting bariatric surgery in the DEXBASU study.

title: Respiratory Effects of Treatment with a Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonist in Patients Suffering from Obesity and Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease.

title: Effects of liraglutide vs. lifestyle changes on soluble suppression of tumorigenesis-2 (sST2) and galectin-3 in obese subjects with prediabetes or type 2 diabetes after comparable weight loss.

title: A randomized trial to investigate the efficacy and safety of once-daily liraglutide 1.8 mg in Japanese adults with type 2 diabetes exhibiting an inadequate response to liraglutide 0.9 mg.

extraction_notes: Run-in period of 12 weeks with liraglutide 0.9 mg preceded randomization; only participants with inadequate response (HbA1c ≥7.0% after run-in) were randomized. Pre-trial OAD was discontinued at run-in initiation. Open-label trial design.

title: Quinine Effects on Gut and Pancreatic Hormones and Antropyloroduodenal Pressures in Humans-Role of Delivery Site and Sex.

intervention: Quinine hydrochloride 600 mg administered as 10-mL bolus via intragastric (IG) or intraduodenal (ID) delivery on 2 separate occasions, 3-7 days apart

outcomes_primary: Plasma concentrations of gut hormones (ghrelin, cholecystokinin, peptide YY, GLP-1) and pancreatic hormones (insulin, glucagon); antropyloroduodenal pressures (antral, pyloric, and duodenal pressure waves)
outcomes_secondary: Plasma glucose concentrations; gastrointestinal symptoms (bloating and nausea) assessed by visual analog scale
extraction_notes: Crossover design with randomized, double-blind administration. No placebo control condition included; effects determined relative to baseline. Studies in women performed during follicular phase of menstrual cycle.

title: Cost-Effectiveness of Once-Weekly Semaglutide 1 mg versus Canagliflozin 300 mg in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus in a Canadian Setting.
journal: Applied health economics and health policy
population: Adults aged ≥18 years with type 2 diabetes mellitus, HbA1c levels of 7.0-10.5% (53-91 mmol/mol), on stable daily metformin dose (≥1500 mg or maximum tolerated dose) for ≥90 days, and eGFR ≥60 mL/min/1.73 m²
intervention: Once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide 1 mg
comparison: Once-daily oral canagliflozin 300 mg

title: Clinical Outcomes by Albuminuria Status with Dulaglutide versus Insulin Glargine in Participants with Diabetes and CKD: AWARD-7 Exploratory Analysis.

title: A pilot clinical study to Evaluate Liraglutide-mediated Anti-platelet activity in patients with type-2 Diabetes (ELAID study).

comparison: Placebo (saline) for 6 months

title: Interrupting Prolonged Sitting with Intermittent Walking Increases Postprandial Gut Hormone Responses.

outcomes_secondary: Changes in net dipeptidyl peptidase 4 secretion from adipose tissue primary explants
extraction_notes: Small sample size (n=10). Randomized crossover design. Primary vs secondary outcome distinction not explicitly stated; classified based on emphasis in abstract.

title: Effects of ileal glucose infusion on enteropancreatic hormone secretion in humans: relationship to glucose absorption.

outcomes_secondary: Ghrelin, GIP (glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide), insulin, C-peptide, glucagon secretion; ileal glucose absorption measured by serum 3-O-methylglucose concentrations and glucose in ileostomy effluent; blood glucose
extraction_notes: Study design is double-blind, randomized, crossover. Sample size is 10 subjects. Measurement period was 180 minutes. Primary outcome not explicitly designated; GLP-1 appears to be main outcome of interest based on study purposes.

title: Exenatide for weight-loss maintenance in adolescents with severe obesity: A randomized, placebo-controlled trial.
population: Adolescents aged 12 to <18 years with severe obesity (BMI ≥1.2 × 95th age- and sex-specific percentile or ≥35 kg/m2, whichever was lower), Tanner stage ≥2, who achieved ≥5% BMI reduction during meal replacement therapy run-in phase. outcomes_secondary: Changes from randomization to 52 weeks in: body composition (total body fat and visceral adipose tissue measured by DXA), blood pressure, fasting lipid profile, fasting glucose, fasting insulin, hemoglobin A1c, quality of life (Impact of Weight on Quality of Life-Kids questionnaire); proportion maintaining ≥5% BMI reduction at 52 weeks
extraction_notes: Run-in phase design: participants first underwent 4-8 weeks of meal replacement therapy (~1,400 kcals/day) and only those achieving ≥5% BMI reduction were randomized to the 52-week treatment phase

title: Efficacy and safety of cotadutide, a dual glucagon-like peptide-1 and glucagon receptor agonist, in a randomized phase 2a study of patients with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease.
population: Adults aged 18-84 years with type 2 diabetes mellitus and chronic kidney disease (stage 3, eGFR 30-59 ml/min/1.73 m2), body mass index 25-45 kg/m2, HbA1c 6.5-10.5% (48-91 mmol/mol), glucose control managed with any insulin and/or oral therapy combination except GLP-1 RAs with no significant dose changes (>50%) within 3 months before screening. intervention: Cotadutide, subcutaneous injection, once daily in the morning, dose escalation: 50 μg for 4 days, 100 μg for 7 days, 200 μg for 7 days, then 300 μg for 14 days (total 32 days treatment)
comparison: Placebo, subcutaneous injection, once daily for 32 days
outcomes_primary: Percentage change in mixed-meal tolerance test (MMTT) plasma glucose area under the curve (AUC) from baseline to day 32
outcomes_secondary: Incidence of adverse events and serious adverse events; changes from baseline in vital signs, blood pressure, electrocardiogram, 24-hour pulse rate, bioimpedance spectroscopy, clinical laboratory test results; change from baseline in HbA1c; change from baseline in fasting plasma glucose; percentage of time spent within target interstitial glucose range (70-180 mg/dl or 3.9-10 mmol/L) over 7-day period; percentage and absolute change in bodyweight; pharmacokinetics parameters; anti-drug antibody titre. Exploratory: change from baseline in mean urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR) and eGFR; percentage change and change in total daily insulin dose
extraction_notes: Randomization was 1:1, stratified by insulin dose (≥20 vs <20 units per day). This was a phase 2a study with dose escalation design. Sample size was 41 participants (21 cotadutide, 20 placebo).

title: Efficacy of IDegLira Versus IDegAsp Therapy in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes: A Randomized Crossover Study by isCGM.
population: Adults aged 20-80 years with type 2 diabetes mellitus diagnosed at least 1 year prior, treated with oral hypoglycemic agents or long-acting insulin for at least 6 months, with HbA1c 7.0-11.0%. Exclusions: recent severe ketosis/diabetic coma/precoma, severe hypoglycemia within 6 weeks, severe renal dysfunction (eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m2 or serum creatinine ≥2.0 mg/dL), end-stage renal disease on dialysis, proliferative retinopathy (unless stable after photocoagulation), history of severe gastrointestinal surgery, pregnancy/breastfeeding, severe infections, systemic corticosteroids, severe liver dysfunction (AST or ALT ≥100 IU/L), history of allergies to IDegLira or IDegAsp, malignant tumors
intervention: Insulin degludec/liraglutide (IDegLira) injected once daily just before supper, starting dose 10 doses (1 dose = IDeg 1U + liraglutide 0.036 mg), titrated based on preprandial glucose at breakfast to target 100-119 mg/dL
comparison: Insulin degludec/insulin aspart (IDegAsp) injected once daily just before supper, starting dose 4-20 units (70:30 ratio of IDeg to IAsp), titrated based on preprandial glucose at breakfast to target 100-119 mg/dL
outcomes_primary: Time in range (TIR, glucose 70-180 mg/dL); postprandial glucose levels at 60, 90, and 120 minutes after each meal; time below range level 1 (TBR, glucose <70 mg/dL)
outcomes_secondary: Time above range (TAR, glucose >180 mg/dL); time below range level 2 (glucose <54 mg/dL); nocturnal TBR level 1 (00:00-06:00); 24-hour mean glucose; 00:00-06:00 mean glucose; 24-hour standard deviation of glucose variability; 24-hour coefficient of variation (CV) of glucose variability; rate of 24-hour CV ≤36%; 24-hour M value; mean amplitude of glycemic excursion (MAGE); mean postprandial glucose excursion (MPPGE); mean of daily difference (MODD); preprandial glucose level at each meal; IDeg units in each FRC
extraction_notes: Randomized open-label crossover design with 3-day isCGM assessment periods for each treatment. Hospital-based study with standardized diet. Patients on DPP4 inhibitors at baseline were required to discontinue. Treatment duration approximately 10-11 days titration plus 15-day isCGM period.

title: A study on pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics and safety of lixisenatide in children and adolescents with type 2 diabetes.
population: Male or female individuals aged ≥10 and <18 years with documented type 2 diabetes suboptimally controlled with stable doses of metformin and/or basal insulin for 8 weeks prior to randomization; HbA1c at screening >6.5% and ≤11%; BMI >85th percentile for age and gender; BMI ≤50 kg/m2; fasting C-peptide at screening >0.6 ng/mL; negative test for anti-insulinoma associated protein 2 and anti-glutamic acid decarboxylase autoantibodies; no contraindication for GLP-1 RAs; no use of other antihyperglycemic treatments within 1 month prior to screening
intervention: Lixisenatide subcutaneous injection once daily: 5 μg daily for weeks 1-2, escalated to 10 μg daily for weeks 3-4, then 20 μg daily for weeks 5-6 (total 6 weeks treatment)
comparison: Matching placebo subcutaneous injection once daily for 6 weeks
outcomes_primary: Safety assessed by occurrence of adverse events, treatment-emergent adverse events, clinical laboratory evaluations including vital signs, 12-lead electrocardiogram parameters, body temperature, physical examination, and presence of anti-lixisenatide antibodies
outcomes_secondary: Pharmacokinetic assessments: plasma concentrations, maximum plasma concentration (Cmax), time to reach Cmax (tmax), area under the curve from 0h to 4.5h (AUC0-4.5); Pharmacodynamic assessments: change from baseline in plasma glucose AUC0-4.5, change from baseline in fasting plasma glucose, change from baseline in 2-hour post-prandial glucose excursion, change from baseline in HbA1c, plasma glucose profiles, changes in body weight and BMI
extraction_notes: Phase 1 study; sample size based on empirical considerations with no formal calculation; randomization ratio was 3:1 (lixisenatide:placebo); actual enrolled participants were aged 13-17 years despite eligibility criteria of ≥10 years

title: The effect of liraglutide on cardiac autonomic function in type 2 diabetes: A prespecified secondary analysis from the LIRAFLAME randomized, double-blinded, placebo-controlled trial.

intervention: Liraglutide
comparison: Placebo

Dose, route, frequency, and duration of liraglutide not specified. Primary outcomes not identifiable from title. Cardiac autonomic function listed as secondary outcome based on the secondary analysis designation.

title: Safety and efficacy of combination therapy with semaglutide, cilofexor and firsocostat in patients with non-alcoholic steatohepatitis: A randomised, open-label phase II trial.

comparison: Semaglutide 2.4 mg once weekly monotherapy; semaglutide plus cilofexor 30 mg; semaglutide plus cilofexor 100 mg; semaglutide plus firsocostat; semaglutide plus cilofexor 30 mg plus firsocostat
outcomes_primary: Safety (incidence of adverse events)
outcomes_secondary: All efficacy endpoints were exploratory: liver steatosis measured by MRI-PDFF, liver biochemistry, non-invasive tests of fibrosis, weight loss

title: Efficacy and safety benefits of iGlarLixi versus insulin glargine 100 U/mL or lixisenatide in Asian Pacific people with suboptimally controlled type 2 diabetes on oral agents: The LixiLan-O-AP randomized controlled trial.

extraction_notes: Specific doses for iGlarLixi and lixisenatide not provided in abstract. Duration confirmed as 24 weeks. Primary outcome not explicitly labeled but HbA1c change is implied primary endpoint based on study structure.

title: The effects of empagliflozin, dietary energy restriction, or both on appetite-regulatory gut peptides in individuals with type 2 diabetes and overweight or obesity: The SEESAW randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial.
population: Adults aged 30-75 years with type 2 diabetes (drug naïve or on stable metformin monotherapy; HbA1c 6.0%-10.0% [42-86 mmol/mol]) and body mass index of 25 kg/m2 or higher; men or postmenopausal women; key exclusions: type 1 diabetes, eGFR less than 60 ml/min per 1.73 m2, familial glucosuria, contraindications to SGLT2i therapy, loop diuretics use, severely energy-restricted diet (<800 kcal/day), premenopausal women

outcomes_primary: Change from baseline to 24 weeks in postprandial circulating total peptide-YY (PYY) response during a 3-hour mixed-meal tolerance test, assessed via time-averaged total area under the curve

extraction_notes: Four-arm trial with 1:1:1:1 randomization. Energy restriction in diet groups matched estimated energy deficit from SGLT2i-induced urinary glucose excretion (~360 kcal/day). Trial registration: NCT02798744.

title: Weight regain and cardiometabolic effects after withdrawal of semaglutide: The STEP 1 trial extension.
population: Adults aged 18 years or older with body mass index of 30 kg/m2 or higher, or 27 kg/m2 or higher with at least one weight-related co-morbidity (hypertension, dyslipidaemia, obstructive sleep apnoea or cardiovascular disease), without type 1 or 2 diabetes, with a history of at least one self-reported unsuccessful dietary effort to lose weight

outcomes_secondary: Change in BMI; change in systolic and diastolic blood pressure; change in C-reactive protein; change in HbA1c; change in lipids (triglycerides, total cholesterol, HDL cholesterol, LDL cholesterol, VLDL cholesterol); change in glycaemic category (normoglycaemia, prediabetes, diabetes); proportion of participants with 5% or higher weight loss from baseline at week 120; consistency of 68-week treatment effect between extension and full analysis populations
extraction_notes: This is an extension study of STEP 1 trial (NCT03548935). All extension phase analyses were exploratory with no formal statistical hypothesis testing. The extension followed a representative subset of participants from selected countries (Canada, Germany, Japan, UK, United States). No distinction between primary and secondary outcomes as all were exploratory objectives.

title: Efficacy of once-weekly tirzepatide versus once-daily insulin degludec on glycaemic control measured by continuous glucose monitoring in adults with type 2 diabetes (SURPASS-3 CGM): a substudy of the randomised, open-label, parallel-group, phase 3 SURPASS-3 trial.

comparison: Insulin degludec once-daily
outcomes_primary: Proportion of time in tight target glucose range measured by continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) over 24 hours
outcomes_secondary: Time in tight target range at 24 weeks and 52 weeks

title: Effects of subcutaneous tirzepatide versus placebo or semaglutide on pancreatic islet function and insulin sensitivity in adults with type 2 diabetes: a multicentre, randomised, double-blind, parallel-arm, phase 1 clinical trial.

outcomes_secondary: Change in clamp disposition index from baseline to week 28 (tirzepatide versus semaglutide); glucose control; total insulin secretion rate; M value (insulin sensitivity); fasting and postprandial glucagon concentrations. extraction_notes: Randomisation ratio was 3:3:2 (tirzepatide:semaglutide:placebo). Study was phase 1, multicentre, conducted at two centres in Germany.

title: Effect of tirzepatide versus insulin degludec on liver fat content and abdominal adipose tissue in people with type 2 diabetes (SURPASS-3 MRI): a substudy of the randomised, open-label, parallel-group, phase 3 SURPASS-3 trial.

extraction_notes: Baseline HbA1c threshold for eligibility is truncated in abstract. Dose frequency and route of administration for tirzepatide and insulin degludec not specified. Duration of treatment is 52 weeks based on outcome assessment timepoint. Open-label design noted.

title: Mechanisms underlying the blood pressure lowering effects of dapagliflozin, exenatide, and their combination in people with type 2 diabetes: a secondary analysis of a randomized trial.

outcomes_primary: Activity in central reward and satiety circuits in response to food related stimuli (primary endpoint of main trial)
outcomes_secondary: Mechanisms underlying blood pressure reduction including: plasma volume (calculated by Strauss formula, bioimpedance spectroscopy, hematocrit), autonomic nervous system activity (heart rate variability measures: LF/HF ratio, SDNN, RMSSD), arterial stiffness (augmentation index at heart rate 75), systemic hemodynamic parameters (systolic blood pressure, diastolic blood pressure, mean arterial pressure, heart rate, stroke volume, cardiac output, systemic vascular resistance), natriuresis (24-hour urinary sodium excretion), 24-hour urinary volume, glucose excretion, extracellular and intracellular fluid volume

title: Combination therapy with exenatide decreases the dapagliflozin-induced changes in brain responses to anticipation and consumption of palatable food in patients with type 2 diabetes: A randomized controlled trial.
population: Men and postmenopausal women, aged 18-75 years, with stable body weight (<5% reported change during the previous 3 months), body mass index >27 kg/m2, diagnosed with type 2 diabetes, on metformin with or without sulphonylurea derivatives (stable dose for ≥3 months), HbA1c 7-10% (53-86 mmol/mol) for metformin monotherapy or 7.5-10% (58-86 mmol/mol) for metformin plus sulphonylurea

outcomes_primary: Brain responses (BOLD fMRI signal) to anticipation of palatable food (chocolate milk versus tasteless solution) and to actual food receipt (chocolate milk receipt versus tasteless solution receipt) in predefined regions of interest (insula, striatum including putamen and caudate nucleus, amygdala, orbitofrontal cortex)
outcomes_secondary: Energy intake at ad libitum lunch buffet; percentage of kcal derived from fat, protein and carbohydrates; body weight; HbA1c
extraction_notes: This is a prespecified secondary analysis of the DECREASE study (NCT03361098). Primary outcomes focus on fMRI measures at baseline, 10 days, and 16 weeks. The study randomized 1:1:1:1 to four treatment arms.

title: Effects of glepaglutide, a long-acting glucagon-like peptide-2 analog, on intestinal morphology and perfusion in patients with short bowel syndrome: Findings from a randomized phase 2 trial.
journal: JPEN. Journal of parenteral and enteral nutrition
population: Patients with short bowel syndrome (SBS) with malabsorption defined as fecal output ≥1500 g/day, stable in their SBS and parenteral support volume (<25% change in volume or energy content for four weeks before randomization), without intestinal strictures or active inflammatory bowel disease or fistula, time from last intestinal resection more than one year, no radiation enteritis, no celiac disease, no history of colon cancer

comparison: Patients served as their own control in a two-period crossover design with washout period of four to eight weeks between treatment periods; each patient received two of three different doses
outcomes_primary: Absolute change from baseline in fecal output assessed by metabolic balance studies
outcomes_secondary: Changes from baseline in plasma citrulline (marker of enterocyte mass). Exploratory outcomes: changes in intestinal morphology assessed in mucosa biopsies by immunohistochemistry (villus height, crypt depth, epithelium height, chromogranin A-positive cells, GLP-2-positive cells); expression of genes associated with absorption, proliferation, and markers of tight-junction integrity in mucosa biopsies by quantitative PCR (MKI67, ACTA2, CD68, SLC5A1, SLC5A2, SLC5A5, CLDN7, CLDN15, OCEL1); intestinal perfusion assessed by laser speckle contrast imaging and quantitative fluorescence angiography with indocyanine green
extraction_notes: This is a phase 2 randomized crossover dose-finding trial without a placebo arm. The primary outcome (fecal output) was reported in a previous publication; this paper focuses on secondary and exploratory endpoints related to intestinal morphology and perfusion.

title: Effect of once-weekly semaglutide versus thrice-daily insulin aspart, both as add-on to metformin and optimized insulin glargine treatment in participants with type 2 diabetes (SUSTAIN 11): A randomized, open-label, multinational, phase 3b trial.
population: Adults with inadequately controlled type 2 diabetes (HbA1c >7.5% to ≤10.0%; >58 to ≤86 mmol/mol) treated with insulin glargine and metformin ± one additional oral antihyperglycaemic drug, willing to undergo individualized treatment intensification toward an HbA1c target of 6.5% to 7.5% (48-58 mmol/mol)

outcomes_primary: Change in HbA1c (% points) from randomization to end of treatment (week 52)
outcomes_secondary: Confirmatory secondary endpoints: time to first event adjudication committee-confirmed severe hypoglycaemic episode; time to first EAC-confirmed severe hypoglycaemic episode requiring hospitalization or documented medical help, or that was life-threatening; change in body weight (kg) from randomization to end of treatment. Supportive secondary endpoints: glycaemic control measures, hypoglycaemia (severe, documented symptomatic, asymptomatic, pseudo-hypoglycaemia, clinically significant hypoglycaemia), anthropometric outcomes, patient-reported outcomes (SF-36v2, DQLCTQ-R, TRIM-D). Safety endpoints: adverse events, serious adverse events, adverse events with fatal outcome, adverse events leading to premature treatment discontinuation
extraction_notes: Run-in period of 12 weeks to optimize insulin glargine before randomization. Study was open-label. Hierarchical testing was used; confirmatory testing stopped after severe hypoglycaemia endpoint failed to show superiority, so superiority for body weight was not formally tested.

title: Association between inflammatory markers and survival in comatose, resuscitated out-of-hospital cardiac arrest patients.
population: Comatose, resuscitated out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) patients
intervention: Exenatide (dose, route, frequency, and duration not specified in abstract)

outcomes_primary: Time to death for up to 180 days

The primary focus of this analysis was the association between inflammatory markers (leucocyte count, neutrophil levels) measured the day following admission and outcomes. Exenatide dose, route, frequency, and duration not specified.

title: Effect of expanded dulaglutide weekly doses (3.0 mg and 4.5 mg) on cardiovascular disease risk factors in participants with type 2 diabetes at increased cardiovascular disease risk: a post hoc analysis of the AWARD-11 study.
population: Adults with type 2 diabetes for ≥6 months, HbA1c between ≥7.5% and ≤11%, body mass index ≥25 kg/m², insulin- and GLP-1 RA-naïve, taking metformin for ≥3 months. intervention: Dulaglutide 3.0 mg or 4.5 mg once weekly subcutaneous injection for 52 weeks
comparison: Dulaglutide 1.5 mg once weekly subcutaneous injection for 52 weeks
outcomes_primary: This was a post hoc analysis; original primary outcome was HbA1c. outcomes_secondary: Body weight, glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c), shifts in Framingham CVD risk category from baseline to 52 weeks
extraction_notes: This is a post hoc analysis of the AWARD-11 study (NCT03495102). No placebo group was included in the original study design. Randomization was 1:1:1 to the three dulaglutide doses. The analysis focused on CVD risk factor changes rather than cardiovascular events.

title: The effects of macronutrients composition on hormones and substrates during a meal tolerance test in drugnaive and sitagliptin-treated individuals with type 2 diabetes: a randomized crossover study.
population: Drug-naive individuals with type 2 diabetes mellitus, aged 40-70 years, recently diagnosed (<3 months), confirmed by 2-hour OGTT with plasma glucose >200 mg/dL and HbA1c ≥6.5%, BMI 20-35 kg/m2, who had never been treated with oral antidiabetic agents or had not taken any antidiabetic agent for at least 12 weeks before study entry and never received antidiabetic agents for >3 months at any time in the past

outcomes_secondary: Plasma insulin, C-peptide, total GLP-1, glucagon, and non-esterified fatty acids (NEFA) levels during meal tolerance tests; HOMA-IR; Matsuda insulin sensitivity index; QUICKI; adipose tissue insulin resistance index (Adipo-IR); insulin/glucagon AUC ratio; insulin/NEFA AUC ratio

The primary outcomes were not explicitly designated as primary versus secondary in the text; classification based on main focus of results reporting. Sample size was 16 participants (8 per treatment arm at each crossover period).

title: Sperm count is increased by diet-induced weight loss and maintained by exercise or GLP-1 analogue treatment: a randomized controlled trial.

intervention: 8-week low-calorie diet (800 kcal/day) followed by 52 weeks of one of: liraglutide 3 mg/day subcutaneously plus habitual activity, or liraglutide 3 mg/day subcutaneously combined with exercise training (150 min/week moderate or 75 min/week vigorous physical activity)
comparison: Placebo plus habitual activity; exercise training (150 min/week moderate or 75 min/week vigorous physical activity) plus placebo

extraction_notes: This is a substudy of the S-LITE trial. Semen analysis was preregistered as explorative endpoint, not primary. The primary endpoint of weight change was for the main S-LITE trial. Number of participants providing semen samples was 56 (47 completed 8-week diet, 37 completed 52-week follow-up). Liraglutide starting dose 0.6 mg/day with weekly increases until reaching 3.0 mg/day or highest tolerable dose.

title: Effects of Semaglutide on Stroke Subtypes in Type 2 Diabetes: Post Hoc Analysis of the Randomized SUSTAIN 6 and PIONEER 6.
population: Adults with type 2 diabetes at high cardiovascular risk; aged ≥50 years with established cardiovascular disease (myocardial infarction, history of symptomatic coronary heart disease, coronary/carotid/peripheral arterial revascularization, stroke, transient ischemic attacks, >50% stenosis of coronary/carotid/lower extremities arteries), chronic heart failure or chronic kidney disease, or aged ≥60 years with cardiovascular risk factors

comparison: Placebo (subcutaneous or oral matched to intervention)

outcomes_secondary: Time to first major adverse cardiovascular event (MACE); subgroup analyses examining treatment effects on stroke by prior stroke status, prior myocardial infarction or stroke, prior atrial fibrillation, age, sex, systolic blood pressure, and estimated glomerular filtration rate
extraction_notes: This is a post hoc analysis pooling data from two cardiovascular outcome trials (SUSTAIN 6 and PIONEER 6). The primary outcomes of the original trials were cardiovascular safety endpoints; stroke and stroke subtypes were analyzed as post hoc exploratory endpoints. Trial durations not explicitly stated in this abstract/methods section.

title: Brain Activation in Response to Low-Calorie Food Pictures: An Explorative Analysis of a Randomized Trial With Dapagliflozin and Exenatide.
population: Men and postmenopausal women with type 2 diabetes, aged 18 to 75 years, stable body weight (<5% reported change during previous 3 months), BMI >25 kg/m2, using metformin with or without sulfonylurea (stable dose for ≥3 months), HbA1c 7%-10% for metformin monotherapy or 7.5%-10% for metformin plus sulfonylurea. extraction_notes: This is an exploratory analysis of the DECREASE trial. Primary and secondary outcomes were not explicitly labeled; brain activation to low-calorie food pictures was the focus of this exploratory analysis. The original trial had different primary outcomes.

title: Plasma metabolites associated with functional and clinical outcomes in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction with and without type 2 diabetes.

intervention: Liraglutide (GLP-1 receptor agonist) versus placebo
comparison: Placebo

outcomes_secondary: Exercise capacity measured by 6-minute walk distance (6MWD) at baseline and 90 days; serum NT-proBNP at baseline and 90 days; plasma metabolite levels and their association with functional and clinical outcomes; time to mortality or heart failure hospitalization
extraction_notes: This is a secondary analysis/biomarker substudy of the FIGHT trial focusing on metabolomic profiling. The primary trial was negative for liraglutide benefit. Drug dose, route, frequency and duration for liraglutide not specified in this paper. 254 of 300 original participants included in this biomarker substudy.

title: Once-Weekly Dulaglutide for the Treatment of Youths with Type 2 Diabetes.

population: Youths aged 10 to <18 years with type 2 diabetes mellitus, body-mass index >85th percentile, being treated with lifestyle modifications alone or with metformin, with or without basal insulin

comparison: Placebo (once-weekly subcutaneous injection)
outcomes_primary: Change from baseline in glycated hemoglobin level at 26 weeks
outcomes_secondary: Glycated hemoglobin level of less than 7.0%; change from baseline in fasting glucose concentration; change from baseline in BMI; safety
extraction_notes: Open-label 26-week extension study followed the double-blind phase where placebo group crossed over to dulaglutide 0.75 mg

title: Tirzepatide Once Weekly for the Treatment of Obesity.

comparison: Placebo once weekly subcutaneous injection for 72 weeks

outcomes_secondary: Prespecified cardiometabolic measures; weight reduction of 20% or more

title: Efficacy and Safety of Once-Weekly Efpeglenatide Monotherapy Versus Placebo in Type 2 Diabetes: The AMPLITUDE-M Randomized Controlled Trial.
population: Adults with type 2 diabetes inadequately controlled with diet and exercise alone, HbA1c ≥7% and ≤10% (53-86 mmol/mol) at screening, no glucose-lowering therapy within 3 months prior to screening. comparison: Placebo administered subcutaneously once weekly for up to 56 weeks
outcomes_primary: Change in HbA1c from baseline to week 30
outcomes_secondary: Change in HbA1c from baseline to week 56; proportion achieving HbA1c <7% (53 mmol/mol) at week 30; change in fasting plasma glucose from baseline to week 30; change in body weight from baseline to weeks 30 and 56
extraction_notes: Trial conducted at 54 sites in 5 countries (Germany, Poland, UK, US, Ukraine). Randomization was 1:1:1:1. Open-label rescue medication was permitted according to predefined criteria.

title: Once-Weekly Exenatide in Youth With Type 2 Diabetes.
population: Children and adolescents aged 10 to <18 years with type 2 diabetes, glycated hemoglobin 6.5-11% (not taking insulin or sulfonylurea) or 6.5-12% (taking insulin or sulfonylurea), treated with diet and exercise alone or in combination with stable dose of oral glucose-lowering drug (metformin and/or sulfonylurea) and/or insulin for at least 2 months prior to enrollment, C-peptide >0.6 ng/mL, serum creatinine ≤1.5 mg/dL (males) or ≤1.4 mg/dL (females)

comparison: Matching placebo once-weekly injection for 24 weeks
outcomes_primary: Change in glycated hemoglobin from baseline to week 24
outcomes_secondary: Change in fasting plasma glucose, change in body weight, change in systolic blood pressure, change in fasting insulin levels, lipid profiles, proportion of participants with glycated hemoglobin <7%, ≤6.5%, or <6.5% at week 24, proportion of participants requiring rescue treatment, incidence of adverse events, incidence of hypoglycemic events, laboratory parameters, heart rate, Tanner stage
