title: Circulating total and intact GDF-15 levels are not altered in response to weight loss induced by liraglutide or lorcaserin treatment in humans with obesity.
population: Adults with obesity aged 26-64 years with BMI 35.6-37.4 kg/m2; Study 1: subjects with metabolic comorbidities (insulin resistance, hypertension, or dyslipidemia); excluded: severe renal or hepatic impairment, congestive heart failure, autoimmune diseases, uncontrolled endocrine conditions, history of pancreatitis, gallstones, excessive alcohol consumption, use of warfarin, hormones, or oral anti-diabetic agents except metformin; Study 2: excluded: type 2 diabetes mellitus, severe renal and hepatic impairment, congestive heart failure, autoimmune diseases, eating disorders, uncontrolled endocrine conditions, use of weight loss medication, warfarin, hormones, phosphodiesterase inhibitors, serotonergic medications, bupropion, tricyclic antidepressants, valproic acid, codeine, tamoxifen, timolol

title: Liraglutide 3 mg on weight, body composition, and hormonal and metabolic parameters in women with obesity and polycystic ovary syndrome: a randomized placebo-controlled-phase 3 study.

outcomes_secondary: Body composition by dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry; proportion achieving at least 5% weight reduction; oral glucose tolerance test parameters; sex steroids; lipids; safety assessed in all patients receiving at least one dose
extraction_notes: Route of administration not explicitly stated but liraglutide is typically subcutaneous. Lifestyle intervention details not specified.

title: Bromocriptine quick-release as adjunct therapy in youth and adults with type 1 diabetes: A randomized, placebo-controlled crossover study.
population: Adolescents and adults with type 1 diabetes, aged 12-60 years, with clinical course consistent with type 1 diabetes, duration >9 months, HbA1c 6.5-10% for adults and ≤12% for adolescents. Exclusion criteria: heart failure, active/end stage liver disease, end stage kidney disease, cancer, undertreated thyroid disease, pregnancy, rheumatological disease, history of psychosis, current use of tobacco/drugs, systemic steroids, antipsychotics, neuroleptics, ergot-related medications, triptan medications for migraine, or diabetes medications other than insulin.
intervention: Bromocriptine Quick Release (BCQR) tablets, dosed daily in the morning, titrated weekly from 0.8 mg for one week, to 1.6 mg for one week, to 3.2 mg for remainder of 4 weeks (minimum tolerated dose 1.6 mg/day required to remain in study), for 4 weeks total treatment duration

outcomes_primary: Mean CGM glucose and insulin total daily dose (TDD)
outcomes_secondary: Blood pressure (systolic, diastolic, MAP), lipids, peripheral arterial stiffness, autonomic function measures (HRV including SDNN, RMSSD, triangular index; orthostatic BP and HR changes; Valsalva ratio), mixed meal tolerance test measures (glucose AUC, insulin AUC, GLP-1 AUC, glucagon AUC, C-peptide AUC, triglycerides AUC, NEFA AUC), CGM measures (SD, percent time >180 mg/dL, percent time <70 mg/dL), creatinine, estimated GFR (eGFRCr, eGFRCr-and-cystatin C), estimated insulin sensitivity (eIS), indirect calorimetry (fasting REE, respiratory quotient, ΔRQ), hypoglycemia awareness, cardiac output, systemic vascular resistance, urine albumin/creatinine ratio, adiponectin

title: FGF21 contributes to metabolic improvements elicited by combination therapy with exenatide and pioglitazone in patients with type 2 diabetes.

outcomes_secondary: Glucose tolerance, insulin sensitivity, β-cell function, plasma total FGF21 levels, plasma bioactive FGF21 levels (measured before and during 2-hour 75-g oral glucose tolerance test at baseline and following 3 years of treatment)

The study appears to be a mechanistic analysis examining FGF21 as a potential contributor to metabolic improvements rather than a primary efficacy trial.

title: Comparing the effects of twice-daily exenatide and insulin on renal function in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus: secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial.

extraction_notes: This is a secondary analysis of an RCT originally designed to evaluate carotid intima-media thickness. Dose, route, and frequency of insulin aspartate 30 not specified. Exenatide dose not specified beyond twice-daily administration.

title: A phase 1b randomised controlled trial of a glucagon-like peptide-1 and glucagon receptor dual agonist IBI362 (LY3305677) in Chinese patients with type 2 diabetes.

outcomes_secondary: Pharmacokinetics (Cmax, Tmax, t½, AUC0-168h); immunogenicity (anti-drug antibodies and neutralizing antibodies); change from baseline to week 12 in HbA1c, fasting plasma glucose, fasting insulin levels; change from baseline to week 12 in post-mixed-meal tolerance test glucose, insulin, C peptide, GLP-1 and OXM levels; seven-point self-measured blood glucose profile. title: Liraglutide Plus Dapagliflozin for High Uric Acid and Microalbuminuria in Diabetes Mellitus Complicated With Metabolic Syndrome.

title: Randomized Comparison of Initiating the Fixed-Ratio Combination of iGlarLixi or Biosimilar Insulin Glargine Together With Gliclazide in Participants of South Asian Origin With Type 2 Diabetes: VARIATION 2 SA Trial.

title: Effect of race on cardiometabolic responses to once-weekly exenatide: insights from the Exenatide Study of Cardiovascular Event Lowering (EXSCEL).
population: Adults aged 18 years or older with type 2 diabetes, HbA1c 6.5-10.0% (48-86 mmol/mol), with or without previous cardiovascular disease, treated with a maximum of three oral blood glucose-lowering drugs or insulin alone or in combination with up to two oral blood glucose-lowering drugs, approximately 70% with previous cardiovascular disease, self-identifying as White, Asian, Black, or Other Race

title: DUAL I China: Improved glycemic control with IDegLira versus its individual components in a randomized trial with Chinese participants with type 2 diabetes uncontrolled on oral antidiabetic drugs.
population: Chinese adults with type 2 diabetes, aged ≥18 years, with HbA1c 53.0-85.8 mmol/mol (7.0%-10.0%), BMI ≤40 kg/m², on stable dose of metformin (≥1500 mg or maximum tolerated) with or without one other oral antidiabetic drug (α-glucosidase inhibitor, sulfonylurea, glinide, or thiazolidinedione at least half the local-label maximum approved dose) for ≥60 days before screening

title: Evaluation of the Clinical Efficacy of the Treatment of Overweight and Obesity in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus by the Telemedicine Management System Based on the Internet of Things Technology.

outcomes_primary: Not explicitly specified as primary
outcomes_secondary: Body mass index (BMI), weight, systolic blood pressure (SBP), diastolic blood pressure (DBP), fasting plasma glucose (FPG), 2-hour postprandial blood glucose (2hPG), glycosylated hemoglobin (HbA1c), insulin resistance index (HOMA-IR), islet beta cell secretion function index (HOMA-β), total cholesterol (TC), triglyceride (TG), low-density lipoprotein (LDL), adverse reactions including hypoglycemia incidence, gastrointestinal reactions, rash, urine leukocyte

title: Endogenous Glucose-Dependent Insulinotropic Polypeptide Contributes to Sitagliptin-Mediated Improvement in β-Cell Function in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes.

title: Effects of GLP-1 and GIP on Islet Function in Glucose-Intolerant, Pancreatic-Insufficient Cystic Fibrosis.

title: The probiotic

intervention: Insulin glargine at bedtime titrated to target fasting glucose ≤5.3 mmol/l plus twice-daily exenatide (5 μg twice daily before breakfast and dinner for first 4 weeks, then 10 μg twice daily for next 4 weeks) for 8 weeks, followed by 12-week washout
comparison: Insulin glargine alone at bedtime titrated to target fasting glucose ≤5.3 mmol/l; Insulin glargine at bedtime plus thrice-daily pre-meal insulin lispro titrated to target fasting glucose ≤5.3 mmol/l and 2-hour postprandial glucose <8 mmol/l
outcomes_primary: Endothelial function assessed by Reactive Hyperemia Index (RHI) measured by peripheral arterial tonometry
outcomes_secondary: Systolic blood pressure; diastolic blood pressure; heart rate
extraction_notes: This is an ancillary/pre-specified secondary analysis of the PREVAIL trial; primary outcome of the main trial was beta-cell function. RHI assessment completed in only 73 of 102 participants due to COVID-19 pandemic disruptions.

title: Biomarker Changes Associated With Both Dulaglutide and Cardiovascular Events in the REWIND Randomized Controlled Trial: A Nested Case-Control Post Hoc Analysis.
population: REWIND trial participants with type 2 diabetes; nested case-control design including participants with MACE during follow-up and matched non-MACE participants
intervention: Dulaglutide (glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist), weekly administration
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Two-year changes in 19 protein biomarkers from baseline; association of biomarker changes with both dulaglutide treatment and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE)
outcomes_secondary: Two-year changes in 135 metabolites from baseline; association of metabolite changes with both dulaglutide treatment and MACE
extraction_notes: This is a post hoc nested case-control analysis of the REWIND trial. Dose and duration of dulaglutide treatment not specified in abstract. Primary outcomes of original REWIND trial (MACE) served as selection criteria for case-control matching rather than outcomes in this biomarker analysis.

title: Effect of once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide 2.4 mg on weight- and health-related quality of life in an East Asian population: Patient-reported outcomes from the STEP 6 trial.
population: Adults from East Asia with body mass index (BMI) ≥27.0 kg/m²
intervention: Once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide 2.4 mg; once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide 1.7 mg
comparison: Placebo
extraction_notes: Abstract appears truncated. Outcomes mentioned include weight-related quality of life (WRQOL) and health-related quality of life (HRQOL), but it is unclear whether these are primary or secondary outcomes. Unable to determine outcome hierarchy from available text. Full population eligibility criteria may be incomplete due to truncation.

title: The effect of GLP-1RA exenatide on idiopathic intracranial hypertension: a randomized clinical trial.
population: Women aged 18-60 years with active idiopathic intracranial hypertension meeting diagnostic criteria, with normal brain imaging (except radiological signs of raised ICP), optic nerve head swelling in at least one eye, and ICP >25 cmCSF. Excluded: significant comorbidities, prior CSF diversion procedures, current use of GLP-1 receptor agonists or DPP-4 inhibitors, drugs thought to reduce ICP, pregnancy or planning pregnancy.
intervention: Subcutaneous exenatide (Byetta): loading dose of 20 μg on day 1, then 10 μg twice daily self-administered for 12 weeks
comparison: Subcutaneous 0.9% saline placebo: equivalent volume loading dose on day 1, then equivalent volume twice daily self-administered for 12 weeks
outcomes_primary: Intracranial pressure (ICP) measured by telemetric ICP catheter at 2.5 hours, 24 hours, and 12 weeks post-drug administration
outcomes_secondary: Monthly headache days, headache severity, monthly analgesia days, logMAR visual acuity (ETDRS charts), perimetric mean deviation (Humphrey 24-2 SITA), BMI, health-related quality of life (SF-36 and HIT-6)
extraction_notes: Alpha for statistical significance was pre-specified at 0.1 rather than conventional 0.05. Exploratory analyses included continuous ICP monitoring over first 2.5 hours and overnight between 24.00-07.00 hours.

title: Effect of Various Dosing Schedules on the Pharmacokinetics of Oral Semaglutide: A Randomised Trial in Healthy Subjects.
population: Healthy subjects aged 18-64 years with body mass index 20-29.9 kg/m2, considered generally healthy based on medical history, physical examination, vital signs, electrocardiogram, and clinical laboratory tests. Excluded: glycated haemoglobin ≥6.5%, clinically significant gastrointestinal disorders, personal or first-degree relative history of multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2 or medullary thyroid cancer, major surgical procedures involving the stomach, presence or history of pancreatitis, smoking >5 cigarettes per day
intervention: Oral semaglutide co-formulated with SNAC, once daily for 10 days (3 mg for first 5 days, then 7 mg for last 5 days), administered with no more than 120 mL water, with alternative dosing schedules: (1) 2-hour pre-dose fast followed by 30-min post-dose fast (2 h–30 min), (2) 4-hour pre-dose fast followed by 30-min post-dose fast (4 h–30 min), (3) 6-hour pre-dose fast followed by 30-min post-dose fast (6 h–30 min), (4) 2-hour pre-dose fast followed by overnight post-dose fast (2 h–night)
comparison: Reference arm: overnight pre-dose fast (at least 6 hours, approximately 11 hours average) followed by 30-min post-dose fast (night–30 min), oral semaglutide co-formulated with SNAC, once daily for 10 days (3 mg for first 5 days, then 7 mg for last 5 days), administered with no more than 120 mL water
outcomes_primary: Area under the semaglutide plasma concentration-time curve during a 24-hour interval after the 10th dose of oral semaglutide (AUC0-24h,sema,Day10)
outcomes_secondary: Maximum observed semaglutide plasma concentration after the 10th dose of oral semaglutide (Cmax,sema,Day10); time to maximum observed semaglutide plasma concentration after the 10th dose (tmax,sema,Day10)
extraction_notes: This is a pharmacokinetic study in healthy volunteers, not a clinical efficacy trial. The trial had 5 parallel arms with randomization ratio 1:1:1:1:2 (alternative schedules:reference). Safety outcomes were assessed but not specified as primary or secondary endpoints.

title: Semaglutide 2·4 mg once weekly in patients with non-alcoholic steatohepatitis-related cirrhosis: a randomised, placebo-controlled phase 2 trial.
population: Adults aged 18-75 years with biopsy-confirmed non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH)-related compensated cirrhosis (Kleiner F4 according to NASH Clinical Research Network classification), body-mass index of 27 kg/m² or greater, and histological NAFLD activity score of 3 or more with a score of 1 or more for both lobular inflammation and hepatocyte ballooning. Key exclusions: history of hepatic decompensation (ascites, variceal bleeding, hepatic encephalopathy, spontaneous bacterial peritonitis), liver transplantation, hepatocellular carcinoma, or gastro-oesophageal varices within past 360 days.
intervention: Once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide, escalated from 0.24 mg initial dose to 0.5 mg after 4 weeks, then to 1.0 mg, 1.7 mg, and finally 2.4 mg once weekly after 16 weeks of treatment, continued for 48 weeks total with 7-week follow-up
comparison: Visually matching placebo, once-weekly subcutaneous injection for 48 weeks with 7-week follow-up
outcomes_primary: Proportion of patients with an improvement in liver fibrosis of one stage or more on biopsy (using the NASH CRN classification) without worsening of NASH after 48 weeks. Worsening of NASH defined as worsening of one grade or more of either lobular inflammation, hepatocyte ballooning, or steatosis.
outcomes_secondary: Relative change in liver fat content measured by MRI-PDFF from baseline to week 48; relative change in liver stiffness measured by MRE from baseline to week 48; change in NASH resolution on biopsy; change in stage of fibrosis according to NASH CRN criteria; change in NAS according to NASH CRN criteria; number of treatment-emergent adverse events
extraction_notes: Primary endpoint was changed from MRE to liver biopsy on Feb 21, 2020 after completion of study protocol but before unblinding, to align with new regulatory standards. Randomization was stratified by presence or absence of type 2 diabetes. Study conducted at 38 centres in Europe and USA.

title: Weight loss maintenance with exercise and liraglutide improves glucose tolerance, glucagon response, and beta cell function.

intervention: Combination of exercise and liraglutide (glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist) for 1-year maintenance period
comparison: Placebo, exercise alone, liraglutide alone
outcomes_primary: Glucose tolerance (postprandial glucose response)
outcomes_secondary: Glucagon response, beta cell function
extraction_notes: BMI range appears truncated in abstract (32-43 kg/m). Specific doses, frequencies, and exercise protocols not provided in abstract. Primary vs secondary outcome designation inferred from study objective emphasis.

title: iGlarLixi provides a higher derived time-in-range versus insulin glargine 100 U/mL or lixisenatide in Asian Pacific people with type 2 diabetes: A post hoc analysis.
population: Asian Pacific population with type 2 diabetes; two subgroups analyzed: (1) insulin-naive patients from LixiLan-O-AP trial, (2) insulin-treated patients from LixiLan-L-CN trial
intervention: iGlarLixi (fixed-ratio combination of insulin glargine and lixisenatide)
comparison: LixiLan-O-AP trial: insulin glargine 100 U/mL (iGlar) or lixisenatide (Lixi); LixiLan-L-CN trial: insulin glargine 100 U/mL (iGlar)
outcomes_primary: Changes in derived time-in-ranges from baseline to end-of-treatment; estimated treatment differences in derived time-in-range (dTIR)
outcomes_secondary: Proportion of patients achieving ≥70% derived time-in-range (dTIR); proportion achieving ≥5% dTIR improvement; proportion achieving composite triple target (≥70% dTIR, <4% derived time-below-range [dTBR], and <25% derived time-above-range [dTAR])
extraction_notes: This is a post hoc analysis of two phase III trials (LixiLan-O-AP and LixiLan-L-CN). Derived time-in-range calculated from seven-point self-measured blood glucose. Exact doses, frequencies, and treatment durations for interventions not specified in abstract.

title: Effects of semaglutide and empagliflozin on oxygenation, vascular autoregulation, and central thickness of the retina in people with type 2 diabetes: A prespecified secondary analysis of a randomised clinical trial.
journal: Journal of diabetes and its complications

comparison: Tablet placebo
outcomes_primary: Venular oxygenation of the retina
outcomes_secondary: Retinal arteriolar oxygenation, venular-arteriolar oxygenation, retinal vessel diameter, central retinal thickness

title: Safety, pharmacokinetics, and pharmacodynamics of TG103, a novel long-acting GLP-1/Fc fusion protein after a single ascending dose in Chinese healthy subjects.

intervention: TG103 (GLP-1/Fc fusion protein) single subcutaneous injection at 3 mg, 7.5 mg, 15 mg, or 22.5 mg doses

outcomes_primary: Safety and tolerability; pharmacokinetics (PK) profiles; pharmacodynamics (PD) profiles

title: The Effects of Exercise on Appetite-Regulating Hormone Concentrations over a 36-h Fast in Healthy Young Adults: A Randomized Crossover Study.
population: Healthy young adults aged 18-35 years, able to exercise at vigorous intensity without restrictions (assessed by PAR-Q), BMI 18.5-30 kg/m2, not diagnosed with metabolic disease, orthopedic impairment, or eating disorder, not taking metabolism-altering medications, consuming less than 60 mg caffeine daily, not pregnant or lactating, not postmenopausal, not practicing calorie or carbohydrate restricted diets
intervention: 36-hour water-only fast initiated with a bout of treadmill exercise at 70% heart rate reserve, exercise duration individualized to expend approximately equal calories to standardized pre-fast meal (approximately 587.6 kcal), followed by 36-hour water-only fast with blood draws every 12 hours
comparison: 36-hour water-only fast without exercise (fasting alone), with blood draws every 12 hours
outcomes_primary: Area under the curve for plasma concentrations of appetite-regulating hormones (ghrelin, GLP-1, PYY, PP, leptin, insulin, GIP) over 36-hour fast
outcomes_secondary: Time course differences in plasma hormone concentrations at 0, 12, 24, and 36 hours for each hormone (ghrelin, GLP-1, PYY, PP, leptin, insulin, GIP)
extraction_notes: This is a secondary analysis of a previously published primary study. Randomized crossover design with counterbalanced conditions and minimum 6-day washout period. Sample size of 20 participants (11 males, 9 females). Standardized pre-fast meal provided 25% of estimated daily caloric requirements with standardized macronutrient composition (60% carbohydrate, 15% protein, 25% fat).

title: Preliminary observations on the administration of a glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist on body weight and select carbohydrate endpoints in persons with spinal cord injury: A controlled case series.
journal: The journal of spinal cord medicine

comparison: No treatment (control) for 26 weeks
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly differentiated in the abstract. This is a small open-label randomized case series with only 5 participants (3 intervention, 2 control).

title: Effect of the glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist liraglutide, compared to caloric restriction, on appetite, dietary intake, body fat distribution and cardiometabolic biomarkers: A randomized trial in adults with obesity and prediabetes.
population: Adults aged 18-65 years with obesity (BMI ≥30 kg/m2) and prediabetes (defined by American Diabetes Association criteria: impaired fasting serum glucose level 100-125 mg/dL, impaired glucose tolerance 140-199 mg/dL at 2 hours after 75-g oral glucose challenge, or fasting serum glycated haemoglobin level 5.7%-6.4%). Exclusions: pregnant or lactating, type 1 or 2 diabetes, resistant hypertension, history of pancreatitis, significant cardiovascular disease, asthma with regular inhaler use, impaired kidney function (GFR <60 mL) or liver function, gastrointestinal malabsorption, family or personal history of multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2 or familial medullary thyroid carcinoma, self-reported weight change >2 kg within 6 months of enrolment, history of alcohol or illicit drug abuse.
intervention: Liraglutide subcutaneous injection: 0.6 mg/d for week 1, escalated to 1.2 mg/d for week 2, then maintained at 1.8 mg/d for 14 weeks (study weeks 3-16), administered daily between 9:00 PM and 10:00 PM, plus oral placebo daily at 7:00 AM.
comparison: 1) Caloric restriction: daily caloric goal to achieve energy deficit of 390 kcal below resting energy expenditure for 14 weeks, with dietitian counseling every 2 weeks; 2) Sitagliptin (DPP-4 inhibitor as weight-neutral comparator): 100 mg/d orally each morning at 7:00 AM plus subcutaneous placebo daily between 9:00 PM and 10:00 PM for 14 weeks.
outcomes_primary: Endothelial function measured by flow-mediated dilatation (reported in prior publication).
outcomes_secondary: Proportion of fat to lean tissue mass (body composition via dual energy x-ray absorptiometry); body weight change; weight loss ≥5% of baseline; total fat mass; percent body fat; lean tissue mass; truncal fat percentage; android to gynoid fat ratio; visceral adipose tissue mass; appetite and hunger ratings via visual analogue scales (hunger, satisfaction, fullness, prospective food consumption); food preference ratings (desire for sweet, salty, savoury, fatty foods); dietary intakes (energy, macronutrients, total sugars, added sugars, glycemic load); resting energy expenditure via indirect calorimetry; substrate oxidation; cardiometabolic biomarkers (fasting glucose, insulin, HOMA-IR, lipid profile including triglycerides, HDL cholesterol, TG/HDL ratio).
extraction_notes: Primary outcome (endothelial function) was reported in a prior publication (reference 21), not in this paper. Randomization ratio was 2:1:1 (liraglutide:sitagliptin:CR). 6-week run-in period for cardiovascular risk factor management preceded randomization. Drug treatment was double-blinded; CR group was open-label.

title: Reducing BMI below the obesity threshold in adolescents treated with once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide 2.4 mg.

comparison: Placebo plus lifestyle intervention (counseling in healthy nutrition and a goal of 60 minutes of moderate- to high-intensity physical activity per day)
outcomes_primary: Achievement of improvement in BMI category by week 68; attainment of normal-weight or overweight BMI by week 68
extraction_notes: This is a post hoc analysis of the STEP TEENS trial. Primary and secondary outcomes are not explicitly distinguished in the abstract; outcomes listed appear to be the focus of this post hoc analysis rather than pre-specified primary/secondary endpoints.

title: Efficacy and Safety of Oral Small Molecule Glucagon-Like Peptide 1 Receptor Agonist Danuglipron for Glycemic Control Among Patients With Type 2 Diabetes: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
population: Adults aged 18-75 years with type 2 diabetes inadequately controlled by diet and exercise, with or without metformin treatment; HbA1c 7% to 10.5% at screening; body weight greater than 50 kg and stable; BMI 22.5 (Asia) or 24.5 (North America and Europe) to 45.4; at least 80% of enrolled participants required to be taking metformin before screening with no more than 20% treated with diet and exercise alone
intervention: Danuglipron (PF-06882961) 2.5 mg, 10 mg, 40 mg, 80 mg, or 120 mg orally twice daily with food for 16 weeks; for doses of 40 mg twice daily and above, weekly dose escalation steps were incorporated using a prespecified fixed schedule over up to 6 weeks
comparison: Matching placebo orally twice daily with food for 16 weeks
outcomes_primary: Change from baseline in glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) at week 16
outcomes_secondary: Change from baseline in HbA1c at weeks 2, 4, 6, 8, and 12; proportion of participants achieving HbA1c less than 7% at week 16; change from baseline in fasting plasma glucose (FPG) at weeks 2, 4, 6, 8, 12, and 16; change from baseline in body weight at weeks 2, 4, 6, 8, 12, and 16; safety assessments including treatment-emergent adverse events, protocol-defined hypoglycemia, and treatment-emergent clinical laboratory abnormalities, vital sign abnormalities, and electrocardiogram abnormalities; exploratory endpoints included proportion of participants achieving body weight loss of 5% or more at week 16 and changes from baseline in fasting insulin, HOMA-IR, and glucagon at week 16
extraction_notes: Phase 2b dose-ranging study with 6 parallel groups; study conducted during COVID-19 pandemic from July 2020 to July 2021; participants on metformin required stable dose for 60 days or more before screening and remained on same dose throughout study

title: Comparative Effects of Glucose-Lowering Medications on Kidney Outcomes in Type 2 Diabetes: The GRADE Randomized Clinical Trial.
population: Adults with type 2 diabetes for less than 10 years, hemoglobin A1c level between 6.8% and 8.5%, estimated glomerular filtration rate greater than or equal to 60 mL/min/1.73 m2, receiving metformin treatment
intervention: Addition of insulin glargine, glimepiride, liraglutide, or sitagliptin to metformin, with the medication combination continued until HbA1c was greater than 7.5%; thereafter, insulin was added to maintain glycemic control
comparison: Four-arm comparison: insulin glargine vs glimepiride vs liraglutide vs sitagliptin (all added to metformin)
outcomes_primary: Chronic eGFR slope (change in eGFR between year 1 and trial end); composite kidney disease progression outcome (albuminuria, dialysis, transplant, or death due to kidney disease)
outcomes_secondary: Incident eGFR less than 60 mL/min/1.73 m2; 40% decrease in eGFR to less than 60 mL/min/1.73 m2; doubling of urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR) to 30 mg/g or greater; progression of Kidney Disease Improving Global Outcomes stage
extraction_notes: Specific dosing for each medication not stated in abstract. This is a secondary analysis of the GRADE trial focused on kidney outcomes.

title: Efficacy of Exenatide Administered Twice Daily in Body Mass Index Reduction in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.
population: Adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus; subgroups defined by baseline BMI (<24 kg/m² vs ≥24 kg/m²), HbA1c (<9% vs ≥9%), and carotid intima-media thickness (<1 mm vs ≥1 mm)
intervention: Exenatide 5 μg subcutaneously twice daily (60 min before breakfast and dinner), titrated to 10 μg twice daily after 4 weeks, combined with metformin 500 mg three times daily, for 52 weeks

outcomes_primary: Change in BMI from baseline to week 52
outcomes_secondary: Correlations between BMI reduction and cardiometabolic indices: HbA1c, high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP), systolic blood pressure (SBP), and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C)
extraction_notes: This is a retrospective cohort analysis using only the exenatide arm (n=27) from a previous RCT; the insulin comparator arm was not included in this analysis; small sample size

title: Tirzepatide versus insulin glargine as second-line or third-line therapy in type 2 diabetes in the Asia-Pacific region: the SURPASS-AP-Combo trial.

outcomes_secondary: Non-inferiority and superiority of all tirzepatide doses in HbA1c reduction; proportion of patients achieving HbA1c < 7.0% at week 40; body weight change at week 40
extraction_notes: Open-label trial design. Primary endpoint specified for 10 mg and 15 mg doses only, while secondary endpoints included all three tirzepatide doses.

title: Orforglipron (LY3502970), a novel, oral non-peptide glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist: A Phase 1b, multicentre, blinded, placebo-controlled, randomized, multiple-ascending-dose study in people with type 2 diabetes.
population: Adults with type 2 diabetes aged 18 to 70 years with glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c) levels ≥53.0 mmol/mol (7.0%) and ≤91.3 mmol/mol (10.5%)

title: Evaluating potential predictors of weight loss response to liraglutide in adolescents with obesity: A post hoc analysis of the randomized, placebo-controlled SCALE Teens trial.

intervention: Liraglutide 3.0 mg (or maximum tolerated dose) subcutaneous injection daily, initiated at 0.6 mg daily and escalated weekly by 0.6 mg until target dose reached, as adjunct to lifestyle therapy, for 56 weeks

title: Once-weekly semaglutide in people with HIV-associated lipohypertrophy: a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 2b single-centre clinical trial.
population: Adults ≥18 years old with documented HIV-1 infection, cumulative ART duration ≥1 year, receiving stable ART regimen for ≥12 weeks, HIV-1 RNA <400 copies/mL for ≥6 months prior to entry, subjective observation of increased abdominal girth occurring after ART initiation, waist circumference >95 cm (men) or >94 cm (women), waist-to-hip ratio >0.94 (men) or >0.88 (women), BMI ≥25 kg/m², without known history of diabetes
intervention: Once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide with 8-week dose titration (0.25 mg weekly for 4 weeks, then 0.5 mg weekly for 4 weeks) followed by 24 weeks at 1.0 mg weekly, for a total treatment duration of 32 weeks
comparison: Matching placebo (saline) administered subcutaneously once weekly for 32 weeks with identical titration schedule
outcomes_primary: Changes in adipose tissue quantity by body compartment at 32 weeks: total body fat, limb fat, trunk fat, abdominal total adipose tissue, abdominal subcutaneous adipose tissue, abdominal visceral adipose tissue, and pericardial fat
outcomes_secondary: Changes in abdominal adipose tissue density (fat quality), total right psoas muscle area (muscle mass), total right psoas density (ectopic intermuscular fat), liver fat, lean body mass, anthropometric measurements (weight, BMI, waist circumference, waist-to-hip ratio), glucose metabolism (HbA1c%, fasting glucose, 2-hour oral glucose tolerance test), insulin resistance (fasting and 2-hour OGTT insulin, HOMA-IR), vital signs (heart rate, blood pressure), caloric intake, physical activity, ASCVD risk estimate, and adverse events
extraction_notes: Single-center study conducted at University Hospitals Cleveland Medical Center, Cleveland, Ohio, USA. Phase IIb trial. Study used 1.0 mg semaglutide (the FDA-approved dose at time of study initiation), which is lower than current recommended doses of 2.0-2.4 mg.

title: Growth differentiation factor 15 is not modified after weight loss induced by liraglutide in South Asians and Europids with type 2 diabetes mellitus.
population: Dutch Europid and Dutch South Asian adults aged 18-69 years with type 2 diabetes mellitus, BMI ≥ 25 kg/m², HbA1c levels 7.0%-10.0% (53-86 mmol/mol) despite use of metformin and/or sulfonylurea derivatives and/or insulin. Exclusion criteria included use of other glucose-lowering medication, history of renal or hepatic disease, surgery, pancreatitis, pregnancy or lactation, and contraindications for MRI.
intervention: Liraglutide (Victoza) subcutaneous injection, starting at 0.6 mg per day, titrated over 3 weeks to maximum 1.8 mg once daily, for 26 weeks, added to standard care
comparison: Placebo (subcutaneous injection) for 26 weeks, added to standard care
outcomes_primary: Plasma growth differentiation factor 15 (GDF15) levels
outcomes_secondary: Body weight, HbA1c levels, correlation between changes in GDF15 levels and changes in body weight, correlation between changes in GDF15 levels and changes in HbA1c, correlation between metformin dose and GDF15 levels
extraction_notes: Secondary analysis of two previously performed double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomized clinical trials (NCT01761318 and NCT02660047). Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly labeled as such; classification based on stated study aims. Randomization stratified by sex and insulin use with 1:1 allocation.

title: Continuous Glucose Monitoring and the Effect of Liraglutide in Cardiac Surgery Patients: A Substudy of the Randomized Controlled GLOBE Trial.
journal: Journal of cardiothoracic and vascular anesthesia
population: Patients undergoing cardiac surgery at a single-center academic hospital in the Netherlands
intervention: Preoperative liraglutide administration plus Dexcom G5 continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) system from the day before surgery until discharge from the intensive care unit
comparison: Placebo plus Dexcom G5 continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) system
outcomes_primary: Accuracy and reliability of CGM assessed by comparison with arterial blood gas glucose measurements (mean absolute relative difference); sensor interruption characteristics
outcomes_secondary: Glycemic time in range; perioperative glucose control as captured by CGM
extraction_notes: This is a substudy/prespecified analysis of the larger GLOBE trial. Sample size was 25 patients. Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract; classification inferred from objectives statement.

title: Efficacy and safety of oral semaglutide vs sitagliptin in a predominantly Chinese population with type 2 diabetes uncontrolled with metformin: PIONEER 12, a double-blind, Phase IIIa, randomised trial.
population: Adults aged ≥18 years (≥20 years in Taiwan) with type 2 diabetes diagnosed ≥60 days prior to screening, HbA1c 53–91 mmol/mol (7.0–10.5%) inclusive, on stable metformin dose (≥1500 mg or maximum tolerated dose) for ≥60 days prior to screening. Predominantly Chinese population (75.2% from China region including mainland China, Taiwan and Hong Kong). Exclusion criteria included treatment with other diabetes or obesity medication in 60 days prior to screening (except metformin or short-term insulin ≤14 days), history of pancreatitis, renal impairment, and unstable diabetic retinopathy or maculopathy.
intervention: Once-daily oral semaglutide at 3 mg, 7 mg, or 14 mg for 26 weeks. Oral semaglutide initiated at 3 mg and escalated every 4 weeks to randomised dose (3 mg, 7 mg, or 14 mg). All participants also received sitagliptin placebo (double-dummy design). Background metformin continued.
comparison: Once-daily oral sitagliptin 100 mg for 26 weeks. Participants also received oral semaglutide placebo (double-dummy design). Background metformin continued.
outcomes_primary: Change in HbA1c from baseline to week 26
outcomes_secondary: Confirmatory secondary endpoint: change in body weight (kg) from baseline to week 26. Supportive secondary endpoints: change from baseline to week 26 in fasting plasma glucose, 7-point self-monitored plasma glucose, body weight (%), BMI, waist circumference, fasting lipid profile; achievement of HbA1c <53 mmol/mol (<7.0%), HbA1c ≤48 mmol/mol (≤6.5%), HbA1c reduction ≥10.9 mmol/mol (≥1 percentage point), body weight loss ≥3%, ≥5%, or ≥10% at week 26; composite endpoints of HbA1c <53 mmol/mol without hypoglycaemia and no body weight gain, and HbA1c reduction ≥10.9 mmol/mol with body weight loss ≥3%; patient-reported outcomes (SF-36v2). Safety endpoints: treatment-emergent adverse events, hypoglycaemic episodes, laboratory assessments, vital signs.

title: Efficacy and safety of oral semaglutide monotherapy vs placebo in a predominantly Chinese population with type 2 diabetes (PIONEER 11): a double-blind, Phase IIIa, randomised trial.
population: Adults aged ≥18 years (≥20 years in Taiwan) with diagnosed type 2 diabetes, HbA1c 53-86 mmol/mol (7.0-10.0%), not receiving any glucose-lowering drugs, insufficiently controlled with diet and exercise alone. Key exclusions: treatment with glucose-lowering medication or obesity medication within 60 days before screening (except short-term insulin ≤14 days), renal impairment (eGFR <60 ml/min per 1.73 m²), history/presence of pancreatitis, history/presence of malignant neoplasms within 5 years, family or personal history of multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2 or medullary thyroid carcinoma, uncontrolled diabetic retinopathy or maculopathy. Predominantly from China region (mainland China and Taiwan).
intervention: Once-daily oral semaglutide at 3 mg, 7 mg, or 14 mg for 26 weeks. Treatment initiated at 3 mg once daily with fixed 4-week dose-escalation regimen for higher doses (7 mg reached after 4 weeks, 14 mg after 8 weeks). Administered as once-daily tablet in morning with up to 120 ml water in fasting state, at least 30 min before first meal.
comparison: Placebo (matching oral tablet) once daily for 26 weeks
outcomes_primary: Change in HbA1c from baseline to week 26
outcomes_secondary: Confirmatory secondary endpoint: Change in body weight (kg) from baseline to week 26. Supportive secondary endpoints: Achievement of HbA1c ≤48 mmol/mol (≤6.5%) (AACE target), achievement of HbA1c <53 mmol/mol (<7.0%) (ADA target), body weight loss ≥5%, body weight loss ≥10%, change from baseline to week 26 in fasting plasma glucose, 7-point self-monitored plasma glucose profile, body weight (%), BMI, waist circumference, blood pressure, fasting lipid profile. Composite endpoints: HbA1c <53 mmol/mol without treatment-emergent severe or blood glucose-confirmed symptomatic hypoglycaemia and no body weight gain; HbA1c reduction ≥10.9 mmol/mol (≥1%) and body weight loss ≥3%. Patient-reported outcomes (SF-36v2). Safety endpoints: adverse events, hypoglycaemic episodes, changes in vital signs and laboratory assessments.
extraction_notes: Trial conducted across 52 sites in China region (mainland China and Taiwan), Hungary, Serbia and Ukraine. Randomisation criterion for HbA1c at visit 3 was 53-80 mmol/mol (7.0-9.5%), which is narrower than screening criterion. Two estimands defined: trial product estimand (primary) and treatment policy estimand (secondary).

title: Metabolic effects of very-low calorie diet, Semaglutide, or combination of the two, in individuals with type 2 diabetes mellitus.
population: Individuals with type 2 diabetes mellitus, age 18-75 years, BMI 27-50 kg/m²
intervention: Combination of very-low calorie diet (VLCD) and Semaglutide (GLP-1 receptor agonist)
comparison: Very-low calorie diet (VLCD) alone; Semaglutide alone
outcomes_primary: Body weight change, fat mass change
outcomes_secondary: HbA1c, fasting glucose, fasting insulin, HOMA-IR, insulin first phase response during intravenous glucose tolerance test (IVGTT), body composition, metabolic outcomes
extraction_notes: Specific doses, routes, frequencies, and durations for VLCD and Semaglutide interventions were not provided in the abstract. The abstract was truncated at the METHODS section describing the 30 participants, cutting off detailed methodology. Primary vs secondary outcome designation was inferred from emphasis in text.

title: Intraduodenal calcium enhances the effects of L-tryptophan to stimulate gut hormone secretion and suppress energy intake in healthy males: a randomized, crossover, clinical trial.
journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
population: Healthy males with normal weight
intervention: Intraduodenal infusion of L-tryptophan (Trp) combined with calcium at two doses (500 mg and 1000 mg)
comparison: Intraduodenal L-tryptophan alone (Ca-0+Trp), calcium alone (500 mg and 1000 mg doses)
outcomes_primary: Plasma concentrations of gastrointestinal hormones (cholecystokinin, GLP-1, PYY, GIP), pyloric pressures, energy intake
extraction_notes: Randomized crossover design with 15 participants. Specific primary vs secondary outcome designation not explicitly stated in abstract. Baseline characteristics mentioned (age: 26 ± 7 years; BMI: 22 ± 2 kg/m²) but full BMI value appears truncated in source text.

title: A Randomized, Crossover Trial Assessing Appetite, Energy Metabolism, Blood Biomarkers, and Ad Libitum Food Intake Responses to a Mid-Morning Pecan Snack vs. an Equicaloric High-Carbohydrate Snack in Healthy Volunteers with Overweight/Obesity.
population: Healthy adults aged 20-50 years with overweight and obesity (BMI 27-40 kg/m2), habitual breakfast eaters, weight stable for 6 months, willing to consume test snacks, not regular pecan consumers (≤3×/week). Excluded: nut allergies, uncontrolled thyroid disorders, diabetes mellitus, eating disorders, pregnancy/lactating, uncontrolled hypertension, actively dieting, intensive physical activity (>300 min/week exercise), medical history or medications affecting appetite.
intervention: Mid-morning snack of roasted lightly salted pecans, 250 kcal (1.25 ounces, 45 mg sodium/ounce), consumed 2 hours after standardized breakfast, single exposure
comparison: Equicaloric mid-morning snack of lightly salted tortilla chips, 250 kcal (1.79 ounces, 55 mg sodium/ounce), consumed 2 hours after standardized breakfast, single exposure
outcomes_primary: Subjective appetite measures (visual analog scale ratings of hunger, fullness, desire to eat, prospective consumption); ad libitum energy intake and macronutrient composition at self-selected lunch
outcomes_secondary: Blood biomarkers (glucose, insulin, free fatty acids, triglycerides, ghrelin, peptide YY, GLP-1, leptin, HOMA-IR); resting and postprandial energy expenditure (indirect calorimetry); respiratory quotient
extraction_notes: Randomized crossover design with at least 1-week washout between treatments. Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in text; classification based on study aims stated in introduction.

title: Effect of pemvidutide, a GLP-1/glucagon dual receptor agonist, on MASLD: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study.
population: Patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) with BMI ≥28.0 kg/m²
intervention: Pemvidutide, a GLP-1/glucagon dual receptor agonist, administered weekly (dose not specified in abstract)
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Liver fat content (LFC)
outcomes_secondary: Markers of hepatic inflammation, body weight
extraction_notes: Specific dose of pemvidutide not stated in abstract. BMI criterion appears truncated in text (≥28.0 kg/m). Duration of treatment not specified in abstract.

title: Improving insulin resistance by sulforaphane
extraction_notes: No abstract text available for extraction. Unable to identify any PICO elements.

title: The role of glucagon-like peptide 1 in the postprandial effects of metformin in type 2 diabetes: a randomized crossover trial.
population: Individuals with type 2 diabetes
intervention: Metformin treatment for 14 days, combined with mixed meal tests with either continuous intravenous exendin(9-39)NH2 or saline infusion
comparison: Placebo treatment for 14 days; each treatment period preceded by 14 days without any glucose-lowering medicine
outcomes_primary: Postprandial plasma glucose excursions; effect of GLP-1 receptor antagonization on metformin-induced improvement in postprandial glucose tolerance
outcomes_secondary: Fasting plasma glucose; fasting plasma GLP-1; postprandial GLP-1 responses
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract; classification inferred from study aims. Crossover design with randomized order for both treatment periods and meal test conditions.

title: Effects of semaglutide, empagliflozin and their combination on renal diffusion-weighted MRI and total kidney volume in patients with type 2 diabetes: a post hoc analysis from a 32 week randomised trial.
population: Adults with type 2 diabetes and HbA1c ≥48 mmol/mol (6.5%), either: (1) age ≥50 years with established CVD and/or heart failure and/or CKD (eGFR <60 ml/min per 1.73m2 but ≥45 ml/min per 1.73m2), or (2) age ≥60 years with high risk of CVD (e.g. smoking or albuminuria). Exclusion criteria included treatment with SGLT-2I, GLP-1RA or DPP4-I within 30 days before randomisation, cardio- or cerebrovascular event within last 90 days, or planned revascularisation.
intervention: Semaglutide 1 mg (or highest tolerated dose) subcutaneous injection once weekly for 16 weeks, then continued with addition of either tablet placebo (semaglutide group) or empagliflozin 10 mg tablet once daily (combination-therapy group) for a further 16 weeks (total 32 weeks)
comparison: Four groups (n=20 each): (1) Tablet placebo for 32 weeks; (2) Empagliflozin 10 mg tablet once daily for 32 weeks; (3) Semaglutide plus tablet placebo; (4) Semaglutide plus empagliflozin combination therapy
outcomes_primary: Changes in apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) from diffusion-weighted MRI including cortical ADC, medullary ADC, and cortico-medullary difference (ΔADC); Total kidney volume (TKV) measured by MRI
outcomes_secondary: Associations of ADC changes with changes in GFR, albuminuria (UACR), HbA1c, weight, blood pressure, TKV, renal perfusion, and inflammatory markers (IL-6, hs-CRP); Associations of TKV changes with GFR, UACR, HbA1c, perfusion, and haematocrit
extraction_notes: This is a post hoc analysis/substudy of the SEMPA trial. The co-primary endpoints of the main trial were arterial stiffness and renal oxygenation, not the ADC/TKV outcomes reported here. The first 80 of 120 total participants underwent MRI scans as prespecified.

title: Effect of oral semaglutide on energy intake, appetite, control of eating and gastric emptying in adults living with obesity: A randomized controlled trial.
population: Adults with obesity
intervention: Once-daily oral semaglutide, dose-escalated to 50 mg, for 20 weeks
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Relative change from baseline in ad libitum energy intake at week 20
outcomes_secondary: Body weight change; appetite ratings (hunger, fullness, satiety); Control of Eating Questionnaire responses (food cravings, control of eating); gastric emptying measured using paracetamol absorption following a standardized breakfast

title: Tirzepatide and blood pressure reduction: stratified analyses of the SURMOUNT-1 randomised controlled trial.
population: Adults with body mass index (BMI) ≥30 kg/m2 or ≥27 kg/m2 with at least one weight-related complication, excluding diabetes; excluded if systolic blood pressure ≥160 mm Hg or diastolic blood pressure ≥100 mm Hg at screening
intervention: Once weekly subcutaneous tirzepatide (5 mg, 10 mg, or 15 mg) for 72 weeks as an adjunct to lifestyle intervention
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Change from baseline in systolic blood pressure
outcomes_secondary: Change from baseline in diastolic blood pressure; changes in blood pressure by age, sex, BMI, blood pressure categories, and use of antihypertensive medications; blood pressure category shifts; proportion of blood pressure reduction mediated by weight loss; blood pressure-related adverse events
extraction_notes: This is a post hoc analysis of the SURMOUNT-1 trial. The primary outcome (systolic blood pressure change) and secondary outcome (diastolic blood pressure change) designations are based on the statement that these were 'prespecified key secondary and secondary endpoints of SURMOUNT-1, respectively.' Post hoc endpoints were also analyzed.

title: Liraglutide Improves Myocardial Perfusion and Energetics and Exercise Tolerance in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology
population: Adults with type 2 diabetes diagnosed at least 6 months before enrollment, HbA1c level no more than 86 mmol/mol, either drug-naïve or on treatment with oral glucose-lowering therapies for at least 12 weeks prior to screening, without established cardiovascular disease, left ventricular ejection fraction ≥50%, no prior myocardial infarction or ischemia on CMR dobutamine-stress perfusion imaging, eGFR ≥30 ml/min/m2, no history of pancreatitis, liver disease, multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2 syndrome, diabetic gastroparesis, no current use of PPAR-γAs, fibrates, GLP-1RAs or insulin
intervention: Liraglutide initiated at 0.6 mg subcutaneous injection once-weekly, titrated to 1.2 mg once-weekly in 2 weeks, for 16 weeks
comparison: Pioglitazone initiated at 15 mg orally once-daily, with dose increased by 15 mg every other week reaching target dose of 45 mg once-daily after 4 weeks, for 16 weeks (crossover design with 8-week washout period between treatments)
outcomes_primary: Change in myocardial perfusion reserve (MPR) and global stress myocardial blood flow (stress-MBF) after treatment
outcomes_secondary: Change in rest and dobutamine stress myocardial phosphocreatine to ATP ratio (PCr/ATP); exploratory outcomes included change in global longitudinal shortening (GLS), HOMA-IR, triglyceride-index, left ventricular volumes, visceral and epicardial fat area, and 6-minute walk distance
extraction_notes: Open-label randomized crossover trial design. Outcomes measured using cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) and 31phosphorus magnetic resonance spectroscopy (31P-MRS). The abstract mentions liraglutide 1.2 mg once-weekly but this appears to be an error as GLP-1RAs are typically administered daily; the methods section confirms once-weekly titration schedule.

title: Estimated glomerular filtration rate slope and risk of primary and secondary major adverse cardiovascular events and heart failure hospitalization in people with type 2 diabetes: An analysis of the EXSCEL trial.
population: People with type 2 diabetes, including those with and without previous history of cardiovascular disease
intervention: Once-weekly exenatide
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Major adverse cardiovascular events/hospitalization for heart failure (MACE/hHF), defined as composite of non-fatal myocardial infarction, non-fatal stroke, cardiovascular death, or hospitalization for heart failure
extraction_notes: This is a post-hoc analysis of the EXSCEL trial examining the association between eGFR slope and cardiovascular outcomes rather than evaluating treatment effect. The primary focus is on eGFR decline as a predictor rather than exenatide efficacy. Secondary outcomes not specified in abstract.

title: Efficacy and safety of once-weekly semaglutide 2·4 mg versus placebo in people with obesity and prediabetes (STEP 10): a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicentre phase 3 trial.
population: Adults aged 18 years or older with BMI of 30 kg/m² or greater and prediabetes
intervention: Once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide 2.4 mg
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Bodyweight reduction; reversion to normoglycaemia
outcomes_secondary: Not explicitly stated in abstract
extraction_notes: BMI threshold appears truncated in abstract text. Secondary outcomes not explicitly defined. Trial duration not specified in abstract.

title: Bitter-tasting drugs tune GDF15 and GLP-1 expression via bitter taste or motilin receptors in the intestine of patients with obesity.
population: Healthy female volunteers (for clinical trial component); patients with obesity undergoing Roux-en-Y gastric bypass surgery or sleeve gastrectomy (for in vitro studies); normal-weight organ donors (for tissue comparison studies)
intervention: Oral intake of Plaquenil (hydroxychloroquine sulfate) 310 mg total (two tablets) with 240 mL water, single dose administration
comparison: Placebo tablets with 240 mL water
outcomes_primary: Plasma GDF15 levels measured over time (baseline to 90 minutes post-administration)
outcomes_secondary: Hunger scores measured on 100 mm visual analog scale; plasma ghrelin levels; correlation between GDF15 levels and hunger scores; correlation between GDF15 levels and ghrelin levels
extraction_notes: This is a mixed study design including: 1) a placebo-controlled, double-blind, randomized, two-visit crossover clinical trial in healthy volunteers (n=10), and 2) in vitro mechanistic studies using primary jejunal cultures from patients with obesity. The abstract combines findings from both study types. The clinical trial population was exclusively female. Primary outcomes for in vitro components included GDF15 and GLP-1 mRNA expression in response to various bitter compounds.

title: Gut-derived appetite hormones do not explain energy intake differences in humans following low-carbohydrate versus low-fat diets.
population: Adults aged 18-50 years, weight stable (within 5% in past 6 months), BMI ≥20 kg/m², body weight ≥53 kg, able to complete daily bouts of stationary cycling at moderate rate and intensity. Exclusions: metabolic or cardiovascular disease, diabetes, thyroid disease, cancer, prescription medications influencing metabolism, pregnancy or lactation, regular exercise program (>2 h/week vigorous activity), habitual caffeine >300 mg/day, regular alcohol/tobacco/drug use, eating disorders or other psychological conditions, claustrophobia, implants interfering with MRI, strict dietary concerns, non-English speakers.
intervention: Low-carbohydrate (LC) animal-based ketogenic diet (approximately 10% carbohydrate, 75% fat, 15% protein) for 2 weeks, followed by LC liquid test meal (30% of estimated daily calorie requirements) on test day
comparison: Low-fat (LF) plant-based diet (approximately 10% fat, 75% carbohydrate, 15% protein) for 2 weeks, followed by isocaloric LF liquid test meal (30% of estimated daily calorie requirements) on test day; randomized crossover design
outcomes_primary: Mean daily ad libitum energy intake (primary endpoint of original trial)
outcomes_secondary: Postprandial plasma concentrations of gut-derived appetite hormones (active GLP-1, total GIP, PYY, total ghrelin, active ghrelin, leptin) measured at 0, 10, 20, 30, 60, 90, 120, 180, 240, 300, and 360 minutes after test meals; ad libitum energy intake at lunch, dinner, and snacks following test meal; relative energy intake as proportion of energy expenditure; mass of food eaten
extraction_notes: This is described as an exploratory analysis of data from a registered clinical trial (NCT03878108). Gut hormone outcomes were not pre-specified as primary or secondary outcomes of the main study. Inpatient randomized crossover design with single 4-week stay.

title: Real world study of GLP-1 receptor agonists in overweight or obese type 2 diabetes by using repeated measurement analysis of variance.
population: Overweight or obese patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus; diagnostic criteria: American Diabetes Association 2020 criteria for type 2 diabetes; BMI ≥ 24 kg/m2; age 20 to 80 years; able to communicate in language or words; exclusion: previous use of GLP-1 receptor agonists, acute complications of diabetes mellitus, combined digestive system and other serious diseases, infections or malignant tumors, pregnant or lactating women
intervention: Metformin plus dulaglutide (1.5 mg subcutaneous once weekly) or semaglutide (0.5 mg subcutaneous once weekly, maximum dose 1 mg per week); treatment duration 12 months; both groups received MMC (Metabolic Management Center) management including enrollment, follow-up every 3 months by phone and every 6 months in-person, and health education
comparison: Metformin alone with MMC management mode
outcomes_primary: Hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c), fasting plasma glucose (FPG), body mass index (BMI) measured before treatment, 6 months after treatment, and 12 months after treatment
outcomes_secondary: Safety outcomes including incidence of adverse reactions (hypoglycemia, gastrointestinal discomfort) at 12 months after treatment
extraction_notes: Study described as randomized but no blinding mentioned; single-center study; dulaglutide and semaglutide combined in experimental group; 3 patients withdrew from test group due to economic reasons

title: A comparison of the effects of dairy products with their plant-based alternatives on metabolic responses in healthy young Canadian adults: a randomized crossover study.
journal: Applied physiology, nutrition, and metabolism = Physiologie appliquee, nutrition et metabolisme
population: Healthy young Canadian adults; sixteen participants (eight males and eight females)
intervention: Experiment 1: Greek yogurt (175 g), cheddar cheese (30 g), plant-based cheese (30 g), or plant-based yogurt (175 g). Experiment 2: Cow's milk (250 mL), vanilla soy beverage (250 mL), vanilla almond beverage (250 mL), cheddar cheese (30 g), or plant-based cheese (30 g)
comparison: Dairy products compared with their plant-based alternatives (Greek yogurt vs plant-based yogurt; cheddar cheese vs plant-based cheese; cow's milk vs vanilla soy beverage vs vanilla almond beverage)
outcomes_primary: Postprandial glycemia (blood glucose), metabolic hormones (insulin), appetite measured at baseline, post-treatment, and following a fixed-size pasta meal (post-meal) within 15-30 min
outcomes_secondary: C-peptide, glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1), and ghrelin (measured in experiment 2 only)
extraction_notes: Abstract appears truncated. Study uses randomized crossover design with two separate experiments. Fixed-size pasta meal (12 kcal/kg body weight) was used as test meal in both experiments.

title: Reduced plasma interleukin-6 concentration after transcranial direct current stimulation to the prefrontal cortex.
population: Healthy adults with obesity (BMI ≥30 kg/m2), without diabetes, weight stable, from Phoenix, Arizona metropolitan area
intervention: Anodal transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) to the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (L-DLPFC), 2 mA constant current, 40 minutes duration, administered on 3 consecutive mornings; anode placed at F3, cathode at right supraorbital region (Fp2), 35 cm2 sponge electrodes dampened with 0.9% sodium chloride solution
comparison: Sham tDCS (10 seconds of stimulation followed by no current for remaining time, same electrode placement)
outcomes_primary: Fasting plasma concentrations of IL-6, orexin, cortisol, TNF-α, IL-1β, total ghrelin, PYY, and GLP-1 measured before initial and after final tDCS sessions
outcomes_secondary: Ad libitum energy intake (kilocalories) and macronutrient content during 3-day vending machine period; association between calorie intake and hormone concentrations
extraction_notes: This is described as a secondary exploratory analysis of a randomized parallel-design study (NCT00739362). The primary aim of the original study was to assess effects of tDCS on food intake; hormone concentrations were a secondary aim. Sample size was powered for the primary food intake objective, not hormone outcomes.

title: Effect of Semaglutide on Epicardial Adipose Tissue in Type 2 Diabetes: Insights From the STOP (Semaglutide Treatment effect On coronary atherosclerosis Progression) Randomized Trial.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology
extraction_notes: No abstract text available for extraction. Title suggests study involves patients with type 2 diabetes, semaglutide intervention, and epicardial adipose tissue outcomes from the STOP randomized trial, but no explicit information can be extracted without the abstract text.

title: GLP-1 therapy increases visceral adipose tissue metabolic activity: lessons from a randomized controlled trial in obstructive sleep apnea.

intervention: GLP-1 therapy-based weight loss regimen for 24 weeks
comparison: Continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP); Combination of GLP-1 therapy and CPAP
outcomes_primary: Visceral adipose tissue (VAT) metabolic activity, expressed as VAT target to background ratio, measured by 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose (18F-FDG) positron emission tomography-computed tomography (PET-CT)
outcomes_secondary: Weight loss
extraction_notes: Specific GLP-1 analogue drug name, dose, route, and frequency not specified. Sample size is 30 participants total across all arms. Study described as proof-of-concept. Primary vs secondary outcome designation not explicitly stated in abstract.

title: Application of the integrated data platform combined with dietary management for adults with diabetes: A prospective randomized controlled trial.
population: Adults aged over 18 years with confirmed diagnosis of type 2 diabetes, HbA1c above 7.0% measured within previous 2 weeks, strong self-management ability, possession of a smartphone, and capability to learn to use the internet. Exclusion criteria: acute complications, severe liver and kidney function impairment, severe cardiovascular diseases, communication disorders or mental disorders, and pregnancy.
intervention: Integrated data platform of cloud hospital combined with dietary management, including personalized diabetes education videos delivered to patients' mobile phones, blood glucose monitoring programs, complimentary access to consult physicians with feedback within 24 hours, and proactive messages from medical staff every 2 weeks for 12 weeks.
comparison: Routine standard diabetes care with hospital visits at week 12.
outcomes_primary: Change in HbA1c from baseline to week 12; change in body weight from baseline to week 12.
outcomes_secondary: Incidence of hypoglycemia; adherence to anti-diabetic medications (compliance score based on 4 questions, maximum 8 points); satisfaction with health system support (based on 5 criteria, scale 0-2 points each); quality of life score (EQ-5D-3L).
extraction_notes: Subgroup analyses were performed on overweight/obese subjects and by anti-diabetic medication usage (semaglutide vs non-GLP-1), but these were post-hoc analyses within the experimental group only.

title: Patient and public involvement and engagement in the ASCEND PLUS trial: reflections from the design of a streamlined and decentralised clinical trial.
population: Approximately 20,000 individuals with type 2 diabetes aged 55 and over in the UK, with no history of heart attack or stroke (primary prevention population)
intervention: Oral semaglutide (dose, frequency, and duration not specified in abstract)
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Primary prevention of cardiovascular events
outcomes_secondary: Other cardiovascular and non-cardiovascular outcomes (not further specified); quality of life assessed using EQ-5D, SF-12, and Problem Areas in Diabetes (PAID) questionnaire
extraction_notes: This paper focuses on patient and public involvement and engagement (PPIE) in trial design rather than clinical outcomes. Specific dose, frequency, and duration of oral semaglutide not provided. Trial is ongoing with estimated primary completion date of 2028. The abstract mentions 'cardiovascular and other outcomes' but does not provide detailed outcome definitions.

title: Semaglutide and cardiovascular outcomes in patients with obesity and prevalent heart failure: a prespecified analysis of the SELECT trial.
population: Adults aged 45 years and older with BMI of 27 kg/m² or higher, with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, including subgroups with and without prevalent heart failure, and subgroups with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction versus heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
intervention: Once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide 2.4 mg
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE)
outcomes_secondary: Composite heart failure endpoints, ischaemic cardiovascular outcomes, heart failure cardiovascular outcomes
extraction_notes: This is a prespecified subgroup analysis of the SELECT trial. Full BMI threshold value appears truncated in abstract. Specific definitions of heart failure subtypes (HFpEF vs HFrEF) and composite heart failure endpoints not fully detailed in abstract.

title: Effect of semaglutide on primary prevention of diabetic kidney disease in people with type 2 diabetes: A post hoc analysis of the SUSTAIN 6 randomized controlled trial.
population: Adults with type 2 diabetes without diabetic kidney disease (DKD) at baseline, from the SUSTAIN 6 trial, grouped by baseline DKD risk calculated using a validated model
intervention: Semaglutide 0.5 mg or 1.0 mg subcutaneous (dose and frequency not explicitly stated in abstract)
