intervention: Once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide 2.4 mg for 68 weeks, in addition to counseling on physical activity and a reduced-calorie diet
comparison: Placebo (once-weekly subcutaneous injection) in addition to counseling on physical activity and a reduced-calorie diet
outcomes_primary: Percentage change in body weight from baseline to week 68; Change in Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Osteoarthritis Index (WOMAC) pain score (scale 0-100, higher scores reflecting worse outcomes) from baseline to week 68
outcomes_secondary: Physical-function score on the 36-Item Short Form Health Survey (SF-36) version 2 (scale 0-100, higher scores indicating greater well-being) as key confirmatory secondary end point
extraction_notes: Randomization ratio was 2:1 (semaglutide:placebo). Trial conducted at 61 sites in 11 countries. Secondary outcomes beyond the key confirmatory endpoint (SF-36 physical function) were not specified in the abstract.

title: Pharmacokinetic Properties of a Once-Weekly Fixed-Ratio Combination of Insulin Icodec and Semaglutide Compared with Separate Administration of Each Component in Individuals with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.
population: Adults aged 18–64 years diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus at least 180 days before screening, treated with metformin ± one other oral antidiabetic drug (sulphonylurea, dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitor, or sodium-glucose transport protein-2 inhibitor) for at least 90 days before screening, body weight 80–120 kg, glycosylated haemoglobin 6.0–8.5%. Exclusions: current or previous regular insulin treatment, recurrent severe hypoglycaemia or hypoglycaemia unawareness, blood pressure outside 90–159 mmHg systolic or 50–99 mmHg diastolic, history or presence of clinically relevant respiratory, metabolic, renal, hepatic, gastrointestinal or endocrinological conditions (except mild diabetes complications), pregnant women.
intervention: Single subcutaneous injection of IcoSema containing 175 U insulin icodec (1050 nmol) and 0.5 mg semaglutide (121.5 nmol) administered in a three-period crossover design with 6–9 weeks washout between periods
comparison: Single subcutaneous injection of insulin icodec alone (175 U, 1050 nmol); Single subcutaneous injection of semaglutide alone (0.5 mg, 121.5 nmol)
outcomes_primary: Area under the concentration-time curve from zero to last quantifiable observation after a single dose (AUC0–t,SD) for insulin icodec and semaglutide
outcomes_secondary: Maximum concentration after a single dose (Cmax,SD) for insulin icodec and semaglutide; time to maximum concentration after a single dose (tmax,SD); model-predicted maximum concentration at steady state (Cmax,SS); safety assessments including adverse events, hypoglycaemic episodes, vital signs, electrocardiogram, clinical laboratory assessments, physical examination, anti-icodec and anti-semaglutide antibodies
extraction_notes: This was a randomized, double-blind, three-period crossover pharmacokinetic study (N=31 randomized, 27 completed). Primary and secondary outcome designations were inferred from study design description as formal designations were not explicitly stated in the abstract or methods.

title: Non-clinical and first-in-human characterization of ECC5004/AZD5004, a novel once-daily, oral small-molecule GLP-1 receptor agonist.
population: Single-ascending dose (SAD) study: healthy adult volunteers aged 18-65 years with BMI 18.0-32.0 kg/m2. Multiple-ascending dose (MAD) study: adult patients aged 18-70 years with BMI 24.0-40.0 kg/m2, HbA1c 7.0%-10.5%, type 2 diabetes mellitus treated with metformin.
intervention: SAD study: single oral doses of ECC5004 (1 mg, 4 mg, 10 mg, 25 mg, 50 mg, 100 mg, 200 mg, 300 mg) with 14-day washout periods between doses; fasted 10 hours before and 4 hours after dosing. MAD study: oral ECC5004 once daily for 28 days at 5 mg, 10 mg, 30 mg, or 50 mg; the 50 mg cohort was up-titrated (10 mg days 1-7, 25 mg days 8-14, 50 mg days 15-28); fasted 10 hours before and 4 hours after dosing.
comparison: Placebo. SAD study: 6:2 ratio (active:placebo) with each participant receiving up to 3 doses of ECC5004 and 1 dose of placebo. MAD study: 9:3 ratio (active:placebo).
outcomes_primary: Safety and tolerability (adverse events, serious adverse events, treatment-emergent adverse events, laboratory assessments, 12-lead electrocardiography recordings, vital signs).
outcomes_secondary: Pharmacokinetic parameters (Cmax, tmax, t1/2, AUC, dose proportionality). Exploratory pharmacodynamic parameters: SAD study - oral glucose tolerance test (plasma glucose AUC, insulin levels); MAD study - mixed-meal tolerance test (fasting glucose, glucose AUC0-4, insulin AUC0-4, C-peptide AUC0-4, glucagon AUC0-4), body weight change from baseline.
extraction_notes: Phase I first-in-human study (NCT05654831). Double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled design. No formal sample size calculation performed. Small sample sizes typical for phase I studies (SAD: n=16 completers; MAD: n=48 completers). Elimination half-life not accurately determined due to limited PK sampling duration (48 hours post-dose).

title: Association between weight reduction achieved with tirzepatide and quality of life in adults with obesity: Results from the SURMOUNT-1 study.
population: Adults with obesity (BMI ≥30) or overweight, without type 2 diabetes. Exclusion: baseline PHQ-9 score ≥15
intervention: Tirzepatide (glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist) 5 mg, 10 mg, or 15 mg subcutaneously once weekly for 72 weeks, with up to 20-week dose-escalation period, in conjunction with reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity
comparison: Placebo once weekly in conjunction with reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity
outcomes_primary: Not explicitly specified as primary in this PRO analysis; prespecified secondary endpoints from SURMOUNT-1 included health-related quality of life outcomes
outcomes_secondary: Patient-reported outcomes: Impact of Weight on Quality of Life-Lite Clinical Trials version (IWQOL-Lite-CT) total score and composite scores (Physical, Physical Function, Psychosocial); Short Form Survey-36 version 2 (SF-36v2) Physical Component Summary, Mental Component Summary, and domain scores; EQ-5D-5L utility/health state index and visual analogue scale; Patient Global Impression of Status for physical activity (PGIS); Patient Health Questionnaire-2 (PHQ-2); proportion achieving meaningful within-patient change in physical function
extraction_notes: This is a secondary analysis of PRO data from SURMOUNT-1 trial (NCT04184622). The original primary efficacy endpoints of SURMOUNT-1 were body weight reduction, not PROs. Weight reduction category analyses (>0 to <5%, ≥5 to <10%, ≥10 to <20%, ≥20%) were post hoc and included only tirzepatide-treated participants.

title: Semaglutide improved sperm morphology in obese men with type 2 diabetes mellitus and functional hypogonadism.
population: Men aged 18-65 years with type 2 diabetes on oral antidiabetic treatment, BMI above 30 kg/m2, and functional hypogonadism (defined as total testosterone less than 11 nmol/L measured on at least two separate morning measurements at least 4 weeks apart after an overnight fast, along with at least two symptoms of sexual dysfunction and low or inappropriately normal gonadotropin levels). Exclusion criteria included primary or secondary hypogonadism, hyperprolactinaemia, endogenous Cushing syndrome, hypopituitarism, pituitary or hypothalamic tumours, hemochromatosis, active malignant disease, thrombophilia, venous thrombosis within 6 months, recent acute myocardial infarction or stroke, PSA higher than 3 ng/L, severe LUTS with IPSS above 19, severe sleep apnoea syndrome, haematocrit greater than 0.5, significant kidney or liver disease, ongoing treatment with opioid analgesics, antipsychotics or glucocorticoids, alcohol abuse, severe ongoing mental illness, personal history of pancreatitis or medullary thyroid carcinoma, and personal or family history of MEN 2.
intervention: Semaglutide 1 mg subcutaneously once weekly for 24 weeks (titrated: 0.25 mg weekly for first month, 0.5 mg weekly for second month, 1 mg weekly from third month onwards)
comparison: Testosterone undecanoate 1000 mg intramuscularly once every 10-12 weeks for 24 weeks
outcomes_primary: Change in sperm parameters: semen volume, sperm concentration, total sperm number, total motility, morphologically normal sperm
outcomes_secondary: Change in total testosterone concentration, LH, FSH, IIEF-15 score (International Index of Erectile Function-15), AMS score (Aging Male Symptoms), HbA1c, body mass, BMI, percentage of body fat, estimated visceral adipose tissue, fasting lipids
extraction_notes: Open-label randomized controlled trial. Both groups received lifestyle measures counseling. All patients were on metformin 1000 mg BID as background therapy.

title: Postprandial Effects of Four Test Meals Containing Wholegrain Rye or Refined Wheat Foods on Circulating Incretins, Ghrelin, Glucose, and Inflammatory Markers.
population: Healthy adults aged 30-70 years with BMI 27-35 kg/m2, blood pressure ≤160/105 mm Hg, fasting serum triglycerides ≤2.6 mmol/L, serum thyroid-stimulating hormone ≤3.7 mIE/L, hemoglobin ≥117g/L for women and ≥134 g/L for men, plasma low-density lipoprotein ≤5.3 mmol/L. Exclusion criteria included smoking or use of nicotine products, chronic gastrointestinal conditions, thyroid disorder, type 1 diabetes, medication for type 2 diabetes, or medication for weight management.
intervention: Hypocaloric diet rich in wholegrain rye cereals providing approximately one-third of total energy, administered over intervention days with meals at 08:00 (breakfast: cereal puffs with milk), 12:00 (lunch: tomato soup, crisp bread and cheese/jam), 15:00 (afternoon snack: crisp bread with cheese/jam), and 19:00 (dinner: goulash soup with soft bread and jam/cheese). Total energy 1300-2300 kcal/d calculated as estimated energy requirements with 500 kcal deficit.
comparison: Hypocaloric diet with corresponding refined wheat cereal products providing approximately one-third of total energy, with same meal structure and timing as intervention diet.
outcomes_primary: Total area under the curve (tAUC) for gut hormones (glucose-dependent insulinotropic peptide, glucagon-like peptide-1, ghrelin); incremental area under the curve (iAUC) from continuous glucose monitoring data for postprandial glucose control.
outcomes_secondary: Mean concentrations of gut hormones and glucose; measures of glycemic variability (SD, CV, mean amplitude of glycemic excursion, peak glucose concentration); inflammatory biomarkers (glycoprotein N-acetylation A, glycoprotein N-acetylation B, supramolecular phospholipid composite peak, C-reactive protein); plasma insulin concentrations; subjective appetite measures (fullness, hunger, desire to eat).
extraction_notes: Randomized crossover trial with 1-week washout between interventions. Study was prospectively registered (NCT05004584). Primary aim was to detect differences in subjective appetite ratings; gut hormone and glycemic outcomes were secondary objectives. Sample size determined for primary aim of detecting 10% within-group differences in subjective appetite ratings.

title: Weight Loss Induces Changes in Vitamin D Status in Women With Obesity But Not in Men: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
population: Adults aged 18-65 years with obesity (BMI 32-43 kg/m2) without diabetes who completed an 8-week low-calorie diet and lost >5% body weight
intervention: Liraglutide 3.0 mg/day subcutaneous self-administered (initiated at 0.6 mg/day with weekly escalations of 0.6 mg/day until reaching 3.0 mg/day or highest tolerable dose) with habitual physical activity for 52 weeks; OR Liraglutide 3.0 mg/day plus exercise intervention (150 minutes moderate intensity or 75 minutes vigorous intensity physical activity per week) for 52 weeks
comparison: Placebo with habitual physical activity for 52 weeks; Placebo with exercise intervention for 52 weeks
outcomes_primary: Change in body weight (primary endpoint of original trial)
outcomes_secondary: Change in serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D (25(OH)D); change in serum parathyroid hormone (PTH); change in serum calcium; change in albumin-corrected calcium; body composition assessed by dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry
extraction_notes: This is a secondary analysis of the S-LiTE trial; the primary endpoint of the original trial was change in body weight. The vitamin D outcomes reported here were secondary and exploratory analyses. All participants first underwent an 8-week low-calorie diet (800 kcal/day) before randomization to the 52-week intervention phase.

title: De-intensification of basal-bolus therapy by replacing prandial insulin with once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide in individuals with well-controlled type 2 diabetes: A single-centre, open-label randomised trial (TRANSITION-T2D).
population: Adults aged 18-75 years with type 2 diabetes and HbA1c ≤7.5% (≤58 mmol/mol) on multiple daily injections of insulin (MDI, defined as ≥3 daily injections of insulin analogues including ≥2 injections of prandial insulin), total daily dose (TDD) ≤120 units/day, prandial insulin ≤0.5 units/kg per day. Only metformin and/or SGLT2-inhibitors allowed as background diabetes therapy. Key exclusion criteria: positive GAD-65 antibodies, end-stage kidney disease, history of bariatric surgery, use of steroids >5 mg prednisone or equivalent.
intervention: Subcutaneous semaglutide initiated at 0.25 mg once weekly, increased as tolerated to 0.5 mg at Week 4 and 1.0 mg at Week 8, plus insulin degludec once daily. Prandial insulin completely stopped on the day of first semaglutide injection. Basal insulin maintained at pretrial levels if ≤0.5 units/kg per day or adjusted to maximum 0.5 units/kg daily.
comparison: Continue MDI with daily insulin degludec plus prandial insulin aspart, with insulin adjustment protocol to optimize management and sliding scale to correct pre-meal glucose values >150 mg/dL.
outcomes_primary: Percentage of participants maintaining HbA1c ≤7.5% (≤58 mmol/mol) at Week 26.
outcomes_secondary: Changes from baseline to Week 26 in: HbA1c, body weight (percent and absolute changes), percent changes in total daily dose and daily basal insulin dose. Additional secondary endpoints: absolute changes in insulin doses (basal, prandial, total), percent change in prandial insulin, percentage of participants who had to resume prandial insulin in the semaglutide arm before Week 26, changes in treatment satisfaction (DTSQs and DTSQc). Post hoc outcomes: percentages achieving >10% categorical weight loss and >50% reduction in insulin TDD. Safety assessments: rate of hypoglycaemic events (overall and by severity level), adverse events including serious adverse events and events leading to drug discontinuation or dose decrease.
extraction_notes: Open-label design. 2:1 randomization ratio. Single-centre study conducted at two Cleveland Clinic sites. 26-week duration.

title: Tirzepatide for Obesity Treatment and Diabetes Prevention.
journal: The New England journal of medicine
population: Adults with obesity and prediabetes
intervention: Tirzepatide subcutaneous injection, once weekly, at doses of 5 mg, 10 mg, or 15 mg, for 176 weeks
comparison: Placebo, once weekly, for 176 weeks
outcomes_primary: Not explicitly specified as primary outcome in abstract
outcomes_secondary: Percent change in body weight from baseline to week 176; onset of type 2 diabetes during the 176-week period; onset of type 2 diabetes during the 193-week period (including 17-week off-treatment period)
extraction_notes: Primary outcome not explicitly labeled in abstract. The three key secondary end points were specified as controlled for type I error. Trial is SURMOUNT-1 (NCT04184622). Full population was 2539 participants with obesity, of whom 1032 had prediabetes; current analysis focused on the prediabetes subgroup. Randomization ratio was 1:1:1:1.

title: Glycemia reduction in type 2 diabetes-Hypoglycemia outcomes: A randomized clinical trial.
population: Adults with type 2 diabetes, duration <10 years, age >30 years at diagnosis (>20 years in Native Americans), baseline HbA1c 6.8–8.5% (50.8–69.4 mmol/mol), taking only metformin at baseline
intervention: Addition of one of four medications to metformin: insulin glargine U100 (titrated to achieve pre-breakfast glucose 80–130 mg/dL), glimepiride (titrated up to maximum approved dose), liraglutide (titrated to 1.8 mg/day), or sitagliptin (dose based on renal function per package insert)
comparison: Four-arm comparison: glargine U100 vs glimepiride vs liraglutide vs sitagliptin, all added to metformin background therapy
outcomes_primary: Adjudicated severe hypoglycemia
outcomes_secondary: Hypoglycemic symptoms within last 30 days (reported at quarterly visits); measured glucose <70 mg/dL (3.9 mmol/L) within last 30 days (glargine and glimepiride groups only); any hypoglycemia (composite of severe hypoglycemia, hypoglycemic symptoms, or measured glucose <70 mg/dL); time to first severe hypoglycemia
extraction_notes: Per-protocol analysis of 4,830 participants (excluded 217 who never took assigned medication or never attended follow-up). Mean follow-up 5.0 ± 1.3 years. Rescue insulin (glargine and/or aspart) was added if HbA1c >7.5% was confirmed. Glucose monitoring materials only provided to glargine and glimepiride groups, limiting confirmation of hypoglycemia in liraglutide and sitagliptin groups.

title: Effects of tirzepatide on circulatory overload and end-organ damage in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and obesity: a secondary analysis of the SUMMIT trial.
population: Adults aged ≥40 years with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF, left ventricular ejection fraction ≥50%), BMI ≥30 kg/m², chronic NYHA class II-IV heart failure, exercise limitation with 6-minute walk distance 100-425 m, Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Clinical Summary Score ≤80, and objective evidence of HF (elevated NT-proBNP, structural heart disease, or elevated filling pressures). Additionally required either HF decompensation in preceding 12 months or eGFR <70 ml/min/1.73 m²
intervention: Tirzepatide (long-acting glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide receptor and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist) starting at 2.5 mg per week subcutaneously, increased by 2.5 mg every 4 weeks as tolerated to target dose of 15.0 mg per week, in addition to usual therapy
comparison: Matching placebo subcutaneously, with same dose escalation schedule, in addition to usual therapy
outcomes_primary: This is a secondary mechanistic analysis; outcomes assessed include systolic blood pressure, diastolic blood pressure, pulse pressure, estimated blood volume, estimated plasma volume, estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR using cystatin C-based CKD-EPI formula), urine albumin-creatinine ratio (UACR), high-sensitivity C-reactive protein, high-sensitivity troponin T, NT-proBNP levels
outcomes_secondary: Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Clinical Summary Score (KCCQ-CSS), 6-minute walk distance (6MWD), body weight; correlations between changes in circulatory load, inflammation and end-organ damage measures with clinical outcomes
extraction_notes: This is a prespecified secondary mechanistic analysis of the SUMMIT trial (NCT04847557). The primary trial outcomes (cardiovascular death or worsening heart failure) were reported separately. Estimated blood volume and plasma volume analyses were post hoc. Correlation analyses exploring relationships between variables were exploratory and post hoc.

title: Tirzepatide for Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction and Obesity.
journal: The New England journal of medicine
population: Patients with heart failure, ejection fraction of at least 50%, and body-mass index of at least 30
intervention: Tirzepatide up to 15 mg subcutaneously once per week for at least 52 weeks
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Composite of adjudicated death from cardiovascular causes or a worsening heart-failure event (assessed in time-to-first-event analysis); Change from baseline to 52 weeks in Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire clinical summary score (KCCQ-CSS)
extraction_notes: Secondary outcomes not explicitly stated in abstract

title: Effects of Tirzepatide on the Clinical Trajectory of Patients With Heart Failure, Preserved Ejection Fraction, and Obesity.
population: Adults ≥40 years of age with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), chronic New York Heart Association (NYHA) class II to IV heart failure, left ventricular ejection fraction ≥50%, body mass index ≥30 kg/m2, 6-minute walk distance 100-425 m, Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Clinical Summary Score ≤80, and objective evidence of heart failure (elevated NT-proBNP ≥200 pg/mL in sinus rhythm or ≥600 pg/mL in atrial fibrillation, structural heart disease defined by left atrial enlargement, or elevated filling pressures at rest or with exercise). Patients also required either heart failure decompensation in the preceding 12 months or estimated glomerular filtration rate <70 mL·min−1·1.73 m−2
intervention: Tirzepatide subcutaneous injection, starting at 2.5 mg weekly, titrated by 2.5 mg every 4 weeks as tolerated up to 15 mg weekly, added to background therapy
comparison: Matching placebo subcutaneous injection, added to background therapy
outcomes_primary: Time to first worsening heart failure event or cardiovascular death; change in Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Clinical Summary Score at 52 weeks
outcomes_secondary: Change in 6-minute walk distance; change in body weight; change in high-sensitivity C-reactive protein; EQ-5D-5L health state index; Patient Global Impression of Severity Overall Health score; NYHA functional class; use of heart failure medications; hierarchical composite based on all-cause death, worsening heart failure, and 52-week changes in Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Clinical Summary Score and 6-minute walk distance
extraction_notes: Median follow-up was 104 weeks. Worsening heart failure event defined as exacerbation of symptoms requiring hospitalization, intravenous drugs for heart failure in urgent care setting, or intensification of oral diuretics. Primary outcomes had pre-specified alpha allocation (0.04 for events composite, 0.01 for KCCQ-CSS).

title: Gastrointestinal hormones and subjective ratings of appetite after low-carbohydrate vs low-fat low-energy diets in females with lipedema - A randomized controlled trial.
population: Females with obesity and lipedema
intervention: Low-carbohydrate diet (LCD) with 75 g carbohydrates for 8 weeks
comparison: Isocaloric low-fat low energy diet (LED) with 180 g carbohydrates for 8 weeks
outcomes_primary: Changes in ghrelin plasma concentrations (fasting and postprandial states)
outcomes_secondary: Changes in satiety hormones (peptide YY, cholecystokinin, glucagon-like peptide 1) in fasting and postprandial states; subjective ratings of appetite
extraction_notes: Energy intake level not specified for either diet. Primary outcome inferred from stated primary objective; secondary outcomes from stated secondary objectives.

title: Tirzepatide Reduces LV Mass and Paracardiac Adipose Tissue in Obesity-Related Heart Failure: SUMMIT CMR Substudy.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology
population: Patients with obesity-related heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF)
intervention: Tirzepatide 2.5 mg subcutaneously weekly, increasing to a maximum of 15 mg weekly
comparison: Matching placebo
outcomes_primary: Between-group changes in left ventricular (LV) mass
outcomes_secondary: Paracardiac (epicardial plus pericardial) adipose tissue; left atrial structure and function; LV structure and function; correlations of LV mass change with body weight, waist circumference, blood pressure, LV end-diastolic volume, left atrial end-diastolic and end-systolic volumes
extraction_notes: This is a CMR substudy of the SUMMIT trial (NCT04847557). Of 175 patients who underwent baseline CMR, 106 completed CMR at both baseline and 52 weeks with adequate image quality for analysis.

title: Osteoprotegerin, Osteopontin, and Osteocalcin Are Associated With Cardiovascular Events in Type 2 Diabetes: Insights From EXSCEL.
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes
intervention: Once-weekly exenatide
comparison: Not explicitly stated in abstract (placebo implied from trial design)
outcomes_primary: First occurrence of major cardiovascular events (MACE): composite of cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or nonfatal stroke
outcomes_secondary: All-cause death, cardiovascular death; association of bone metabolism biomarkers (osteoprotegerin, osteopontin, sclerostin, osteocalcin) with cardiovascular events
extraction_notes: This is a biomarker substudy of the EXSCEL trial focusing on associations between bone metabolism biomarkers and cardiovascular outcomes. Comparator arm not explicitly described in abstract. Sample size for biomarker analysis was 5,473 participants.

title: Differential effects of imeglimin and metformin on insulin and incretin secretion-An exploratory randomized controlled trial.
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes, aged 18-75 years, drug-naïve or on a single oral hypoglycaemic agent (sulfonylurea, glinide, alpha-glucosidase inhibitor, DPP-4 inhibitor, pioglitazone, or SGLT2 inhibitor), HbA1c 7.0%-9.0% (drug-naïve) or 6.0%-8.0% (on single OHA), BMI 18-35 kg/m2, Hb >12.5 g/dL (males) or >12.0 g/dL (females). Exclusions: renal dysfunction (eGFR <45 mL/min/1.73m2), prior metformin/imeglimin/insulin/GLP-1 receptor agonist use, hepatic dysfunction (AST/ALT/γ-GTP >3x upper limit of normal), SGLT2 inhibitor use with heart failure, severe retinopathy, history of gastrointestinal surgery, malignancy within 5 years, severe infection/perioperative/severe trauma, excessive drinking
intervention: Imeglimin 1000 mg orally twice daily (2000 mg/day total) for 24 weeks
comparison: Metformin 250 mg orally twice daily, raised to 500 mg twice daily (1000 mg/day total) for 24 weeks
outcomes_primary: Change in HbA1c from baseline to 12 and 24 weeks in each group
outcomes_secondary: Change in blood glucose, insulin, C-peptide, glucagon, total GLP-1, active GLP-1, total GIP, active GIP during OGTT from baseline to 12 and 24 weeks; changes in insulinogenic index, HOMA-IR, and HOMA-β from baseline to 12 and 24 weeks; comparison of changes in primary and secondary endpoints between imeglimin and metformin groups
extraction_notes: 8-week washout period for patients on single OHA before randomization. Open-label design. Single-center study in Japan.

title: Liraglutide and Colesevelam Change Serum and Fecal Bile Acid Levels in a Randomized Trial With Patients With Bile Acid Diarrhea.
population: Adults with idiopathic or postcholecystectomy, SeHCAT-verified moderate-to-severe bile acid diarrhea (SeHCAT test result ≤10%), no diabetes, and no other gastrointestinal diseases
intervention: Liraglutide administered subcutaneously once daily, uptitrated by weekly increments of 0.6 mg from 0.6 to 1.8 mg over 3 weeks, for 6 weeks total
comparison: Colesevelam administered orally 1,875 mg twice daily for 6 weeks
outcomes_primary: Changes in serum and fecal concentrations of individual bile acids (primary, secondary, conjugated, unconjugated bile acid species)
outcomes_secondary: Fecal microbiome composition assessed by 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing (alpha diversity including observed species and Shannon indices, beta diversity using Bray-Curtis and Jaccard distance matrices)
extraction_notes: This paper reports predefined secondary endpoints from a previously published head-to-head comparison trial. The primary endpoint of the original trial (reduction in daily bowel movements) is referenced but not the focus of this publication. Sample sizes were n=26 per group at randomization.

title: Albiglutide and atrial fibrillation in patients with Type 2 diabetes and established cardiovascular disease: insights from the Harmony Outcomes trial.
population: Patients aged >40 years with Type 2 diabetes and established cardiovascular disease
intervention: Albiglutide, a glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Composite of major adverse cardiac events (MACE): non-fatal myocardial infarction, non-fatal stroke, and cardiovascular death
outcomes_secondary: Atrial fibrillation events during follow-up; cardiovascular effects in patients with and without atrial fibrillation history
extraction_notes: Dose, route, frequency, and duration of albiglutide not specified in abstract. This is a secondary analysis of the Harmony Outcomes trial focusing on atrial fibrillation.

title: Similar weight loss with semaglutide regardless of diabetes and cardiometabolic risk parameters in individuals with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease: Post hoc analysis of three randomised controlled trials.
population: Adults with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) confirmed by magnetic resonance imaging or biopsy-proven metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH); includes individuals with type 2 diabetes (diagnosed with type 2 diabetes or HbA1c ≥6.5%), pre-type 2 diabetes (HbA1c ≥5.7 to <6.5%), or no type 2 diabetes (HbA1c <5.7%); MASH participants had fibrosis stages F1-F3 or F4 (compensated liver cirrhosis)
intervention: Subcutaneous semaglutide 0.4 mg once daily or semaglutide 2.4 mg once weekly for 48-72 weeks
comparison: Placebo (subcutaneous injection, matching frequency and duration)
outcomes_primary: Change in body weight from baseline (secondary endpoint in original trials, primary outcome in this post hoc analysis)
outcomes_secondary: Weight changes analyzed by type 2 diabetes status; correlations between weight change and baseline cardiometabolic parameters (fasting plasma glucose, HbA1c, C-peptide, fasting insulin, HOMA-IR, diabetes duration, lipid concentrations including triglycerides, LDL, HDL, and lipid ratios)
extraction_notes: This is a post hoc analysis pooling data from three randomized controlled trials (NCT03357380, NCT02970942, NCT03987451). Weight change was a secondary endpoint in original trials. Only semaglutide 0.4 mg once daily and 2.4 mg once weekly arms were included based on pharmacokinetic equivalence; lower dose arms from NCT02970942 were excluded.

title: Regulation of proglucagon derived peptides by carbohydrate and protein ingestion in young healthy males-A randomized, double-blind, cross-over trial.
population: Apparently healthy, normal-weight males; young healthy males
intervention: Isocaloric high-protein breakfast containing 65 g of glucose and 60 g of protein
comparison: Carbohydrate-rich breakfast containing 125 g of glucose
outcomes_primary: Levels of seven proglucagon-derived peptides (PGDPs): glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1), glucagon-like peptide-2 (GLP-2), oxyntomodulin, glicentin, major pro-glucagon fragment (MPGF), glucagon, and proglucagon; glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide/gastric inhibitory polypeptide total and total plus (GIP total and GIP total plus) levels measured at baseline, every 15 minutes for the first hour, and every 30 minutes for the second and third hours after each meal
outcomes_secondary: Glycemic responses; insulinemic responses; total amino acids
extraction_notes: Sample size is 10 participants. Primary vs secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in the abstract; classification based on stated study aims. Study described as randomized, double-blind, crossover design.

title: Impaired postprandial GLP-2 response enhances endotoxemia, systemic inflammation, and kidney injury in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH): effect of phospholipid curcumin meriva.
population: Adults with biopsy-proven metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), stratified for baseline diabetes, liver fibrosis stage (F0-2 vs F3-4), chronic kidney disease (presence/absence), and obesity status; age-, gender-, BMI-, and diabetes-matched controls without liver or kidney disease
intervention: Phospholipid curcumin formulation Meriva 2 g/day orally for 72 weeks
comparison: Placebo for 72 weeks
outcomes_primary: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) presence and regression, defined according to KDIGO guidelines as sustained eGFR ≥90 mL/min/1.73 m2 and normalization of albumin excretion rate (<30 mg/day), documented on 2 occasions at least 3 months apart
outcomes_secondary: Change in absolute values and KDIGO categories of eGFR and albumin excretion rate; postprandial response of incretins (GLP-1, GIP), GLP-2, zonulin, lipopolysaccharide (LPS), FGF-21, adiponectin, MCP-1; NF-kB activation in circulating mononuclear cells; liver histology (NAFLD activity score, fibrosis stage); metabolic parameters (HbA1c, HOMA-IR, lipid profile)
extraction_notes: This is a secondary analysis of a multicenter randomized trial; primary trial outcomes may differ from those reported in this analysis focused on CKD and GLP-2 pathway

title: Combined training and hormones/enzymes with insulinotropic actions in individuals with overweight and type 2 diabetes mellitus: A randomized controlled trial.
population: Adults aged 40-60 years with previously diagnosed type 2 diabetes mellitus and overweight (BMI 25-35 kg/m2), sedentary lifestyle, not having performed training and diet in the last 12 months; both sexes included. Exclusion criteria: cardiac arrhythmia, cardiac ischemia, coronary artery disease, severe arterial hypertension, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, anemia, uncontrolled hypothyroidism, limiting bone-joint diseases, severe specific complications of T2DM, use of exogenous insulin, thiazolidinediones, beta-blockers, anticoagulants, anti-inflammatories, or any medication that could interfere with physiological responses to tests or training

outcomes_primary: Concentrations of hormones/enzymes with insulinotropic actions: GLP-1 (glucagon-like peptide-1), GIP (glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide), DPP-4 (dipeptidyl peptidase-4), amylin/IAPP (islet amyloid polypeptide), and IDE (insulin-degrading enzyme)
outcomes_secondary: Functional variables (VO2max, 1RM leg press, 1RM bench press), body composition (BMI, fat percentage, lean mass, waist and neck circumferences), clinical markers (glucose, HbA1c, insulin, C peptide, HOMA-IR, HOMA-Beta, triglycerides, total cholesterol, HDL, VLDL, LDL), resting metabolic rate, resting heart rate, blood pressure
extraction_notes: This is a secondary analysis from a previously published randomized controlled trial (UTN: U1111-1202-1476). Primary outcomes for the original trial related to body composition were previously published. The distinction between primary and secondary outcomes for this secondary analysis is inferred from study objectives.

title: Metabolic and Hormonal Responses to Isomaltulose Ingestion Before or During Sustained Submaximal Exercise in Adults with Type 1 Diabetes Using Automated Insulin Delivery Systems.
population: Adults aged 18-75 years with type 1 diabetes for ≥2 years, HbA1c ≥7.5% (58 mmol/mol), using insulin pump treatment for ≥12 months, using continuous or intermittently scanned glucose monitoring for ≥6 months, using insulin aspart for ≥1 week, treated with MiniMed 780G automated insulin delivery system for >4 weeks
intervention: Isomaltulose 0.75g carbohydrate/kg body mass given as three separate isocaloric servings (0.25g carbohydrate/kg body mass each) as 10% solution mixed with water, administered orally immediately before exercise (t=0 min), at mid-point of exercise (t=+20 min), and toward end of exercise (t=+40 min), without bolus insulin, with temporary glucose target (150 mg/dL) applied 15 min before exercise commencement until 15 min after exercise (during exercise carbohydrates - DEC)

outcomes_primary: Plasma glucose concentrations, exercise-induced change in plasma glucose, rate of plasma glucose change during exercise
outcomes_secondary: Gut incretin hormones (GLP-1 and GIP), pancreatic glucagon, exogenous insulin concentrations, plasma lactate, whole-body fuel oxidation rates (carbohydrate and lipid oxidation), respiratory exchange ratio, time in range, time below range, time above range

Primary outcome not explicitly designated; outcomes listed are inferred from methods section describing parameters determined.

title: Dose-related effects of intraduodenal quinine on plasma glucose, glucoregulatory hormones and gastric emptying of a nutrient drink, and energy intake, in men with type 2 diabetes: a double-blind, randomised, crossover study.

outcomes_secondary: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) levels, insulin/C-peptide levels, gastric emptying rate

title: Glepaglutide, a Long-Acting Glucagon-like Peptide-2 Analogue, Reduces Parenteral Support in Patients With Short Bowel Syndrome: A Phase 3 Randomized Controlled Trial.

extraction_notes: Intervention route not explicitly stated but implied subcutaneous based on typical GLP-2 analogue administration. PS volume reduction protocol described: volume was equivalently reduced if mean urine volume of a 48-hour balance period exceeded baseline values by >10%.

title: Safety and efficacy of GLP-1/FGF21 dual agonist HEC88473 in MASLD and T2DM: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study.

outcomes_primary: MRI-proton density fat fraction (MRI-PDFF) for liver fat assessment
outcomes_secondary: HbA1c (glycated hemoglobin), fasting glucose levels, postprandial glucose levels, lipid profiles, insulin resistance, safety and tolerability (adverse events)
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in the abstract; classification inferred from reporting emphasis. Randomization ratio was 10:2 (HEC88473:placebo). This was a multiple-ascending-dose phase Ib/IIa trial.

title: Determinants of Liraglutide Treatment Discontinuation in Type 1 Diabetes: A Post Hoc Analysis of ADJUNCT ONE and ADJUNCT TWO Randomized Placebo-Controlled Clinical Studies.
journal: Journal of diabetes science and technology
population: Participants with type 1 diabetes (T1D) receiving insulin therapy
intervention: Liraglutide as adjunct to insulin therapy at doses of 1.8 mg, 1.2 mg, or 0.6 mg
comparison: Placebo
extraction_notes: This is a post hoc analysis of two phase 3 randomized controlled studies (ADJUNCT ONE NCT01836523 and ADJUNCT TWO NCT02098395). The analysis focuses on determinants of treatment discontinuation including baseline characteristics and adverse event rates comparing completers vs non-completers. Primary and secondary outcomes are not explicitly defined in this abstract as it represents a post hoc analysis rather than the original trial reports.

title: Tirzepatide Associated With Reduced Albuminuria in Participants With Type 2 Diabetes: Pooled Post Hoc Analysis From the Randomized Active- and Placebo-Controlled SURPASS-1-5 Clinical Trials.
population: Adults aged ≥18 years with type 2 diabetes, HbA1c 7.0-10.5% (varying by trial), BMI ≥23-25 kg/m2 (varying by trial), stable weight in 3 months prior to enrollment. Background therapy varied: diet and exercise alone (SURPASS-1), stable metformin monotherapy (SURPASS-2), metformin with or without SGLT2i (SURPASS-3), metformin, sulfonylurea, or SGLT2i combination (SURPASS-4), insulin glargine with or without metformin (SURPASS-5).
intervention: Tirzepatide 5 mg, 10 mg, or 15 mg administered as weekly subcutaneous injections for 40-52 weeks
comparison: Pooled comparators including: placebo (SURPASS-1 and SURPASS-5), semaglutide 1 mg once weekly (SURPASS-2), insulin degludec daily (SURPASS-3), insulin glargine (SURPASS-4)
outcomes_primary: Percent change in urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR) from baseline to week 40 or week 42
outcomes_secondary: Change in estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) over time to week 40/42
extraction_notes: Post hoc pooled analysis of SURPASS-1-5 trials. Randomization ratios were 1:1:1:1 in all trials except SURPASS-4 (1:1:1:3). SURPASS-2, -3, and -4 were open-label; SURPASS-1 and -5 were double-blind. Primary outcomes of original trials were glycemic control, not kidney endpoints.

title: Effect of semaglutide 2.4 mg on use of antihypertensive and lipid-lowering treatment in five randomized controlled STEP trials.
population: Adults aged ≥18 years with overweight or obesity (BMI ≥27 kg/m2) with or without type 2 diabetes. intervention: Semaglutide 2.4 mg subcutaneous injection (dose escalation to 2.4 mg), administered for 68 weeks
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Changes in antihypertensive or lipid-lowering treatment intensity from randomization to end of treatment (week 68), including: treatment intensity increase (dose escalation or addition of another medication), treatment intensity decrease (dose reduction or discontinuation of a medication), stopped (discontinuation of all antihypertensive or lipid-lowering medications)
outcomes_secondary: Systolic and diastolic blood pressure, lipid levels, hypertension remission (defined as BP <140/90 mm Hg without antihypertensive medications), changes in body weight from randomization to week 68, initiation of antihypertensive or lipid-lowering medications in participants not on these medications at randomization
extraction_notes: This is a post hoc analysis of pooled data from five STEP trials. Primary and secondary outcomes from original STEP trials differ from the outcomes analyzed in this post hoc analysis. Exact semaglutide dose escalation schedule and administration frequency not specified in abstract but referenced in methods as previously published.

title: Effects of Metformin on Postprandial Blood Pressure, Heart Rate, Gastric Emptying, GLP-1, and Prevalence of Postprandial Hypotension in Type 2 Diabetes: A Double-Blind Placebo-Controlled Crossover Study.
population: Individuals with type 2 diabetes
intervention: Metformin (dose, route, frequency, and duration not specified)
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Postprandial blood pressure, postprandial hypotension (PPH) events
outcomes_secondary: Heart rate, glucose, insulin, glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1), gastric emptying
extraction_notes: Study design is double-blind placebo-controlled crossover. Metformin dosing details not provided in abstract. Hierarchy of primary vs secondary outcomes not explicitly stated; categorization based on title emphasis and abstract structure.

title: Greater improvement in insulin sensitivity per unit weight loss associated with tirzepatide versus semaglutide: An exploratory analysis.

comparison: Semaglutide 1 mg; Placebo
outcomes_primary: Change in insulin sensitivity determined from hyperinsulinemic euglycemic clamp (M value)
outcomes_secondary: Change in insulin sensitivity from mixed-meal tolerance testing (Matsuda index); Change in body weight; Change in fat mass; Relationship between change in body weight and change in insulin sensitivity
extraction_notes: This is a post hoc exploratory analysis of a 28-week double-blind randomized trial. Route of administration for tirzepatide and semaglutide not specified. Primary versus secondary outcome distinction not explicitly stated in abstract.

title: evoke and evoke+: design of two large-scale, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 studies evaluating efficacy, safety, and tolerability of semaglutide in early-stage symptomatic Alzheimer's disease.
population: Men or women aged 55-85 years with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) or mild dementia due to Alzheimer's disease with confirmed amyloid abnormalities (assessed by positron emission tomography or cerebrospinal fluid analysis). MCI defined as CDR global score of 0.5 with CDR domain score ≥0.5 in at least one of three activities of daily living categories; mild AD dementia defined as CDR global score of 1.0. Required RBANS delayed memory index score ≤85 and MMSE score ≥22. evoke+ additionally allows participants with significant small vessel pathology (defined as more than one lacunar infarct and/or age-related white matter changes >2). Participants with type 2 diabetes allowed (up to planned maximum 30% of population).
intervention: Oral semaglutide once daily for 156 weeks (104-week main treatment phase plus 52-week extension). 8-week dose escalation regimen: 3 mg weeks 0-4, 7 mg weeks 4-8, then 14 mg weeks 8-156. Flexible dosing allowed including extension of dose-escalation intervals, dose reduction, and treatment pauses.
comparison: Matching placebo once daily following same dosing regimen for 156 weeks
outcomes_primary: Change from baseline to week 104 in Clinical Dementia Rating – Sum of Boxes (CDR-SB) score
outcomes_secondary: Confirmatory secondary: change from baseline to week 104 in AD Cooperative Study Activities of Daily Living – MCI (ADCS-ADL-MCI) score; time to progression to CDR global score ≥1.0 among participants with CDR global score 0.5 at baseline. Supportive secondary: change from baseline to week 104 in MMSE score, MoCA score, ADAS-Cog-13 score, ADCOMS score, NPI score; time to progression in disease stage based on global CDR score; number of treatment-emergent adverse events; change in high-sensitivity CRP level; time to first occurrence of stroke; time to first occurrence of MACE; change in EQ-5D-5L proxy score; change from baseline to week 156 in CDR-SB score, ADCS-ADL-MCI score, and time to dementia progression
extraction_notes: This is a protocol/design paper for two parallel phase 3 trials (evoke and evoke+) with identical designs except evoke+ allows small vessel pathology. Planned enrollment 1840 participants per trial. CSF sub-study planned for 210 participants. Exploratory biomarker endpoints include plasma NfL, GFAP, p-tau181 and CSF neuroinflammation markers.

title: Exploring Predictors of Treatment Response to GLP-1 Receptor Agonists for Smoking Cessation.
journal: Nicotine & tobacco research : official journal of the Society for Research on Nicotine and Tobacco
population: Smokers with prediabetes and/or overweight
intervention: Exenatide 2 mg subcutaneously once weekly plus nicotine patch 21 mg plus brief smoking cessation counseling
comparison: Placebo once weekly plus nicotine patch 21 mg plus brief smoking cessation counseling
outcomes_primary: Biologically confirmed 7-day point prevalence abstinence at week 6 (end-of-treatment)
extraction_notes: This is a secondary/post-hoc analysis of a parent trial (n=84). No secondary outcomes explicitly defined in abstract.

title: Dose-related Effects of Calcium to Enhance the Effects of L-tryptophan on Gut Hormones and Energy Intake in Obesity.
journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
population: Adult males with obesity without type 2 diabetes, body mass index approximately 30 kg/m², age approximately 27 years, weight-stable (<5% fluctuation in preceding 3 months), no dietary restrictions in preceding 3 months, excluded if history of gastrointestinal disorders or symptoms, cardiovascular or respiratory diseases or surgery, use of supplements or medications affecting gastrointestinal functions and/or appetite, protein supplement consumption, >2 standard drinks of alcohol >5 days/week, lactose intolerance, vegetarian, smokers, or high-performance athletes
intervention: 150-minute intraduodenal infusions of calcium 1000 mg alone (t=0-75 minutes) followed by calcium 1000 mg combined with L-tryptophan 0.1 kcal/min (t=75-150 minutes), infusion rate 3 mL/min, isosmotic solutions (300 mOsm)
comparison: Intraduodenal infusions of calcium 0 mg (control) alone then combined with L-tryptophan 0.1 kcal/min; intraduodenal infusions of calcium 500 mg alone then combined with L-tryptophan 0.1 kcal/min
outcomes_primary: Ad libitum energy intake at standardized buffet-style meal quantified by weighing food items consumed
outcomes_secondary: Plasma concentrations of gut hormones (gastrin, cholecystokinin, glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide, glucagon-like peptide-1, peptide tyrosine-tyrosine), antropyloroduodenal motility (antral pressures, isolated pyloric pressure waves number and amplitude, duodenal pressures/motility index), appetite perceptions (hunger, fullness), gastrointestinal symptoms (nausea, bloating), drowsiness assessed by visual analog scale
extraction_notes: Randomized double-blind crossover design with 3 study occasions separated by 3-7 days. Sample size of 15 participants. No explicit primary/secondary outcome designation in text; classification based on stated study objectives and analysis hierarchy. Energy intake calculated using Foodworks software.

title: Gastrointestinal tolerability and weight reduction associated with tirzepatide in adults with obesity or overweight with and without type 2 diabetes in the SURMOUNT-1 to -4 trials.
population: Adults aged 18 years or older with obesity (BMI ≥30 kg/m2) or overweight (BMI ≥27 kg/m2) with at least one weight-related comorbidity (hypertension, dyslipidemia, obstructive sleep apnea, or cardiovascular disease), with or without type 2 diabetes. Key exclusion criteria included type 1 diabetes, known clinically significant gastric emptying abnormality, and history of pancreatitis.
intervention: Tirzepatide administered as once weekly subcutaneous injection at doses of 5 mg, 10 mg, 15 mg, or maximum tolerated dose (MTD, 10 or 15 mg) for 72 weeks (SURMOUNT-1, -2, -3) or 88 weeks (SURMOUNT-4), with a 20-week dose escalation period
comparison: Placebo (once weekly subcutaneous injection)
outcomes_primary: Percent change in weight from baseline to the primary endpoint (Week 72 for SURMOUNT-1, -2, -3; Week 88 for SURMOUNT-4)
outcomes_secondary: Gastrointestinal adverse events (nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, dyspepsia), concomitant medications related to gastrointestinal adverse events (antidiarrheal and antiemetic medication use), treatment discontinuation due to gastrointestinal adverse events, mediation analysis of gastrointestinal adverse events on weight reduction
extraction_notes: This is a post hoc analysis pooling data from four Phase 3 trials (SURMOUNT-1 to -4). SURMOUNT-3 included a 12-week intensive lifestyle programme prior to randomization. SURMOUNT-4 included a 36-week open-label tirzepatide lead-in period before randomization. The primary outcomes listed are for the original trials; this post hoc analysis focused on the relationship between GI AEs and weight reduction.

title: Subcutaneous weekly semaglutide with automated insulin delivery in type 1 diabetes: a double-blind, randomized, crossover trial.
population: Adults aged 18 years or older with type 1 diabetes diagnosed for 1 year or longer, using an insulin pump for 3 months or longer, with HbA1c of 11% or less. Exclusion criteria included current or recent use of antihyperglycemic agents other than insulin, planned or ongoing pregnancy or breastfeeding, severe hypoglycemic episode within 3 months, diabetic ketoacidosis requiring medical attention within 6 months, history of acute or chronic pancreatitis or gallbladder disease, BMI of 21 kg/m² or less, personal or family history of medullary thyroid cancer or type 2 multiple endocrine neoplasia, bariatric surgery within 6 months, prior adverse reaction to GLP1-RAs, clinically significant diabetic retinopathy or gastroparesis.
intervention: Subcutaneous semaglutide titrated over 11 weeks (0.25 mg weekly for 4 weeks, then 0.5 mg weekly for 4 weeks, then 1 mg weekly or maximum tolerated dose), followed by 4 weeks of automated insulin delivery system use
comparison: Placebo (saline) administered subcutaneously with identical titration schedule over 11 weeks, followed by 4 weeks of automated insulin delivery system use
outcomes_primary: Percentage of time spent in the target glucose range of 3.9–10.0 mmol/L during the last 4 weeks of each intervention
outcomes_secondary: Mean glucose level; standard deviation and coefficient of variation of glucose levels; time spent in hyperglycemia (above 10.0 and 13.9 mmol/L); time spent in hypoglycemia (below 3.0 and 3.9 mmol/L); daytime and nighttime glucose outcomes; HbA1c; fructosamine; lipid profile; weight; BMI; waist circumference; hip circumference; insulin requirements; carbohydrate intake; adverse events including diabetic ketoacidosis, severe hypoglycemia, euglycemic ketosis
extraction_notes: Crossover trial design with 2-week washout period between interventions. Maximum tolerated dose varied among participants (0.25 mg, 0.5 mg, or 1 mg). Research-based AID system used during outcome assessment period included Ypsomed pump, Dexcom G6 CGM, and McGill insulin dosing algorithm.

title: Allocation of Semaglutide According to Coronary Artery Calcium and BMI: Applying the SELECT Trial to MESA.
population: Adults aged 45-84 years without diabetes and without clinical cardiovascular disease (myocardial infarction, stroke, heart failure, peripheral arterial disease) with BMI ≥27 kg/m2 who underwent coronary artery calcium scoring on cardiac computed tomography; participants from the MESA (Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis) cohort including White, Black, Hispanic, and Chinese participants
intervention: Semaglutide at weight loss dose (modeled allocation based on coronary artery calcium burden)
comparison: Coronary artery calcium burden categories: CAC = 0 versus CAC 1-99 versus CAC 100-299 versus CAC ≥300; BMI categories: 27-29 kg/m2 versus 30-34 kg/m2 versus ≥35 kg/m2
outcomes_primary: Major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) defined as cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or nonfatal stroke
outcomes_secondary: Heart failure (defined by persistent symptoms such as shortness of breath and edema plus objective criteria including physician diagnosis, pulmonary edema or congestion on chest x-ray, and/or abnormal ventricular function on echocardiography); chronic kidney disease (defined using ICD-9 and ICD-10 codes); all-cause mortality; composite outcomes including CVD (MACE or HF), CKM (MACE or HF or CKD), and any first obesity-related CKM event (MACE, HF, CKD, or all-cause mortality); number needed to treat calculations
extraction_notes: This is a modeling study applying risk reduction estimates from the SELECT trial to observational MESA cohort data, not a randomized controlled trial of semaglutide. Semaglutide dose, route, frequency, and duration were not specified as this was a modeled intervention based on SELECT trial relative risk reductions (20% for MACE, 18% for HF, 19% for all-cause mortality, 22% for CKD)

title: Time to weight plateau with tirzepatide treatment in the SURMOUNT-1 and SURMOUNT-4 clinical trials.
population: Adults with obesity (BMI ≥30 kg/m2) or overweight (BMI ≥27 to <30 kg/m2) with at least one adiposity-related complication, without type 2 diabetes. Post-hoc analysis included participants adherent to tirzepatide treatment (received at least 75% of study doses), achieved at least 5% weight loss by primary endpoint, reached assigned dose by week 24, and had no dose reduction.
intervention: Tirzepatide 5 mg, 10 mg, or 15 mg once weekly subcutaneous injection for 72 weeks (SURMOUNT-1) or 88 weeks total (36 weeks open-label to maximum tolerated dose of 10 or 15 mg followed by 52 weeks continued treatment; SURMOUNT-4)
comparison: Placebo (SURMOUNT-1: 1:1:1:1 randomization to tirzepatide 5, 10, or 15 mg, or placebo; SURMOUNT-4: randomization to continue tirzepatide or switch to placebo after open-label period). Note: This post-hoc analysis focused on tirzepatide-treated participants only.
outcomes_primary: Time to weight plateau, defined as time from randomization to the start of the first 12-week interval with weight change <5% that was maintained through all subsequent 12-week intervals
outcomes_secondary: Proportion of participants reaching weight plateau by end of study; association between baseline characteristics (tirzepatide dose, age, sex, race, BMI category, waist circumference) and time to weight plateau
extraction_notes: This is a post-hoc exploratory analysis of SURMOUNT-1 and SURMOUNT-4 trials. Primary outcomes of the original trials were not the focus of this analysis. The analysis included only tirzepatide-treated participants who met adherence criteria, excluding placebo arm from main analyses.

title: Once-weekly IcoSema versus once-weekly semaglutide in adults with type 2 diabetes: the COMBINE 2 randomised clinical trial.
population: Adults aged ≥18 years with type 2 diabetes inadequately managed (HbA1c 53.0–85.8 mmol/mol [7.0–10.0%]) receiving stable doses of daily or weekly GLP-1 receptor agonists (excluding once-weekly semaglutide >1.0 mg) for at least 90 days before screening, with or without stable doses of additional oral glucose-lowering medications
intervention: Once-weekly IcoSema (combination of basal insulin icodec and semaglutide), subcutaneous injection, starting dose 40 dose steps (equivalent to 40 U icodec and 0.114 mg semaglutide), titrated in 10 dose-step increments/decrements weekly based on pre-breakfast self-measured blood glucose (target 4.4–7.2 mmol/l), maximum dose 350 dose steps (350 U icodec/1.0 mg semaglutide), for 52 weeks

outcomes_primary: Change in HbA1c from baseline to week 52
outcomes_secondary: Change in fasting plasma glucose from baseline to week 52; change in body weight from baseline to week 52; combined clinically significant (level 2; <3.0 mmol/l) or severe (level 3; requiring external assistance) hypoglycaemia from baseline to week 57; clinically significant hypoglycaemic episodes from baseline to week 57; severe hypoglycaemic episodes from baseline to week 57; pre-breakfast SMBG by week; treatment dose at weeks 50–52; achievement of HbA1c <53.0 mmol/mol at week 52; achievement of HbA1c <53.0 mmol/mol at week 52 without clinically significant or severe hypoglycaemia in previous 12 weeks; achievement of HbA1c <53.0 mmol/mol at week 52 without weight gain and without clinically significant or severe hypoglycaemia in previous 12 weeks; changes in BP, waist circumference and lipids; adverse events

title: Clinical characteristics affecting weight loss in an East Asian population receiving semaglutide: A STEP 6 subgroup analysis.

title: The safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of an optimized dual GLP-1/GIP receptor agonist (BGM0504) in healthy volunteers: A dose-escalation Phase I study.

title: Semaglutide in obesity-related heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and type 2 diabetes across baseline HbA

title: Effects of Semaglutide Treatment on Psoriatic Lesions in Obese Patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: An Open-Label, Randomized Clinical Trial.
population: Adults aged 18-70 years with moderately-severe to severe plaque psoriasis (PASI score ≥10), type 2 diabetes mellitus diagnosed at least 6 months prior and treated with metformin, and obesity (BMI >30 kg/m2, HbA1c >7%)

title: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Two-Way Cross-over Study to Evaluate the Efficacy of Liraglutide Treatment in Patients Undergoing Transoral Outlet Reduction Endoscopy for Weight Regain Post Roux-en-Y Gastric Bypass.

outcomes_primary: Percent total body weight loss (%TBWL) at 12 and 24 months
extraction_notes: Cross-over design where all participants received both liraglutide and placebo for equal duration over 24-month treatment phase; specific liraglutide dose not stated; secondary outcomes not specified

title: Association of bodyweight loss with changes in lipids, blood pressure, and fasting serum glucose following tirzepatide treatment in Japanese participants with type 2 diabetes: A post hoc analysis of the SURPASS J-mono trial.

title: Exenatide once a week versus placebo as a potential disease-modifying treatment for people with Parkinson's disease in the UK: a phase 3, multicentre, double-blind, parallel-group, randomised, placebo-controlled trial.

outcomes_secondary: Fasting blood glucose; continuous glucose monitoring parameters (mean blood glucose, time in range, time above range, time below range, standard deviation, coefficient of variation, area under curve for hyperglycemia and hypoglycemia); triglyceride-glucose index; body composition parameters (weight, BMI, body fat mass, percent body fat, visceral fat area, fat mass index, fat free mass, skeletal muscle mass, skeletal lean mass, skeletal muscle mass index); waist circumference; waist-to-height ratio; blood pressure (systolic and diastolic); serum amylase; serum lipase; hemoglobin; lipid parameters; adverse events

title: Effects of retatrutide on body composition in people with type 2 diabetes: a substudy of a phase 2, double-blind, parallel-group, placebo-controlled, randomised trial.
population: Adults aged 18-75 years with type 2 diabetes, HbA1c criteria (specific threshold not fully stated in abstract)
intervention: Retatrutide (glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide, glucagon-like peptide-1, and glucagon receptor agonist) at doses of 0.5 mg, 4 mg, 8 mg, or 12 mg
comparison: Placebo; Dulaglutide 1.5 mg
outcomes_primary: Percent change from baseline to week 36 in total body fat mass
outcomes_secondary: Lean mass loss to weight loss proportion; adverse events; serious adverse events
extraction_notes: This is a body composition substudy of a larger phase 2 trial. The 4 mg and 8 mg retatrutide groups were pooled from multiple dosing regimens. HbA1c eligibility criterion is truncated in abstract. Route and frequency of administration not specified. Duration of treatment was 36 weeks.

title: Changes in β-Cell Function and Insulin Sensitivity During Treatment With Dapagliflozin Alone or in Combination With Exenatide in Type 2 Diabetes.
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes; 90 patients enrolled
intervention: Dapagliflozin alone, exenatide alone, or dapagliflozin/exenatide combination therapy
comparison: Placebo (n=15); dapagliflozin alone (n=25); exenatide alone (n=25); dapagliflozin/exenatide combination (n=25)
outcomes_primary: β-cell function (BCF) indices calculated during 180-min oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT)
outcomes_secondary: Corrected Matsuda index (cMI) for urinary glucose loss; insulin secretion; insulin sensitivity
extraction_notes: Study design includes both acute (single dose) and chronic (1 and 4 months) assessments. Specific doses, routes, and frequencies of dapagliflozin and exenatide not stated in abstract.

title: Dapagliflozin's impact on hormonal regulation and ketogenesis in type 1 diabetes: a randomised controlled crossover trial.
population: Adults with type 1 diabetes with C-peptide concentrations <0.1 nmol/l, diabetes duration >5 years, and BMI 20-29 kg/m2. intervention: Dapagliflozin 10 mg orally once daily for 7 days as adjunct to standard insulin therapy
comparison: Placebo orally once daily for 7 days as adjunct to standard insulin therapy (crossover design with 14 day washout period)
outcomes_primary: GLP-1 concentrations during OGTT clamp (OGTTC), measured every 15 minutes over 120 minutes
outcomes_secondary: GLP-1 concentrations during hyperinsulinaemic-euglycaemic clamp (HEC); glucagon concentrations during OGTTC and HEC; somatostatin concentrations during OGTTC and HEC; total ketone body concentrations at baseline and every 15 minutes during OGTTC and HEC
extraction_notes: Exploratory outcome was plasma glucose concentrations during OGTTC. Original protocol specified AUC for GLP-1 as primary outcome but was changed to unit-based outcomes from repeated-measures mixed-model analysis.

title: Long-acting PYY
population: Phase 1: Adult male participants aged 18-55 years, body weight ≥70 kg, BMI 25.0-34.9 kg/m², HbA1c <6.5%. Phase 2: Male and female adult participants with obesity, BMI 30.0-45.0 kg/m², HbA1c <6.5%, no history of type 1 or type 2 diabetes.
intervention: Phase 1 Part 1: Single subcutaneous dose of PYY1875 (0.1, 0.3, 0.6, 1.2, or 2.1 mg). Phase 1 Part 2: Single subcutaneous dose of PYY1875 (0.03, 0.1, 0.3, 0.6, 1.2, or 1.7 mg) plus semaglutide 0.25 mg.
