comparison: Phase 1: Placebo (randomized 6:2 PYY1875:placebo). Phase 2: Placebo as add-on to semaglutide 2.4 mg (randomized 2:1 PYY1875:placebo at each dose level).
outcomes_primary: Phase 1: Number of treatment emergent adverse events (TEAEs) from day 1 to follow-up (day 36 or day 54). Phase 2 Part 1: Number of TEAEs from dosing (day 1) to end of study (week 24). Phase 2 Part 2: Change (percentage) in body weight from baseline (week 32) to end of treatment (week 48).
outcomes_secondary: Phase 1: Pharmacokinetic endpoints (AUC0-INF, AUC0-168h, Cmax, tmax, t1/2). Phase 2: Number of TEAEs and serious TEAEs from week 0 to end of study (week 56); change from baseline to end of treatment in body weight (kg), HbA1c (percentage points), fasting plasma glucose, fasting insulin, waist circumference; relative change in total, HDL, LDL, VLDL cholesterol, triglycerides, and free fatty acids.
extraction_notes: This publication reports multiple studies (preclinical rat studies, phase 1 study, phase 2 study with parts 1 and 2). PICO elements extracted for clinical studies only. Phase 2 Part 2 included 32-week open-label semaglutide run-in before randomization.

title: Effect of the GLP-1 receptor agonist exenatide on pro-inflammatory and metabolic biomarkers in individuals with alcohol use disorder: Post hoc results from a randomized, double-blinded, placebo-controlled clinical trial.
population: Individuals diagnosed with alcohol use disorder (AUD), aged 18-70 years. Key exclusion criteria: severe psychiatric or somatic comorbidity and concomitant pharmacotherapy against AUD. A comparison group of individuals without AUD matched on sex, age, and educational status was also included.
intervention: Exenatide (GLP-1 receptor agonist) 2 mg administered subcutaneously once weekly for 26 weeks
comparison: Placebo (once weekly for 26 weeks); additional cross-sectional comparison with individuals without AUD
outcomes_primary: Not explicitly specified as primary. 25 biomarkers measured: pro-inflammatory markers (IFN-γ, TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-2, IL-4, IL-6, IL-8, IL-10, IL-12p70, IL-13, MCP-1, hsCRP) and metabolic biomarkers (C-peptide, GIP, GLP-1, glucagon, insulin, leptin, PP, adiponectin, FGF-21, total cholesterol, HDL, LDL, triglycerides)
outcomes_secondary: Not explicitly specified
extraction_notes: This is a post hoc analysis of biomarkers from a previously published RCT (NCT03232112). The original trial's primary outcome was alcohol consumption, not biomarkers. Primary and secondary outcomes not distinguished in this post hoc analysis. Comparison group for cross-sectional baseline analysis (n=23 without AUD) was originally recruited for fMRI sub-study.

title: Predictors of Initial and Sustained Glycemic and Weight Response to Tirzepatide: A Post Hoc Analysis of SURPASS-4.
population: Adults aged ≥18 years with type 2 diabetes inadequately controlled (HbA1c 58–91 mmol/mol [7.5–10.5%]) with any combination of metformin, sulfonylurea, and/or sodium–glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor, BMI ≥25 kg/m², stable weight during previous 3 months, and at increased risk of cardiovascular events
intervention: Tirzepatide 5 mg, 10 mg, or 15 mg subcutaneously once weekly
comparison: Treat-to-target insulin glargine once daily
outcomes_primary: Change in HbA1c at 52 weeks
outcomes_secondary: Achievement of HbA1c ≤48 mmol/mol (6.5%) at 52 weeks; achievement of HbA1c <39 mmol/mol (5.7%) at 52 weeks; sustained glycemic control (no rise in HbA1c >2.2 mmol/mol above week 52 value) after 52 weeks; achievement of ≥10% weight reduction at 52 weeks; sustained weight loss (no increase >2 kg from week 52 measurement) after 52 weeks; predictors of initial and sustained glycemic and weight response
extraction_notes: This is a post hoc analysis of the SURPASS-4 trial. The original trial primary endpoint was at 52 weeks with variable treatment period up to 104 weeks. Randomization ratio was 1:1:1:3 for tirzepatide 5mg, 10mg, 15mg, and insulin glargine groups respectively.

title: Semaglutide Improves Lipid Subfraction Profiles in Type 2 Diabetes: Insights from a One-Year Follow-Up Study.
population: Adults aged over 45 years with type 2 diabetes mellitus for at least 5 years, inadequate glycemic control on metformin monotherapy (HbA1c 6.5-10%), BMI >25 kg/m², eGFR >60 mL/min/1.73 m². Exclusions: type 1 diabetes, previous GLP-1RA or DPP-4 inhibitor treatment, active smoking, alcohol consumption, pregnancy, breastfeeding, documented coronary or cerebrovascular event, clinically significant heart failure (NYHA II-IV), acute pancreatitis, pancreatic or thyroid cancer, severe liver failure (Child-Pugh B and C), chronic systemic glucocorticoids or immunosuppressive drugs, advanced diabetic retinopathy (proliferative stage), diabetic nephropathy or severe renal impairment (eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73 m² and/or significant proteinuria), active malignant disease
intervention: Subcutaneous semaglutide once weekly (titration: 0.25 mg/week starting dose, increased to 0.5 mg/week at week 4, and 1 mg/week at week 8 as target dose) added to metformin monotherapy, for 52 weeks
comparison: Oral sitagliptin 100 mg once daily added to metformin monotherapy; non-diabetic obese age- and body weight-matched controls (medication-free)
outcomes_primary: Not explicitly specified as primary outcome
outcomes_secondary: Changes in anthropometric measurements (BMI, waist circumference), glycemic parameters (fasting glucose, fructosamine, HbA1c), lipid parameters (triglycerides, total cholesterol, LDL cholesterol, HDL cholesterol, non-HDL cholesterol), LDL and HDL lipoprotein subfractions measured by Lipoprint gel electrophoresis, apolipoprotein A1, apolipoprotein B, hsCRP, renal function parameters (creatinine, eGFR), liver enzymes
extraction_notes: Primary outcome not explicitly designated; all outcomes appear to be analyzed without hierarchy. Study described as randomized but randomization method not detailed. Sample size is small (n=34 diabetic patients total: 18 semaglutide, 16 sitagliptin). Control group (n=31) was non-diabetic and medication-free, serving as reference rather than active comparator.

title: Gradual Titration of Semaglutide Results in Better Treatment Adherence and Fewer Adverse Events: A Randomized Controlled Open-Label Pilot Study Examining a 16-Week Flexible Titration Regimen Versus Label-Recommended 8-Week Semaglutide Titration Regimen.
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes (T2D)
intervention: Flexible titration of semaglutide: starting at 0.0675 mg (measured as five clicks made by the dose selector dial), with gradual increases by 0.0675 mg/week and delays for gastrointestinal adverse events, over 16 weeks
comparison: Label-recommended titration of semaglutide: 0.25 mg, 0.5 mg, 1 mg at 4-week intervals (8-week titration regimen)
outcomes_primary: Treatment adherence; gastrointestinal adverse events (GI-AEs)
outcomes_secondary: Withdrawal due to GI-AEs; nausea; asthenia; number of days experiencing nausea; HbA1c change; BMI change
extraction_notes: Study duration was 26 weeks total. The abstract does not explicitly distinguish primary from secondary outcomes; categorization based on stated objective. Sample size: 104 patients randomized.

title: Weight reduction over time in tirzepatide-treated participants by early weight loss response: Post hoc analysis in SURMOUNT-1.
population: Adults with body mass index (BMI) ≥30 kg/m2 or ≥27 kg/m2 with at least one weight-related complication, excluding diabetes; participants treated with tirzepatide who received ≥75% of assigned treatment doses and had weight measurements at Weeks 0, 12, 24 and 72
intervention: Tirzepatide 5 mg, 10 mg, or 15 mg once weekly subcutaneous injection; initiated at 2.5 mg once weekly and increased in 2.5 mg increments every 4 weeks through 20-week dose escalation period; target dose achieved at Week 4 (5 mg), Week 12 (10 mg), or Week 20 (15 mg); 72-week treatment duration; plus lifestyle counselling with 500 calorie/day deficit and at least 150 minutes physical activity per week
comparison: Placebo (original SURMOUNT-1 trial); this post hoc analysis compared late responders (<5% weight reduction at Week 12) versus early responders (≥5% weight reduction at Week 12)
outcomes_primary: Proportion of participants achieving weight reduction targets (≥5%, ≥10%, ≥15%, ≥20%, ≥25%) at Week 24 and Week 72
outcomes_secondary: Mean percent body weight reduction trajectory over time; time to reach 5% weight reduction
extraction_notes: This is a post hoc analysis of the SURMOUNT-1 trial (NCT04184622). The analysis focused on tirzepatide-treated participants only, categorized by early vs late response status. Primary outcomes of the original trial are not explicitly stated in this abstract.

title: The effects of collagen peptide supplementation on appetite and post-exercise energy intake in females: a randomised controlled trial.
population: Healthy, physically active females aged 18-30 years, classified as Tier 1 (recreationally active) or Tier 2 (trained/developmental) according to participant classification framework, not taking supplements or medications that may interfere with appetite, free from health conditions or food allergies that could affect study outcomes
intervention: 15 g/day of bovine collagen peptides consumed orally upon waking for 7 days, with final dose consumed 10 minutes after exercise on day 7
comparison: Taste-matched non-energy control (water with cherry flavouring) consumed orally upon waking for 7 days, with final dose consumed 10 minutes after exercise on day 7
outcomes_primary: Ad libitum energy intake at pasta meal 60 minutes post-supplementation on day 7
outcomes_secondary: Subjective appetite sensations (hunger, fullness, desire to eat, thirst, prospective food consumption, composite appetite score) measured via visual analogue scale; gastrointestinal symptoms (nausea, headache, GI discomfort, urge to defecate); blood glucose concentrations; plasma hormone concentrations (total ghrelin, glucagon-like peptide-1, peptide YY, cholecystokinin, dipeptidyl peptidase-4, leptin, insulin); eating rate
extraction_notes: Sample size of 15 completers (2 excluded from initial 17 recruited). Blood data presented for n=14 due to inability to obtain samples from one participant. CCK data presented for n=9 due to samples above detection limits. Physical activity data presented for n=13 due to watch failures.

title: Tirzepatide Treatment and Associated Changes in β-Cell Function and Insulin Sensitivity in People With Obesity or Overweight With Prediabetes or Normoglycemia: A Post Hoc Analysis From the SURMOUNT-1 Trial.
population: Adults with obesity (BMI ≥30 kg/m2) or overweight (BMI ≥27 kg/m2) with one or more weight-related comorbidity, excluding diabetes, with either prediabetes or normoglycemia at baseline
intervention: Tirzepatide 5 mg, 10 mg, or 15 mg subcutaneous injection once weekly for 72 weeks, in conjunction with lifestyle modification
comparison: Placebo once weekly for 72 weeks, in conjunction with lifestyle modification
outcomes_primary: Not explicitly specified as primary in this post hoc analysis; main outcomes assessed include model-derived parameters of β-cell function (insulin secretion rate, β-cell glucose sensitivity, ISR at 5.4 mmol/L, total insulin secretion during OGTT, potentiation of ISR, β-cell rate sensitivity, 30-min insulinogenic index) and insulin sensitivity (Matsuda index, oral glucose insulin sensitivity, HOMA2-IR)
outcomes_secondary: Changes in HbA1c, fasting serum glucose, fasting insulin, body weight, glucose and insulin AUC during OGTT, C-peptide concentrations during OGTT
extraction_notes: This is a post hoc analysis of the SURMOUNT-1 trial. Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in this analysis. Randomization ratio was 1:1:1:1 across three tirzepatide doses and placebo.

title: Impact of Body Mass Index, Central Adiposity, and Weight Loss on the Benefits of Tirzepatide in HFpEF: The SUMMIT Trial.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology
population: Patients with NYHA functional class II-IV heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) and body mass index (BMI) ≥30 kg/m²
intervention: Tirzepatide (long-acting glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide receptor and glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonist)
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Composite of cardiovascular death or worsening heart failure
outcomes_secondary: 6-minute walk distance (6MWD), body weight change, Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Clinical Summary Score (KCCQ-CSS), systolic blood pressure, C-reactive protein (CRP), waist circumference (WC)
extraction_notes: This is a secondary analysis of the SUMMIT trial examining effects by baseline BMI tertile, waist-to-hip ratio (WHR), and weight loss achieved. Full tirzepatide dosing details not provided in abstract. NCT04847557.

title: Effect of semaglutide versus placebo on cardiorenal outcomes by prior cardiovascular disease and baseline body mass index: Pooled post hoc analysis of SUSTAIN 6 and PIONEER 6.
population: Adults with type 2 diabetes at high cardiovascular risk or with established cardiovascular disease; age ≥50 years with established CVD (including previous cardiovascular, cerebrovascular or peripheral vascular disease), chronic heart failure or chronic kidney disease, or age ≥60 years with at least one CV risk factor; excluded if on long-term or intermittent haemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis; PIONEER 6 also excluded eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m²
intervention: Semaglutide: once-weekly subcutaneous 0.5 mg or 1.0 mg (SUSTAIN 6) or once-daily oral 14 mg (PIONEER 6)
comparison: Placebo (pooled from both trials)
outcomes_primary: Time to first primary major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), defined as composite of cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, or non-fatal stroke
outcomes_secondary: Time to expanded MACE (primary MACE plus hospitalisation for unstable angina pectoris or heart failure); time to cardiovascular death; time to all-cause death; time to first new or worsening nephropathy (composite of new onset of persistent macroalbuminuria ≥300 mg/g, persistent doubling of serum creatinine level and eGFR ≤45 mL/min/1.73 m², continuous kidney replacement therapy, or death due to kidney disease; SUSTAIN 6 population only); individual components of primary MACE (non-fatal MI, non-fatal stroke)
extraction_notes: Post hoc pooled analysis of two CVOTs (SUSTAIN 6 and PIONEER 6); kidney composite outcome assessed in SUSTAIN 6 population only as PIONEER 6 did not assess kidney outcomes; subgroup analyses by prior CVD status and baseline BMI categories

title: Effects of combined metformin and semaglutide therapy on body weight, metabolic parameters, and reproductive outcomes in overweight/obese women with polycystic ovary syndrome: a prospective, randomized, controlled, open-label clinical trial.
population: Overweight or obese women with PCOS (BMI ≥ 24 kg/m²) diagnosed according to Rotterdam criteria, aged 18-40 years, who had not responded to lifestyle interventions for 3 months prior to enrollment. Exclusion criteria included allergy to GLP-1 RAs or metformin, pre-existing diabetes (type 1 or 2), comorbid conditions such as congenital adrenal hyperplasia, Cushing's syndrome, or androgen-secreting tumors, abnormal liver or kidney function (ALT > 2.5 times upper limit of normal, eGFR < 60 mL/min/1.73 m²), use of glucocorticoids, estrogen, progesterone, insulin, or other drugs affecting reproduction within 3 months, other gynecological conditions causing severe infertility or severe male infertility in partner, inability to comply with follow-up, and patients planning pregnancy within 16 weeks or currently pregnant.
intervention: Combination therapy (COM): Metformin 1000 mg twice daily plus semaglutide 1 mg once weekly for 16 weeks. Metformin started at 500 mg daily and increased by 500 mg every 3 days until reaching 1000 mg twice daily. Semaglutide initiated at 0.25 mg, increased to 0.5 mg at 4 weeks and 1 mg at 8 weeks. After 16 weeks, semaglutide was discontinued and metformin 1000 mg twice daily continued for an additional 24 weeks.
comparison: Metformin (MET) monotherapy: Metformin 1000 mg twice daily for 16 weeks, started at 500 mg daily and increased by 500 mg every 3 days until reaching target dose. Continued at 1000 mg twice daily for an additional 24 weeks.
outcomes_primary: Changes in anthropometric measures related to obesity including body weight, BMI, and waist-to-hip ratio (WHR), assessed at Week 0 and Week 16.
outcomes_secondary: Alterations in reproductive hormone levels (testosterone, SHBG, DHEA-S, E2, PRL, FAI, LH/FSH, AMH), glucose metabolism parameters (HbA1c, FBG, FINS, HOMA-IR), lipid metabolism parameters (TG, TC, HDL-C, LDL-C), C-reactive protein (CRP) levels, Chinese visceral adiposity index (CVAI), menstrual cycle recovery, and pregnancy outcomes (natural pregnancy rate, total pregnancy rate) assessed between Weeks 16 and 40.
extraction_notes: Sample size was 100 patients randomized, with 80 completing the study. Additionally, 40 healthy controls were enrolled for baseline comparison but were not part of the randomized intervention groups. Trial registration: ChiCTR2400090908.

title: Early-Onset Obesity and Tirzepatide Treatment: A Post Hoc Analysis of the SURMOUNT Clinical Trials.
population: Adults aged 18 years or older with BMI ≥30 kg/m2 or BMI ≥27 kg/m2 with at least one weight-related comorbidity (hypertension, dyslipidemia, obstructive sleep apnea, cardiovascular disease), who reported one or more unsuccessful dietary efforts to lose weight, without diabetes. Participants categorized by age at obesity diagnosis: early-onset obesity (<25 years) versus later-onset obesity (≥25 years)
intervention: Tirzepatide 5 mg, 10 mg, or 15 mg once weekly subcutaneous injection, or maximally tolerated dose. Treatment duration 72-88 weeks
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Percent change and absolute change from baseline in body weight at 72 weeks (SURMOUNT-1 and SURMOUNT-3) and 88 weeks (SURMOUNT-4) in participants with early-onset versus later-onset obesity
outcomes_secondary: Proportion of participants reaching body weight reduction thresholds; changes in glycemia (HbA1c); changes in cardiometabolic parameters including waist circumference, blood pressure, lipids (triglycerides, HDL cholesterol, LDL cholesterol); insulin sensitivity (HOMA2-IR); treatment-emergent adverse events; serious adverse events
extraction_notes: This is a post hoc analysis pooling data from SURMOUNT-1, SURMOUNT-3, and SURMOUNT-4 trials. SURMOUNT-3 included participants who achieved ≥5.0% body weight reduction after 12-week intensive lifestyle intervention before randomization. SURMOUNT-4 included a 36-week open-label tirzepatide lead-in period before randomization. Key exclusion criteria included diabetes, body weight change >5 kg within 90 days prior to screening, previous or planned surgical treatment for obesity, and treatment with weight loss medication within 90 days before screening.

title: Efficacy and safety of beinaglutide with continuous subcutaneous infusion in newly diagnosed patients with type 2 diabetes: a randomized, control, open-labeled clinical trial.
population: Newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes patients
intervention: Continuous subcutaneous glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist infusion (CSGI) with beinaglutide added to continuous subcutaneous insulin infusion (CSII) for 4 weeks
comparison: Continuous subcutaneous insulin infusion (CSII) alone for 4 weeks
outcomes_primary: Body weight change from baseline to endpoint
outcomes_secondary: BMI change; proportion losing ≥5% body weight; glycemic control; insulin dose requirements; β-cell function; adverse events
extraction_notes: Open-label study design; dose and frequency of beinaglutide not specified in abstract; sample size is 30 patients randomized 1:1

title: Exenatide Once Weekly in the Treatment of Patients with Multiple System Atrophy.
population: Men and women aged 30 to 80 years with diagnosis of possible or probable multiple system atrophy (MSA) of parkinsonian (MSA-P) or cerebellar subtype (MSA-C) according to Gilman Criteria; less than 5 years from documented MSA diagnosis or from previously documented parkinsonian/ataxic neurological condition later re-diagnosed as MSA; able to walk at least 10 meters (with or without assistance); anticipated survival of at least 3 years. Exclusions: concurrent dementia (MoCA score <21), BMI <18.5, HbA1c ≥48 mmol/mol or random blood glucose >11.1 mmol/L, previous exenatide exposure within 90 days, concurrent severe depression (BDI-II ≥30), active malignancy, clinically significant medical diagnosis, speech impairment (UMSARS question 1 score ≥3), swallowing impairment (UMSARS question 2 score ≥3), impairment in ambulation (UMSARS question 7 score >3), falling more than once per week (UMSARS question 8 score ≥3)
intervention: Subcutaneous exenatide (Bydureon or Bydureon BCise) 2 mg once weekly self-administered for 48 weeks, in addition to standard of care, followed by 48-week washout period
comparison: Standard of care alone (no exenatide)
outcomes_primary: Unified Multiple System Atrophy Rating Scale (UMSARS) parts I and II combined score at 48 weeks
outcomes_secondary: Loss of independent ambulation (UMSARS part I item 7 score of 4); timed walk; MSA-Quality of Life (MSA-QOL) scores; UMSARS parts I, II, III, and IV scores; anti-parkinsonian or anti-orthostatic hypotension medication use; number of falls; proportion of participants reaching score ≥3 on UMSARS part I items 1 (speech), 2 (swallowing), and 8 (falling); Clinician Global Impression of Change (CGI); Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) scores. Exploratory outcomes: digital mobility outcomes (daily step count, walking speed, stride length), grey matter/white matter volume on MRI, plasma and CSF neurofilament light chain levels, CSF alpha-synuclein oligomer levels
extraction_notes: Open-label trial design acknowledged by authors as limitation. Single-center study. Two control participants obtained exenatide outside trial protocol. Assessor not blinded to randomization.

title: Effects of Semaglutide With or Without Concomitant Mineralocorticoid Receptor Antagonist Use in Participants With Type 2 Diabetes and Chronic Kidney Disease: A FLOW Trial Prespecified Secondary Analysis.
population: Adults with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease (eGFR 25-75 mL/min/1.73 m2 with UACR >300 to <5,000 mg/g if eGFR ≥50 mL/min/1.73 m2, or UACR >100 to <5,000 mg/g if eGFR 25 to <50 mL/min/1.73 m2), receiving a stable maximal labeled or tolerated dose of a renin-angiotensin system inhibitor (or eligible if unable to tolerate or contraindicated)
intervention: Subcutaneous semaglutide 1.0 mg once weekly
comparison: Matching placebo once weekly
outcomes_primary: Five-component composite of time to first persistent ≥50% reduction in eGFR from baseline (sustained for at least 28 days), kidney failure (commencement of chronic dialysis, kidney transplant, or reduction in eGFR to <15 mL/min/1.73 m2 sustained for at least 28 days), or death from kidney or cardiovascular causes
outcomes_secondary: Rate of loss of kidney function (total eGFR slope - annual rate of change in eGFR based on serum creatinine); time to first major adverse cardiovascular event (MACE - composite of nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, or cardiovascular death); death from any cause; four-component kidney-specific composite outcome (excluding cardiovascular death from primary outcome); change in UACR; eGFR slope based on cystatin C
extraction_notes: This is a prespecified secondary analysis of the FLOW trial assessing efficacy and safety by baseline mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist (MRA) use. The primary outcomes are analyzed by MRA user subgroup (n=257) versus non-MRA user subgroup (n=3,276). Finerenone was not available until after recruitment ended; baseline MRA use was predominantly spironolactone.

title: The Effects of 8-Week Hydrogen-Rich Water Consumption on Appetite, Body Composition, Sleep Quality, and Circulating Glucagon-like Peptide-1 in Obese Men and Women (HYDRAPPET): A Randomized Controlled Trial.
population: Adults aged 18-65 years classified as obese (body fat >30% for women and >25% for men), sedentary (engaging in less than 150 min of moderate physical activity per week). Exclusion criteria: major chronic diseases or acute injuries, dietary supplement use within four weeks prior to study, use of obesity-related pharmaceuticals within eight weeks prior to study, refusal to consent to randomization, concurrent participation in other trials.
intervention: Hydrogen-rich water 1.0 L daily (containing 15 mg of H2 total; 5 mg per 333 mL serving) administered three times daily (morning, early afternoon, and before dinner) for eight weeks
comparison: Control water (tap water) 1.0 L daily (0 mg of H2) administered three times daily (morning, early afternoon, and before dinner) for eight weeks
outcomes_primary: Change in appetite (total cravings score) from baseline to 8-week follow-up, measured using the Food Cravings Questionnaire (FCQ)
outcomes_secondary: Body composition indices (fat mass, fat-free mass, muscle mass, body water, protein mass, mineral mass, total body calcium, glycogen mass) assessed by bioelectrical impedance; anthropometric measurements (weight, BMI, waist circumference); obesity-related quality of life assessed by Impact of Weight on Quality of Life-Lite (IWQOL-Lite) questionnaire; sleep quality assessed by Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI); biochemical markers including fasting glucose, total cholesterol, triglycerides, lipoprotein levels, serum short-chain fatty acids (acetic acid, propionic acid, butyric acid), plasma glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) levels, breath molecular hydrogen levels; prevalence and severity of side effects
extraction_notes: Primary endpoint explicitly stated as change in appetite (total cravings score). Sample size calculation was based on primary endpoint. Study registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06722326).

title: Germinated and Extruded Sorghum Beverage Presented Good Sensorial Acceptance and Improves Insulin and Satiety in Normoglycemic Adults: An Acute Randomized Controlled Crossover Trial.
journal: Journal of the American Nutrition Association
population: Normoglycemic adults
intervention: Germinated and extruded BRS305 whole sorghum beverage (strawberry-flavored)
comparison: Control beverage
outcomes_primary: Glycemic response, insulin response, glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) response
outcomes_secondary: Food intake/consumption, subjective appetite sensations, subjective satiety sensations, glycemic index of beverages
extraction_notes: Crossover design with acute (single-dose) consumption. Sensory analysis performed with 60 adults, but acute clinical trial conducted with 14 normoglycemic individuals. Dose, frequency, and duration of beverage consumption not specified in abstract.

title: Exenatide for diagnosing endogenous hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia: a randomized placebo-controlled, double-blind, cross-over proof-of-principle study.
population: Patients with confirmed endogenous hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia (EHH) diagnosed by 72 h fasting test, with matched controls
intervention: 10 μg intravenous exenatide
comparison: Placebo (double-blind, randomized cross-over in EHH patients); matched controls received 10 μg exenatide unblinded
outcomes_primary: Induction of diagnostic hypoglycemia
outcomes_secondary: Time to glucose nadir, glucose nadir levels, proinsulin levels at 120 min post-exenatide, time to hypoglycemia compared to fasting test, tolerability, patient preference
extraction_notes: This is a proof-of-principle study with small sample size (14 EHH patients, 14 controls). Primary vs secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract. Monitoring duration was 4 hours with measurements of glucose, insulin, C-peptide, and proinsulin.

title: Oral Semaglutide in an East Asian Population With Overweight or Obesity, With or Without Type 2 Diabetes: The OASIS 2 Randomized Clinical Trial.
population: East Asian adults (Japan and South Korea) with BMI ≥27.0 with 2 or more weight-related complications or BMI ≥35.0 with 1 or more weight-related complications; approximately 25% planned to have type 2 diabetes at screening
intervention: Once-daily oral semaglutide 50 mg plus lifestyle recommendations for 68 weeks
comparison: Placebo plus lifestyle recommendations for 68 weeks
outcomes_primary: Percentage change in body weight from baseline; proportion of participants achieving ≥5% body weight reduction

population: Adults aged 20-65 years with BMI >35 at 12-36 months after anatomically correct adjustable gastric band, sleeve gastrectomy, one anastomosis gastric bypass, or Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (confirmed with barium swallow and/or endoscopy) who achieved stable weight (within 4-kg range during 3-month period) with suboptimal weight loss defined as: excess body weight loss 25-40% or total body weight loss 5-12% for adjustable gastric band; excess body weight loss 25-60% or total body weight loss 10-20% for sleeve gastrectomy, Roux-en-Y gastric bypass, and one anastomosis gastric bypass; or regained 10% excess body weight loss or 5% total body weight loss after reaching nadir weight
intervention: Liraglutide 6 mg/mL in prefilled multidose disposable pens, self-administered daily subcutaneously, self-titrated from 0.6 mg in week 1 increasing by 0.6 mg/day per week until 3.0 mg reached by week 5, intended treatment duration 12 months
comparison: Placebo (saline) in prefilled multidose disposable pens, self-administered daily with same titration schedule
outcomes_primary: Percentage of weight loss achieved after enrollment at 12 months
outcomes_secondary: Safety measures (mortality, adverse effects grade 3 or higher, need for reoperation for complication of metabolic bariatric surgery procedure); health benefit measures (improvement in diabetes and hypertension); nutrition measures (iron, vitamins B12, B1, and D, calcium, albumin); function and well-being measures (36-Item Short-Form Medical Outcomes Study [SF-36], Beck Depression Index, Euro QOL 5-dimensions health utility survey, quality of swallowing, reflux, and satisfaction questionnaire); drug adherence
extraction_notes: Study was halted early due to nonavailability of study medication. COVID-19 pandemic caused significant delays and protocol modifications. Eligibility criteria expanded during trial from adjustable gastric band only to include sleeve gastrectomy, one anastomosis gastric bypass, and Roux-en-Y gastric bypass. No patients with RYGB or OAGB were ultimately enrolled.

title: Efficacy and safety of tirzepatide added to basal insulin in patients with type 2 diabetes in China (SURPASS-CN-INS): a double-blind, multicentre, randomised, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial.

comparison: Placebo by subcutaneous injection once weekly for 40 weeks
outcomes_primary: Change in HbA1c from baseline
extraction_notes: Secondary outcomes not explicitly stated in abstract. Primary outcome inferred from context mentioning HbA1c reductions as main efficacy measure. Stratification by HbA1c mentioned but text appears truncated. Findings section text appears truncated.

title: Semaglutide Use With Automated Insulin Delivery in Adults With Type 1 Diabetes: Qualitative Analyses and Patient-reported Outcomes From a Randomized Controlled Trial.
population: Adults with type 1 diabetes using automated insulin delivery
intervention: Semaglutide for 15 weeks
comparison: Placebo for 15 weeks (crossover design)
outcomes_secondary: Diabetes Distress Scale; Hypoglycemia Fear Survey; Diabetes Treatment Satisfaction Questionnaire; Insulin-delivery Systems: Perceptions, Ideas, Reflections and Expectations (INSPIRE); Diabetes Bowel Symptom Questionnaire (DBSQ); qualitative semistructured interviews assessing patient experience and themes
extraction_notes: Primary outcome not explicitly defined in abstract; study design is double-blind randomized crossover trial; outcomes focus on patient-reported outcomes and qualitative experience

title: Liraglutide in Acute Minor Ischemic Stroke or High-Risk Transient Ischemic Attack With Type 2 Diabetes: The LAMP Randomized Clinical Trial.
population: Patients aged 50 years or older with type 2 diabetes (known or newly diagnosed) who had minor acute ischemic stroke (National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score ≤3) or high-risk transient ischemic attack (ABCD2 score ≥4), within 24 hours of symptom onset, with modified Rankin Scale score 0-1 if previous stroke history. intervention: Liraglutide subcutaneous injection once daily for 90 days (0.6 mg daily for first week, increased to 1.2 mg daily in second week, then 1.8 mg daily from week 3 until day 90), in addition to standard therapy according to guidelines
comparison: Standard treatment alone according to guidelines (secondary prevention medications for acute ischemic stroke, blood pressure and blood glucose management per American Heart Association/American Stroke Association guidelines, China Secondary Prevention Guidelines, and China Diabetes Prevention Guidelines). Dipeptidyl peptidase-IV inhibitors and sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors prohibited in both groups.
outcomes_primary: Stroke recurrence (ischemic or hemorrhagic) at 90 days
outcomes_secondary: New clinical vascular events (ischemic stroke, hemorrhagic stroke, TIA, myocardial infarction, vascular death) at 90 days; excellent functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale score ≤1) at 90 days; favorable functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale score ≤2) at 90 days. Safety outcomes: symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage, hypoglycemia, gastrointestinal disorders, pneumonia, pancreatitis, and all-cause death within 90 days.
extraction_notes: Trial was terminated early before reaching target sample size of 1708 patients due to lower-than-expected enrollment and financial limitations; 636 patients were randomized. Open-label design with blinded endpoint assessment. Study conducted at 27 hospitals in China.

title: People With Lowest Physical Functioning Scores Showed Greatest Improvement After Tirzepatide Treatment.

intervention: Tirzepatide 5 mg, 10 mg, or 15 mg administered subcutaneously once weekly as adjunct to lifestyle counseling (500 kcal/day deficit diet and ≥150 min physical activity/week); SURMOUNT-1: 72 weeks treatment; SURMOUNT-3: maximum tolerated dose (10 or 15 mg) for 72 weeks following 12-week intensive lifestyle modification lead-in; SURMOUNT-4: maximum tolerated dose continued for 52 weeks following 36-week tirzepatide lead-in period
comparison: Placebo administered subcutaneously once weekly as adjunct to lifestyle counseling

outcomes_secondary: Change from baseline in waist circumference, change from baseline in BMI, change from baseline in IWQOL-Lite-CT Total score, change from baseline in IWQOL-Lite-CT Psychosocial composite score, change from baseline in SF-36v2 domain scores (General Health, Role-Physical, Bodily Pain, Vitality, Social Functioning, Role-Emotional, Mental Health), correlation between weight reduction and improvement in physical function
extraction_notes: This is a post hoc analysis pooling data from three phase 3 trials (SURMOUNT-1, SURMOUNT-3, SURMOUNT-4). Primary and secondary outcome distinction not explicitly stated; outcomes listed are based on the analysis focus. SURMOUNT-4 comparator group received tirzepatide during lead-in then placebo, so only tirzepatide continuation arm results were reported for that trial.

title: Improved health-related quality of life with tirzepatide versus semaglutide in adults with obesity or overweight from the SURMOUNT-5 trial.
population: Adults aged 18 years or older with obesity (BMI ≥30 kg/m2) or overweight (BMI ≥27 kg/m2 with at least one weight-related complication including hypertension, dyslipidaemia, obstructive sleep apnoea, or cardiovascular disease), experiencing at least one unsuccessful dietary effort for weight reduction, without diabetes diagnosis, no past or planned surgical treatment for obesity, no treatment with weight reduction medication or GLP-1 receptor agonist, and no change in body weight >5 kg within 3 months prior to screening
intervention: Once weekly subcutaneous tirzepatide at maximum tolerated dose (MTD, 10 mg or 15 mg) for 72 weeks, with dose escalation consistent with US Prescribing Information
comparison: Once weekly subcutaneous semaglutide at maximum tolerated dose (MTD, 1.7 mg or 2.4 mg) for 72 weeks, with dose escalation consistent with US Prescribing Information
outcomes_primary: Changes from baseline in Short Form-36 Health Survey Version 2 (SF-36v2) norm-based scores including Physical Component Summary (PCS) and Mental Component Summary (MCS), and individual domains (Physical Functioning, Role-Physical, Bodily Pain, General Health, Vitality, Social Functioning, Role-Emotional, Mental Health) at Week 72
outcomes_secondary: Categorical shift from baseline in Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) score at Week 72; categorical shift from baseline in Patient Global Impression of Status (PGI-S) for Physical Activity score at Week 72; post hoc analyses of SF-36v2 scores in participants with limited baseline physical function; post hoc analyses of SF-36v2 scores by body weight reduction thresholds
extraction_notes: This is an open-label trial. The analysis included on-treatment data from participants who received ≥1 dose of study drug at their maximum tolerated dose. Primary outcomes for the overall SURMOUNT-5 trial were body weight reduction and waist circumference; this publication reports health-related quality of life outcomes which were prespecified exploratory endpoints.

title: Tirzepatide and change in uric acid and its association with weight reduction: post hoc analyses of the SURMOUNT-1 randomised placebo-controlled trial.
population: Adults with obesity or overweight (body mass index ≥30 kg/m² or ≥27 kg/m² with weight-related comorbidities)
intervention: Tirzepatide (dual GLP-1RA/GIP agonist) at 5 mg, 10 mg, and 15 mg doses
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Change in serum uric acid (SUA) levels
outcomes_secondary: Association between weight reduction and SUA reduction; SUA changes by baseline uric acid quartiles; SUA changes by baseline BMI values
extraction_notes: This is a post hoc analysis of the SURMOUNT-1 trial. Route, frequency, and duration of tirzepatide administration not explicitly stated in abstract. Total sample size mentioned as 2539 adults. BMI criterion text appears truncated in abstract.

title: Adjunctive Semaglutide in Patients Undergoing Intragastric Balloon for Weight Loss: 12-Month Prospective Comparative Study.
population: Adults aged 18 to 65 years with body mass index (BMI) of 27 kg/m² or higher; exclusion criteria: history of previous bariatric surgery, contraindications to IGB insertion or semaglutide use, gastrointestinal disorders such as inflammatory bowel disease or gastroparesis, severe organ dysfunction (renal, hepatic, or cardiac), pregnancy, and current use of other anti-obesity medications

comparison: Intragastric balloon (IGB) insertion alone with standardized dietary protocol and lifestyle modification counseling
outcomes_primary: Percentage change in body weight from baseline to 12 months after intervention; weight and BMI measured at baseline and at 3, 6, and 12 months; Total Body Weight Loss (TBWL) percentage and Excess Weight Loss (EWL) percentage
outcomes_secondary: Safety outcomes including incidence and nature of treatment-related complications (nausea, vomiting, gastroparesis, pancreatitis, and other clinically relevant complications); serious complications defined as adverse events requiring discontinuation, hospitalization, or posing significant health risks; adherence to treatment protocol; patient-reported tolerance
extraction_notes: Open-label trial; randomization performed but neither participants nor investigators were blinded to group assignments; no semaglutide-only or placebo control group included

title: Semaglutide for the treatment of cognitive dysfunction in major depressive disorder: A randomized clinical trial.

intervention: Adjunctive oral semaglutide 14 mg for 16 weeks
comparison: Adjunctive placebo
outcomes_primary: Executive function composite score comprising the digit symbol substitution test, the Stroop test, and the n-back test
outcomes_secondary: Global cognition composite score, measures of functioning, depressive symptom severity, suicidality, body weight
extraction_notes: Dose frequency not explicitly stated; allocation ratio was 1:1

title: Roux-en-Y Gastric Bypass Improves Insulin Response and Secretion of GLP-1 and PYY in Response to Postprandial Acute Exercise.
population: Women with severe obesity (age 37 ± 7 years; BMI 47.6 ± 5.6 kg/m²)
intervention: Roux-en-Y gastric bypass surgery with postprandial acute exercise session (resistance training plus aerobic exercise)
comparison: Pre-surgery (same subjects before bariatric surgery)
extraction_notes: This is a single-arm pre-post study design without a separate control group. Primary and secondary outcomes were not explicitly designated in the abstract. Outcomes measured included glucose metabolism, insulin response, gut hormones (GLP-1, PYY), and inflammatory markers assessed at baseline, immediately after, and 30 minutes after exercise. Blood samples collected at multiple timepoints.

title: Effect of ketogenic diet plus dulaglutide on glucose and lipid metabolism in diabetes mellitus.
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (n=104)
intervention: Dulaglutide plus ketogenic diet
comparison: Dulaglutide alone
outcomes_secondary: Blood glucose levels, blood lipid levels, insulin resistance index, insulin sensitivity index, Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index score, quality of life
extraction_notes: Primary outcomes not explicitly distinguished from secondary outcomes in the abstract. Dose, route, frequency, and duration of dulaglutide not specified. Duration of ketogenic diet intervention not specified. Follow-up period mentioned as 6 months.

title: Tirzepatide in Adults With Type 1 Diabetes: A Phase 2 Randomized Placebo-Controlled Clinical Trial.
population: Adults aged 18-60 years with at least 2-year history of type 1 diabetes and BMI ≥30 kg/m2. Exclusions: GLP-1 receptor agonist, sodium-glucose cotransporter inhibitor, or glucocorticoid use in prior 6 weeks; diabetic ketoacidosis, severe hypoglycemia, coronary event, or stroke in preceding 3 months; gastroparesis, pancreatitis, cholecystitis, previous weight loss surgery, estimated glomerular filtration rate <45 mL/min/1.73 m2, significant liver disease (known cirrhosis or liver function tests greater than three times upper limit of normal); currently pregnant or breastfeeding; proliferative diabetic retinopathy or macular edema
intervention: Once-weekly subcutaneous tirzepatide, 2.5 mg for 4 weeks then 5.0 mg for 8 weeks (12 weeks total)
comparison: Identical-appearing, volume-matched placebo saline subcutaneous injection, same dosing schedule
outcomes_primary: Change in body weight at 12 weeks
outcomes_secondary: Change in body composition (fat mass and fat-free mass) by air displacement plethysmography; total body water by bioelectrical impedance; arterial stiffness by carotid femoral pulse wave velocity and augmentation index; HbA1c; fasting lipid profile; glucagon; GLP-1 and GIP (exploratory); resting energy expenditure and respiratory quotient by indirect calorimetry; continuous glucose monitoring metrics; insulin dosing; dietary intake; gastrointestinal symptoms (Patient Assessment of Upper Gastrointestinal Disorders Symptom Severity Index); eating behavior (Three-Factor Eating Questionnaire-R18); physical activity (International Physical Activity Questionnaire Short Form); treatment satisfaction
extraction_notes: Phase 2 trial; single-site study; sample size calculation based on 20 participants (10 per group) with 24 randomized anticipating 20% dropout; some secondary outcomes described as exploratory

title: Cardiometabolic Parameter Change by Weight Regain on Tirzepatide Withdrawal in Adults With Obesity: A Post Hoc Analysis of the SURMOUNT-4 Trial.
population: Adults with obesity (BMI ≥30) or overweight (BMI ≥27) with at least 1 weight-related complication, who achieved ≥10% weight reduction after 36 weeks of tirzepatide treatment at maximum tolerated dose (10 mg or 15 mg), without diabetes, without prior or planned surgical treatment for obesity, and without treatment with weight-reducing medication within 3 months prior to enrollment
intervention: Withdrawal of tirzepatide (switch to placebo) for 52 weeks after initial 36-week open-label tirzepatide treatment, as adjunct to reduced calorie diet (500 kcal/day deficit) and increased physical activity (≥150 minutes/week)
comparison: Categories of weight regain at week 88 as percentage of weight lost during tirzepatide treatment: <25%, 25% to <50%, 50% to <75%, and ≥75% weight regain
outcomes_primary: Changes from week 36 to week 88 in cardiometabolic parameters by degree of weight regain, including waist circumference, systolic blood pressure, diastolic blood pressure, triglycerides, non-HDL cholesterol, HDL cholesterol, hemoglobin A1c, fasting serum glucose, fasting insulin, HOMA2-IR, and HOMA2-B
outcomes_secondary: Changes from week 0 to week 36 and changes over week 0 to week 88 in weight, BMI, and cardiometabolic parameters by categories of weight regain
extraction_notes: This is a post hoc analysis of the SURMOUNT-4 trial. The analysis focused only on participants randomized to placebo (tirzepatide withdrawal) who achieved ≥10% weight reduction at week 36. Primary and secondary outcomes are not explicitly designated; outcomes listed are those assessed in the analysis.

title: Effects of liraglutide treatment for 18 days on metabolic parameters, regional body composition and the myostatin-activin-follistatin-IGF-1 axis: Results from an exploratory, randomized, placebo-controlled, crossover study.
population: Adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus
intervention: Liraglutide up to 1.8 mg/day for 18 days
comparison: Placebo for 18 days
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract. Outcomes assessed included: total body mass, regional body composition (fat, lean, and bone compartments measured by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry including android fat, trunk fat mass), circulating C-peptide, and myostatin-activin-follistatin-IGF-1 (MAFI) axis components measured by ELISA. This was a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, crossover trial with washout period. Sample size was 20 adults.

title: Effects of semaglutide in obesity-related heart failure with preserved ejection fraction across the age spectrum: Findings from the STEP-HFpEF programme.
population: Adults with symptomatic heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF, left ventricular ejection fraction ≥45%) and obesity (body mass index ≥30 kg/m²) with objective evidence of HFpEF based on elevated filling pressures or elevated natriuretic peptide levels and echocardiographic abnormalities, or heart failure hospitalization in the previous 12 months. STEP-HFpEF DM included only patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus.
intervention: Semaglutide 2.4 mg subcutaneous once weekly for 52 weeks in addition to standard care
comparison: Matching placebo once weekly for 52 weeks in addition to standard care
outcomes_primary: Dual primary endpoints: (1) Change in Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire clinical summary score (KCCQ-CSS) from baseline to 52 weeks; (2) Percentage change in body weight from baseline to 52 weeks
outcomes_secondary: Confirmatory secondary endpoints: Change in 6-minute walk distance (6MWD); Change in C-reactive protein (CRP); Hierarchical composite endpoint comprising all-cause death (baseline to 57 weeks), heart failure events (hospitalizations or urgent visits requiring intravenous therapy), changes in KCCQ-CSS and 6MWD. Exploratory endpoint: Change in N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) from baseline to week 52. Safety endpoints: Serious adverse events (SAEs), SAEs leading to permanent treatment discontinuation, cardiac and gastrointestinal SAEs, atrial fibrillation events, bone/joint injuries.
extraction_notes: This is a pre-specified pooled subanalysis of STEP-HFpEF and STEP-HFpEF DM trials stratified by age (<55, 55-64, 65-74, ≥75 years). Heart failure events were an exploratory endpoint in individual trials but included in hierarchical composite secondary endpoint in pooled analysis.

title: Association of baseline characteristics with clinical outcomes of tirzepatide treatment in Japanese patients with obesity disease: A subgroup analysis of the SURMOUNT-J trial.
population: Japanese adults aged ≥20 years without type 2 diabetes meeting Japanese Society for the Study of Obesity criteria for obesity disease requiring pharmacological treatment: BMI ≥27 kg/m2 and <35 kg/m2 plus two or more obesity-related health disorders, or BMI ≥35 kg/m2 plus one or more obesity-related health disorders. Key exclusions: diabetes, treatment with DPP-4 inhibitors, oral GLP-1 receptor agonists, or any injectable T2D therapy within 3 months prior to screening, and liver disease other than MASLD.
intervention: Once-weekly subcutaneous tirzepatide 10 mg or tirzepatide 15 mg, escalated by 2.5 mg from initial dose of 2.5 mg every 4 weeks until assigned maintenance dose reached, as adjunct to lifestyle modifications, for 72 weeks
comparison: Once-weekly subcutaneous placebo as adjunct to lifestyle modifications for 72 weeks
outcomes_primary: Percentage change from baseline body weight to week 72; proportion of participants achieving at least 5% body weight reduction at week 72
outcomes_secondary: Change from baseline in blood pressure, lipids, and fasting serum glucose at week 72; proportion of participants experiencing treatment-emergent adverse events, treatment-related adverse events, serious adverse events, and discontinuation due to adverse events
extraction_notes: This is a prespecified subgroup analysis of the SURMOUNT-J trial examining efficacy and safety by baseline characteristics (sex, age <65 vs ≥65 years, BMI <35 vs ≥35 kg/m2). The cardiometabolic parameter analyses by subgroup were conducted post hoc.

title: The Effect of Increased Sodium Intake with a Carbohydrate-Rich Meal on Glucose Homeostasis in People without Diabetes after Roux-en-Y Gastric Bypass: a Proof-of-Concept, Randomized, Open-Label, Crossover Study.
population: Adults who had Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (RYGB) surgery at least 12 months prior to study participation, without established diagnosis of post-bariatric hypoglycemia (PBH), not on treatment with medications that can affect glucose homeostasis (e.g. glucose-lowering agents, systemic steroids), without current diagnosis of diabetes, and without previous revisional metabolic and bariatric surgery
intervention: Mixed meal tolerance test (MMTT) consisting of 170 mL smooth orange juice with 2 g of sodium chloride (NaCl, 785 mg sodium) dissolved, followed by a yoghurt snack pot (total: 245 kcal, 40 g carbohydrates, 7.5 g protein, 5.5 g fat, 108 mg sodium), consumed within ten minutes, administered orally on a single occasion
comparison: Mixed meal tolerance test (MMTT) consisting of 170 mL smooth orange juice without additional NaCl, followed by a yoghurt snack pot (total: 245 kcal, 40 g carbohydrates, 7.5 g protein, 5.5 g fat, 108 mg sodium), consumed within ten minutes, administered orally on a single occasion
outcomes_primary: Difference in nadir (lowest) postprandial plasma glucose between conditions
outcomes_secondary: Differences in fasting, area under the curve (AUC 0-180 minutes), and peak levels of glucose, insulin, c-peptide, and glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1); Edinburgh Hypoglycemia Symptom Scale (EHSS) scores; Sigstad dumping syndrome symptom questionnaire scores
extraction_notes: Open-label randomized crossover design with minimum 7-day washout period. Sample size was 11 participants included in analysis (12 recruited, 1 excluded due to cannulation issues). Blood samples collected at fasting and 15, 30, 60, 90, 120, 150, and 180 minutes post-MMTT.

title: Effects of CT-388, a once-weekly signaling-biased dual GLP-1/GIP receptor agonist, on weight loss and glycemic control in preclinical models and participants with obesity.
population: Adults aged 18-65 years with overweight (BMI ≥25 kg/m2) or obesity (BMI ≥30 kg/m2), otherwise healthy, without current diagnosis of diabetes; prediabetes allowed if controlled with diet and exercise alone
intervention: CT-388, a cAMP signal-biased dual GLP-1/GIP receptor agonist, administered subcutaneously. Single ascending dose (SAD): single doses of 0.5, 2.0, 5.0, 6.0, or 7.5 mg. Multiple ascending dose (MAD): 4 once-weekly doses with titration schemes - Cohort 6: 5/5/5/7.5 mg; Cohort 7: 5/5/8/12 mg; Cohort 8: 5/8/12/12 mg
comparison: Placebo (volume-matched)
outcomes_primary: Safety and tolerability including treatment-emergent adverse events, serious adverse events, TEAEs leading to discontinuation, safety laboratory parameters, vital signs, and ECG parameters
outcomes_secondary: Pharmacokinetics (AUC, Cmax, t1/2, tmax); pharmacodynamics including change from baseline in body weight, hip and waist circumference, glycated hemoglobin, fasting glucose, fasting insulin, HOMA-IR, appetite and satiety by visual analog scale, glucose and insulin responses during oral glucose tolerance test
extraction_notes: Phase 1, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled study (NCT04838405). SAD portion conducted in Australia, MAD portion conducted in Mexico. Paper also includes extensive preclinical data in mice and cynomolgus monkeys which were not extracted as clinical PICO was prioritized.

title: Liraglutide in mild to moderate Alzheimer's disease: a phase 2b clinical trial.
population: Adults aged 50 years or older with clinical diagnosis of mild to moderate Alzheimer's disease syndrome based on NINCDS-ADRDA criteria, MMSE score of 15 or higher, CDR Global score of 0.5, 1, or 2, without diabetes mellitus
intervention: Liraglutide, daily subcutaneous injection, starting dose 0.6 mg once daily escalated to 1.8 mg within 4 weeks (participants unable to tolerate 1.8 mg remained on 1.2 mg), for 52 weeks
comparison: Placebo, daily subcutaneous injection, for 52 weeks
outcomes_primary: Change in cerebral glucose metabolic rate (rCMRglc) in cortical regions (combination of hippocampal, medial temporal lobe, and posterior cingulate) from baseline to 52 weeks, measured by fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography ([18F] FDG PET)
outcomes_secondary: Safety and tolerability (incidence and severity of treatment-emergent adverse events and clinically important changes in safety assessments); change in ADAS-Exec z-score (combination of ADAS-Cog and Executive domain scores from Neuropsychological Test Battery); change in CDR-SoB score; change in ADCS-ADL score; MRI changes in volume of ventricles and composite region (hippocampus and entorhinal cortex)
extraction_notes: Exploratory outcomes included MRI volumes of temporal lobe, total gray matter, parietal lobe, frontoparietal lobe, and voxel-based morphometry analyses. Optional outcomes (TSPO PET, tau PET, amyloid load, APOE4 status) were not completed. Genotyping and plasma markers not yet analyzed.

title: CagriSema Reduces Blood Pressure in Adults With Overweight or Obesity: REDEFINE 1.
population: Adults without diabetes with body mass index ≥30 kg/m2, or ≥27 kg/m2 with ≥1 obesity-related complication
intervention: CagriSema (fixed-dose combination of semaglutide 2.4 mg/cagrilintide 2.4 mg) administered once weekly subcutaneously for 68 weeks, plus lifestyle intervention
comparison: Semaglutide 2.4 mg once weekly, cagrilintide 2.4 mg once weekly, or placebo, all plus lifestyle intervention
outcomes_primary: Change in systolic blood pressure from baseline to week 68 for CagriSema versus placebo (secondary confirmatory efficacy end point)
outcomes_secondary: Change in diastolic blood pressure from baseline to week 68 for CagriSema versus placebo; change in number of participants taking antihypertensive medication (increase, no change, decrease, or stop) from baseline to week 68; proportion of participants achieving ACC/AHA blood pressure targets (<130/80 mm Hg)
extraction_notes: This is a secondary and post hoc analysis of the REDEFINE 1 trial. The primary outcome of the original trial was body weight reduction, not blood pressure. Change in SBP and DBP were secondary endpoints in the original trial. Randomization ratio was 21:3:3:7 (CagriSema:semaglutide:cagrilintide:placebo). Route of administration not explicitly stated in abstract but implied subcutaneous based on drug class.

title: Semaglutide and Early-Stage Metabolic Abnormalities in Individuals With Schizophrenia Spectrum Disorders: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
population: Adults aged 18-65 years with schizophrenia spectrum disorders who initiated clozapine or olanzapine within the past 5 years, with early-stage glycemic dysregulation (hemoglobin A1c 5.4%-7.4%), not receiving antidiabetic therapy
intervention: Once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide 1 mg adjunctive to second-generation antipsychotic therapy for 26 weeks
comparison: Matching placebo once-weekly subcutaneous injection adjunctive to second-generation antipsychotic therapy for 26 weeks
outcomes_primary: Change in hemoglobin A1c level from baseline to week 26
outcomes_secondary: Body weight change, waist circumference change, fat mass change, proportion achieving low-risk HbA1c levels (<5.4%), lipid levels, liver function, blood pressure, psychiatric symptoms

title: Impact of Oral Semaglutide on Kidney Outcomes in People With Type 2 Diabetes: Results From the SOUL Randomized Trial.
population: Adults with type 2 diabetes and atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) and/or chronic kidney disease (CKD), defined as eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73 m2 with no lower limit; participants receiving kidney replacement therapy (dialysis or kidney transplant) at screening were excluded

comparison: Matching placebo once daily in addition to standard of care
outcomes_primary: Five-point composite kidney outcome: persistent ≥50% reduction in eGFR from baseline, persistent eGFR <15 mL/min/1.73 m2, initiation of long-term kidney replacement therapy (dialysis or kidney transplant), or death from kidney-related or cardiovascular causes
outcomes_secondary: Four-point kidney-specific composite outcome (five-point composite excluding cardiovascular death); annual rate of change in eGFR (total eGFR slope) from baseline to end of treatment using CKD-EPI equation; individual components of composite outcomes; serious adverse events including serious kidney adverse events and acute kidney injury
extraction_notes: The five-point composite kidney outcome was a prespecified secondary endpoint in the trial hierarchy. Trial was not powered for kidney outcomes. Urinary albumin was not measured. The primary endpoint of the SOUL trial was cardiovascular (major adverse cardiovascular events), not kidney outcomes.

title: Combination metformin and liraglutide in PCOS: clinical efficacy in women and preclinical insights from gut microbiome modulation in rats.
population: Overweight or obese women with PCOS (BMI ≥24 kg/m² for Chinese population), aged >18 years, premenopausal, diagnosed by Rotterdam criteria (hyperandrogenemia, menstrual abnormalities, polycystic ovarian morphology). Excluded: cardiovascular, kidney, hepatic, pituitary, or thyroid disease; use of antiandrogen agents, diabetic drugs, glucocorticoids, or other steroid agents within 90 days before study.
intervention: Metformin 0.85g orally twice daily combined with liraglutide 1.2mg subcutaneously once daily (starting at 0.6mg once daily for first week, then increased to 1.2mg) for 12 weeks

outcomes_primary: Absolute changes from baseline to week 12 in body weight, hormonal parameters, lipid profiles, and measures of glucose metabolism
outcomes_secondary: Safety and tolerability monitoring; proportion achieving clinically significant (≥5%) weight reduction; changes in BMI, waist-hip ratio, visceral fat area, body fat percentage; changes in fasting blood glucose, fasting insulin, OGTT values, HbA1c, HOMA-IR; changes in free testosterone, total testosterone, SHBG, LH, FSH, LH/FSH ratio, FAI; proportion with insulin resistance (HOMA-IR ≥2.69); proportion with hyperandrogenemia (FAI ≥6.4); adverse events
extraction_notes: This study includes both a clinical trial in women and a parallel animal experiment in rats. PICO extraction focused on the clinical trial component only. The study was open-label with assessor blinding for data collection and analysis.

title: Long-acting GIPR agonist LY3537021 reduces body weight and fasting blood glucose in patients with T2D: Preclinical development and phase 1 randomized ascending dose studies.
population: Healthy participants and patients with type 2 diabetes (T2D), aged 21-70 years, BMI 18.5-40 kg/m². Healthy participants had HbA1c ≤6.5%. Patients with T2D had HbA1c 6.5%-11.0% (SAD) or 6.5%-10.0% (MAD), treated with diet and exercise alone or stable dose of metformin for at least 3 months.
