title: The Impact of a Fat-Dominant Preload Before a Carbohydrate-Rich Meal on Glucose Homeostasis in Patients Without Diabetes After Sleeve Gastrectomy: A Proof-of-Concept, Randomised, Open-Label, Crossover Study.
population: Adults aged 18-65 years without diabetes who had undergone sleeve gastrectomy more than one year prior; excluded if established diagnosis of postprandial hyperinsulinaemic hypoglycaemia, on treatment with medications affecting glucose homeostasis, history of bariatric procedure other than sleeve gastrectomy, or presence of diabetes
intervention: Fat-dominant preload consisting of 28 g Brazil nuts (201 kcal, 19.5 g fat, 0.8 g carbohydrate, 4.8 g protein) with 80 mL water consumed over 10 minutes, 30 minutes before a standardised mixed-meal tolerance test (220 mL Nutricia Fortisip Milkshake containing 330 kcal, 12.8 g fat, 40.5 g carbohydrates, 13.2 g protein)
comparison: 100 mL water alone consumed 30 minutes before the standardised mixed-meal tolerance test
outcomes_primary: Difference in nadir plasma glucose concentration after the standardised mixed-meal tolerance test
outcomes_secondary: Fasting and pre-MMTT levels of glucose, insulin, GLP-1, c-peptide, and paracetamol; overall (0-180 min) and early (0-30 min) post-MMTT incremental area under the curve (iAUC) for glucose, insulin, GLP-1, c-peptide, and paracetamol; peak concentrations of glucose, insulin, c-peptide, and GLP-1; hypoglycaemia symptoms assessed by Edinburgh Hypoglycaemia Scale; dumping symptoms assessed by Sigstad dumping score
extraction_notes: Small sample size (n=10); proof-of-concept study; paracetamol gastric emptying data could not be used due to laboratory reporting limitations; glucagon and GIP not measured; crossover design with 7-day washout period

title: Improved quality of life with semaglutide in schizophrenia: Secondary analyses from a randomized controlled trial.
population: Adults with schizophrenia spectrum disorder, prediabetes, and overweight or obesity
intervention: Semaglutide, once-weekly, for 30 weeks
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: SF-36v2 Physical Component Summary score (PCS); SF-36v2 Mental Component Summary score (MCS); Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale, 6-item version (PANSS-6)
outcomes_secondary: Causal mediation effects of weight loss on outcomes at weeks 15 and 30
extraction_notes: This is a secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial. Semaglutide dose not specified. Primary vs secondary outcome distinction not explicitly stated in abstract; all outcomes listed under primary based on methods description.

title: Effect of lixisenatide on arterial stiffness in people with type 2 diabetes and kidney disease: Results of a randomised controlled trial.
population: Adults aged over 35 years with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease (CKD), with eGFR more than 30 mL/min, on maximum tolerated and stable dose of ACE-inhibitor or angiotensin receptor blocker for at least 3 months. Exclusions: CVD event within past 12 months, non-diabetic renal disease, recent or current GLP-1 RA use, connective tissue disease or inflammatory arthritis, uncontrolled hypertension (SBP >180 or DBP >100 mmHg), pregnancy, lactation, history of pancreatitis, active GI or biliary disease, planned major GI surgery, history or family history of thyroid cancer or MEN-2, known allergy to GLP-1 RA or study components
intervention: Lixisenatide 10 mcg subcutaneous once daily increased to 20 mcg after 2 weeks, for 24 weeks, added to existing standard medical therapy
comparison: Matching placebo for 24 weeks, added to existing standard medical therapy
outcomes_primary: Change in aortic pulse wave velocity (Ao-PWV) from baseline to week 24
outcomes_secondary: Change in albuminuria, central aortic blood pressure, serum sKlotho levels, HbA1c, serum electrolytes (sodium, potassium), lipids (cholesterol, HDL, LDL, triglycerides), haematocrit, haemoglobin, central systolic blood pressure, central diastolic blood pressure, seated brachial blood pressure, weight, eGFR, augmentation index (AIx)
extraction_notes: Single-center proof-of-concept trial. Trial suspended during COVID-19 pandemic; originally planned for 120 participants but achieved 101 randomized with 90 eligible for final mITT analysis. SGLT-2 inhibitors were permitted but not standard of care at time of study design.

title: Efficacy and safety of bofanglutide, a GLP-1 receptor agonist, in Chinese adults with overweight or obesity: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 2b trial.
population: Chinese adults aged 18-75 years with overweight (BMI ≥24, <28 kg/m²) and at least one weight-related comorbidity (prediabetes, hypertension, dyslipidemia, fatty liver, weight-bearing joint pain, obesity-related dyspnea, or obstructive sleep apnea syndrome), or obesity (BMI ≥28 kg/m²)
intervention: Bofanglutide (GLP-1 receptor agonist) administered subcutaneously at five dose regimens: 12 mg biweekly (Q2W), 18 mg Q2W, 24 mg Q2W, 48 mg Q2W, or 24 mg once weekly (QW); dose escalation period of 10-18 weeks followed by dose maintenance period of 12-20 weeks at target doses; total treatment duration 30 weeks
comparison: Matching placebo with same injection volume and schedule within each dose group (4:1 randomization ratio for most groups, 5:1 for 48 mg Q2W group)
outcomes_primary: Percentage change in body weight from baseline to week 30
outcomes_secondary: Proportion of participants achieving body weight loss of ≥5%, ≥10%, ≥15%, and ≥20% at week 30; change from baseline to week 30 in body weight, waist circumference, BMI; changes in glucose metabolism parameters (HbA1c, fasting plasma glucose, fasting insulin, HOMA-IR); changes in cardiovascular risk factors (blood pressure, lipid profiles including total cholesterol, LDL cholesterol, HDL cholesterol, triglycerides); exploratory endpoints included changes in serum uric acid, ALT, AST, and quality of life measures (IWQOL-Lite-CT, SF-36); safety endpoints included incidence of TEAEs, SAEs, AESIs (hypoglycemic episodes, gastrointestinal AEs); pharmacokinetic endpoints; immunogenicity endpoints
extraction_notes: Phase 2b trial; lifestyle intervention provided to all participants as background therapy (dietary counseling targeting ~500 kcal/day deficit and 150-220 min/week moderate-intensity exercise)

title: Efficacy and safety of once-daily oral orforglipron compared with oral semaglutide in adults with type 2 diabetes (ACHIEVE-3): a multinational, multicentre, non-inferiority, open-label, randomised, phase 3 trial.
population: Adults aged 18 years or older with type 2 diabetes inadequately controlled with metformin (at least 1500 mg per day)
intervention: Once-daily oral orforglipron 12 mg or 36 mg
comparison: Oral semaglutide 7 mg or 14 mg
outcomes_primary: Mean change in HbA1c from baseline at week 52
extraction_notes: HbA1c baseline eligibility criteria appear truncated in abstract. Secondary outcomes not explicitly listed. Open-label design noted.

title: Heterogeneous effect of saxagliptin on glucose fluctuation and β-cell function in T1DM: a multicentre, randomised trial.
population: T1DM patients aged 12 to 65 years with HbA1c level of 6.5-10.0% and positivity for at least one islet autoantibody (IA2A, GADA, or ZnT8A), treated with either multiple daily injections (MDI) or continuous subcutaneous insulin infusion (CSII)
intervention: Saxagliptin 5 mg orally every morning plus insulin therapy for 24 weeks
comparison: Insulin therapy only for 24 weeks
outcomes_primary: Change from baseline in mean amplitude of glycaemic excursions (MAGE) at week 24, measured by continuous glucose monitoring system (CGMS)
outcomes_secondary: Change from baseline in islet function during 3-hour steamed bread meal tolerance test (BMTT) including fasting C-peptide, C-peptidemax, AUCC-peptide; change in HbA1c levels; change in insulin dosage. Exploratory outcome: influence of SNPs in incretin-related genes (GCG, GLP1R, DPP4, PCSK1, GIP, GIP1R) on saxagliptin treatment outcomes
extraction_notes: Open-label study design. Six centres in China. 184 patients randomized 1:1. Adolescent patients (12.5%) included in population.

title: Bimagrumab plus semaglutide alone or in combination for the treatment of obesity: a randomized phase 2 trial.
population: Adults aged 18-80 years with obesity (BMI ≥30 kg/m² or BMI ≥27 kg/m² with at least one obesity-associated comorbidity such as hypertension, insulin resistance, sleep apnea, or dyslipidemia, excluding diabetes); stable body weight (±5 kg) within 90 days of screening; body weight less than 150 kg; history of at least one unsuccessful behavioral effort to lose weight; excluded if diagnosis of diabetes requiring antidiabetic drug or HbA1c ≥6.5%
intervention: Bimagrumab (10 mg/kg or 30 mg/kg intravenously every 12 weeks with additional loading doses at randomization and week 4) alone or in combination with semaglutide (1.0 mg or 2.4 mg subcutaneously once weekly) for 48 weeks primary treatment period with 24-week open-label extension to week 72
comparison: Placebo (for bimagrumab); nine treatment groups in 1:1:1:1:1:1:1:1:1 ratio: placebo, bimagrumab 10 mg/kg, bimagrumab 30 mg/kg, semaglutide 1.0 mg, semaglutide 2.4 mg, bimagrumab 10 mg/kg plus semaglutide 1.0 mg, bimagrumab 10 mg/kg plus semaglutide 2.4 mg, bimagrumab 30 mg/kg plus semaglutide 1.0 mg, bimagrumab 30 mg/kg plus semaglutide 2.4 mg
outcomes_primary: Absolute change from baseline in body weight at week 48
outcomes_secondary: Absolute change from baseline in body weight at week 72; total body fat mass (by DXA); total body lean mass (by DXA); visceral adipose tissue (by DXA); appendicular lean mass (by DXA); HbA1c; waist circumference; SF-36 Physical Functioning score; IWQOL-Lite-CT Physical Function score; systolic blood pressure; diastolic blood pressure; pulse rate; safety and tolerability (adverse events, serious adverse events); exploratory endpoints including bone mineral density, lipid parameters (total cholesterol, HDL, LDL, triglycerides), fasting insulin, free testosterone, grip strength, hsCRP, leptin, adiponectin, dietary intake
extraction_notes: Open-label semaglutide used due to unavailability of matched placebo at trial initiation; randomization stratified by sex; trial also includes 32-week treatment-withdrawal follow-up period (not reported in this publication)

title: Acute interleukin-1β antagonism decreases systemic inflammation, increases GLP-1 release, and modulates insulin secretion in individuals with prediabetes.
journal: American journal of physiology. Endocrinology and metabolism
population: Adult patients with prediabetes (defined as HbA1c 5.7-6.4% or fasting plasma glucose level of 6.1-6.9 mmol/l), BMI ≥28 kg/m², and high sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP) ≥2 mg/l; otherwise healthy; excluded if history of upper gastrointestinal surgery or type 2 diabetes diagnosis
intervention: Anakinra (Kineret®; recombinant IL-1 receptor antagonist) 100 mg/0.67 ml solution, two subcutaneous injections administered approximately 12 hours apart (one on the evening before and one on the morning of the study day, one hour before mixed meal tolerance test)
comparison: Placebo (0.9% saline) administered as two subcutaneous injections in identical manner
outcomes_primary: Difference in insulin secretion following standardized mixed-meal test, including changes in insulin, glucose, and c-peptide concentration and area under curve (AUC), and changes in insulinogenic index ((I30 - I0)/(G30 - G0))
outcomes_secondary: Effects during mixed meal tolerance test on peak and nadir values and slopes of glucose, insulin, GLP-1, glucagon; effects on insulin resistance; exploratory outcomes included changes in inflammatory cytokines (IL-1β, IL-1Ra, IL-6, IL-18, IFN-γ) in serum at baseline and 60 minutes after mixed meal ingestion
extraction_notes: Monocentric, placebo-controlled, double-blinded, randomized, crossover proof-of-concept study conducted in Basel, Switzerland. Minimum 7-day washout period between crossover phases.

title: Semaglutide Effects on Insulin Sensitivity and β-Cell Function in Patients With Schizophrenia, Prediabetes, and Obesity Treated With Second-Generation Antipsychotics: Findings From the HISTORI Trial, a 30-Week Randomized, Placebo-Controlled Trial With Semaglutide 1.0 mg Weekly.
population: Adults aged 18-60 years with schizophrenia, schizotypal disorder, or schizoaffective disorder (ICD-10 codes F20.x, F21.x, F25.x) receiving stable second-generation antipsychotic treatment, with prediabetes (HbA1c 39-47 mmol/mol) and overweight/obesity (BMI ≥27 kg/m2)
intervention: Semaglutide 1.34 mg/mL subcutaneous injection, uptitrated to 1.0 mg weekly, for 30 weeks
comparison: Matching placebo injection weekly for 30 weeks
outcomes_primary: Change in HbA1c
outcomes_secondary: Changes in fasting glucose, fasting insulin, fasting C-peptide, HOMA2 of β-cell function (HOMA2-B), HOMA2 of insulin sensitivity (HOMA2-S), HOMA of insulin resistance (HOMA-IR), body weight, BMI, waist circumference, triglycerides, cholesterol (HDL and LDL), blood pressure, cardiovascular autonomic neuropathy, schizophrenia symptom severity, quality of life, physical activity levels, adherence to antipsychotic treatment
extraction_notes: The abstract states this reports prespecified secondary endpoints; the primary endpoint (HbA1c change) was reported in a prior publication. The trial used semaglutide 1.0 mg weekly rather than higher doses (2.4 mg) as the study was initiated before Wegovy approval.

title: A single dose of cannabidiol increases ad libitum energy intake in healthy adults but does not affect postprandial glucose or lipid metabolism.
population: Healthy adults
intervention: 298 mg cannabidiol (CBD), single oral dose
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Ad libitum energy intake at lunch (180 min post-CBD ingestion)
outcomes_secondary: Subjective appetite ratings (recorded hourly); postprandial glucose metabolism; postprandial lipid metabolism; blood-based energy substrates and hormones; indirect calorimetry measures
extraction_notes: Small sample size (n=15, four females). Abstract appears truncated. Primary vs secondary outcome distinction not explicitly stated in abstract - categorized based on emphasis in text.

title: Effect of Prebiotic Supplementation With and Without Physiotherapy on Pain and Pain Sensitivity in People with Knee Osteoarthritis.
population: Community-dwelling adults with knee osteoarthritis; excluded individuals with fibromyalgia or IBS
intervention: Inulin 20 g/day orally for 6 weeks; Digital physiotherapy-supported exercise (PSE) via Joint Academy platform for 6 weeks with daily engagement; Combined inulin 20 g/day plus digital PSE for 6 weeks
comparison: Maltodextrin 10 g/day orally for 6 weeks plus usual care (placebo control)
outcomes_primary: Pain measured by Numerical Rating Scale (NRS) 0-10 at baseline and 6 weeks
outcomes_secondary: 30-second sit-to-stand test (30-CST); Timed up and go (TUG) test; Grip strength measured by hand dynamometer; Quantitative sensory testing including pressure pain detection threshold (PPT) at five anatomical sites and temporal summation (TS); Serum short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) including acetate, propionate, and butyrate; Serum glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1)
extraction_notes: GLP-1 measurement was exploratory and not prespecified in the original protocol. KOOS was collected as exploratory patient-reported outcome and not a prespecified primary or secondary outcome. Study was not powered to detect synergistic interaction between interventions. Lower maltodextrin dose (10g vs 20g inulin) selected for ethical reasons related to potential postprandial glycaemic effects.

title: Changes of gut microbiota, hormone and glycolipid metabolism by dietary fiber (oat bran) supplementation in patients with laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy and Roux-en-Y gastric bypass: A randomized controlled study.
population: Post-bariatric surgery patients who underwent laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy or Roux-en-Y gastric bypass
intervention: Standard care plus 30 g/d oat bran (providing 9.0 g dietary fiber) for 12 weeks
comparison: Standard care alone (control)
outcomes_secondary: Gut microbiota composition, glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) levels, peptide-YY (PYY) levels, glycolipid parameters, percentage of excess weight loss (EWL%)
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract; all outcomes listed under secondary. Trial duration was 12 weeks. Sample size was 63 patients randomized.

title: ARD-101, a gut-restricted TAS2R agonist, reduces hunger in adults and promotes weight loss in DIO mice with DPP-4 inhibition.
population: Adults with obesity (BMI between 30 and 45 kg/m2); healthy adult participants
intervention: ARD-101 (oral denatonium acetate) 200 mg twice daily for 28 days (adults with obesity); ARD-101 800 mg single dose (healthy participants)
comparison: Matching placebo (containing same inactive excipients as ARD-101 but lacking denatonium acetate)
outcomes_primary: Body weight change; Control of Eating Questionnaire (CoEQ) scores including hunger ratings and food cravings
outcomes_secondary: Metabolic parameters (lipid parameters including cholesterol, LDL cholesterol, HDL cholesterol, non-HDL cholesterol, triglycerides; HbA1c); gut hormone levels (GLP-1 total, PYY, CCK, ghrelin total); adverse events and tolerability
extraction_notes: Multiple studies reported in single publication: Phase 2 proof-of-concept study in adults with obesity (NCT05121441) and exploratory clinical pharmacology study in healthy adults (IRAS 1011885). Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly designated as such in the abstract or methods; classification based on stated study objectives. Preclinical mouse studies also reported but excluded from PICO extraction per clinical focus.

title: Holding vs Continuing GLP-1/GIP Agonists Before Upper Endoscopy: The OCULUS Randomized Clinical Trial.
population: Adults aged 18 years or older scheduled for elective upper endoscopy (EGD, EUS, or ERCP) with or without colonoscopy, under moderate sedation or monitored anesthesia care, taking a stable dose of a GLP-1 or GLP-1/GIP agonist for at least 1 month. Exclusion criteria: prior foregut surgery, achalasia, documented gastroparesis based on 4-hour solid phase gastric emptying study, residual gastric volume on previous endoscopy, gastric outlet obstruction, planned general anesthesia, or chronic opioid use.
intervention: Continue GLP-1 or GLP-1/GIP agonist medication at the same dosage and scheduled times prior to the procedure
comparison: Hold 1 dose of GLP-1 or GLP-1/GIP agonist medication (medication-free period of 7-13 days before procedure for weekly medications or at least 1 day for daily medications)
outcomes_primary: Clinically significant residual gastric volume (RGV), defined as a composite of gastric contents that (1) precludes endoscopic examination, (2) requires premature termination or endotracheal intubation, and/or (3) results in an aspiration event that necessitates extended observation or monitoring, unplanned therapeutics, or hospital admission
outcomes_secondary: Increased RGV, defined as any amount of solid content or more than 0.8 mL/kg of fluid content
extraction_notes: Study was designed as a noninferiority trial but was terminated early at the 50% interim analysis when results exceeded the prespecified O'Brien-Fleming stopping boundary, demonstrating superiority of holding medication. Specific GLP-1/GIP agonist drug names and doses varied among participants and were not specified as part of the intervention definition.

title: Exploratory Analysis of Liraglutide Effects on Obstructive Sleep Apnea and Health-Related Quality of Life in Individuals With Obesity and COPD: A Secondary Analysis of a Randomised Controlled Trial.
population: Adults aged 40-70 years with COPD (defined as FEV1/FVC < 70% after maximal bronchodilation), former smokers, with overweight or obesity (BMI > 27 kg/m²). Exclusion criteria: current smoker, treatment with systemic corticosteroids, diabetes mellitus of any type, interstitial pulmonary disease, severe hepatic, renal or heart disease, pancreatitis, pregnancy, or breastfeeding.
intervention: Liraglutide 3.0 mg subcutaneous injection for 40 weeks (with titration up to 3.0 mg)
comparison: Placebo subcutaneous injection for 40 weeks
outcomes_primary: This is a secondary exploratory analysis; outcomes analyzed include: OSA prevalence and severity (Apnea-Hypopnea Index [AHI], Oxygen Desaturation Index [ODI]), daytime sleepiness (Epworth Sleepiness Scale [ESS]), health-related quality of life (Short Form-36 version 2 [SF-36v2] domain scores)
outcomes_secondary: Not separately defined as this is a secondary analysis of a trial with pulmonary function as the primary outcome
extraction_notes: This is a secondary exploratory analysis of an RCT primarily designed to investigate respiratory effects on pulmonary function. The outcomes listed are exploratory secondary outcomes of the original trial. Small sample size (40 randomized, 30 completed).

title: Pharmacological and metabolic effects of Bifidobacterium triple viable capsules and Five-animal Play in patients with impaired glucose tolerance.
population: Patients with impaired glucose tolerance (IGT), a pre-diabetic condition
intervention: Bifidobacterium triple viable capsules for four weeks; Huatuo Five-animal Play exercise for four weeks
comparison: Low-intensity aerobic activity for four weeks
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished. Outcomes measured include: fasting blood glucose (FBG), 2h post-load glucose (2hFBG), glycosylated hemoglobin (HbA1c), fasting insulin, homeostasis model assessment of insulin resistance (HOMA-IR), serum lipids (TC, TG, LDL-C, HDL-C), circulating GLP-1, Wnt5a and Sfrp5, and kidney/liver safety. Sample size was 90 participants in this randomized parallel-group trial.

title: Oral Semaglutide and Change in Cardiovascular Risk Factors in High-Risk Type 2 Diabetes: A Post Hoc Secondary Analysis of the SOUL Randomized Clinical Trial.
population: Adults aged 50 years or older with type 2 diabetes, HbA1c between 6.5% and 10.0%, and at least one of the following: coronary heart disease, cerebrovascular disease, symptomatic peripheral artery disease, and/or chronic kidney disease. Exclusions included myocardial infarction, stroke, hospitalization for unstable angina pectoris or transient ischemic attack within 60 days prior to screening, planned coronary/carotid/peripheral artery revascularization, heart failure New York Heart Association class IV, and/or treatment with any GLP-1 RA within 30 days before screening.
intervention: Once-daily oral semaglutide (maximum dose 14 mg) in addition to standard of care
comparison: Matching placebo once daily in addition to standard of care
outcomes_primary: Association of oral semaglutide vs placebo with glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c), body weight, and blood pressure using estimated treatment differences (ETDs); association with high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP) and lipid plasma levels (total cholesterol, non-HDL-C, HDL-C, LDL-C, triglycerides) using estimated treatment ratios (ETRs)
outcomes_secondary: Change in HbA1c and change in body weight (supportive secondary end points); post hoc analyses included blood pressure (systolic BP, diastolic BP, pulse pressure), pulse, plasma levels of hsCRP and lipids
extraction_notes: This is a post hoc secondary analysis of the SOUL randomized clinical trial. Primary outcomes as defined here refer to the focus of this secondary analysis, not the original SOUL trial primary outcome (major adverse cardiovascular events). The original trial was event-driven with a mean follow-up of 47.5 months.

title: Weight Changes With Tirzepatide and Concomitant Weight-Inducing Medications: Post Hoc Analysis of Randomized Clinical Trials.
population: Adults with obesity (BMI ≥30) or overweight (BMI ≥27) with at least one weight-related condition, excluding type 2 diabetes, who initiated at least one weight-inducing medication during the trial period (nonsteroid medications used for ≥3 months or oral corticosteroids used for ≥1 week)
intervention: Tirzepatide subcutaneous injection once weekly; SURMOUNT-1: 5 mg, 10 mg, or 15 mg for 72 weeks; SURMOUNT-3: maximum tolerated dose (10 or 15 mg) for 72 weeks after 12-week intensive lifestyle intervention; SURMOUNT-4: maximum tolerated dose (10 or 15 mg) for 88 weeks after 36-week open-label tirzepatide lead-in period
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Percentage change in body weight from randomization to week 72 (SURMOUNT-1 and SURMOUNT-3) or week 88 (SURMOUNT-4)
extraction_notes: This is a post hoc analysis of the SURMOUNT-1, -3, and -4 trials focusing on the subgroup of participants who initiated concomitant weight-inducing medications during the study. Secondary outcomes were not explicitly defined for this post hoc analysis. Current or recent use of weight-inducing medication was an exclusion criterion at study entry, but these medications could be initiated during the study.

title: Safety and efficacy of switching from dulaglutide to tirzepatide across clinically relevant baseline characteristics in participants with T2D: subgroup analysis of SURPASS-SWITCH.
population: Adults ≥18 years of age with type 2 diabetes, HbA1c ≥7.0% to ≤9.5%, BMI ≥25 kg/m², on a stable non-maximal dose of once-weekly dulaglutide (0.75 mg or 1.5 mg) for at least 6 months, and treatment with a stable dose of 0-3 oral antihyperglycemic medications (any combination of metformin, sulfonylurea, and sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 inhibitor) for at least 3 months, with stable body weight
intervention: Switch to tirzepatide 2.5 mg once weekly with escalation to 15 mg or maximum tolerated dose, with dose escalations performed every 4 weeks
comparison: Continue with dulaglutide and escalate to dulaglutide 4.5 mg once weekly or maximum tolerated dose, with dose escalations performed every 4 weeks
outcomes_primary: Change from baseline in HbA1c at week 40
outcomes_secondary: Change from baseline in body weight at week 40; treatment-emergent adverse events including gastrointestinal events (nausea, diarrhea) and hypoglycemia (level 1: blood glucose ≥54 and <70 mg/dL; level 2: blood glucose <54 mg/dL)
extraction_notes: This is a subgroup analysis of SURPASS-SWITCH examining efficacy and safety across prespecified baseline subgroups including age, HbA1c, duration of T2D, baseline dulaglutide dose, duration of dulaglutide dose, BMI, ethnicity, and sex. Phase IV, randomized, open-label, active-controlled, parallel-group trial. Treatment period was 40 weeks with 4-week safety follow-up.

title: GZR18, a GLP-1 analog with once-weekly or bi-weekly dosing for body weight management: A randomized, placebo-controlled, phase 1b/2a trial.
population: Chinese adults aged 18-65 years with overweight (BMI 24.0-28.0 kg/m2 with comorbidities) or obesity (BMI ≥28.0 kg/m2); exclusion criteria included type 1 or type 2 diabetes, fasting plasma glucose ≥7.0 mmol/L, prior bariatric surgery, severe hypertension, decompensated heart failure, history of pancreatitis, and use of GLP-1 receptor agonists or weight-affecting medications within 3 months
intervention: GZR18 (bofanglutide), a subcutaneously administered GLP-1 receptor agonist; Part A: dose escalation from 0.6 mg to 4.8 mg once-weekly for 26 weeks; Part B: dose escalation from 1.5 mg to 30 mg once-weekly (QW) or bi-weekly (Q2W) for 35 weeks
comparison: Matching placebo administered subcutaneously at the same frequency (once-weekly or bi-weekly)
outcomes_primary: Safety assessed by incidence of treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) and serious adverse events (SAEs), including gastrointestinal adverse events, hypoglycemic episodes, injection site reactions, vital signs, physical examinations, 12-lead ECGs, clinical laboratory parameters, and immunogenicity (anti-GZR18 and neutralizing antibodies); Part A also included change from baseline in body weight at end of treatment
outcomes_secondary: Efficacy endpoints: change from baseline in body weight, BMI, waist circumference, blood pressure (systolic and diastolic), fasting blood glucose, fasting insulin, and lipid profiles (total cholesterol, triglycerides); proportion of participants achieving ≥5% reduction in body weight from baseline; pharmacokinetic endpoints: trough concentrations of GZR18 following repeated doses
extraction_notes: Two-part trial with different populations (Part A included overweight with comorbidities or obese; Part B included only obese). Randomization was 3:1 (GZR18:placebo). In Part B, assignment to QW vs Q2W dosing frequency was based on participant preference after reaching 9 mg/week dose, not randomized. Small sample size (N=60 total).

title: Dulaglutide and neurodegeneration biomarkers: REWIND post hoc analysis.
journal: Alzheimer's & dementia : the journal of the Alzheimer's Association
population: Adults aged at least 50 years with type 2 diabetes and either a previous cardiovascular event or cardiovascular risk factors, glycated hemoglobin ≤9.5% (≤80 mmol/mol), body mass index ≥23 kg/m2, taking up to two oral glucose-lowering drugs with or without basal insulin at stable doses for at least 3 months. Exclusions: coronary or cerebrovascular event within previous 2 months, estimated glomerular filtration rate <15 mL/min/1.73 m2 or undergoing renal dialysis, severe hypoglycemia within past year, cancer within past 5 years, history of pancreatitis, bariatric surgery, or known abnormal gastric emptying, or previous participation in any dulaglutide study.
intervention: Dulaglutide 1.5 mg once-weekly subcutaneous injection over median follow-up of 5.4 years
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Change in plasma neurofilament light chain (NfL), phosphorylated tau217 (p-tau217), and glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) biomarker levels over 2 years
outcomes_secondary: Substantive cognitive impairment (SCI), defined as the first occurrence of a follow-up score on the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) or Digit Symbol Substitution Test (DSST) with a standard deviation of 1.5 or more below the mean baseline country-standardized score, over 5 years
extraction_notes: Post hoc analysis of the REWIND cardiovascular outcomes trial. Primary and secondary outcomes designation based on analysis structure described in methods (ANCOVA for biomarker changes as primary endpoint, Cox model for SCI as secondary endpoint). Biomarker data available for 7368 of 8828 participants with cognitive testing data.

title: Efficacy and safety of co-administered cagrilintide and semaglutide versus semaglutide alone in adults with overweight or obesity with or without type 2 diabetes in Japan and Taiwan (REDEFINE 5): a multicentre, randomised, active-controlled, phase 3a trial.
population: Adults aged at least 18 years with BMI of at least 27 kg/m², with or without type 2 diabetes, in Japan and Taiwan (east Asian population)
intervention: Fixed-dose combination of cagrilintide 2.4 mg and semaglutide 2.4 mg, subcutaneous (route implied), for 68 weeks
comparison: Semaglutide 2.4 mg alone
outcomes_primary: Change in bodyweight from baseline to week 68
outcomes_secondary: Not explicitly stated in abstract
extraction_notes: BMI threshold description appears truncated in abstract. Secondary outcomes not explicitly defined. Route of administration not explicitly stated but implied subcutaneous based on drug class.

title: Once-weekly semaglutide versus placebo in patients with alcohol use disorder and comorbid obesity: a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial.
population: Treatment-seeking participants with moderate to severe alcohol use disorder and comorbid obesity
intervention: Semaglutide 2.4 mg subcutaneously once-weekly for 26 weeks, in addition to standard cognitive behavioural therapy
comparison: Placebo (saline subcutaneously) once-weekly, in addition to standard cognitive behavioural therapy
outcomes_primary: Reduction in the number of heavy drinking days assessed after 26 weeks of intervention
outcomes_secondary: Multiple secondary alcohol-related and somatic outcomes (not further specified in abstract)
extraction_notes: Secondary outcomes are mentioned but not explicitly defined in the abstract. Safety was assessed in all treated patients as an additional outcome.

title: Plasma enteroglucagon after jejunoileal bypass with 3:1 or 1:3 jejunoileal ratio.
population: Morbidly obese patients
intervention: Jejunoileal bypass with 1:3 jejunoileal ratio of the functioning segment
comparison: Jejunoileal bypass with 3:1 jejunoileal ratio of the functioning segment; unoperated patients
outcomes_primary: Plasma enteroglucagon concentration (fasting values and postprandial integrated increments after a test meal)
extraction_notes: This is a non-randomized comparative study. Sample sizes are small (n=24 total: 12 with 1:3 bypass, 6 with 3:1 bypass, 6 unoperated). No explicit designation of primary vs secondary outcomes; all outcomes listed as primary. Drug dosing not applicable as intervention is surgical.

title: The effect of pirenzepine on meal-stimulated gastrointestinal hormones.
population: Healthy subjects
intervention: Pirenzepine 10 mg in 2 ml solvent given intravenously 30 min before a standard normal breakfast (2220 kJ)
comparison: 2 ml saline (0.15 mol/l) given intravenously 30 min before a standard normal breakfast
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished. Outcomes measured included plasma concentrations of gut hormones (insulin, glucagon, gastric inhibitory peptide, neurotensin, vasoactive intestinal peptide, somatostatin, pancreatic polypeptide, motilin, enteroglucagon, gastrin) in fasting and postprandial states. Crossover design with random order on separate days. Small sample size (n=6).

title: Gut and pancreatic hormones after jejunoileal bypass with 3:1 or 1:3 jejunoileal ratio.
population: Obese patients, including those waiting for bypass surgery and those who had undergone jejunoileal bypass surgery 3, 9, or 15 months earlier
intervention: Jejunoileal bypass with 1:3 jejunoileal ratio (short jejunal and long ileal segment)

title: Pharmacokinetic, insulinotropic, and glucagonostatic properties of GLP-1 [7-36 amide] after subcutaneous injection in healthy volunteers. Dose-response-relationships.

title: Glucagon-like peptide-1 7-36 amide and peptide YY from the L-cell of the ileal mucosa are potent inhibitors of vagally induced gastric acid secretion in man.

title: Fat-induced ileal brake in humans: a dose-dependent phenomenon correlated to the plasma levels of peptide YY.

title: Voglibose (AO-128) is an efficient alpha-glucosidase inhibitor and mobilizes the endogenous GLP-1 reserve.

title: Potential therapeutic levels of glucagon-like peptide I achieved in humans by a buccal tablet.

title: Effects of glucagon-like peptide 1 (7-36 amide) on whole-body protein metabolism in healthy man.
